title: [HIGH] Legacy resume age check ignores state updated_at fallback
description:
Review of 8f7a6f48 ([bug-fix][bd-omfqk] enforce stale resume guard for legacy state files) found a regression in resumeCheckpointTime.

Before the commit, applyResumeOptions used LastCheckpointAt and fell back to ExecutionState.UpdatedAt when LastCheckpointAt was zero:

  checkpoint := state.LastCheckpointAt
  if checkpoint.IsZero() {
      checkpoint = state.UpdatedAt
  }

The new resumeCheckpointTime expands the legacy fallback to child StepResult/foreach/parallel/in-flight timestamps, but it no longer considers state.UpdatedAt at all. If a legacy state has LastCheckpointAt omitted, UpdatedAt set to an old value, and no child timestamps (for example a run cancelled or persisted before any step result, or an older/minimal state fixture), resumeCheckpointTime returns the zero time. applyResumeOptions then skips the MaxResumeAge check because checkpoint.IsZero() is true, allowing stale state to resume.

Impact: stale legacy state files can bypass the MaxResumeAge guard. This weakens the resume safety contract and can revive old pipeline work that the operator explicitly bounded.

Likely fix: include state.UpdatedAt in resumeCheckpointTime before or after FinishedAt, e.g. checkpoint = mostRecentTime(checkpoint, state.UpdatedAt), while preserving the newer child timestamp scan for legacy states with missing/zero UpdatedAt. Add a regression test where LastCheckpointAt is zero, UpdatedAt is older than MaxResumeAge, StartedAt and child timestamps are zero/missing, and ResumeWithOptions rejects the stale state.

No direct fix applied in this review pass because the requested CRITICAL/HIGH fix policy restricts fixes to NEW files only, while the production fix belongs in internal/pipeline/state_resume.go.
close_reason: Production fix landed at d8e724c2 (peer commit absorbed my work). resumeCheckpointTime now falls back to UpdatedAt; Resume() defers StartedAt/UpdatedAt mutations until after applyResumeOptions accepts the prior state, so legacy state with only UpdatedAt cannot bypass MaxResumeAge. TestResumeRejectsLegacyStateWithOnlyUpdatedAt added.

title: [MEDIUM] AgentScripter delayed responses survive MockTmuxClient.Reset
description: Review of 700a3e42 found that MockTmuxClient.Reset clears pane output/history and resets AgentScripter.used/produced, but delayed responses launched by deliverScriptedResponse keep running in goroutines. After Reset, those stale goroutines still append their old response and call markProduced(), contaminating the fresh mock state and making tests that reuse a delayed scripter flaky. Reset needs a generation/cancel mechanism or delayed delivery must verify it still belongs to the active script generation before appending.
close_reason: Added atomic generation counter on AgentScripter that bumps on Reset(); deliverScriptedResponse goroutines capture the generation at match time and drop the delivery if Reset happened in between. Two regression tests cover (a) stale STALE response not appended after Reset and (b) fresh delivery still works on the new generation.

title: Scope idempotent replay to request shape and preserve replay metadata
description: Fresh-eyes audit found that internal/serve idempotency middleware caches responses only by raw Idempotency-Key. Reusing the same key across different methods or routes can replay the wrong response body, and replayed bodies can carry stale request_id metadata that no longer matches headers. Scope cache entries to the request shape, preserve cached replay headers/metadata, and add regression coverage.
close_reason: Scoped idempotent replay by request shape, preserved replay request metadata, added regressions, and verified with rch build + idempotency serve tests.

title: [MEDIUM] robot/causality: oversized pipeline state files silently dropped, no warning surfaced
description:
In internal/robot/causality.go loadPipelineCausalityEvents, when readPipelineStateFile returns ANY error — including the new 'exceeds limit' error from bd-w3ft1 (e7387292) — the caller silently continues:

  st, err := readPipelineStateFile(filepath.Join(dir, entry.Name()))
  if err != nil {
    continue
  }

There is no log, no entry appended to output.Warnings, and no per-source CausalitySourceStatus entry like the agentmail and session loaders produce. From the operator's perspective the --robot-causality output looks clean but is silently missing data.

This matters specifically because the size cap is the only way the command admits to data loss. Other readPipelineStateFile errors (corrupt JSON, permission denied) are also dropped silently, but those are pre-existing — the new cap makes silent dropping easier to trigger because it has a deterministic bound rather than depending on filesystem corruption.

Fix: when readPipelineStateFile fails with the 'exceeds limit' error (or really any error), append to output.Warnings (e.g. 'pipeline_state run-1234.json skipped: file size exceeds 16MB cap') AND add a CausalitySourceStatus entry so consumers can see which runs were skipped. Pattern is already established by the agentmail loader (statuses + warnings on each failed sub-source).

Severity: MEDIUM — observability bug, not a correctness bug, but it interacts badly with the bd-w3ft1 cap: the cap is precisely what users will trip when they have a too-busy pipeline, and they will have no idea their causality data is incomplete.

Source: internal/robot/causality.go loadPipelineCausalityEvents:612-614.
close_reason: loadPipelineCausalityEvents now returns ([]CausalityEvent, []string, error). On readPipelineStateFile error (oversized file under bd-w3ft1 16MB cap, corrupt JSON, perm denied) the loader appends 'pipeline_state <name> skipped: <err>' to warnings. buildCausalityOutput merges those warnings into output.Warnings so the robot envelope surfaces what was dropped. New tests: TestLoadPipelineCausalityEvents_OversizedFileSurfacesWarning writes a >16MB dummy file and asserts events=0, warnings=1 mentioning the filename; TestBuildCausalityOutput_PipelineWarningsAppearInEnvelope verifies envelope merge. All 4 in-tree pipeline loader fakes updated to the new signature.

title: [HIGH] swarm/synthetic: bd-75unj renames goroutines→goroutines_leaked (breaking JSON), drops absolute count
description:
Commit 1ad88868 (bd-75unj 'clamp synthetic memory growth and report goroutine leak delta') makes two changes that together are a backwards-incompatible API change with information loss:

1. Field rename: SyntheticMetrics.Goroutines (json:'goroutines') → SyntheticMetrics.GoroutinesLeaked (json:'goroutines_leaked'). No schema version on SyntheticRunResult. Any consumer that still reads the 'goroutines' JSON tag — historical artifacts persisted by TestSyntheticHarnessLargeOptInWritesArtifact, dashboards, alerting — silently parses a missing field as zero. There is no MarshalJSON/UnmarshalJSON shim and no migration path.

2. Semantic flip: the field used to report the absolute goroutine count (always positive, ~5-10 for healthy program). Now it reports a non-negative delta (zero if no leak). The absolute baseline is no longer observable. If the harness develops a real, persistent goroutine leak the per-run delta may be 0 (steady-state at +N leaked since process start) while the absolute count continues to grow. The renamed metric cannot detect this case.

Suggested fix: keep both fields. Goroutines int (absolute, after-run) + GoroutinesLeaked int (post-clamp delta). Or version the artifact and provide a reader that handles both names. Until then this is a silent breaking change for anyone with stored artifacts.

Source: 1ad88868 internal/swarm/synthetic.go SyntheticMetrics fields. Tests in internal/swarm/synthetic_test.go assert non-negativity of the new field but do not exercise back-compat against an artifact written before the rename.
close_reason: Restored Goroutines int json:'goroutines' field alongside GoroutinesLeaked. Run() now sets both: Goroutines=goroutinesAfter (absolute count), GoroutinesLeaked=non-negative delta. slog Info now logs both. Doc-comment explains the steady-state leak rationale. Pre-bd-75unj artifacts and dashboards continue to parse the 'goroutines' tag without breakage; new GoroutinesLeaked carries the per-run delta semantics. swarm tests still pass.

title: OnSuccess children with explicit IDs nested in foreach body collide across iterations/rounds (sibling of bd-2ubxp.22)
description:
## Summary

`runOnSuccessSteps` (internal/pipeline/control_flow.go:309-362) stores child results at `state.Steps[child.ID]` directly. Only when `child.ID == ""` does it derive `parent.ID + "_on_success_" + i+1` (line 329-330); otherwise it uses the workflow-author-supplied ID verbatim.

When such an OnSuccess child is nested inside a foreach body (or a max_rounds body), the parent step's ID gets the `_iter<N>` (and `_round<N>` if max_rounds > 1) suffixes, but the explicit OnSuccess child ID does not. So the SAME `child.ID` is used across iterations/rounds, and `state.Steps[child.ID] = result` (line 339) clobbers earlier writes last-writer-wins.

Reproduce sketch:
```yaml
- id: outer
  foreach:
    items: ["a","b"]
    steps:
      - id: body
        command: "echo ${item}"
        on_success:
          - id: notify     # explicit ID — NOT prefixed
            command: "echo notified-for-${item}"
```
After both iterations, `state.Steps["notify"]` only reflects iteration 1's result. The `${item}` substitution still works (the on_success child runs twice), but only the last write survives.

This is the same class of bug as bd-2ubxp.22 (Branch/Parallel children), just for OnSuccess. The bd-2ubxp.21 docstring on `rewriteRoundStepIDs` enumerates Foreach/Loop (chain) and Branch/Parallel (don't chain) but does not mention OnSuccess.

## Severity

P3. Workflows that put OnSuccess inside a foreach body and rely on per-iteration `state.Steps[notify_id]` are uncommon but plausible (notification fan-outs, audit log dispatches). The substitution / dispatch still works; only the persisted result is clobbered. Severity matches bd-2ubxp.22.

## Suggested approach

In `runOnSuccessSteps`, when child.ID is non-empty, prefix it with `parent.ID + "_on_success_"` (or similar) before storing to state.Steps — same chaining contract as Foreach/Loop. Adjust the empty-ID branch to use the same shape so both paths are uniform.

## Acceptance

- A regression test exercises a foreach with N items where each iteration's body has OnSuccess[explicit-id]: after the run, state.Steps has N distinct entries (not 1).
- The rewriteRoundStepIDs docstring updates to enumerate OnSuccess alongside Branch/Parallel.

## Files

- internal/pipeline/control_flow.go (runOnSuccessSteps state.Steps key construction)
- internal/pipeline/foreach_max_rounds.go (rewriteRoundStepIDs docstring)

## Related

- bd-2ubxp.22 (Branch/Parallel sibling)
- bd-2ubxp.21 (rewriteRoundStepIDs contract docs)
close_reason: Fixed: OnSuccess child steps now derive parent-scoped execution IDs, foreach body steps fire OnSuccess after completion, foreach materialization substitutes OnSuccess child fields, and rewriteRoundStepIDs docs include the OnSuccess chaining contract. Added regression coverage for explicit on_success IDs inside foreach producing distinct per-iteration state.Steps keys.

title: [HIGH] Rejected stale resume refreshes checkpoint and bypasses MaxResumeAge
description: Review of 7304d410 found Resume() persists state after applyResumeOptions rejects a stale resume. persistState() unconditionally sets LastCheckpointAt and UpdatedAt to time.Now(), so a state rejected as older than MaxResumeAge is rewritten with a fresh checkpoint. A second resume attempt against the same run can then pass the stale-age guard and resume work that should remain blocked. Repro shape: stale persisted state with LastCheckpointAt 48h old, ResumeWithOptions(... MaxResumeAge: 1h ...) fails once, state file now has last_checkpoint_at near now, second call succeeds. Expected: failed resume validation must not refresh checkpoint freshness; persist the failure without advancing LastCheckpointAt, or skip persistence for stale-age rejection. Source commit: 7304d410 feat(pipeline): persist resumable execution state (bd-3nebw).
close_reason: Resume() no longer calls persistState() on the applyResumeOptions failure path so a rejected stale-age resume does not rewrite LastCheckpointAt/UpdatedAt to time.Now(). The error is still returned to the caller; the on-disk state file keeps its real age so a second attempt sees the same stale-age guard. Added TestResumeRejectingStaleStateDoesNotRefreshCheckpoint to assert one rejection does not unblock a follow-up.

title: [HIGH] pipeline resume accepts state from a different workflow
description:
Commit 7304d410 introduced persisted resume state, but Executor.Resume never checks that prior.WorkflowID matches the Workflow.Name being resumed. It only fills WorkflowID when the prior state is empty, then applyResumeState marks any completed StepResult IDs as executed in the current graph. If an operator passes a run ID from a different pipeline, steps with matching IDs can be skipped and their old outputs/variables reused in an incompatible workflow.

Impact: wrong workflow resumes can silently skip required commands/templates and produce stale or corrupted outputs. Resume should reject non-empty prior.WorkflowID values that do not match the loaded workflow (or require an explicit unsafe override).

Review source: 7304d410 feat(pipeline): persist resumable execution state (bd-3nebw).
close_reason: Resume now rejects non-empty prior.WorkflowID values that do not match workflow.Name with a clear error naming both workflows. Empty prior.WorkflowID still backfills (legacy compat). Three new resume_test.go cases: mismatched workflow rejection, matching-name happy path, and legacy empty-WorkflowID backfill.

title: [LOW] cli/work_queue_dry_test: TestQueueDryReservationTimeoutIsInteractive pins literal timeout value, brittle
description: internal/cli/work_queue_dry_test.go TestQueueDryReservationTimeoutIsInteractive (e03d18a6) asserts 'queueDryReservationTimeout != 2*time.Second' fails. Pinning the literal value adds no behavioral coverage — it's just a tautology that the constant equals what we wrote. Future tuning (say 3s for slow CI hosts, or making it configurable) breaks the test for no reason. Better pattern: assert the timeout falls in an 'interactive' range (e.g. 'queueDryReservationTimeout < 5*time.Second' AND '> 0') so the intent (must feel snappy) is what the test guards, not the magic number. This bead is LOW because it's a test smell, not a runtime defect, but worth fixing so peers don't pattern-match on this approach.
close_reason: Replaced literal-value pin (queueDryReservationTimeout != 2*time.Second) with an intent-based range check: queueDryReservationTimeout > 0 && < 5*time.Second. The 5s ceiling matches the agent-mail unhealthy-pause threshold and captures the 'must feel snappy' contract; the >0 floor catches an accidental zero that would disable the timeout. Future tuning (1.5s, 3s, configurable) no longer breaks the test for no reason. queue-dry tests still pass.

title: Fix agent status showing 'unknown' instead of actual state
description:
## Problem
Agent status in the detail panel shows "unknown" instead of the actual agent state (working, idle, waiting_input, etc.).

## Screenshot Evidence
Detail panel shows:
```
Status
  • unknown
```

## Code Locations
- internal/status/detector.go - UnifiedDetector implementation
- internal/tui/dashboard/dashboard.go - StatusUpdateMsg handling (line 1192+)
- internal/tui/dashboard/panels/detail.go - Detail panel rendering

## Possible Causes
1. **Status detection timeout** - Detector may be timing out before getting status
2. **Pane parsing failure** - Unable to parse pane content for status indicators
3. **Race condition** - Status fetch completing after pane data is stale
4. **Missing status patterns** - New agent output patterns not recognized
5. **Async timing** - Status update arriving before pane data is set

## Investigation Steps
1. Enable debug logging in status detector
2. Check if pane content is being captured correctly
3. Verify status patterns match current agent output
4. Check timing of StatusUpdateMsg vs pane data updates

## Diagnostic Code
\`\`\`go
func (d *UnifiedDetector) DetectStatus(pane tmux.Pane) status.AgentStatus {
    log.Debug("detecting status", 
        "pane_id", pane.ID,
        "content_len", len(pane.Content),
        "content_preview", truncate(pane.Content, 100))
    
    status := d.detect(pane)
    log.Debug("status detected",
        "pane_id", pane.ID,
        "status", status.State,
        "confidence", status.Confidence)
    
    return status
}
\`\`\`

## Fix Pattern
\`\`\`go
// Ensure status is never "unknown" if we have pane content
func (d *UnifiedDetector) detect(pane tmux.Pane) AgentStatus {
    if len(pane.Content) == 0 {
        return AgentStatus{State: "no_content", Confidence: 0}
    }
    
    // Try all detection methods
    if s := d.detectByPrompt(pane); s.Confidence > 0.5 {
        return s
    }
    if s := d.detectByActivity(pane); s.Confidence > 0.5 {
        return s
    }
    if s := d.detectByOutput(pane); s.Confidence > 0.5 {
        return s
    }
    
    // Fallback with reason
    return AgentStatus{
        State: "unrecognized",
        Confidence: 0.1,
        Reason: "no patterns matched",
    }
}
\`\`\`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Status shows actual agent state (working/idle/waiting/etc.)
- [ ] "unknown" only shown when genuinely unable to determine
- [ ] Status updates within 2 seconds of pane change
- [ ] Status confidence indicator shown when low confidence

## Unit Tests
1. TestStatusDetector_WorkingPattern - detects "working" from tool output
2. TestStatusDetector_IdlePattern - detects "idle" from prompt
3. TestStatusDetector_WaitingPattern - detects "waiting_input" from input prompt
4. TestStatusDetector_EmptyPane - returns "no_content" not "unknown"
5. TestStatusDetector_UnrecognizedReturnsReason - fallback includes reason

## E2E Tests
1. Spawn Claude agent - verify status shows "working" during task
2. Complete task - verify status shows "idle" at prompt
3. Ask question - verify status shows "waiting_input"
4. Rapid status changes - verify UI updates correctly

## Logging
- INFO: Log status changes with before/after
- DEBUG: Log detection method used and confidence
- WARN: Log when falling back to unknown/unrecognized
- ERROR: Log detection failures with pane content sample

title: EPIC: Fleet Management Commands (scale, rebalance, review-queue)
description:
## Goal
Provide a cohesive set of commands for managing agent fleet composition, workload distribution, and batch operations.

## Commands in Scope

### ntm scale
Manual scaling to target agent counts without autonomous auto-scaling.
- `ntm scale <session> --cc=N --cod=N --gmi=N`
- Computes delta vs current counts and calls ntm add/kill
- Safe confirmations for scale-down
- Never auto-kills user pane

### ntm rebalance
Manual rebalance suggestions when agents join/leave or workloads become uneven.
- `ntm rebalance <session>` shows imbalance and suggests reassignments
- `ntm rebalance <session> --apply` applies after confirmation
- Detects dead agents and suggests orphan task reassignment

### ntm review-queue
Suggests review prompts for idle agents to keep them productive.
- `ntm review-queue <session>` lists idle agents + recommended prompts
- `ntm review-queue <session> --send` dispatches after confirmation
- Configurable idle threshold and review templates

### ntm send --batch
Explicit batch prompt delivery from files.
- `ntm send <session> --batch file.txt` sends prompts in order
- Supports comments (#) and separators (---) in batch files
- Agent targeting: --filter, --agent, --broadcast

## Design Philosophy
- All commands are **manual** (user-initiated), not autonomous
- All modifications require **confirmation** (unless --force)
- All commands support **--dry-run** for safe preview
- All commands support **--format json** for robot mode
- Graceful degradation when assignment tracking unavailable

## Success Criteria
- Commands work without assignment tracking (basic mode)
- Commands enhance with assignment tracking when available
- Clear, deterministic output for same input state
- No background daemons or automatic triggers
- Comprehensive logging for debugging
notes:

## LimitDetector: Capture Pane Output via tmux capture-pane

### Purpose
Implement the pane output capture functionality that feeds pattern matching.

### Implementation Details

**File:** Part of `internal/swarm/limit_detector.go`

**Function:**
```go
// capturePaneOutput captures the last N lines from a pane.
func (d *LimitDetector) capturePaneOutput(sessionPane string, lines int) (string, error) {
    // sessionPane format: "session_name:window.pane" (e.g., "cc_agents_1:1.3")
    
    // Use /usr/bin/tmux to avoid zsh plugin issues
    args := []string{
        "capture-pane",
        "-t", sessionPane,
        "-p",                          // Print to stdout
        fmt.Sprintf("-S", "-%d", lines), // Start line (negative = from end)
    }
    
    cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "/usr/bin/tmux", args...)
    output, err := cmd.Output()
    if err != nil {
        return "", fmt.Errorf("capture-pane failed: %w", err)
    }
    
    return string(output), nil
}
```

**Integration with Existing Code:**
The `internal/tmux/session.go` already has capture-pane functionality. Reuse that:

title: Feature: Ensemble Orchestrator - Spawning and mode assignment
description:
# Feature: Ensemble Orchestrator - 3-Stage Pipeline Coordinator

Orchestrates the full ensemble pipeline: Intake → Mode Run → Synthesis.

## Pipeline Stages

### Stage 1: Intake (Coordinated)
1. Check context pack cache
2. If miss: generate context pack via ContextPackGenerator
3. If context thin: prompt user with targeted questions
4. Cache context pack for reuse

### Stage 2: Mode Run (Parallel)
1. Load ensemble definition (e.g., 'project-diagnosis')
2. Resolve mode IDs to full ReasoningMode objects
3. Generate prompts via PromptInjector (base + preamble + schema)
4. Spawn N agents in parallel tmux windows
5. Monitor progress, token spend, early stop conditions
6. Collect outputs as agents complete

### Stage 3: Synthesis (Sequential)
1. Validate all outputs against OutputSchema
2. Run mechanical merging (grouping, de-duplication)
3. Spawn Synthesizer agent with merged inputs
4. Spawn Disagreement Auditor with synthesis + raw outputs
5. Combine into final report

## EnsembleManager Core
```go
type EnsembleManager struct {
    Config          *EnsembleConfig
    ContextGen      *ContextPackGenerator
    PromptInjector  *PromptInjector
    BudgetTracker   *BudgetTracker
    OutputCollector *OutputCollector
    Synthesizer     *Synthesizer
    Auditor         *DisagreementAuditor
    Metrics         *MetricsCollector
}

func (m *EnsembleManager) Run(ensemble string, problem string) (*EnsembleResult, error)
func (m *EnsembleManager) RunStage1() (*ContextPack, error)
func (m *EnsembleManager) RunStage2(ctx *ContextPack) ([]ModeOutput, error)
func (m *EnsembleManager) RunStage3(outputs []ModeOutput) (*SynthesisReport, error)
```

## Agent Assignment Strategy

### Default: Round-Robin
Distribute modes across available agent types (claude, codex, gemini).

### Affinity-Based
Some modes work better with certain agents:
- Formal modes → Claude (strong logical reasoning)
- Creative modes → Gemini (divergent thinking)
- Analytical modes → Codex (code understanding)

### User Override
Allow explicit agent assignment per mode.

## State Tracking

Track ensemble state for recovery and monitoring:
```go
type EnsembleState struct {
    SessionName  string
    Ensemble     string
    Stage        PipelineStage  // intake, mode_run, synthesis
    Agents       []AgentState
    Budget       BudgetState
    StartedAt    time.Time
}
```

## Files
- internal/ensemble/manager.go - Core orchestration
- internal/ensemble/assignment.go - Agent assignment
- internal/ensemble/state.go - State tracking
- internal/swarm/ensemble_integration.go - Tmux/swarm integration

title: E2E Tests: Dashboard visual regression with VHS recordings
description:
## Overview
End-to-end visual regression tests using VHS (terminal recording) to verify the dashboard renders correctly across different scenarios.

## Prerequisites
- VHS installed: \`brew install vhs\` or \`go install github.com/charmbracelet/vhs@latest\`
- ffmpeg for video processing
- ImageMagick for screenshot comparison

## Test File Location
- tests/e2e/dashboard_visual_test.go
- testdata/vhs/*.tape (VHS tape files)
- testdata/golden/*.png (golden screenshots)

## VHS Tape Files

### 1. Basic Render Test

### 3. Navigation Test

Set FontSize 14

# Navigate down
Type "j"
Sleep 300ms
Screenshot testdata/screenshots/nav-down1.png

Type "k"
Sleep 300ms

# Select by number
Type "5"
Sleep 500ms

### 4. Refresh Test (No Accumulation)
\`\`\`tape
# File: testdata/vhs/dashboard-refresh.tape
Output testdata/vhs/dashboard-refresh.gif
Set FontSize 14
Set Width 1200
Set Height 800

Type "ntm dashboard test-session"
Enter
Sleep 2s

# Manual refresh
Type "r"
Sleep 2s
Screenshot testdata/screenshots/refresh-after1.png

Type "r"
Sleep 2s
Screenshot testdata/screenshots/refresh-after2.png

Type "r"
Sleep 2s
Screenshot testdata/screenshots/refresh-after3.png
\`\`\`

## Visual Comparison Script
\`\`\`bash
#!/bin/bash
# scripts/visual-regression.sh

set -euo pipefail

TESTDATA="testdata"
GOLDEN="$TESTDATA/golden"
SCREENSHOTS="$TESTDATA/screenshots"
THRESHOLD=100  # Maximum pixel difference allowed

echo "Running VHS tapes..."
for tape in $TESTDATA/vhs/*.tape; do
    echo "  Running: $tape"
    vhs "$tape" 2>&1 | tee -a vhs.log
done

echo "Comparing screenshots..."
FAILED=0
for golden in $GOLDEN/*.png; do
    name=$(basename "$golden")
    screenshot="$SCREENSHOTS/$name"
    
    if [[ ! -f "$screenshot" ]]; then
        echo "  MISSING: $name"
        FAILED=1
        continue
    fi
    
    # Compare with ImageMagick
    diff=$(compare -metric AE "$golden" "$screenshot" /dev/null 2>&1 || true)
    
    if [[ "$diff" -gt "$THRESHOLD" ]]; then
        echo "  FAIL: $name (diff: $diff pixels)"
        # Generate diff image for debugging
        compare "$golden" "$screenshot" "$TESTDATA/diff-$name" || true
        FAILED=1
    else
        echo "  PASS: $name (diff: $diff pixels)"
    fi
done

if [[ "$FAILED" -eq 1 ]]; then
    echo ""
    echo "Visual regression tests FAILED"
    echo "Check testdata/diff-*.png for differences"
    exit 1
fi

echo ""
echo "All visual regression tests PASSED"
\`\`\`

## E2E Test Wrapper
\`\`\`go
// tests/e2e/dashboard_visual_test.go
func TestDashboard_VisualRegression(t *testing.T) {
    if os.Getenv("RUN_VISUAL_TESTS") == "" {
        t.Skip("set RUN_VISUAL_TESTS=1 to run visual regression tests")
    }
    
    // Run visual regression script
    cmd := exec.Command("bash", "scripts/visual-regression.sh")
    cmd.Dir = projectRoot()
    output, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
    
    t.Log(string(output))
    
    if err != nil {
        t.Fatalf("visual regression failed: %v", err)
    }
}
\`\`\`

## Specific Assertions

### No Status Bar Duplication
Check that screenshots contain exactly one instance of status bar text.

### Proper Layout at All Sizes
- 80x24: Compact mode, essential elements visible
- 120x40: Standard mode, all panels visible
- 200x60: Wide mode, expanded layout

### Animation Stability
Multiple screenshots at same state should be visually identical (except for animations).

## CI Integration
\`\`\`yaml
visual-tests:
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - name: Install VHS
      run: |
        brew install vhs imagemagick ffmpeg
    - name: Run visual tests
      run: |
        RUN_VISUAL_TESTS=1 go test -v ./tests/e2e/...
    - name: Upload diff images
      if: failure()
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
      with:
        name: visual-diffs
        path: testdata/diff-*.png
\`\`\`

## Updating Golden Files
\`\`\`bash
# After intentional UI changes, update golden files:
UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 RUN_VISUAL_TESTS=1 go test -v ./tests/e2e/...

# Or manually:
cp testdata/screenshots/*.png testdata/golden/
\`\`\`

## Logging
All test runs should log:
- VHS version
- Terminal size for each tape
- Screenshot file paths
- Pixel difference for each comparison
- Full command output on failure

title: Task: Implement EarlyStopDetector for marginal utility stopping
description:
# Task: EarlyStopDetector Implementation

Stop ensemble when new findings rate drops below threshold.

## Implementation
```go
// internal/ensemble/early_stop.go
type EarlyStopConfig struct {
    MinAgentsBeforeStop int     // Run at least N agents first
    FindingsThreshold   float64 // Stop if findings/token < threshold
    SimilarityThreshold float64 // Stop if output similarity > threshold
    WindowSize          int     // Evaluate over last N agents
    Enabled             bool
}

type EarlyStopDetector struct {
    Config        EarlyStopConfig
    Outputs       []ModeOutput
    TokensSpent   []int
}

type StopDecision struct {
    ShouldStop    bool
    Reason        string
    FindingsRate  float64
    SimilarityScore float64
    AgentsRun     int
}

func NewEarlyStopDetector(cfg EarlyStopConfig) *EarlyStopDetector
func (d *EarlyStopDetector) RecordOutput(output ModeOutput, tokens int)
func (d *EarlyStopDetector) ShouldStop() StopDecision
func (d *EarlyStopDetector) CalculateFindingsRate() float64
func (d *EarlyStopDetector) CalculateSimilarity() float64
```

## Stopping Criteria

### Findings Rate Drop
```
Rate = (new unique findings in window) / (tokens spent in window)
Stop if: rate < threshold AND agents_run >= min_agents
```

### Output Similarity
```
Similarity = average pairwise similarity of outputs in window
Stop if: similarity > threshold (outputs are redundant)
```

## Logging
- Log each decision with metrics
- Log when approaching threshold
- Log final stop reason

## File: internal/ensemble/early_stop.go

title: Skip-reason taxonomy (SkipKind enum) — distinguish when/dep/limit/not-impl
description:
## Background

Phase A + Phase B beads use Status=Skipped for many distinct cases:
- step.When evaluated false
- Step kind not yet implemented (Phase B in-flight)
- Failed dependency (transitive)
- --start-from skipped
- foreach iteration skipped via filter
- foreach iteration skipped via loop_control: continue

Operators can't distinguish via grep; the SkipReason text is free-form.

## Spec

Add a structured `SkipKind` enum to StepResult:

```go
type SkipKind string
const (
    SkipKindNone               SkipKind = ""
    SkipKindWhenCondition      SkipKind = "when_false"
    SkipKindNotImplemented     SkipKind = "phase_b_not_implemented"
    SkipKindFailedDependency   SkipKind = "failed_dependency"
    SkipKindStartFrom          SkipKind = "start_from_excluded"
    SkipKindForeachFilter      SkipKind = "foreach_filter_excluded"
    SkipKindForeachContinue    SkipKind = "foreach_loop_control_continue"
    SkipKindForeachBreak       SkipKind = "foreach_loop_control_break_after"

title: AgentLauncher: Handle window:pane addressing (session:1.N format)
description:
## Purpose
Set working directory to the assigned project path before launching each agent, ensuring agents operate in the correct context.

## Implementation Details

```go
// PaneLauncher handles agent launching with directory setup
type PaneLauncher struct {
    tmux          *tmux.Client
    cmdBuilder    *LaunchCommandBuilder
    orchestrator  *session.SessionOrchestrator
    logger        *slog.Logger
}

// LaunchAgentInPane sets up and launches an agent in a specific pane
func (pl *PaneLauncher) LaunchAgentInPane(ctx context.Context, sessionName string, paneSpec PaneSpec) error {
    // Validate project path exists
    if _, err := os.Stat(paneSpec.Project); err != nil {
        pl.logger.Error("project path does not exist",
            "project", paneSpec.Project,
            "error", err)
        return fmt.Errorf("project path %s: %w", paneSpec.Project, err)
    }
    
    pl.logger.Info("preparing pane for agent launch",
        "session", sessionName,
        "pane_index", paneSpec.Index,
        "project", paneSpec.Project,
        "agent_type", paneSpec.AgentType)
    
    // Get pane ID from orchestrator
    paneID, err := pl.orchestrator.GetPaneID(sessionName, paneSpec.Index)
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("get pane ID: %w", err)
    }
    
    // Step 1: Change to project directory
    cdCmd := fmt.Sprintf("cd %q", paneSpec.Project)
    if err := pl.tmux.SendKeys(paneID, cdCmd, true); err != nil {
        pl.logger.Error("failed to cd to project",
            "pane", paneID,
            "project", paneSpec.Project,
            "error", err)
        return fmt.Errorf("cd to project: %w", err)
    }
    
    pl.logger.Debug("changed directory",
        "pane", paneID,
        "project", paneSpec.Project)
    
    // Brief pause to ensure cd completes
    time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond)
    
    // Step 2: Build and send launch command
    launchCmd := pl.cmdBuilder.BuildLaunchCommand(paneSpec, paneSpec.Project)
    shellCmd := launchCmd.ToShellCommand()
    
    if err := pl.tmux.SendKeys(paneID, shellCmd, true); err != nil {
        pl.logger.Error("failed to launch agent",
            "pane", paneID,
            "command", shellCmd,
            "error", err)
        return fmt.Errorf("launch agent: %w", err)
    }
    
    pl.logger.Info("agent launched successfully",
        "session", sessionName,
        "pane", paneID,
        "agent_type", paneSpec.AgentType,
        "project", filepath.Base(paneSpec.Project),
        "command", shellCmd)
    
    return nil
}
```

## Integration with Existing Code
- Use internal/session.SessionOrchestrator for pane management
- Use internal/tmux.Client for SendKeys

## Logging Requirements
- Log project path validation
- Log directory change step
- Log launch command execution
- Include pane ID and session name in all logs

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Validate project path exists before launch
- [ ] Change directory before agent launch
- [ ] Small delay between cd and launch for reliability
- [ ] Quote paths to handle spaces
- [ ] Comprehensive error logging
- [ ] Integration with SessionOrchestrator
- [ ] Unit tests with mock tmux client

## Problem Being Solved

Multi-agent swarms benefit from having a "controller" agent that coordinates the others. Currently this requires manual setup.

```

### Behavior

Your role: coordinate work, prevent conflicts, ensure quality.
Use ntm robot commands to monitor other agents.

Use /usr/bin/tmux full path for reliable Enter key sending
description:
## Problem

When running tmux send-keys commands from certain shell environments (particularly when zsh tmux plugin is active), the bare `tmux` command gets intercepted by shell functions/aliases, causing:
- Commands fail silently or produce errors like `_zsh_tmux_plugin_run: command not found`
- Enter key not actually sent to panes
- Users see success messages but agents don't receive input

## Root Cause

The zsh tmux plugin defines functions that wrap tmux, and when running from within tmux (or from scripts sourced in zsh), these can interfere with direct tmux calls.

## Solution

Use the full path `/usr/bin/tmux` (or `$(which tmux)` resolved at startup) for ALL tmux operations throughout ntm, especially:
- `send-keys` commands
- `capture-pane` commands  
- Any command that needs to reliably communicate with tmux

## Files to Update

- All Go files that shell out to tmux
- Ensure tmux binary path is resolved once at startup and used consistently

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All tmux calls use full path (not bare `tmux`)
- [ ] Works correctly in zsh with tmux plugin active
- [ ] Works from within tmux sessions

title: Task: --robot-is-working Command Implementation
description:
## Task: --robot-is-working Command Implementation

### Why This Command Exists

This is the DIRECT ANSWER to the users critical requirement:

> "NEVER interrupt agents doing useful work\!\!\!"

Before ANY restart action, a controller agent must be able to ask: "Is this agent actively working?" This command provides that answer with structured, actionable output.

### Command Specification

```bash
# Check single pane
ntm --robot-is-working=myproject --panes=2

# Check multiple panes
ntm --robot-is-working=myproject --panes=2,3,4

# Check all agent panes (excludes pane 1 control shell)
ntm --robot-is-working=myproject --panes=all

# With verbosity (include raw sample for debugging)
ntm --robot-is-working=myproject --panes=2 --verbose
```

### Output Format (JSON)

```json
{
  "session": "myproject",
  "timestamp": "2026-01-20T15:30:00Z",
  "query": {
    "panes_requested": [2, 3, 4],
    "lines_captured": 100
  },
  "panes": {
    "2": {
      "agent_type": "cc",
      "is_working": true,
      "is_idle": false,
      "is_rate_limited": false,
      "is_context_low": false,
      "context_remaining": null,
      "confidence": 0.95,
      "indicators": {
        "work": ["```", "Writing to ", "Created "],
        "limit": []
      },
      "recommendation": "DO_NOT_INTERRUPT",
      "recommendation_reason": "Agent is actively writing code"
    },
    "3": {
      "agent_type": "cod",
      "is_working": false,
      "is_idle": true,
      "is_rate_limited": false,
      "is_context_low": true,
      "context_remaining": 12.0,
      "confidence": 0.90,
      "indicators": {
        "work": [],
        "limit": []
      },
      "recommendation": "SAFE_TO_RESTART",
      "recommendation_reason": "Agent idle with low context (12%)"
    },
    "4": {
      "agent_type": "gmi",
      "is_working": false,
      "is_idle": false,
      "is_rate_limited": true,
      "is_context_low": false,
      "context_remaining": null,
      "confidence": 0.85,
      "indicators": {
        "work": [],
        "limit": ["rate limit", "quota exceeded"]
      },
      "recommendation": "RATE_LIMITED_WAIT",
      "recommendation_reason": "Agent hit rate limit"
    }
  },
  "summary": {
    "total_panes": 3,
    "working_count": 1,
    "idle_count": 1,
    "rate_limited_count": 1,
    "context_low_count": 1,
    "by_recommendation": {
      "DO_NOT_INTERRUPT": [2],
      "SAFE_TO_RESTART": [3],
      "RATE_LIMITED_WAIT": [4]
    }
  }
}
```

### Recommendation Values and Their Meaning

| Recommendation | Meaning | Controller Action |
|----------------|---------|-------------------|
| `DO_NOT_INTERRUPT` | Agent is actively producing output | Leave alone\! |
| `SAFE_TO_RESTART` | Agent is idle, can be restarted | Safe to send exit + new prompt |
| `CONTEXT_LOW_CONTINUE` | Working but low context | Let finish current task, then restart |
| `RATE_LIMITED_WAIT` | Hit usage limit | Wait for reset or switch account |
| `ERROR_STATE` | Agent in error state | Investigate before action |
| `UNKNOWN` | Could not determine state | Manual inspection needed |

### Implementation Flow

```go
package robot

import (
    "github.com/username/ntm/internal/agent"
)

type IsWorkingResult struct {
    Session   string                     `json:"session"`
    Timestamp string                     `json:"timestamp"`
    Query     IsWorkingQuery             `json:"query"`
    Panes     map[string]PaneWorkStatus  `json:"panes"`
    Summary   IsWorkingSummary           `json:"summary"`
}

type IsWorkingQuery struct {
    PanesRequested []int `json:"panes_requested"`
    LinesCaptured  int   `json:"lines_captured"`
}

type PaneWorkStatus struct {
    AgentType            string            `json:"agent_type"`
    IsWorking            bool              `json:"is_working"`
    IsIdle               bool              `json:"is_idle"`
    IsRateLimited        bool              `json:"is_rate_limited"`
    IsContextLow         bool              `json:"is_context_low"`
    ContextRemaining     *float64          `json:"context_remaining,omitempty"`
    Confidence           float64           `json:"confidence"`
    Indicators           WorkIndicators    `json:"indicators"`
    Recommendation       string            `json:"recommendation"`
    RecommendationReason string            `json:"recommendation_reason"`
    RawSample            string            `json:"raw_sample,omitempty"` // Only with --verbose
}

func IsWorking(session string, panes []int, verbose bool) (*IsWorkingResult, error) {
    result := &IsWorkingResult{
        Session:   session,
        Timestamp: time.Now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339),
        Query: IsWorkingQuery{
            PanesRequested: panes,
            LinesCaptured:  100, // configurable
        },
        Panes: make(map[string]PaneWorkStatus),
    }
    
    parser := agent.NewParser()
    
    for _, pane := range panes {
        // Step 1: Capture pane output
        output, err := capturePaneOutput(session, pane, 100)
        if err \!= nil {
            // Record error but continue with other panes
            result.Panes[strconv.Itoa(pane)] = PaneWorkStatus{
                Recommendation:       "ERROR_STATE",
                RecommendationReason: fmt.Sprintf("Failed to capture: %v", err),
            }
            continue
        }
        
        // Step 2: Parse with agent parser
        state, err := parser.Parse(output)
        if err \!= nil {
            result.Panes[strconv.Itoa(pane)] = PaneWorkStatus{
                Recommendation:       "UNKNOWN",
                RecommendationReason: fmt.Sprintf("Parse failed: %v", err),
            }
            continue
        }
        
        // Step 3: Build status
        status := PaneWorkStatus{
            AgentType:        string(state.Type),
            IsWorking:        state.IsWorking,
            IsIdle:           state.IsIdle,
            IsRateLimited:    state.IsRateLimited,
            IsContextLow:     state.IsContextLow,
            ContextRemaining: state.ContextRemaining,
            Confidence:       state.Confidence,
            Indicators: WorkIndicators{
                Work:  state.WorkIndicators,
                Limit: state.LimitIndicators,
            },
            Recommendation:       string(state.GetRecommendation()),
            RecommendationReason: getRecommendationReason(state),
        }
        
        if verbose {
            status.RawSample = state.RawSample
        }
        
        result.Panes[strconv.Itoa(pane)] = status
    }
    
    // Step 4: Build summary
    result.Summary = buildSummary(result.Panes)
    
    return result, nil
}

func getRecommendationReason(state *agent.AgentState) string {
    rec := state.GetRecommendation()
    switch rec {
    case agent.RecommendDoNotInterrupt:
        return "Agent is actively producing output"
    case agent.RecommendSafeToRestart:
        return "Agent is idle"
    case agent.RecommendContextLowContinue:
        return fmt.Sprintf("Working but low context (%.0f%%)", *state.ContextRemaining)
    case agent.RecommendRateLimitedWait:
        return "Agent hit rate limit"
    case agent.RecommendErrorState:
        return "Agent in error state"
    default:
        return "Could not determine agent state"
    }
}
```

### Integration with Existing NTM Infrastructure

This command builds on existing robot mode infrastructure:

```go
// Uses existing --robot-tail to capture output
func capturePaneOutput(session string, pane int, lines int) (string, error) {
    // Internally calls same logic as:
    // ntm --robot-tail=session --panes=pane --lines=lines
    return robot.TailPane(session, pane, lines)
}
```

### Files to Create/Modify

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `cmd/ntm/robot_is_working.go` | CLI flag handling, arg parsing |
| `internal/robot/is_working.go` | Core logic (above) |
| `internal/robot/is_working_test.go` | Unit tests |

### Exit Codes

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| 0 | All panes analyzed successfully |
| 1 | Some panes could not be analyzed |
| 2 | Session not found |
| 3 | Invalid arguments |

### Usage Examples for Controllers

```bash
# Controller workflow: Check before restart
result=$(ntm --robot-is-working=myproject --panes=2)
recommendation=$(echo "$result" | jq -r ".panes.\"2\".recommendation")

if [ "$recommendation" = "DO_NOT_INTERRUPT" ]; then
    echo "Agent is working, leaving alone"
elif [ "$recommendation" = "SAFE_TO_RESTART" ]; then
    echo "Safe to restart"
    ntm --robot-smart-restart=myproject --panes=2
elif [ "$recommendation" = "RATE_LIMITED_WAIT" ]; then
    echo "Rate limited, waiting"
    # Could trigger caam account switch here
fi
```

### Why This Must Be Done Before Smart Restart

`--robot-smart-restart` (bd-2c7f4) DEPENDS on this command. The smart restart command calls `--robot-is-working` internally before taking any action. Without this foundation, smart restart cannot be implemented.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

# Configuration
LOG_FILE=/tmp/ntm-e2e-assign-full-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).log
SESSION="ntm-e2e-test-$$"

# Logging functions
log_debug() { echo "[$(date -Iseconds)] [DEBUG] $*" >> "$LOG_FILE"; }
log_info()  { echo "[$(date -Iseconds)] [INFO] $*" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"; }
log_warn()  { echo "[$(date -Iseconds)] [WARN] $*" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"; }
log_error() { echo "[$(date -Iseconds)] [ERROR] $*" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE" >&2; }
log_pass()  { echo "[$(date -Iseconds)] [PASS] $*" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"; }
log_fail()  { echo "[$(date -Iseconds)] [FAIL] $*" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE" >&2; }

assert_eq() {
    local desc="$1" expected="$2" actual="$3"
    log_debug "[ASSERT] Checking: $desc"
    log_debug "[ASSERT] Expected: $expected"
    log_debug "[ASSERT] Actual: $actual"
    if [[ "$expected" == "$actual" ]]; then
        log_pass "[ASSERT] $desc"
        return 0
    else
        log_fail "[ASSERT] $desc"
        log_error "[ASSERT] Expected: $expected, Got: $actual"
        return 1
    fi
}

run_cmd() {
    local cmd="$1"
    log_debug "[CMD] Running: $cmd"
    local output
    output=$(eval "$cmd" 2>&1) || {
        log_error "[CMD] Command failed: $cmd"
        log_error "[CMD] Output: $output"
        return 1
    }
    log_debug "[CMD] Output: $output"
    echo "$output"
}

    log_info "NTM Assign E2E Tests - $(date)"
    log_info "Session: $SESSION"
    log_info "=========================================="

trap cleanup EXIT
main

```

## Synthesis Algorithms

### Finding Deduplication
1. Group findings by evidence_pointer proximity
2. Cluster similar text using Jaccard similarity
3. Merge overlapping findings, combine contributing modes
4. Aggregate confidence scores (weighted average)

### Recommendation Prioritization
1. Score = priority × (# modes recommending)
2. Deduplicate similar recommendations
3. Link to supporting findings

### Executive Summary Generation
1. Extract key themes from theses
2. Highlight highest-impact findings
3. Note agreement/disagreement patterns
4. Keep under 500 words

title: Feature: Robot Environment Info Command (--robot-env)
description:
## Overview

Add `ntm --robot-env=SESSION` command that exposes environment quirks and configuration for correct agent operation.

## IMPORTANT: API Design Consistency

This command follows the established robot mode patterns:
- **Primary flag**: `--robot-env=SESSION` (not positional args)
- **All outputs**: JSON format
- **Optional session**: Can also run without session for global env info

## Command Interface

```bash
# Get environment info for a session
ntm --robot-env=myproject

# Get global environment info (no session context)
ntm --robot-env=global
```

## Output Schema

```json
{
  "session": "myproject",
  "tmux": {
    "binary_path": "/usr/bin/tmux",
    "version": "3.4",
    "shell_alias_detected": true,
    "recommended_path": "/usr/bin/tmux"
  },
  "session_structure": {
    "window_index": 1,
    "control_pane": 1,
    "agent_pane_start": 2,
    "agent_pane_end": 16,
    "total_agent_panes": 15
  },
  "shell": {
    "type": "zsh",
    "tmux_plugin_detected": true,
    "oh_my_zsh_detected": true
  },
  "timing": {
    "ctrl_c_gap_ms": 100,
    "post_exit_wait_ms": 3000,
    "cc_init_wait_ms": 6000,
    "prompt_submit_delay_ms": 1000
  },
  "targeting": {
    "pane_format": "session:window.pane",
    "example_agent_pane": "myproject:1.2",
    "example_control_pane": "myproject:1.1"
  }
}
```

## Why Each Field Matters

1. **tmux.binary_path**: Use this exact path, not just "tmux"
2. **tmux.shell_alias_detected**: Warning that tmux command may be aliased
3. **session_structure**: Exact pane targeting information
4. **timing**: Eliminates trial-and-error for timing-sensitive operations
5. **targeting.example_***: Copy-paste examples for correct pane targeting

## Detection Methods

- tmux path: `which tmux`, check against known paths
- shell alias: check for tmux function/alias in shell config
- window/pane structure: parse `tmux list-panes -F` output
- shell type: check $SHELL and common plugin indicators

## Use Cases

1. Agent bootstrap: read env first to configure operations
2. Debugging: understand why commands fail
3. Automation: get timing constants programmatically

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `--robot-env=SESSION` flag registered in root.go
- [ ] `--robot-env=global` works without session context
- [ ] JSON output matches schema exactly (all fields present)
- [ ] tmux.binary_path returns absolute path (not "tmux")
- [ ] tmux.version correctly parsed from `tmux -V`
- [ ] shell_alias_detected checks ~/.bashrc, ~/.zshrc for tmux aliases
- [ ] session_structure accurately reflects actual pane layout
- [ ] timing constants match config values
- [ ] Exit code 0 on success, 1 on partial data, 2 on error
- [ ] Non-existent session returns error JSON (not crash)

## Testing Requirements

### Unit Tests (internal/cli/robot_env_test.go)
- [ ] Flag parsing for --robot-env
- [ ] tmux binary detection logic
- [ ] tmux version parsing (various formats)
- [ ] Shell alias detection logic
- [ ] Session structure detection (mock tmux output)
- [ ] JSON output serialization
- [ ] Error handling for missing sessions

### E2E Tests (scripts/e2e_robot_env.sh)
```bash
#\!/bin/bash
# [E2E-ENV] Robot Env Info Command Tests
set -euo pipefail
LOG_PREFIX="[E2E-ENV]"

echo "$LOG_PREFIX Starting robot env E2E tests"

# Test 1: Global environment (no session)
echo "$LOG_PREFIX Test 1: Global environment info"
RESULT=$(ntm --robot-env=global)
echo "$LOG_PREFIX Result: $RESULT"
[[ $(echo "$RESULT" | jq -r ".tmux.binary_path") \!= "" ]] || exit 1
[[ $(echo "$RESULT" | jq -r ".tmux.version") \!= "" ]] || exit 1

# Test 2: Session-specific environment
TEST_SESSION="e2e_env_$$"
echo "$LOG_PREFIX Creating test session: $TEST_SESSION"
ntm spawn "$TEST_SESSION" --cc=1 --no-prompt
sleep 3

echo "$LOG_PREFIX Test 2: Session environment info"
RESULT=$(ntm --robot-env="$TEST_SESSION")
echo "$LOG_PREFIX Result: $RESULT"
[[ $(echo "$RESULT" | jq -r ".session") == "$TEST_SESSION" ]] || exit 1
[[ $(echo "$RESULT" | jq ".session_structure.total_agent_panes") -ge 1 ]] || exit 1
[[ $(echo "$RESULT" | jq -r ".targeting.example_agent_pane") \!= "" ]] || exit 1

# Test 3: Non-existent session
echo "$LOG_PREFIX Test 3: Non-existent session error"
RESULT=$(ntm --robot-env="nonexistent_session_xyz" 2>&1) || true
echo "$LOG_PREFIX Result: $RESULT"
[[ $(echo "$RESULT" | jq -r ".error" 2>/dev/null) \!= "" ]] || exit 1

# Cleanup
echo "$LOG_PREFIX Cleanup: Destroying test session"
tmux kill-session -t "$TEST_SESSION" 2>/dev/null || true

echo "$LOG_PREFIX All robot env E2E tests passed"
```

title: Implement --label flag for goal-labeled multi-session support (GH#49)
description:
## Problem

Users need to run multiple agent swarms on the same project directory simultaneously (e.g., frontend team and backend team). Currently each ntm session maps 1:1 to a project directory via `GetProjectDir()` in `internal/config/config.go:2995-2999`. There's no way to have `myproject--frontend` and `myproject--backend` sessions that both resolve to `~/projects/myproject/`.

## Current Implementation

`GetProjectDir()` at config.go:2995-2999:
```go
func (c *Config) GetProjectDir(session string) string {
    base := ExpandHome(c.ProjectsBase)
    return filepath.Join(base, session)
}
```

This joins the session name directly, so `myproject--frontend` would look for `~/projects/myproject--frontend/` (wrong directory).

## Implementation Plan

NOTE: This bead already has 5 sub-beads (bd-3cu02.11 through bd-3cu02.15) with detailed implementation plans. The core work is:

### 1. Create SessionBase() helper

Add a function that strips the label suffix from session names:
```go
func SessionBase(session string) string {
    if idx := strings.Index(session, "--"); idx > 0 {
        return session[:idx]
    }
    return session
}
```

### 2. Modify GetProjectDir() (config.go:2996)

One-line change:
```go
return filepath.Join(base, SessionBase(session))
```

### 3. Add --label flag to spawn command (spawn.go ~line 945)

Register the flag:
```go
cmd.Flags().StringVarP(&label, "label", "l", "", "Goal label for multi-session support (e.g., --label frontend)")
```

In the RunE handler, construct session name:
```go
sessionName := args[0]
if label != "" {
    sessionName = sessionName + "--" + label
}
```

### 4. Session name validation

The regex at `internal/tmux/session.go:1214` (`^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$`) already allows dashes, so `myproject--frontend` passes validation.

### 5. Pane title parsing

The pane title regex at `internal/tmux/session.go:26` matches `myproject--frontend__cc_1` correctly since `--` is just consecutive dashes.

## Files to Modify

- `internal/config/config.go` lines 2995-2999 (GetProjectDir + new SessionBase helper)
- `internal/cli/spawn.go` ~line 945 (add --label flag registration and session name construction)
- Tests for SessionBase and GetProjectDir with labels

## NOT implementing (per owner directive)

- Git worktree isolation (explicitly rejected)
- Any directory-level isolation between labeled sessions
acceptance_criteria:
1. `ntm spawn myproject --label frontend --cc=3` creates session named `myproject--frontend`
2. Session directory resolves to `~/projects/myproject/` (label stripped)
3. `ntm spawn myproject --label backend --cod=2` creates separate session `myproject--backend` in same directory
4. `ntm list` shows both sessions as distinct entries
5. `ntm kill myproject--frontend` kills only the frontend session
6. Session name validation passes for `--` separator
7. Pane titles work correctly: `myproject--frontend__cc_1`
8. Spawn without --label works exactly as before (no regression)
9. `ntm list --project myproject` shows all labeled sessions (if bd-3cu02.14 also implemented)
10. Agent Mail, CASS, checkpoints work correctly with shared directory
notes:
## Unit Tests

1. **TestSessionBase_WithLabel**: Assert SessionBase("myproject--frontend") == "myproject"
2. **TestSessionBase_NoLabel**: Assert SessionBase("myproject") == "myproject"
3. **TestSessionBase_MultipleDashes**: Assert SessionBase("my-project--my-label") == "my-project"
4. **TestSessionBase_EmptyLabel**: Assert SessionBase("myproject--") == "myproject"
5. **TestGetProjectDir_WithLabel**: Set ProjectsBase="~/projects". Assert GetProjectDir("myproject--frontend") == "~/projects/myproject"
6. **TestGetProjectDir_NoLabel**: Assert GetProjectDir("myproject") == "~/projects/myproject" (unchanged)

## E2E Test Script (scripts/test_label_sessions.sh)

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
echo "=== ntm --label E2E test ==="
PASS=0; FAIL=0

# Ensure test project dir exists
TEST_PROJECT="ntm_label_test_$$"
mkdir -p "$HOME/projects/$TEST_PROJECT"

# Test 1: Spawn with label
ntm spawn "$TEST_PROJECT" --label frontend --cc=1 --dry-run 2>&1 | grep -q "${TEST_PROJECT}--frontend" && ((PASS++)) || { echo "FAIL: session name not constructed"; ((FAIL++)); }

# Test 2: Spawn without label (backward compat)
ntm spawn "$TEST_PROJECT" --cc=1 --dry-run 2>&1 | grep -q "$TEST_PROJECT" && ((PASS++)) || { echo "FAIL: no-label spawn broken"; ((FAIL++)); }

# Test 3: Project dir resolution
# (This tests the Go code path, may need integration test)
ntm spawn "$TEST_PROJECT" --label frontend --cc=1 2>&1
sleep 2
# Check that the session exists and is in the right directory
tmux has-session -t "${TEST_PROJECT}--frontend" 2>/dev/null && ((PASS++)) || { echo "FAIL: session not created"; ((FAIL++)); }

# Cleanup
ntm kill "${TEST_PROJECT}--frontend" 2>/dev/null || true

echo "Results: $PASS passed, $FAIL failed"
[[ $FAIL -eq 0 ]] && echo "ALL PASS" || exit 1
```
close_reason: Feature complete via EPIC bd-3cu02 (all 15 sub-tasks). GH#49 request from mjdaly fully addressed: --label flag for goal-labeled multi-session support with shared project directory, --project filter for list/send/kill, comprehensive tests, docs updated.

title: Task: Implement 'ntm ensemble stop' command for graceful cancellation
description:
# Task: Implement Ensemble Stop Command

## Purpose
Allow users to gracefully stop an ensemble run before completion.

## Commands

### ntm ensemble stop [session]
Stop all agents in an ensemble run, save partial state.

### Behavior
1. Signal all ensemble agents to stop (SIGTERM)
2. Wait for graceful shutdown (5s timeout)
3. Force kill remaining agents
4. Collect any partial outputs available
5. Update ensemble state to 'stopped'
6. Show summary of what was captured

## Flags
--force        Skip graceful shutdown, force kill immediately
--no-collect   Don't attempt to collect partial outputs
--quiet        Minimal output

## Robot API
ntm --robot-ensemble-stop=SESSION

## File Location
internal/cli/ensemble_stop.go

## Acceptance Criteria
- Graceful agent shutdown with timeout
- Partial outputs collected when available
- State updated to 'stopped'
- Robot API returns structured result
- Works even if some agents have crashed

## Logging Requirements
- Log each agent stop attempt and result
- Log partial output collection status
- Log final state update
close_reason: Implemented 'ntm ensemble stop' command with CLI flags (--force, --no-collect, --quiet) and robot API (--robot-ensemble-stop). Added EnsembleStopped status, tests pass.

title: Eliminate production placeholders, stubs, and deceptive surfaces across NTM
description:
Background:
A repo-wide production-code audit on 2026-04-02 found multiple categories of incomplete implementation that are currently shipped in normal source paths: empty REST handlers, live routes that return 501 placeholder responses, CLI flags that are accepted but ignored, build-gated commands that default to stubs, platform-specific no-op implementations, heuristic parsers explicitly marked as placeholders, and output-quality paths that knowingly emit partial or fake data.

Goal:
Drive the codebase to a surface-truthfulness standard: every visible command, route, flag, capability, schema field, and public output path must either be fully implemented and tested or not be exposed at all. The project is explicitly early-stage and does not want compatibility shims or tech debt, so the preferred resolution is to implement real behavior where strategically valuable and delete or retire deceptive surfaces where it is not.

Scope:
This epic covers all placeholder/stub/mock-like production surfaces identified in the audit, including serve/router, CLI, legacy compatibility paths, build-gated ensemble surfaces, platform/runtime placeholders, quota parsing heuristics, robot output quality gaps, and regression-prevention guardrails.

Why this matters:
The immediate objective is correctness and operator trust. NTM is an orchestration tool for agents and humans; deceptive surfaces waste time, break automation, and make capability discovery unreliable. The longer-term objective is to enforce development discipline so partially implemented features do not silently accumulate.
design:
Program design:
- Organize work into cluster features so multiple agents can execute in parallel without losing the architectural intent.
- Treat surface truthfulness and verification as inseparable: every implementation bead is expected to land with package-level unit tests, focused integration tests, and user-visible e2e or negative-e2e scenarios where the surface is public, build-mode-sensitive, or operator-facing.
- Require every cluster to update code, tests, help text, route registration, capability output, error messaging, and docs/comments together so no stale surface survives in one layer.
- Make removals user-friendly even without compatibility shims: hidden or retired surfaces should have crisp help/docs updates, unambiguous errors where applicable, and clear migration notes for operators and agents.
- Prefer removal or concealment over warning-and-continue behavior whenever a feature is not actually implemented.
- Land regression guardrails after the functional and verification work so the resulting policy is continuously enforced rather than prematurely freezing debt in place.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance criteria:
- Every production placeholder/stub category identified by the audit is represented by a concrete child bead and no audited item is orphaned.
- The epic cannot be closed until all child feature beads are closed.
- Every remediated user-visible surface has corresponding verification coverage: package-level unit tests, focused integration tests, and e2e or negative-e2e scripts where appropriate.
- Detailed diagnostics exist for failure analysis: structured logging in the implementation paths, rich test logging in e2e/unit suites, and truthful help/capability/docs output.
- The final implementation state achieves surface truthfulness: exposed surfaces are real, retired surfaces are hidden or removed, and guardrails exist to prevent regression.
notes:
Notes:
- This epic is intentionally self-contained so future implementers do not need the original audit writeup.
- Exact file/function references live in the child beads where the work is executed.
- No compatibility debt should be introduced to preserve a placeholder surface that the project no longer wants.
- Verification is now a first-class planning concern in this epic; future work should not treat tests/e2e/logging as optional clean-up.
close_reason: Epic complete: eliminated production placeholders across REST (26 handlers removed), CLI (6 flags removed), legacy BD (daemon CLI+REST retired), ensemble (policy documented), quota (tests added), robot (synthesis/CASS/Rano/rate-limit/scanner fixed), with guardrail tests and verification matrix preventing regression

title: Make serve/router surfaces truthful and remove dormant stub endpoints
description:
Background:
The serve layer currently contains a dormant skeleton of REST handlers in internal/serve/dummy_handlers.go plus commented-out route registrations in internal/serve/server.go. This is worse than dead code alone because tests exercise direct method calls against handlers that are not actually wired, while the source tree visually implies a supported API surface that is not real.

Scope:
Clean up the server/router placeholder surface, decide which endpoints deserve real implementation, and remove or hide the rest. This cluster also includes the legacy /ws route that is live but still returns a placeholder 501 even though a real /api/v1/ws implementation exists elsewhere.

Why this matters:
The serve package is a machine-facing API surface. Placeholder handlers and mixed live-vs-commented routes create false affordances for clients, complicate maintenance, and make tests lie about actual shipped behavior.
design:
Design intent:
- Start with a single route matrix so implementation/removal decisions are made deliberately instead of piecemeal.
- For any endpoint that remains public, wire it through the real router and back it with real service code plus route-level tests and live-server e2e scenarios.
- For any endpoint that is not worth implementing, remove the handler skeleton and the tests that assert branch behavior on a dead surface, then add negative e2e coverage proving the route is absent or intentionally aliased.
- Resolve the /ws vs /api/v1/ws split so there is one truthful legacy story.
- Add strong diagnostics around server behavior in tests: request method/path, auth state, response code/body, and route registration context should be easy to inspect when something fails.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance criteria:
- No empty HTTP handlers remain for public REST surfaces.
- No commented-out route registrations remain as a way of carrying fake API inventory.
- The legacy /ws story is truthful: either a real alias or complete removal.
- Every kept route has package/router tests plus at least one e2e scenario hitting the live server.
- Every retired or hidden route has negative verification proving it is absent or intentionally redirected, and associated help/docs/capabilities are updated.
notes:
Notes:
- Child tasks in this cluster are expected to land with unit tests, router/integration coverage, and live-server e2e or negative-e2e checks.
- Prefer user-facing clarity over silent behavior drift: if a route is retired, surrounding docs/help/capability surfaces must tell the truth immediately.

title: Make exposed CLI flags and hook surfaces truthful
description:
Background:
Several CLI flags and command surfaces are currently user-visible but not real: diff --side-by-side, init --template, init --agents/--auto-spawn, pipeline status --watch, and ensemble --no-questions. The hooks subsystem also declares more hook types than it can generate, so install/status/help imply a broader supported surface than the code actually implements.

Scope:
Make the CLI truthful by either implementing these surfaces fully or removing/hiding them. Every resulting surface must have behavior, tests, and help text aligned.

Why this matters:
CLI truthfulness is central for both humans and agents. A flag that parses but is ignored is effectively a broken API.
design:
Design intent:
- Treat every visible flag and subcommand as a contract.
- Prefer reusing existing session/spawn/diff infrastructure over adding special-case implementations.
- For hooks, align the declared support set with actual script generation instead of keeping unsupported enum values exposed by default.
- For every user-visible CLI behavior in this cluster, add command-level unit tests plus shell-style e2e scripts that exercise the real binary and capture argv, stdout/stderr, exit codes, and helpful diagnostics.
- When a surface is removed instead of implemented, make the CLI easier on users by cleaning up help/completion/examples and by ensuring any remaining error path is crisp and unambiguous rather than warning-heavy.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance criteria:
- No visible CLI flag or subcommand in this cluster is a warning-only, ignored, or dead parameter.
- Help text, completion, examples, and tests all match the final supported behavior.
- Each remediated CLI surface has package-level test coverage and at least one e2e or negative-e2e script hitting the real binary.
- Test and runtime diagnostics are detailed enough to explain build mode, argv, environment assumptions, and failure causes.
notes:
Notes:
- This cluster should optimize for operator trust: a user should never need to infer whether a flag really works.
- Child tasks should treat docs/help/capabilities and test logging as part of the implementation, not post-hoc polish.

description:

design:

- Prefer testable provider abstractions over direct environment-dependent behavior.
- Pair every platform change with deterministic synthetic tests and, where feasible, platform-targeted smoke or fixture-based verification.
- Add structured diagnostics so platform/build context, capability detection, and failure reasons are visible when tests or operators hit cross-platform issues.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance criteria:

NTM has (or will have) several safety-related controls:

- destructive-command policy (DCG)

title: Task: Implement OutputCollector for ensemble outputs
description:
# Task: Implement OutputCollector for ensemble outputs

Collect and normalize outputs from all ensemble agents into a structured SynthesisInput.

## Component Overview
The OutputCollector aggregates per-pane captures, validates them against OutputSchema, and produces a normalized SynthesisInput for downstream synthesis and auditing.

## Implementation Details

### Core Interface
```go
// internal/ensemble/collector.go
type OutputCollector struct {
    SessionName string
    Outputs     map[string]*ModeOutput
    Raw         map[string]string
    Errors      map[string][]error
}

func (c *OutputCollector) Collect(session *EnsembleSession) error
func (c *OutputCollector) CollectWindow(idx int) (*ModeOutput, error)
func (c *OutputCollector) ToSynthesisInput() *SynthesisInput
```

### Collection Strategy
1. Use OutputCapture to fetch raw pane text + parsed YAML
2. Validate ModeOutput via SchemaValidator
3. Attach ModeID/ModeName/ModeCode from assignment metadata
4. **Normalize** with SchemaValidator.Normalize(output, modeID):
   - inject `mode_id` if missing
   - map likelihood/confidence strings (high|medium|low) to floats
5. Normalize into SynthesisInput (deterministic ordering)

### Error Handling
- Partial collection allowed (flagged in SynthesisInput)
- Validation errors recorded per-pane
- Capture errors do not abort entire run

## Logging Requirements
- Log per-pane capture + validation outcomes
- Log injected mode_id occurrences
- Log string-to-float normalization events

## File Location
internal/ensemble/collector.go

## Dependencies
- Requires output capture (bd-1dmet)
- Requires schema validation (bd-1wnxl)
- Feeds synthesis system (bd-2qwm8)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Collects outputs from all panes
- [ ] Handles partial/invalid outputs gracefully
- [ ] Injects `mode_id` when missing
- [ ] Maps string likelihood/confidence values to floats
- [ ] Produces deterministic SynthesisInput
- [ ] Logs per-pane capture + validation outcomes

title: Unit Tests: Round-robin distribution algorithm
description:
## Test Coverage
Unit tests for the round-robin distribution algorithm.

## Test Cases

### Basic Distribution
```go
func TestRoundRobinDistribution(t *testing.T) {
    agents := []string{"cc_1", "cc_2", "cod_1"}
    beads := []string{"b1", "b2", "b3", "b4", "b5", "b6"}

    result := RoundRobin(agents, beads)

    // Expected: cc_1=[b1,b4], cc_2=[b2,b5], cod_1=[b3,b6]
    assert.Equal(t, []string{"b1", "b4"}, result["cc_1"])
    assert.Equal(t, []string{"b2", "b5"}, result["cc_2"])
    assert.Equal(t, []string{"b3", "b6"}, result["cod_1"])
}
```

### Edge Cases
- Empty agents list -> error
- Empty beads list -> empty result
- Single agent -> all beads to one agent
- More agents than beads -> some agents get nothing
- Uneven distribution -> remainder spread

### Logging Requirements
```go
func TestWithLogging(t *testing.T) {
    t.Logf("[TEST-UNIT-RR] test=%s input_agents=%d input_beads=%d",
        t.Name(), len(agents), len(beads))

    result := RoundRobin(agents, beads)

    for agent, assigned := range result {
        t.Logf("[TEST-UNIT-RR] agent=%s assigned_count=%d beads=%v",
            agent, len(assigned), assigned)
    }

    t.Logf("[TEST-UNIT-RR] test=%s status=complete total_assigned=%d",
        t.Name(), totalAssigned(result))
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Basic distribution works correctly
- [ ] All edge cases handled
- [ ] Deterministic ordering
- [ ] Verbose logging for debugging
- [ ] Tests run in < 1s

title: EPIC: Usage Limit Detection & Intelligent Agent Recovery with caut Integration
description:
## EPIC: Usage Limit Detection & Intelligent Agent Recovery with caut Integration

### Executive Summary

This EPIC addresses a CRITICAL operational requirement for NTM multi-agent orchestration: **NEVER interrupt agents that are actively doing useful work**. The system must intelligently distinguish between agents that are productively working versus those that are stuck, rate-limited, or have exhausted their context window.

### Problem Statement

When orchestrating multiple AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI) via NTM, controllers need to make decisions about when to restart agents. Currently, there is no automated way to determine agent state, leading to two failure modes:

1. **Premature Interruption**: Killing an agent mid-task destroys work in progress, wastes tokens/context, and frustrates users
2. **Zombie Agents**: Leaving rate-limited or stuck agents running wastes session slots and blocks progress

### User Incident That Triggered This EPIC

> "omg you need to be WAY more careful about EVER interrupting and stopping and quitting/exiting/terminating any instance of cc, cod, or gmi that is currently usefully doing work!!! WTF dude."

This feedback crystallized the need for intelligent agent state detection before ANY restart action.

### Solution Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    NTM Controller Agent                          │
│                                                                  │
│  1. Before ANY restart decision:                                 │
│     └─> ntm --robot-is-working=session --panes=N                │
│                                                                  │
│  2. For full health picture:                                     │
│     └─> ntm --robot-agent-health=session --panes=N              │
│         ├─> Captures pane output (--robot-tail)                 │
│         ├─> Parses agent-specific patterns (Parser module)      │
│         ├─> Queries provider usage (caut integration)           │
│         └─> Returns structured recommendation                    │
│                                                                  │
│  3. Safe restart (respects working agents):                      │
│     └─> ntm --robot-smart-restart=session --panes=N             │
│         └─> REFUSES to restart if agent is working              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Agent-Specific Behaviors (Critical Context)

Each agent type expresses state differently. This knowledge is ESSENTIAL for parsing:

#### Claude Code (cc)
- **Context indicator**: No explicit percentage. Shows "Tip: This conversation is getting long..." when approaching limit
- **Rate limit**: "You have hit your limit", "Rate limit exceeded", "Please wait..."
- **Working indicators**: Active code block output, file operation messages, "Thinking..." states
- **Header format**: "Opus 4.5 · Claude Max · <Organization>"
- **Exit sequence**: Double Ctrl+C with 0.1s between (CRITICAL timing)

#### Codex CLI (cod)
- **Context indicator**: EXPLICIT percentage! "47% context left · ? for shortcuts"
- **Token usage**: "Token usage: total=219,582 input=206,150 (+ 9,074,560 cached) output=13,432 (reasoning 7,744)"
- **Rate limit**: "You have reached your usage limit", "Rate limit exceeded"
- **Working indicators**: Code output streaming, file modifications
- **Exit sequence**: `/exit` command

#### Gemini CLI (gmi)
- **Context indicator**: Less explicit, shows memory usage "396.8 MB"
- **Rate limit**: Error messages, long pauses (heuristic detection needed)
- **YOLO mode**: "YOLO mode: ON/OFF" - affects execution behavior
- **CRITICAL GOTCHA**: Exclamation marks trigger shell mode! Avoid "!" in prompts
- **Exit sequence**: Escape key exits shell mode, then standard exit

### Integration with caut (coding_agent_usage_tracker)

caut is a Rust CLI that already knows how to query 16+ LLM providers for usage data. Rather than reinvent this wheel, we integrate with caut to get provider-level usage information:

```bash
$ caut usage --provider claude --format json
{
  "schema_version": "caut.v1",
  "data": {
    "payloads": [{
      "provider": "claude",
      "usage": {
        "primary_rate_window": {
          "used_percent": 67.5,
          "window_minutes": 480,
          "resets_at": "2026-01-20T23:00:00Z"
        }
      }
    }]
  }
}
```

This gives us account-level rate limit status that complements per-pane state detection.

### Success Criteria for This EPIC

1. Controller agents can query agent state before ANY restart
2. Working agents are NEVER interrupted (unless --force with confirmation)
3. Rate-limited agents are identified with reset time
4. Low-context agents are flagged for proactive restart
5. All state detection works across cc, cod, gmi agent types
6. Integration with caut provides provider-level usage context
7. E2E tests verify all detection scenarios

### Child Tasks (Dependency Order)

1. **bd-2iw6e**: Parser (Foundation) - MUST be completed first
2. **bd-3uctb**: caut Integration Module - Can parallel with parser
3. **bd-16ptx**: --robot-is-working Command - Depends on parser
4. **bd-2pwzf**: --robot-agent-health Command - Depends on parser + caut + is-working
