title: PromptInjector: Support review-mode prompts for gmi agents
description:
## Purpose
Generate review-mode prompts that instruct agents to analyze and provide feedback on existing code rather than making changes, supporting quality review workflows.

## Implementation Details

```go
// ReviewPromptGenerator creates review-mode prompts for agents
type ReviewPromptGenerator struct {
    templates map[string]string // agent_type -> template
    logger    *slog.Logger
}

// Default review templates per agent type
var defaultReviewTemplates = map[string]string{
    "cc": `Review the code in this project. Focus on:
1. Potential bugs or edge cases
2. Security vulnerabilities
3. Performance concerns
4. Code clarity and maintainability

Do NOT make any changes. Only provide analysis and recommendations.`,
    
    "cod": `Analyze the codebase and identify:
- Code quality issues
- Missing error handling
- Test coverage gaps
- Documentation needs

Output findings only, no modifications.`,
    
    "gmi": `Perform a code review focusing on:
- Architecture patterns
- API design
- Dependency concerns
- Scalability considerations

Analysis mode only - no code changes.`,
}

// GenerateReviewPrompt creates a review prompt for the given context
func (g *ReviewPromptGenerator) GenerateReviewPrompt(agentType, projectPath string, opts ReviewOptions) string {
    template := g.templates[agentType]
    if template == "" {
        template = defaultReviewTemplates[agentType]
    }
    
    prompt := template
    if opts.FocusArea != "" {
        prompt = fmt.Sprintf("Focus specifically on: %s\n\n%s", opts.FocusArea, prompt)
    }
    if opts.FilePattern != "" {
        prompt = fmt.Sprintf("Review files matching: %s\n\n%s", opts.FilePattern, prompt)
    }
    
    g.logger.Info("generated review prompt",
        "agent_type", agentType,
        "project", filepath.Base(projectPath),
        "focus_area", opts.FocusArea,
        "file_pattern", opts.FilePattern,
        "prompt_len", len(prompt))
    
    return prompt
}

type ReviewOptions struct {
    FocusArea   string // e.g., "security", "performance"
    FilePattern string // e.g., "*.go", "internal/**"
}
```

## Logging Requirements
- Log prompt generation with agent type and project
- Log any customization options applied
- Log final prompt length (not content)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Distinct review templates per agent type
- [ ] Templates explicitly forbid code changes
- [ ] Support for focus area customization
- [ ] Support for file pattern scoping
- [ ] Custom template override capability
- [ ] Unit tests for each agent type template
close_reason: Complete: ReviewPromptGenerator implemented with all acceptance criteria met - distinct templates per agent type, no-changes enforcement, focus area/file pattern options, custom override capability, and comprehensive unit tests for all agent types.

title: DCG: Implement send command interception for non-Claude agents
description:
Intercept 'ntm send' commands and run through DCG before forwarding to pane.

## Why Needed

Codex and Gemini agents don't have PreToolUse hooks like Claude Code.
We need to intercept at the NTM level when sending commands to their panes.

## Implementation

### In ntm send command:
1. Before sending to pane, check if target is non-Claude agent
2. If DCG enabled, extract command portion from send payload
3. Run: dcg check --command "<extracted_command>"
4. If dcg returns non-zero, block send and return error
5. If dcg returns zero, proceed with normal send

### Challenges
- Identifying "command" content in arbitrary send payloads
- Some sends are just text, not commands
- Need heuristic: if starts with common command patterns, check DCG

### Heuristics for command detection
- Starts with: git, rm, mv, cp, chmod, chown, kubectl, terraform
- Contains: sudo, -rf, --force, --hard
- Looks like shell: contains |, &&, ||, ;

### Code Location
- internal/commands/send.go (add DCG check)
- internal/integrations/dcg/check.go (dcg invocation wrapper)

## Testing
- Send safe command to Codex pane, verify passes
- Send dangerous command to Codex pane, verify blocked
- Send arbitrary text (not command), verify passes

title: RCH Integration: Remote Compilation Helper for Build Offloading
description:
Integrate RCH (remote_compilation_helper) to offload compilation to remote workers.

## Project Location
/dp/remote_compilation_helper (Rust CLI)

## Problem Being Solved

Multi-agent workflows often trigger parallel builds:
- Agent 1: cargo build on project A
- Agent 2: go build on project B
- Agent 3: cargo test on project A

This causes:
- CPU saturation (all cores maxed)
- Thermal throttling
- Slow agent response times
- Failed builds due to resource contention

## What RCH Does

RCH transparently offloads compilation to remote workers:

### Architecture
1. PreToolUse hook intercepts cargo/go build commands
2. RCH client checks for available workers
3. If worker available, rsync project and run remotely
4. Stream output back to local terminal
5. Rsync artifacts back when done

### Key Features
- Transparent: no agent changes needed
- Deduplication: same build on same worker reuses cache
- Fallback: if no workers, run locally
- Worker fleet: multiple machines can serve as workers

### Key RCH Commands
```bash
rch status            # Show worker status
rch workers list      # List available workers
rch build cargo       # Explicit remote build
rch config            # Configure workers
```

## Integration Strategy for NTM

### 1. PreToolUse Hook (Primary)
Configure hook for all agents to route builds through RCH.

### 2. Dashboard Widget
Show compilation status: local vs remote builds, worker utilization, time saved.

### 3. Robot Mode Commands
- --robot-rch-status: Get RCH and worker status
- --robot-rch-workers: List workers

## Considerations
- Network latency: remote only wins for long builds (>10s)
- Security: workers must be trusted (code execution)
- Artifacts: some builds produce local-only files
- DCG: RCH commands should be whitelisted

## Acceptance Criteria

1. RCH integration module exists at internal/integrations/rch/
2. PreToolUse hook configuration for cargo/go build interception works
3. Dashboard widget shows local vs remote build stats
4. Robot mode commands return valid JSON with worker status
5. Fallback to local build works when no workers available
6. All child beads (bd-1j956, bd-64v8u, bd-1o1q1, bd-398bh, bd-3u84u, bd-1ghcp) completed

## Unit Tests (80% coverage target)
- internal/integrations/rch/rch_test.go
- Test worker detection, build routing, fallback logic

## E2E Test Script
```bash
#\!/bin/bash
# [E2E-RCH] RCH Integration Tests
LOG_PREFIX="[E2E-RCH]"
echo "$LOG_PREFIX Testing RCH integration"
# Test robot-rch-status command
ntm --robot-rch-status | jq -e '.rch_installed \!= null' || exit 1
echo "$LOG_PREFIX RCH status check passed"
```

title: [LOW] loadRecoveryCheckpoint silently rejects working_dir mismatches; no diagnostic log
description:
## Severity: [LOW]

Commit 4d1b14bc (#131) added working-directory gating to `loadRecoveryCheckpoint` (internal/cli/spawn.go:3548). When a checkpoint exists but its recorded `WorkingDir` does not match the spawn directory, the function returns `(nil, nil)` — indistinguishable from "no checkpoint exists":

```go
if !checkpointWorkingDirMatches(cp.WorkingDir, workingDir) {
    // Recorded working dir disagrees with the spawn directory — refuse to
    // surface the checkpoint as recovery context for a different repo.
    return nil, nil
}
```

## Why it matters

A user who shares the tmux session name across two repos and notices their recovery context is empty has no way to figure out *why* without inspecting checkpoint storage manually. The fix is correct (don't cross-contaminate), but the diagnostic surface is invisible.

Compare to other recovery-skip paths in spawn.go that log a slog.Warn on degraded behavior. The cm-context retrieval failure logs `output.PrintWarningf("CM context retrieval failed: %v", err)`; the checkpoint rejection should be similarly observable.

## Fix sketch

```go
if !checkpointWorkingDirMatches(cp.WorkingDir, workingDir) {
    slog.Warn("recovery checkpoint rejected: working dir mismatch",
        "session_name", sessionName,
        "checkpoint_working_dir", cp.WorkingDir,
        "spawn_working_dir", workingDir,
        "checkpoint_id", cp.ID,
    )
    return nil, nil
}
```

Optionally also surface the rejection in the recovery JSON (e.g., a `checkpoint_skipped: { reason: "working_dir_mismatch", checkpoint_id: ... }` field) so downstream tooling can audit gating decisions without parsing logs.

## Acceptance

- A unit test asserts the slog.Warn line is emitted when `loadRecoveryCheckpoint` rejects on working-dir mismatch.
- Existing `TestLoadRecoveryCheckpoint_RejectsCheckpointFromDifferentWorkingDir` still passes.

## Files
- internal/cli/spawn.go:3561-3565
- internal/cli/spawn_recovery_test.go (new assertion)
close_reason: Added slog.Warn to loadRecoveryCheckpoint when working_dir mismatch rejects a checkpoint (internal/cli/spawn.go:3561-3574). Operators can now correlate silent recovery-context drops with the gating decision via logs. Commit 96571455.

title: Feature: Robot Probe Command (--robot-probe)
description:
## Overview

Add `ntm --robot-probe=SESSION` command that actively tests whether panes are responsive.

## IMPORTANT: API Design Consistency

This command follows the established robot mode patterns:
- **Primary flag**: `--robot-probe=SESSION` (not positional args)
- **Pane filter**: `--panes=N` or `--panes=1,2,3` (shared global flag)
- **All outputs**: JSON format

## Command Interface

```bash
# Check all agent panes in session
ntm --robot-probe=myproject

# Check specific panes
ntm --robot-probe=myproject --panes=4

# Use aggressive probing
ntm --robot-probe=myproject --panes=2,3 --probe-method=interrupt_test
```

## Output Schema

```json
{
  "session": "myproject",
  "timestamp": "2026-01-19T23:17:00Z",
  "probes": [
    {
      "pane": 4,
      "responsive": true,
      "method": "keystroke_echo",
      "latency_ms": 45,
      "output_delta_lines": 0,
      "confidence": "high",
      "recommendation": "healthy",
      "reasoning": "Pane responded to probe within 45ms"
    }
  ],
  "summary": {
    "total_probed": 1,
    "responsive": 1,
    "unresponsive": 0
  }
}
```

## Modifier Flags

| Flag | Description | Default |
|------|-------------|---------|
| `--panes=N` | Filter to specific pane(s) | All agent panes |
| `--probe-method=M` | keystroke_echo, status_request, interrupt_test | keystroke_echo |
| `--probe-timeout=MS` | Wait time for response | 5000 |
| `--probe-aggressive` | Fall back to interrupt_test if echo fails | false |

## Probe Methods

1. **keystroke_echo** (default, safest): Send null byte, check cursor movement
2. **status_request**: Send agent-specific status query
3. **interrupt_test**: Send Ctrl-C, check response (may interrupt work)

## Algorithm

```
1. Capture current pane content (baseline)
2. Send probe input based on method
3. Wait probe-timeout milliseconds
4. Capture new pane content
5. Compare and score confidence
6. Return structured result
```

## Confidence Levels

- **high**: Clear response measured
- **medium**: Ambiguous response (minor change)
- **low**: No response but process active

## When to Use

- Before killing a "stuck" agent
- As part of --robot-diagnose workflow
- When timeout-based detection is ambiguous

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `--robot-probe=SESSION` flag registered in root.go
- [ ] `--panes=N` filter works with comma-separated pane IDs
- [ ] `--probe-method` accepts: keystroke_echo, status_request, interrupt_test
- [ ] `--probe-timeout` configurable (default 5000ms)
- [ ] `--probe-aggressive` falls back to interrupt_test on echo failure
- [ ] JSON output matches schema exactly (no extra fields)
- [ ] Confidence levels computed correctly (high/medium/low)
- [ ] Exit code 0 on success, 1 on partial failure, 2 on complete failure
- [ ] Non-existent session returns error JSON (not crash)
- [ ] Non-existent pane returns error in probes array

## Testing Requirements

### Unit Tests (internal/cli/robot_probe_test.go)
- [ ] Flag parsing for all probe options
- [ ] Baseline capture logic (mock tmux)
- [ ] Confidence scoring algorithm
- [ ] JSON output serialization
- [ ] Error handling for missing sessions/panes
- [ ] Timeout handling

### E2E Tests (scripts/e2e_robot_probe.sh)
```bash
#\!/bin/bash
# [E2E-PROBE] Robot Probe Command Tests
set -euo pipefail
LOG_PREFIX="[E2E-PROBE]"

echo "$LOG_PREFIX Starting robot probe E2E tests"

# Setup: Create test session with agent
TEST_SESSION="e2e_probe_$$"
echo "$LOG_PREFIX Creating test session: $TEST_SESSION"
ntm spawn "$TEST_SESSION" --cc=1 --no-prompt

# Wait for agent initialization
sleep 5

# Test 1: Basic probe
echo "$LOG_PREFIX Test 1: Basic probe all panes"
RESULT=$(ntm --robot-probe="$TEST_SESSION")
echo "$LOG_PREFIX Result: $RESULT"
[[ $(echo "$RESULT" | jq -r ".session") == "$TEST_SESSION" ]] || exit 1
[[ $(echo "$RESULT" | jq ".summary.total_probed") -ge 1 ]] || exit 1

# Test 2: Specific pane probe
echo "$LOG_PREFIX Test 2: Probe specific pane"
RESULT=$(ntm --robot-probe="$TEST_SESSION" --panes=1)
echo "$LOG_PREFIX Result: $RESULT"
[[ $(echo "$RESULT" | jq ".probes | length") -eq 1 ]] || exit 1

# Test 3: Non-existent session
echo "$LOG_PREFIX Test 3: Non-existent session error"
RESULT=$(ntm --robot-probe="nonexistent_session_xyz" 2>&1) || true
echo "$LOG_PREFIX Result: $RESULT"
[[ $(echo "$RESULT" | jq -r ".error" 2>/dev/null) \!= "" ]] || exit 1

# Cleanup
echo "$LOG_PREFIX Cleanup: Destroying test session"
tmux kill-session -t "$TEST_SESSION" 2>/dev/null || true

echo "$LOG_PREFIX All robot probe E2E tests passed"
```

title: Fix color bleeding and theme application issues
description:
## Problem
Colors appearing in wrong areas, background colors bleeding, inconsistent theme application.

## Code Review Findings (2026-01-19)

### lipgloss Handles ANSI Resets Correctly

Lipgloss automatically adds ANSI reset codes after styled text. Looking at the codebase:
- All styling goes through lipgloss.Style.Render()
- No manual ANSI code emission found
- Theme colors are applied via semantic styles

### Potential Issues to Verify
1. **Background extending past text** - May be lipgloss Width() setting width wider than content
2. **Plain theme** - Need to verify NO_COLOR and plain theme are truly colorless
3. **Style inheritance** - Check for nested styles that might compound

## Fix Approach

### 1. Audit Background Width Usage
```go
// Potentially problematic - background extends to full width
style := lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(color).Width(w).Render(text)
```

### 2. Verify Plain Theme
```go
func TestPlainThemeNoColors(t *testing.T) {
    old := theme.Current()
    defer theme.SetCurrent(old)

    theme.SetCurrent(theme.Plain)

    styles := NewSemanticStyles(theme.Current())
    rendered := styles.TextSuccess.Render("test")

    // Should contain no ANSI escape codes
    if strings.Contains(rendered, "\x1b[") {

    }
}
```

### 3. Check NO_COLOR Environment
```go
func TestNoColorEnv(t *testing.T) {
    os.Setenv("NO_COLOR", "1")
    defer os.Unsetenv("NO_COLOR")

    // Force lipgloss to check env
    lipgloss.SetColorProfile(lipgloss.Ascii)

    style := lipgloss.NewStyle().Foreground(lipgloss.Color("212"))
    rendered := style.Render("test")

    if strings.Contains(rendered, "\x1b[") {
        t.Error("NO_COLOR should disable all colors")
    }
}
```

```tape
Sleep 2s
```

# Feature: Budget & Resource Control

**Critical for preventing token black holes.** Ensemble runs can be expensive - this feature provides predictability and control.

```yaml
budget:
  per_agent: 4000      # Max tokens per mode agent
  total: 50000         # Max for entire ensemble run
  synthesis: 8000      # Reserved for synthesis phase
  context_pack: 2000   # Reserved for context injection
```

Stop when new findings rate drops below threshold:
```go
type EarlyStopConfig struct {

    SimilarityThreshold float64 // Stop if output similarity > threshold
    WindowSize          int     // Evaluate over last N agents
}
```

title: Feature: Robot Status Enrichments
description:
## Overview

Enrich the existing `ntm --robot-status` output with critical operational data that
is currently missing but essential for automated swarm management.

## Background

The current --robot-status returns basic pane information (index, agent_type, is_active)
but lacks the data needed to:
- Detect rate-limited panes
- Identify hung processes
- Know which PID to kill for restart
- Track output freshness for stuck detection

## Proposed Schema Addition

Each pane object in the status output should include:

```json
{
  "index": 2,
  "agent_type": "claude",
  "pid": 12345,                    // Shell PID (already available)
  "child_pid": 12346,              // NEW: The actual agent process PID
  "last_output_ts": "2026-01-19T...", // NEW: Last output timestamp
  "rate_limit_detected": false,    // NEW: Pattern match on recent output
  "process_state": "running",      // NEW: running|sleeping|zombie|dead
  "memory_mb": 450,                // NEW: Process memory usage
  "output_lines_since_last": 42    // NEW: Activity indicator
}
```

## Justification for Each Field

1. **child_pid**: Required for kill -9 when soft restart fails. Currently operators
   must run `pgrep -P <shell_pid>` manually.

2. **last_output_ts**: Enables timeout-based stuck detection without external state.
   "No output for 5 minutes" = likely stuck.

3. **rate_limit_detected**: Pattern match for "You've hit your limit" or similar.
   This is the #1 failure mode in practice. Must be detected programmatically.

4. **process_state**: From /proc/<pid>/status. Zombie processes need different handling
   than running ones.

5. **memory_mb**: Detect runaway processes consuming excessive memory.

6. **output_lines_since_last**: Quick activity indicator without timestamp parsing.

## Implementation Notes

- child_pid: Use pgrep -P or parse /proc/<pid>/task
- last_output_ts: Track during capture-pane operations
- rate_limit_detected: Grep last N lines of pane output
- process_state: Read /proc/<pid>/status State field
- memory_mb: Read /proc/<pid>/status VmRSS field
- These should be gathered efficiently (single pass where possible)

## Performance Considerations

- Status is called frequently; keep it fast
- Pattern matching for rate limits should be bounded (last 50 lines)
- Process state reads are cheap (procfs)
- Consider caching with short TTL if needed

## Testing Requirements

- Unit tests for each field extraction
- E2E tests with actual stuck/rate-limited agents
- Performance benchmarks for large swarms (20+ panes)

title: Add ntm assign --reassign for moving bead between agents
description:
## Overview
Allow users to move an assignment from one agent to another without losing tracking state.

## Use Cases
1. Agent is stuck and user wants to give bead to a faster agent
2. User realizes a bead is better suited for a different agent type
3. Load balancing - redistribute work mid-session

## Usage
```bash
# Reassign bead to a different pane
ntm assign myproject --reassign bd-xyz --to-pane=4

# Reassign to specific agent type (picks idle agent of that type)
ntm assign myproject --reassign bd-xyz --to-type=codex

# Reassign with new prompt
ntm assign myproject --reassign bd-xyz --to-pane=4 --prompt="Continue from where the previous agent left off"
```

## Workflow
1. Validate bead is currently assigned
2. Get current assignment info
3. Update assignment status to "reassigned"
4. Create new assignment for target agent
5. Release file reservations from old agent (if any)
6. Create file reservations for new agent (if any)
7. Send prompt to new agent
8. Return reassignment result

## Output (Standard Envelope)
```json
{
  "command": "assign",
  "subcommand": "reassign",
  "session": "myproject",
  "timestamp": "2026-01-19T12:00:00Z",
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "reassigned": {
      "bead_id": "bd-xyz",
      "bead_title": "Implement feature X",
      "pane": 4,
      "agent_type": "codex",
      "agent_name": "BlueLake",
      "status": "assigned",
      "prompt_sent": true,
      "assigned_at": "2026-01-19T12:00:00Z",
      "previous_pane": 2,
      "previous_agent": "GreenCastle",
      "previous_agent_type": "claude",
      "previous_status": "working",
      "file_reservations_transferred": true
    }
  },
  "warnings": [],
  "error": null
}
```

## Error Output
```json
{
  "command": "assign",
  "subcommand": "reassign",
  "session": "myproject",
  "timestamp": "2026-01-19T12:00:00Z",
  "success": false,
  "data": null,
  "warnings": [],
  "error": {
    "code": "TARGET_BUSY",
    "message": "pane 4 already has assignment bd-abc",
    "details": {
      "current_bead": "bd-abc",
      "current_status": "working"
    }
  }
}
```

## Error Codes
- NOT_ASSIGNED: Bead doesn't have an active assignment
- TARGET_BUSY: Target pane already has an assignment
- PANE_NOT_FOUND: Target pane doesn't exist
- NO_IDLE_AGENT: No idle agent of specified type

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Reassign bead to specific pane
- [ ] Reassign by agent type (auto-select idle)
- [ ] Transfer file reservations via Agent Mail
- [ ] Update assignment store correctly
- [ ] Optional custom prompt
- [ ] Standard JSON envelope output
- [ ] Clear error codes

## Tests Required
- Unit test: Assignment state update logic
- Unit test: File reservation transfer
- Unit test: Output format validation
- E2E test: Full reassignment workflow

title: Add --stagger flag for delayed agent launches
description:
Add --stagger SECONDS flag to control delay between agent launches.

## Purpose
Prevent overwhelming MCP Agent Mail when launching many agents at once.

## Syntax
```bash
ntm spawn myproject --cc=10 --cod=10 --stagger=30
```

## CRITICAL LESSONS LEARNED
1. Default stagger should be 30 seconds (not 20) - MCP Agent Mail gets overwhelmed
2. Wait 4 seconds after launching agent before sending marching orders
3. Send Enter TWICE after marching orders to ensure submission
4. Log confirmation that Enter was sent for debugging

## Behavior
- Default: 30 seconds (changed from 0 to protect MCP Agent Mail)
- When set: wait N seconds between each agent launch
- Progress indicator showing launch status with confirmation

## Implementation
- Add --stagger flag to spawn command (default: 30)
- Modify agent launch loop to include delay
- Show progress: [5/20] Launching agent... -> Sent message + Enter (x2)

## Code Pattern
```go
// After launching agent
time.Sleep(4 * time.Second)  // Wait for agent to initialize
sendKeys(pane, marchingOrders)
time.Sleep(1 * time.Second)
sendKeys(pane, "Enter")  // First Enter
time.Sleep(500 * time.Millisecond)
sendKeys(pane, "Enter")  // Second Enter - CRITICAL
log.Printf("  -> Sent message + Enter (x2)")
time.Sleep(staggerSeconds)
```
close_reason: Completed: Changed default stagger to 30s, added logging confirmation for Enter key delivery

title: Fix Agent Mail showing 'offline' when connected
description:
## Problem
The Agent Mail status always shows "offline" in the status bar even when the Agent Mail MCP server is available and connected.

## Screenshot Evidence
Status bar shows: "Mail: offline"

## Code Locations
- internal/tui/dashboard/dashboard.go - AgentMailUpdateMsg handling
- internal/agentmail/client.go - Agent Mail client connection
- internal/tui/dashboard/panels/ticker.go - Ticker panel rendering mail status

## Possible Causes
1. **Connection check failing** - Health check returns false even when server is up
2. **MCP server not detected** - Agent Mail MCP tools not being discovered
3. **Async timing** - Mail status check completing before dashboard ready
4. **Configuration issue** - Agent Mail URL/path not configured correctly
5. **Error swallowed** - Connection error not surfaced to UI

## Investigation Steps
1. Check Agent Mail MCP server status directly: \`curl localhost:PORT/health\`
2. Verify MCP tool discovery in Claude Code config
3. Add logging to agentmail.IsAvailable() and agentmail.IsConnected()
4. Check for errors in AgentMailUpdateMsg handling

## Diagnostic Code
\`\`\`go
func (c *Client) CheckStatus() AgentMailStatus {
    log.Debug("checking agent mail status",
        "endpoint", c.endpoint,
        "timeout", c.timeout)
    
    available := c.ping()
    log.Debug("agent mail ping result", "available", available)
    
    if !available {
        return AgentMailStatus{
            Available: false,
            Connected: false,
            Reason: "server not responding",
        }
    }
    
    connected := c.authenticate()
    log.Debug("agent mail auth result", "connected", connected)
    
    return AgentMailStatus{
        Available: available,
        Connected: connected,
    }
}
\`\`\`

## Fix Pattern
\`\`\`go
// Render mail status with more detail
func (t *TickerPanel) renderMailStatus() string {
    if !t.mailAvailable {
        return "Mail: unavailable"
    }
    if !t.mailConnected {
        return "Mail: disconnected"
    }
    if t.mailLocks > 0 {
        return fmt.Sprintf("Mail: %d locks", t.mailLocks)
    }
    return "Mail: ready"
}
\`\`\`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Shows "ready" when Agent Mail is available and connected
- [ ] Shows "disconnected" when server is up but auth fails
- [ ] Shows "unavailable" when server is down
- [ ] Shows lock count when file reservations exist
- [ ] Status updates on Agent Mail state changes

## Unit Tests
1. TestMailStatus_Available - server up shows "ready"
2. TestMailStatus_Unavailable - server down shows "unavailable"
3. TestMailStatus_Disconnected - auth failure shows "disconnected"
4. TestMailStatus_WithLocks - active locks shows count
5. TestMailStatus_Refresh - status updates on AgentMailUpdateMsg

## E2E Tests
1. Start dashboard with Agent Mail running - verify "ready"
2. Stop Agent Mail server - verify status changes to "unavailable"
3. Create file reservation - verify lock count appears
4. Invalid auth - verify "disconnected"

## Logging
- INFO: Log mail status changes
- DEBUG: Log connection check results
- DEBUG: Log lock count updates
- ERROR: Log connection failures with reason

title: Task: Design preamble template structure and base template in internal/ensemble/preamble.go
description:
# Task: Design preamble template structure with schema contract

Each mode prompt has three mandatory sections:
1. Base instructions (tone, constraints)
2. Mode preamble (the reasoning lens)
3. **Output schema contract** (MANDATORY)

## Template Structure
```go
// internal/ensemble/preamble.go
type PreambleTemplate struct {
    BaseInstructions string
    ModeSection      string
    SchemaContract   string  // MANDATORY output format
}

type PreambleData struct {
    Problem         string
    ContextPack     *ContextPack
    Mode            *ReasoningMode
    TokenCap        int
    OutputSchema    string  // YAML schema specification
}

func (t *PreambleTemplate) Render(data *PreambleData) (string, error)
func LoadBaseTemplate() *PreambleTemplate
func GetSchemaContract() string  // Returns mandatory YAML schema
```

## Base Instructions Section
```
You are participating in a reasoning ensemble analyzing: {problem_statement}

Context Pack:
{context_pack}

Your role: Apply your assigned reasoning mode rigorously.

Constraints:
- Stay within your reasoning mode's strengths
- Be explicit about confidence levels (numeric or high|medium|low)
- Reference specific evidence (file:line)
- Flag your mode's known failure modes
- DO NOT exceed {token_cap} tokens
```

## Mode Section (Core + Fallback)
- If a preamble file exists (core tier), render it verbatim.
- Otherwise, **auto-generate** from mode metadata:
  - name + description
  - outputs, best_for, failure_modes
  - differentiator (if present)
  - tier warning for advanced modes

## Schema Contract Section (CRITICAL)
```
## REQUIRED OUTPUT FORMAT

You MUST structure your response as valid YAML with these exact fields:

mode_id: {mode_id}           # optional; system will inject if missing
thesis: |
  Your one-sentence main insight
confidence: 0.0-1.0           # numeric or high|medium|low

top_findings:
  - finding: Description
    impact: critical|high|medium|low
    confidence: 0.0-1.0        # numeric or high|medium|low
    evidence_pointer: path/to/file.go:142
    reasoning: How you reached this

risks:
  - risk: Description
    impact: critical|high|medium|low
    likelihood: 0.0-1.0        # numeric or high|medium|low
    mitigation: Suggested mitigation
    affected_areas: [string]

recommendations:
  - recommendation: What to do
    priority: critical|high|medium|low
    effort: low|medium|high
    rationale: Why this helps
    related_findings: [int]    # indices into top_findings (0-based)

questions_for_user:
  - question: What needs clarification?
    context: Why this matters
    blocking: false
    suggested_answers: [string]

failure_modes_to_watch:
  - mode: Potential failure
    description: What could go wrong
    indicators: [string]
    prevention: How to guard against it

NON-COMPLIANT OUTPUTS WILL BE REJECTED.
```

## Logging
- Log rendered preamble length, mode_id, and schema contract version

## Tests
- Unit: template render with full data
- Unit: fallback auto-generation from mode metadata
- Unit: schema contract inclusion

title: [HIGH] loop steps with loop_control still skip their command body
description:
Review of 3818740f (bug-fix: pipeline: run foreach loop-control body) found that the fix is limited to internal/pipeline/foreach.go. The older but still-supported Step.Loop path remains in LoopExecutor.executeIteration in internal/pipeline/loops.go. That code checks nestedStep.LoopControl before executing the nested step, and returns break or continue immediately when the condition applies.

Impact: a user-facing loop body step such as loop: {items: ..., steps: [{id: stop_on_b, command: "printf stop", when: ..., loop_control: continue}]} still skips the command/template body and applies continue/break first. This is the same functional contract that bd-9yuk0 fixed for foreach:, but workflows using loop: retain the broken behavior. It can drop intended side effects or output capture from the controlling step.

Expected: LoopExecutor should match foreach semantics: only pure control-only steps should apply control before dispatch; steps with real work should execute successfully first, then apply loop_control. Add a parsed-YAML regression for loop: items with command plus loop_control.

No code fix was applied in this review pass because the requested CRITICAL/HIGH auto-fix scope is restricted to NEW files only, while the production fix belongs in internal/pipeline/loops.go.
close_reason: LoopExecutor.executeIteration now matches the foreach contract from bd-9yuk0: pure-control-only steps keep the fast path (evaluate when via new loopControlAppliesForStep helper, apply directive without dispatch), but steps with real work (command/template/prompt/etc.) execute the body first via executeStep and only apply break/continue after a StatusCompleted result. Reuses foreachControlOnlyStep and foreachLoopControlValue. Added TestExecuteIterationLoopControlBodyRunsBeforeBreak (body runs then breaks) and TestExecuteIterationControlOnlyStepStillBreaks (control-only fast path).

After safety and reliability (Tier 1), performance becomes the next concern:

title: Step.Stdin has no size cap — large ${steps.X.output} substitution can balloon memory
description:
## Summary

Commit b4e38cec (bd-zfdjd.7) added Step.Stdin piping into command steps. The substituted payload is read via `strings.NewReader(expandedStdin)` and passed as cmd.Stdin. The commit comment says "Keep the byte cap implicit — Step.Stdin is bounded by workflow file size; large payloads should use file paths per the schema doc."

This reasoning breaks when Stdin uses `${steps.X.output}` substitution: the substituted value comes from another step's captured stdout, which can be up to settings.limits.max_command_stdout_bytes (default 50MB). So a workflow like:

```yaml
- id: source
  command: "cat /tmp/large-file"
- id: sink
  command: "./consume"
  stdin: ${steps.source.output}
```

shovels up to 50MB through Go memory (substitution materializes the full string, NewReader holds it, the whole thing stays alive until cmd.Wait returns). Multiple parallel iterations doing this would multiply memory pressure proportionally.

## Severity

P3. The 50MB ceiling is bounded so this isn't an unbounded memory exploit, but a max_concurrent_foreach=10 of stdout-piping iterations could touch 500MB+ of resident set during the run. The comment claim that "file size" bounds Stdin is incorrect once ${steps.X.output} is in play.

## Suggested approach

Either:
1. Add a configurable max_command_stdin_bytes (default e.g. 1MB) and reject substitutions that exceed it with a clear error pointing the author at file-based stdin.
2. Document the ceiling at the schema level so authors know substituting large outputs is supported but bounded.

Option 1 is the safer default. Option 2 is the smaller change.

## Acceptance

- A unit test pipes a >cap stdin payload and asserts the step fails with a clear "stdin exceeds cap" error (or, for option 2, that no implicit cap is enforced and the test documents the runtime ceiling).
- The schema doc updates to match the chosen behavior.

## Files
- internal/pipeline/executor.go (executeCommand stdin piping)
- internal/pipeline/limits.go (new MaxCommandStdinBytes config)
- internal/pipeline/schema.go (doc Stdin's bound)
close_reason: done

title: CAAM: Implement rate limit detection in agent output
description:
Monitor agent pane output for rate limit signals and trigger account switch.

## Rate Limit Patterns to Detect

### Claude
- "rate_limit_error"
- "You've exceeded"
- "Please wait"
- "Too many requests"

### OpenAI
- "Rate limit reached"
- HTTP 429
- "tokens per min"

### Gemini
- "RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED"
- "Quota exceeded"

## Implementation

### 1. Output Monitor
Already exists in NTM for pane output. Extend with pattern matching.

```go
type RateLimitDetector struct {
    patterns map[string][]*regexp.Regexp  // provider -> patterns
    onLimit  func(provider string, pane string)
}

func (d *RateLimitDetector) Check(output string, pane string) {
    for provider, patterns := range d.patterns {
        for _, p := range patterns {
            if p.MatchString(output) {
                d.onLimit(provider, pane)
                return
            }
        }
    }
}
```

### 2. Trigger Flow
1. Pattern matched -> callback invoked
2. Callback pauses agent (send Ctrl+C or wait)
3. Callback triggers CAAM switch
4. Callback resumes agent

## Code Location
- internal/integrations/caam/detector.go
- internal/pane/output.go (add detector hook)

## Testing
- Inject fake rate limit messages, verify detection
- Test each provider's patterns
- Test custom patterns from config

title: [EPIC] Fix resilience monitor false-positive restarts (GH #48)
description:
## Context
GitHub issue #48 — deeply researched bug report. The resilience monitor auto-restart feature falsely detects working agents as crashed and injects the full spawn command as literal keystrokes into the running tmux pane. This is a P0 bug because it actively disrupts working agents.

## Root Cause Analysis (3 independent causes)

### Root Cause 1: False-positive crash detection via text pattern matching
detectProcessStatus() in internal/health/health.go (lines 461-483) scans the last 50 lines of pane output for strings like "exit status", "process exited", "connection closed". AI coding agents routinely output these strings when discussing processes or debugging, triggering ProcessExited while the agent is actively working.

### Root Cause 2: No PID-alive guard before handleCrash()
The resilience monitor in internal/resilience/monitor.go (lines 314-329) calls handleCrash() immediately upon detecting StatusError or ProcessExited without first checking whether the agent process is actually running via PID. By contrast, --robot-smart-restart in internal/robot/smart_restart.go (lines 268-271) already has a guard.

### Root Cause 3: Restart uses send-keys into live pane
restartAgent() (monitor.go line 634) calls sendKeysFn which uses tmux send-keys -l, injecting the full spawn command as literal text into the live pane. For a true crash this is correct (shell is waiting at prompt), but for false positives, keystrokes are received by the running agent, causing chaos.

## Key Insight
NTM already has PID-based liveness checking (internal/robot/status_enrich.go — getChildPID(), getProcessState()) that works correctly, but it is NOT wired into the resilience monitor path. The Pane.PID field is populated from tmux's pane_pid and available in PaneActivity, but checkAgent() at health.go:223 never uses it.

## Current Workaround
Users can set auto_restart = false in ~/.config/ntm/config.toml under [resilience], but false-positive health reporting and crash notifications still fire.

## Affected Files
- internal/health/health.go (lines 223, 461-483)
- internal/resilience/monitor.go (lines 314-329, 596-683)
- internal/robot/health.go (lines 460-530)
- internal/robot/smart_restart.go (lines 268-271, reference for guard)
- internal/robot/status_enrich.go (PID-based checking, to be reused)

## Sub-tasks (see child beads)
1. P0: Extract PID-based liveness checker to shared package (bd-1ks5x.1)
2. P0: Add PID-alive guard before handleCrash() (bd-1ks5x.2)
3. P1: Add consecutive-failures debounce (bd-1ks5x.3)
4. P1: Update checkProcess in robot/health.go (bd-1ks5x.4)
5. P2: Add final PID guard in restartAgent() (bd-1ks5x.5)
6. P1: Comprehensive unit tests (bd-1ks5x.6)
7. P1: E2E test script (bd-1ks5x.7)

False-positive restarts prevented by 3-layer defense: PID guard in monitor loop, debounce for text-based fallback, final PID guard before sendFunc.

title: Add PID-alive guard before handleCrash() in resilience monitor
description:
## What
Add a PID-based liveness guard in internal/resilience/monitor.go before handleCrash() at lines 314-329. If the agent process is alive (PID check), skip crash handling regardless of what text patterns say.

## Why (P0 — defense in depth)
The resilience monitor currently calls handleCrash() immediately upon detecting StatusError or ProcessExited with NO check for whether the agent process is actually running. The robot path (smart_restart.go:268-271) already has an IsWorking guard. The resilience monitor needs the same protection, but using the more authoritative PID-based check.

## Important: This is a PID-alive check, NOT the full IsWorking analysis
The robot path IsWorking field is a composite signal (output analysis, context window, prompt detection). For the resilience monitor, we use a simpler, more authoritative check: process.IsChildAlive(shellPID). If the shell has a child process, the agent is alive and we must NOT restart it. This is a hard gate, not a heuristic.

## Implementation

### Step 1: Add ShellPID to AgentHealth struct
In internal/health/health.go, add to AgentHealth:
```go
ShellPID int json:"shell_pid" // Shell PID from tmux #{pane_pid}
```

### Step 2: Populate ShellPID in checkAgent()
In checkAgent() (health.go:176), add:
```go
agent.ShellPID = pa.Pane.PID
```

### Step 3: Add guard in monitor.go
At lines 314-329, before handleCrash():
```go
// PID-alive guard: if agent process is running, skip crash handling
if agentHealth.ShellPID > 0 && process.IsChildAlive(agentHealth.ShellPID) {
    log.Printf("[resilience] Agent %s: health check says unhealthy but PID %d has children — skipping crash handling (false positive avoided)", agentState.PaneID, agentHealth.ShellPID)
    continue
}
```

### Step 4: Add import
Add `"github.com/Dicklesworthstone/ntm/internal/process"` to monitor.go imports.

- MODIFY: internal/health/health.go (AgentHealth struct + checkAgent())
- MODIFY: internal/resilience/monitor.go (lines 314-329, add guard + import)
- REFERENCE: internal/robot/smart_restart.go:268-271 (analogous guard)
- REFERENCE: internal/process/liveness.go (from bd-1ks5x.1)

## Behavior Matrix
| PID Check | Text Check | Result |
|-----------|-----------|--------|
| alive     | any       | SKIP crash (PID is authoritative) |
| dead      | error     | proceed to handleCrash (after debounce, see bd-1ks5x.3) |
| dead      | ok        | proceed to handleCrash (PID says dead) |
| unknown   | error     | proceed to handleCrash (after debounce) |
| unknown   | ok        | mark healthy |

title: Add consecutive-failures debounce to resilience monitor
description:
## What
Add ConsecutiveFailures counter to AgentState. Only trigger handleCrash() after N consecutive health check failures (default N=3, configurable). Integrate with the PID-alive guard result from bd-1ks5x.2 to avoid redundant IsChildAlive calls.

## Why (P1)
The debounce is specifically for the TEXT-BASED FALLBACK path (when PID checking is unavailable or returns unknown). For PID-authoritative signals, the behavior is:
- PID alive → always skip (handled by guard in bd-1ks5x.2, never reaches debounce)
- PID dead → immediate restart (no debounce, authoritative)
- PID unknown + text patterns say error → DEBOUNCE (unreliable signal needs temporal smoothing)

This ensures fast response to genuine crashes (PID dead = instant) while protecting against text pattern false positives in the rare case where PID checking is unavailable.

## CRITICAL: Single IsChildAlive call, shared result
The PID-alive guard (bd-1ks5x.2) calls process.IsChildAlive() ONCE. The result MUST be stored and passed to the debounce logic. Do NOT call IsChildAlive a second time — this creates a TOCTOU race where the child could die between the two calls, leading to inconsistent decisions.

Pattern:
```go
// In the monitor loop, SINGLE PID check, reuse result
var pidAlive, pidKnown bool
if agentHealth.ShellPID > 0 {
    pidAlive = process.IsChildAlive(agentHealth.ShellPID)
    pidKnown = true
}

// PID-alive guard (bd-1ks5x.2)
if pidKnown && pidAlive {
    continue // agent running, skip crash handling
}

// Debounce (this bead)
if pidKnown && !pidAlive {
    // PID authoritatively dead — skip debounce, restart immediately
    agentState.ConsecutiveFailures = m.cfg.Resilience.CrashThreshold
} else if !pidKnown {
    // PID unavailable, text-based fallback — increment debounce counter
    agentState.ConsecutiveFailures++
}

if agentState.ConsecutiveFailures >= m.cfg.Resilience.CrashThreshold {
    m.handleCrash(ctx, agentState, reason)
    agentState.ConsecutiveFailures = 0
}
```

## Implementation

### Step 1: Add fields to AgentState
```go
ConsecutiveFailures int    // Consecutive health check failures
LastFailureReason   string // For logging
```

### Step 2: Add config field
In config.toml under [resilience]:
```toml
crash_threshold = 3  # Consecutive failures before restart (for text-based fallback path)
```

In internal/config, add:
```go
CrashThreshold int \`toml:"crash_threshold" default:"3"\`
```

### Step 3: Modify monitor loop (lines 314-329)
Replace the current flow with the single-call pattern shown above. The guard and debounce operate on the SAME pidAlive/pidKnown variables.

### Step 4: Reset on healthy
When agent transitions to healthy:
```go
agentState.ConsecutiveFailures = 0
agentState.Healthy = true
```

## Key Design Decision
Debounce does NOT delay PID-dead restarts. If the PID check authoritatively says the agent is dead, we restart immediately (set failures = threshold). The debounce only gates the unreliable text-based path.

## Key Files
- MODIFY: internal/resilience/monitor.go (AgentState, monitor loop lines 314-334)
- MODIFY: internal/config/config.go or relevant config struct (CrashThreshold)
- MODIFY: config.toml template/defaults

## Testing
- threshold=3, PID dead → restart on first check (failures forced to threshold)
- threshold=3, PID unknown + text error → restart on 3rd check
- threshold=3, PID unknown + text error x 2 then healthy → reset to 0, no restart
- threshold=1, PID unknown + text error → restart on first check (no debounce)
close_reason: Added CrashThreshold config (default 3), ConsecutiveFailures/LastFailureReason to AgentState, refactored monitor loop with single PID check + debounce: PID-dead=instant restart, PID-unknown+text=debounced, PID-alive=reset+skip. Updated test to use CrashThreshold=1.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: RACE CONDITION FIX: The PID-alive guard (bd-1ks5x.2) and debounce (bd-1ks5x.3) should NOT call process.IsChildAlive() independently. The guard checks IsChildAlive first; if it passes (child dead or unknown), store the result in a local variable and pass it to the debounce logic. This avoids a TOCTOU race where the child dies between the guard check and the debounce check. Implementation: the guard call returns a (pidAlive bool, pidKnown bool) tuple; if pidKnown && !pidAlive the debounce immediately sets failures=threshold (skip debounce for authoritative PID-dead). If !pidKnown, increment failures normally (debounce the unreliable text signal).

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: NESTING FIX: The debounce and PID guard code must go INSIDE the existing 'if agentState.Healthy' block at monitor.go:318, NOT outside it. The current code structure is: if StatusError/ProcessExited { if agentState.Healthy { handleCrash() } }. The guard and debounce replace the inner handleCrash() call within that nesting, NOT the outer condition check.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: LOGIC BUG: ConsecutiveFailures not reset when PID-alive guard fires. In the proposed code, when pidKnown and pidAlive, we continue without resetting failures. This creates a slow-burn false restart: Check 1: PID unknown + text error -> failures=1. Check 2: PID alive -> continue (failures stays 1). Check 3: PID unknown + text error -> failures=2. Check 4: PID alive -> continue (stays 2). Check 5: PID unknown + text error -> failures=3 -> RESTART despite being alive in checks 2 and 4. FIX: Reset ConsecutiveFailures in the PID-alive guard path: if pidKnown && pidAlive { agentState.ConsecutiveFailures = 0; continue }. The agent is provably alive so prior failure counts should be wiped.

title: Add final PID guard before sendFunc() in restartAgent()
description:
## What
Add a last-second PID liveness check in restartAgent() at monitor.go ~line 634, just before sendFunc(). If the agent is still alive, abort the restart.

## Why (P2 — final safety net)
The restart path has a delay (RestartDelaySeconds, default 5s) before injecting keys. During this delay, conditions may change — the agent may recover, or a false positive may resolve. A final PID check right before sending keys prevents the most damaging outcome (injecting spawn command as literal keystrokes into a running agent) even if all other guards failed.

## How
1. The shell PID must be available in restartAgent() scope. Currently AgentState has PaneID and PaneIndex but NOT the shell PID. Add ShellPID int to AgentState struct (populated during RegisterAgent() from Pane.PID).
2. Before sendFunc() at line 634:
```go
if agent.ShellPID > 0 && process.IsChildAlive(agent.ShellPID) {
    log.Printf("[resilience] Aborting restart for %s: agent still alive (shell PID %d has children)", agent.PaneID, agent.ShellPID)
    // Mark healthy again since agent is actually running
    m.mu.Lock()
    if a, ok := m.agents[agent.PaneID]; ok {
        a.Healthy = true
    }
    m.mu.Unlock()
    return
}
```
3. Also update RegisterAgent() to populate ShellPID from the Pane struct.

## Key Files
- MODIFY: internal/resilience/monitor.go (AgentState struct + restartAgent() + RegisterAgent())
- REFERENCE: internal/process/liveness.go (IsChildAlive function)

## Edge Cases
- ShellPID = 0: skip the guard (PID unknown, proceed with restart — better than blocking all restarts)
- Race condition: child exits between check and sendFunc. This is acceptable — we gave it our best check. The text injection into an empty shell prompt is the correct behavior for a genuine crash.
- Concurrent restarts: the m.mu.Lock() in restartAgent already serializes access, so no double-restart concern.

AgentState (monitor.go, this bead) is the resilience monitor's PERSISTENT state — populated once during RegisterAgent(), used for the final PID guard in restartAgent(). These are different lifecycle/scope: AgentHealth is ephemeral (per-check), AgentState is long-lived (per-agent-session). Both need ShellPID because they are used in different code paths.

title: E2E test script for resilience monitor false-positive prevention
description:
## What
Create a comprehensive E2E test script (scripts/test_resilience_false_positive.sh) that proves the resilience monitor does NOT falsely restart working agents after the PID-based fix.

## Test Scenarios

### Scenario 1: Agent outputs "exit status" text — NO false restart
1. ntm spawn a single-agent session (cc or cod) with auto_restart=true
2. Wait for agent to become healthy (poll ntm status --json, wait for status=ok)
3. Send a prompt via ntm send: "Explain how Unix processes work. Use the words exit status, process exited, and connection closed in your explanation."
4. Wait 30 seconds (2x health check interval of 15s)
5. Verify: agent NOT restarted:
   - Check ntm log for absence of "[resilience] Agent.*restarted"
   - Check pane PID unchanged: tmux list-panes -F "#{pane_pid}" should match original
6. Log: timestamp, shell PID, child PID, agent output (last 20 lines), restart count from ntm status

### Scenario 2: Agent actually crashes — restart DOES trigger
1. ntm spawn a single-agent session with auto_restart=true
2. Wait for agent to become healthy
3. Record original child PID: pgrep -P $SHELL_PID
4. Kill the agent: kill $CHILD_PID
5. Wait for restart_delay (config default 5s) + 15 seconds
6. Verify: agent WAS restarted:
   - New child PID exists (different from killed PID)
   - ntm log contains "[resilience] Agent.*restarted"
7. Log: original child PID, kill signal, new child PID, restart log entries

### Scenario 3: Text-only fallback with debounce (PID unavailable simulation)
This tests the debounce path when PID checking cannot determine liveness.
NOTE: We cannot easily make the real PID unavailable in E2E. Instead, test the observable behavior: with a healthy agent whose PID is alive, verify that even rapid repeated health checks do not trigger false restarts.
1. ntm spawn with auto_restart=true, crash_threshold=3
2. Wait for agent to become healthy
3. Send rapid prompts that produce exit-related output (3x over 45 seconds)
4. Verify: no restart occurred (PID-alive guard catches everything before debounce matters)
5. Verify: ntm log contains "skipping crash handling" if any false-positive pattern matched
6. Log: health check results, PID check results, failure counts

### Scenario 4: Verify PID guard logging
1. ntm spawn with auto_restart=true
2. Wait for agent to become healthy
3. Run the agent through Scenario 1 steps
4. Check ntm log for guard activation: "[resilience].*PID.*has children.*skipping crash handling"
5. This verifies the logging infrastructure works, confirming the guard is being exercised
6. Log: all [resilience] log lines from the test session

## Script Structure
```bash
#\!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="\$(cd \"\$(dirname \"\$0\")\" && pwd)"
TEST_SESSION="ntm-e2e-resilience-$$"
LOG_FILE="/tmp/\${TEST_SESSION}.log"
NTM_LOG="/tmp/\${TEST_SESSION}-ntm.log"
PASS_COUNT=0
FAIL_COUNT=0
TOTAL_COUNT=0

log()  { printf "[%s] [%-12s] %s\\n" "\$(date -Iseconds)" "\$1" "\$2" | tee -a "\$LOG_FILE"; }
pass() { log "\$1" "PASS: \$2"; PASS_COUNT=\$((PASS_COUNT + 1)); TOTAL_COUNT=\$((TOTAL_COUNT + 1)); }
fail() { log "\$1" "FAIL: \$2"; FAIL_COUNT=\$((FAIL_COUNT + 1)); TOTAL_COUNT=\$((TOTAL_COUNT + 1)); }
skip() { log "\$1" "SKIP: \$2"; TOTAL_COUNT=\$((TOTAL_COUNT + 1)); }

cleanup() {
    log "CLEANUP" "Destroying test session \$TEST_SESSION"
    ntm destroy "\$TEST_SESSION" --force 2>/dev/null || true
    log "CLEANUP" "Log file: \$LOG_FILE"
    log "CLEANUP" "NTM log: \$NTM_LOG"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

wait_healthy() {
    local max_wait=60
    local waited=0
    while [ \$waited -lt \$max_wait ]; do
        if ntm status --json "\$TEST_SESSION" 2>/dev/null | jq -e '.agents[0].status == "ok"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            return 0
        fi
        sleep 2
        waited=\$((waited + 2))
    done
    return 1
}

get_shell_pid() { tmux list-panes -t "\$TEST_SESSION" -F '#{pane_pid}' | head -1; }
get_child_pid() { pgrep -P "\$1" | head -1; }
```

## Summary Report Format
```
=== E2E RESILIENCE TEST RESULTS ===
Scenario 1 (false-positive prevention): PASS/FAIL
Scenario 2 (genuine crash restart):     PASS/FAIL
Scenario 3 (debounce verification):     PASS/FAIL
Scenario 4 (logging verification):      PASS/FAIL
Total: X/4 passed, Y/4 failed
Log: /tmp/ntm-e2e-resilience-XXXX.log
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- Script exits 0 if all 4 scenarios pass
- Script exits 1 if any scenario fails
- All scenarios log detailed diagnostic info to LOG_FILE
- Cleanup destroys test session even on failure
close_reason: Created scripts/e2e/test_resilience_false_positive.sh with 4 scenarios: false-positive text prevention, genuine crash restart, debounce verification, PID guard logging. Uses project e2e framework (lib/log.sh).

title: Task: Add rate_limit_detected field with pattern matching
description:
## What

Add `rate_limit_detected` boolean field that pattern-matches pane output
for rate limit indicators.

## Why

Rate limiting is the #1 failure mode in multi-agent sessions. Operators
currently must manually grep pane output to detect this. Automated detection
enables automated response (wait, switch account, skip pane).

## Rate Limit Patterns

Known patterns to detect:

| Provider | Pattern |
|----------|---------|
| Claude/Anthropic | "You've hit your limit" |
| Claude/Anthropic | "resets .* (America/.*)" |
| OpenAI | "Rate limit exceeded" |
| OpenAI | "Too many requests" |
| Google | "RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED" |
| Generic | "rate limit" (case insensitive) |

## Implementation

```go
var rateLimitPatterns = []*regexp.Regexp{
    regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)you've hit your limit`),
    regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)rate limit`),
    regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)too many requests`),
    regexp.MustCompile(`RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`),
    regexp.MustCompile(`resets \d+[ap]m`),
}

func detectRateLimit(paneContent string) (bool, string) {
    // Check last 50 lines only (performance)
    lines := strings.Split(paneContent, "\n")
    if len(lines) > 50 {
        lines = lines[len(lines)-50:]
    }
    content := strings.Join(lines, "\n")
    
    for _, pattern := range rateLimitPatterns {
        if match := pattern.FindString(content); match != "" {
            return true, match
        }
    }
    return false, ""
}
```

## Output Schema

```json
{
  "panes": [{
    "index": 4,
    "rate_limit_detected": true,
    "rate_limit_match": "You've hit your limit",
    "rate_limit_reset": "4pm ET"  // Parsed if available
  }]
}
```

## Performance

- Only check last 50 lines (configurable)
- Compile patterns once at startup
- Short-circuit on first match

## Configuration

Allow custom patterns via config for unknown providers:
```yaml
rate_limit_patterns:
  - "custom rate limit message"
```

## Testing

- Unit test: Each pattern with mock content
- Integration test: Actual rate-limited pane

   - resets \d+[ap]m

title: [HIGH] pressure: EvaluateSpawnAdmission cap check ignores RunningAgents — spawn batches that individually fit but cumulatively exceed MaxAgents are admitted, bypassing the concurrent agent cap
description:
In internal/pressure/pressure.go EvaluateSpawnAdmission (commit 7a3d732d), the agent-cap branch only checks the size of the *requested* spawn against MaxAgents — RunningAgents is collected, propagated, and reported but never consulted in the decision:

  runningAgents := maxInt(in.RunningAgents, 0)   // line 187 — computed
  ...
  out := SpawnAdmission{
      ...
      RunningAgents: runningAgents,              // line 210 — reflected to output
      ...
  }
  if maxAgents > 0 {
      out.AgentHeadroom = maxAgents - requestedAgents   // ignores running
      if out.AgentHeadroom < 0 { out.AgentHeadroom = 0 }
  }
  switch {
  ...
  case maxAgents > 0 && requestedAgents > maxAgents:    // ignores running
      out.Decision = SpawnAdmissionRefuse
      out.Reason = "agent_limit_exceeded"
      ...
  ...
  }

Concrete bypass: with `caps.ClaudeMaxConcurrent=12, caps.CodexMaxConcurrent=0, caps.GeminiMaxConcurrent=0` (so spawnAdmissionAgentLimit() returns MaxAgents=12), a host that already has 10 agents running can admit a request for 5 more (10 + 5 = 15 > 12), because:
  - requestedAgents (5) > maxAgents (12) → false → no refusal
  - the case branches do not consult runningAgents

The MaxAgents value derives from per-type *MaxConcurrent* caps in spawn_pacing.agent_caps, whose name + sum semantics imply "max simultaneously running agents", not "max in a single request". collectSpawnAdmissionInput in internal/robot/spawn.go enumerates tmux panes specifically to populate input.RunningAgents — code that is now dead-weight w.r.t. the decision.

Concrete repro:
  in := SpawnAdmissionInput{
    RequestedAgents: 5,
    RequestedPanes:  6,
    RunningAgents:   10,
    MaxAgents:       12,
  }
  out := EvaluateSpawnAdmission(in)
  // out.Decision == SpawnAdmissionAdmit
  // post-spawn total would be 15, exceeding MaxAgents=12 by 3 — admission control silently bypassed.

Test gap: TestEvaluateSpawnAdmission_RefusesAgentLimit (pressure_test.go) sets RunningAgents=0 (default), so the buggy branch is exercised but the running+requested case is invisible to CI.

Suggested fix:
  1. Make the cap check consult both fields:
       postSpawn := runningAgents + requestedAgents
       case maxAgents > 0 && postSpawn > maxAgents:
           out.Decision = SpawnAdmissionRefuse
           out.Reason   = "agent_limit_exceeded"
           out.Hint     = "running " + intoa(runningAgents) +
                          " + requested " + intoa(requestedAgents) +
                          " exceeds cap " + intoa(maxAgents)
  2. Recompute AgentHeadroom against post-spawn or against running so the
     reported field matches the decision criterion:
       out.AgentHeadroom = maxAgents - runningAgents - requestedAgents
       if out.AgentHeadroom < 0 { out.AgentHeadroom = 0 }
  3. Add a regression test asserting:
       - RunningAgents=10, RequestedAgents=5, MaxAgents=12 → Refuse.
       - RunningAgents=5,  RequestedAgents=5, MaxAgents=12 → Admit.

Severity HIGH: this is admission control bypassed by a one-shot spawn that fits the request-size check but exceeds the concurrent cap once existing agents are accounted for. The cap exists to prevent OOM / Anthropic-rate-limit / fan-out runaway; the fields needed to enforce it are already wired through both layers but the decision branch never reads them.

Source: internal/pressure/pressure.go EvaluateSpawnAdmission (~line 175); collectSpawnAdmissionInput in internal/robot/spawn.go (~line 105) populates RunningAgents from tmux. Commit 7a3d732d.
close_reason: EvaluateSpawnAdmission cap branch now refuses when runningAgents + requestedAgents > maxAgents instead of just requestedAgents > maxAgents. AgentHeadroom recomputed as maxAgents - runningAgents - requestedAgents (clamped to 0). Hint surfaces 'running N + requested M exceeds cap K' so the operator sees the components. Three new pressure tests pin the contract: refusal when running+requested exceeds cap (the bd-1oenb scenario 10+5 vs 12), admission when they fit (5+5 vs 12 → headroom=2), and admission at exact cap (5+7==12 → headroom=0). Existing TestEvaluateSpawnAdmission_AdmitsWithHeadroom updated because its inputs (5+3 vs 7) relied on the buggy ignore-running behavior — bumped MaxAgents to 10 to test the corrected accounting. Robot-side TestSpawnOptions_DryRunIncludesAdmission and TestSpawnOptions_MultipleAgentTypes also updated: hoisted per-type AgentCaps to 1024 so the admission decision is environment-independent on a busy CI/swarm host (default 3+2+2=7 caps would otherwise refuse on any host with running agent panes). Commit: 1bad81ac. rch exec -- go build ./cmd/ntm and rch exec -- go test -short -timeout 120s ./internal/pressure/... ./internal/robot/ both pass.

title: Add file reservation integration - auto-reserve files mentioned in bead before assigning to agent
description:
## Overview
Integrate with MCP Agent Mail file reservation when assigning beads to agents. This uses the **existing** Agent Mail file reservation system - no new implementation.

## Agent Mail Tools Used (existing)
- `file_reservation_paths` - reserve files for an agent
- `release_file_reservations` - release when done
- `renew_file_reservations` - extend TTL if needed

## How It Works
1. Parse bead description for file paths
2. On assignment, call Agent Mail `file_reservation_paths(project, agent_name, paths, ttl, exclusive)`
3. If conflict detected (another agent holds reservation), skip or warn
4. On completion, call `release_file_reservations`

## File Detection
```go
func ExtractFilePaths(bead Recommendation) []string {
    // Extract paths from bead description/metadata
    // Patterns: src/api/handler.go, lib/*.ts, internal/**/*.go
}
```

## Integration with ntm assign
```
1. Get assignment (bead, agent) pair
2. Extract file paths from bead
3. Call Agent Mail: file_reservation_paths(project, agent_name, paths, ttl=3600, exclusive=true)
4. Handle response:
   - Success: proceed with assignment
   - Conflict: skip (--skip-conflicts) or warn
5. On completion detection: call release_file_reservations
```

## Output Format
```json
{
  "assigned": [...],
  "conflicts": [
    {
      "bead_id": "bd-abc1",
      "conflicting_files": ["src/api/handler.go"],
      "held_by": "GreenCastle",
      "action": "skipped"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Extract file paths from bead description
- [ ] Call Agent Mail file_reservation_paths on assignment
- [ ] Handle conflicts from Agent Mail response
- [ ] Call release_file_reservations on completion
- [ ] Include conflicts in JSON output

## Dependencies
- MCP Agent Mail server running
- Assignment tracking (bd-92e1)
- Completion detection (bd-25cq)

title: Task: Implement ensemble loader with user/project override support
description:
Implement user-defined ensemble configuration system with user/project overrides.

## Configuration File Format

### Locations
```
~/.config/ntm/ensembles.yaml
# or project-local
.ntm/ensembles.yaml
```

### Schema
```yaml
ensembles:
  my-security-review:
    display: "Security Review"
    description: "Security-focused code review ensemble"
    modes:
      - id: deductive         # A1
      - id: root-cause        # E2
      - id: worst-case        # G1
      - id: meta-cognitive    # L1
      - id: systems-thinking  # K1
    synthesis:
      strategy: adversarial
      synthesizer_mode: meta-cognitive
    budget:
      per_agent: 5000
      total: 35000
    allow_advanced: true
    agent_distribution:
      claude: 3
      codex: 2
    tags: [security, review]

  extended-architecture:
    extends: architecture-review
    modes:
      - id: formal-verification  # A3
    synthesis:
      strategy: deliberative

aliases:
  sec: my-security-review
  arch: architecture-review
```

## Implementation
```go
// internal/ensemble/config.go
type EnsembleConfigFile struct {
    Ensembles map[string]*UserEnsemble `yaml:"ensembles"`
    Aliases   map[string]string        `yaml:"aliases"`
}

type UserEnsemble struct {
    Display           string           `yaml:"display"`
    Description       string           `yaml:"description"`
    Extends           string           `yaml:"extends"`
    Modes             []ModeRef        `yaml:"modes"` // id or code
    Synthesis         SynthesisConfig  `yaml:"synthesis"`
    Budget            BudgetConfig     `yaml:"budget"`
    AllowAdvanced     bool             `yaml:"allow_advanced"`
    AgentDistribution map[string]int   `yaml:"agent_distribution"`
    Tags              []string         `yaml:"tags"`
}

func LoadEnsembleConfig() (*EnsembleConfigFile, error)
```

title: Unit Tests: All ntm assign strategies (balanced, speed, quality, dependency)
description:
## Test Coverage
Test all ntm assign strategy algorithms besides round-robin.

## Test Cases

### Balanced Strategy
- Distribute evenly when all agents have 0 assignments
- Prefer agents with fewer current assignments
- Handle tie-breaking (use pane order)
- Update scores after each assignment

### Speed Strategy
- Prefer agents with lower context usage
- Score = 1.0 - (context_pct / 100)
- Handle agents at 100% context (score = 0)
- Prefer fresh agents over loaded ones

### Quality Strategy
- Match bead type to agent capabilities
- Claude for refactoring/architecture
- Codex for feature/bug_fix
- Gemini for documentation/review
- Handle unknown bead types (default score)

### Dependency Strategy
- Prioritize high PageRank beads
- Prioritize high unblocks_count beads
- Score = pagerank * 0.5 + unblocks * 0.5
- Sort beads by score before assignment

### Strategy Selection
- Default to balanced
- Parse --strategy flag correctly
- Error on unknown strategy

## Detailed Logging Requirements (Go test)

### Test Structure
```go
func TestBalancedStrategy(t *testing.T) {
    t.Log("=== TestBalancedStrategy ===")
    
    // Setup
    t.Log("[SETUP] Creating test agents and beads")
    agents := []Agent{...}
    beads := []Bead{...}
    t.Logf("[SETUP] Agents: %d, Beads: %d", len(agents), len(beads))
    
    // Execute
    t.Log("[EXEC] Running balanced strategy")
    result := BalancedStrategy(beads, agents)
    t.Logf("[EXEC] Result: %d assignments", len(result))
    
    // Verify
    t.Log("[VERIFY] Checking distribution")
    for i, a := range result {
        t.Logf("[VERIFY] Assignment %d: bead=%s -> pane=%d, score=%.2f",
            i, a.BeadID, a.Pane, a.Score)
    }
    
    // Assert
    if len(result) != len(beads) {
        t.Errorf("[FAIL] Expected %d assignments, got %d", len(beads), len(result))
    } else {
        t.Log("[PASS] Assignment count correct")
    }
}
```

### Log Points per Test

#### Setup Logging
```go
t.Logf("[SETUP] Test: %s", t.Name())
t.Logf("[SETUP] Input agents: %+v", agents)
t.Logf("[SETUP] Input beads: %+v", beads)
t.Logf("[SETUP] Options: %+v", opts)
```

#### Execution Logging
```go
t.Log("[EXEC] Calling strategy function")
t.Logf("[EXEC] Strategy: %s", strategyName)
t.Logf("[EXEC] Duration: %v", elapsed)
```

#### Scoring Logging (verbose)
```go
t.Logf("[SCORE] Bead %s:", bead.ID)
for _, agent := range agents {
    t.Logf("[SCORE]   Agent %d (%s): score=%.2f", 
        agent.Pane, agent.Type, score)
}
t.Logf("[SCORE] Winner: pane %d with score %.2f", winner.Pane, winner.Score)
```

#### Assertion Logging
```go
// Before assertion
t.Logf("[ASSERT] Checking: %s", description)
t.Logf("[ASSERT] Expected: %v", expected)
t.Logf("[ASSERT] Actual: %v", actual)

// Result
if expected == actual {
    t.Logf("[PASS] %s", description)
} else {
    t.Errorf("[FAIL] %s: expected %v, got %v", description, expected, actual)
}
```

### Table-Driven Tests with Logging
```go
func TestStrategyScoring(t *testing.T) {
    tests := []struct {
        name     string
        strategy string
        agents   []Agent
        beads    []Bead
        want     []Assignment
    }{
        {"balanced_even", "balanced", ...},
        {"balanced_uneven", "balanced", ...},
        {"speed_fresh", "speed", ...},
    }
    
    for _, tt := range tests {
        t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
            t.Logf("[TEST] %s", tt.name)
            t.Logf("[INPUT] Strategy=%s, Agents=%d, Beads=%d",
                tt.strategy, len(tt.agents), len(tt.beads))
            
            got := RunStrategy(tt.strategy, tt.beads, tt.agents)
            
            t.Logf("[OUTPUT] Assignments: %d", len(got))
            for i, a := range got {
                t.Logf("[OUTPUT] [%d] bead=%s pane=%d score=%.2f",
                    i, a.BeadID, a.Pane, a.Score)
            }
            
            if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, tt.want) {
                t.Errorf("[FAIL] Mismatch\nwant: %+v\ngot:  %+v", tt.want, got)
            } else {
                t.Log("[PASS] Output matches expected")
            }
        })
    }
}
```

### Running with Verbose Output
```bash
go test -v -run TestBalancedStrategy ./internal/assign/...
```

## Test File
internal/assign/strategy_test.go

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All strategy algorithms have unit tests
- [ ] Tests log setup, execution, and verification steps
- [ ] Score calculations are logged in detail
- [ ] Failed assertions include context
- [ ] Table-driven tests cover edge cases

## Overview
Add support for local LLM backends (Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio) as first-class agent types, enabling privacy-sensitive work, offline operation, and cost-free experimentation.

## Problem Statement
Current NTM only supports cloud LLM providers (Claude, OpenAI, Gemini). Users need:
- Privacy for sensitive codebases (air-gapped environments)
- Offline operation when internet unavailable
- Cost-free experimentation and learning
- Running specialized/fine-tuned local models

1. New agent type: --local=N or --ollama=N for spawning local agents
2. Model selection: --local-model=codellama:34b
3. Mixed fleets: combine cloud and local agents in same session
4. Performance monitoring: track token/s, memory usage
5. Automatic model management: pull models on demand

   - Connect to local Ollama server (default: localhost:11434)

- NTM_OLLAMA_HOST for custom Ollama URL
- NTM_LOCAL_MODEL for default model
- Per-project config in ntm.yaml

- Can spawn local agents alongside cloud agents
- Local agents participate in normal workflows
- Performance metrics visible in dashboard
- Works fully offline (after model cached)

title: [HIGH] foreach beads iteration source silently truncates to br default 50-result limit
description:
Review of ea60b424 [bug-fix] pipeline: fetch all bead_query results (bd-0e3el) found that the same root cause — invoking 'br list --json' without '--limit 0' and inheriting br's default 50-result cap — still bites the foreach iteration source resolver in internal/pipeline/iteration_sources.go.

ea60b424 only fixed BeadQueryStep.brListArgs in internal/pipeline/bead_query.go, leaving the parallel argv builder for foreach beads-source untouched.

In internal/pipeline/iteration_sources.go (~line 339-374):

  func parseStructuredBeadsQuery(expr string) ([]string, error) {
      args := []string{"list", "--json"}      // <- no --limit 0
      for _, raw := range strings.Split(expr, ",") {
          ...
      }
      return args, nil
  }

This is consumed by IterationSourceResolver.ResolveBeads (~line 115-138), which is the canonical path for foreach iteration sources of the form:

  foreach:
    items: 'beads(label:hypothesis,status:open)'
    steps: ...

br list --help confirms the default limit is 50 and 'unlimited' is opt-in via --limit 0:

      --limit <LIMIT>
          Maximum number of results (0 = unlimited, default: 50)
          [default: 50]

Reproducer:
  Workflow: foreach beads(label:foo,status:open) where the project has > 50 matching open beads.
  Current behavior: parseStructuredBeadsQuery returns ['list','--json','--label','foo','--status','open'].
                    runBr returns the first 50 records, foreach iterates over 50, beads 51..N are silently dropped.
  Expected behavior: same as bd-0e3el: emit '--limit','0' so the foreach plan sees every matching bead.

Impact: workflows that fan out per matching bead (e.g. 'review every open bug') silently skip beads beyond 50 once the project grows past that threshold. This is the exact silent-truncation failure mode that motivated bd-0e3el; the fix needs to be applied symmetrically. Same likely applies to other 'br list --json' callers (internal/bv/bv.go listings, internal/scanner/bridge.go and dedup.go, internal/serve/beads.go, internal/robot/tui_parity.go ~line 3522, internal/cli/completion_helpers.go ~line 272), but the pipeline foreach path is the highest-impact case because the silent dropoff happens at orchestration time and cannot be detected by the pipeline author without instrumenting br directly.

Fix: prepend or append '--limit','0' to the args slice in parseStructuredBeadsQuery (or factor a shared helper used by both BeadQueryStep.brListArgs and parseStructuredBeadsQuery so future br callers in the pipeline package inherit the unlimited default). Add a regression assertion analogous to TestExecuteBeadQueryCapturesTypedRecords that pins the expected argv to ['list','--json','--limit','0', ...].

Source commit: ea60b424 [bug-fix] pipeline: fetch all bead_query results (bd-0e3el)
close_reason: Duplicate of bd-ftsqw; both track parseStructuredBeadsQuery missing br list --limit 0 for foreach beads structured queries.

**Agent Effectiveness Scoring and Learning EPIC**

## What It Does
Track agent effectiveness over time and use that data to improve assignments and workflows.

[CRITICAL] Data race: heartbeat goroutine reads stdoutBuf concurrently with exec.Cmd writer
description:
## Severity: [CRITICAL]

Commit 8ad8ac86 (`feat(pipeline): emit pipeline.command.heartbeat`) introduces a data race in `executeCommand` (internal/pipeline/executor.go:1300-1322).

The heartbeat goroutine reads `stdoutBuf.Len()` while exec.Cmd's internal writer goroutine is writing to the same `cappedWriter` via `cmd.Stdout = stdoutBuf`. `cappedWriter` is explicitly documented as NOT safe for concurrent access (see capped_writer.go:16-20).

## Reproduction

Run with race detector:
```
go test -race -run TestHeartbeatRace -count=1 ./internal/pipeline/
```
with this test:
```go
func TestHeartbeatRaceOnStdoutBuf(t *testing.T) {
    prev := commandHeartbeatInterval
    commandHeartbeatInterval = 5 * time.Millisecond
    t.Cleanup(func() { commandHeartbeatInterval = prev })
    e := newCommandTestExecutor(t)
    step := &Step{ID: "noisy", Command: "for i in $(seq 1 200); do echo line-$i; sleep 0.005; done"}
    _ = e.executeCommand(context.Background(), step, &Workflow{Name: "test"})
}
```

Race detector output:
```
WARNING: DATA RACE
Read at 0x... by goroutine 140:
  bytes.(*Buffer).Len()
  pipeline.(*cappedWriter).Len()
  pipeline.(*Executor).executeCommand.func2() executor.go:1318

Previous write at 0x... by goroutine 139:
  bytes.(*Buffer).grow()
  bytes.(*Buffer).Write()
  pipeline.(*cappedWriter).Write() capped_writer.go:50
  io.copyBuffer / os/exec.(*Cmd).writerDescriptor.func1()
```

## Why this matters in production

- Production cadence is 30s, but any command that emits stdout >30s old will hit this race in production. Pipeline command steps that produce streaming output (long-running brennerbot phases, distill steps, integration tests, etc.) are exactly the case heartbeats target.
- Go data races on bytes.Buffer are undefined behaviour — possible outcomes include torn reads of `bytes_captured` (cosmetic) and corruption of internal Buffer state (memory unsafety; possible panic in subsequent Write or in String() at executor.go:1328).

## Fix sketch

Two viable options:

1. **Add a snapshot accessor to cappedWriter** that takes the buffer mutex (introduce a `sync.Mutex` in cappedWriter; lock around Write/Read/Len/String/Bytes/Total/Truncated). Keep the existing not-safe-for-concurrent-Write claim updated.
2. **Track bytes_captured via atomic.Int64** updated in Write — the heartbeat reads via Load. Doesn't protect String() at line 1328, but String() runs after the writer goroutine drains, so it's fine post-Wait.

Option 2 is the smaller change; Option 1 is more general. Either way, a regression test must run with `-race` and produce streaming output.

## Acceptance

- `go test -race ./internal/pipeline/...` passes including a new test that mirrors the noisy-command reproducer above.
- The heartbeat continues to surface a meaningful `bytes_captured` value.

## Files
- internal/pipeline/executor.go:1300-1322
- internal/pipeline/capped_writer.go (likely needs locking or atomic counter)
- internal/pipeline/executor_test.go (add race regression)
close_reason: Fixed: cappedWriter now serialises access via internal sync.Mutex; regression test TestExecuteCommand_HeartbeatRaceFreeOnNoisyStdout passes under -race. Files: internal/pipeline/capped_writer.go, internal/pipeline/heartbeat_race_demo_test.go

title: Implement session structure detection
description:
Implement session structure detection.

## Fields

- window_index: The window where agents live (typically 1)
- control_pane: Pane index of control shell (typically 1)
- agent_pane_start: First agent pane index (typically 2)
- agent_pane_end: Last agent pane index
- total_agent_panes: Count of agent panes

## Detection Logic

```bash
# Get window info
tmux list-windows -t session -F '#{window_index}'

# Get pane info
tmux list-panes -t session:1 -F '#{pane_index} #{pane_pid}'
```

## NTM Conventions

NTM creates sessions with:
- Single window at index 1 (not 0)
- Pane 1 = control shell (where spawn command was run)
- Panes 2+ = agent panes

## Edge Cases

- Session with multiple windows: document primary
- Non-NTM sessions: best-effort detection
