title: TOON: Research Go integration approach (CGO vs subprocess)
description:
Evaluate approaches for calling toon_rust from Go code.

## Options

### Option A: Subprocess (Simpler)
Call toon CLI as subprocess:
```go
cmd := exec.Command("toon", "encode")
cmd.Stdin = strings.NewReader(jsonData)
toonOutput, _ := cmd.Output()
```

Pros: Simple, no CGO, easy updates
Cons: Process overhead per call, latency

### Option B: CGO + Rust FFI (Faster)
Build toon_rust as C-compatible library, call from Go via CGO.

Pros: Near-zero overhead, native speed
Cons: CGO complexity, cross-platform builds, version coupling

### Option C: WASM (Middle Ground)
Compile toon_rust to WASM, run via Go WASM runtime.

Pros: Sandboxed, cross-platform, single binary
Cons: WASM overhead, runtime dependency

## Recommendation

Start with **subprocess** for simplicity. If latency becomes issue, migrate to CGO.

Robot mode commands are not high-frequency (maybe 1-10/second), so subprocess overhead (~5ms) is acceptable.

## Research Tasks
1. Verify toon CLI exists and has encode/decode commands
2. Benchmark subprocess overhead
3. Evaluate if CGO is needed for any use case
4. Check if toon_rust has WASM build

## Deliverable
Decision document with benchmarks and recommendation.
close_reason: Documented current TOON integration: Go shells out to toon_rust  (no CGO/WASM), with quick local latency measurement; see TOON_INTEGRATION_BRIEF.md + internal/robot/toon.go

title: Task: Ensure common flags consistency across all ntm assign commands
description:
## Overview
Ensure all ntm assign-related commands have consistent common flags.

## Common Flags to Implement
Every ntm command should support:
```bash
--json           # Machine-readable JSON output
-v, --verbose    # Show detailed scoring/decision logs
-q, --quiet      # Suppress non-essential output
--timeout=30s    # Timeout for external calls (bv, br, Agent Mail)
--no-color       # Disable colored output
```

## Agent Type Filter Consistency
Support both styles for agent type filtering:
```bash
# Short form (existing)
--cc-only
--cod-only
--gmi-only

# Long form (new, consistent with --agent in status)
--agent=claude
--agent=codex
--agent=gemini
```

## Commands to Update
- [ ] ntm assign (base command)
- [ ] ntm status --assignments (already has --agent)
- [ ] ntm assign --watch
- [ ] ntm assign --retry
- [ ] ntm assign --reassign
- [ ] ntm assign --clear
- [ ] ntm assign --pane
- [ ] ntm spawn --assign

## Implementation
```go
type CommonFlags struct {
    JSON      bool
    Verbose   int     // -v = 1, -vv = 2
    Quiet     bool
    Timeout   time.Duration
    NoColor   bool
}

func AddCommonFlags(cmd *cobra.Command, flags *CommonFlags) {
    cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&flags.JSON, "json", false, "Output as JSON")
    cmd.Flags().CountVarP(&flags.Verbose, "verbose", "v", "Increase verbosity")
    cmd.Flags().BoolVarP(&flags.Quiet, "quiet", "q", false, "Quiet mode")
    cmd.Flags().DurationVar(&flags.Timeout, "timeout", 30*time.Second, "Command timeout")
    cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&flags.NoColor, "no-color", false, "Disable colors")
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All assign-related commands have common flags
- [ ] Both --cc-only and --agent=claude work
- [ ] --json output is consistent format across commands
- [ ] --verbose increases log detail
- [ ] --quiet suppresses non-error output

title: xf: Implement --robot-xf-search command
description:
## Overview

Add `ntm --robot-xf-search` command for searching X/Twitter archives via xf integration.

## IMPORTANT: API Design Consistency

This command follows the **harmonized** robot mode patterns for tool bridges:
- **Naming**: `--robot-xf-search` (tool prefix: xf, no inline value)
- **Query param**: `--query=QUERY` (standard modifier flag)
- **Shared modifiers**: `--limit=N`, `--since=DATE`, `--until=DATE`, `--offset=N` (global flags)
- **Tool-specific modifiers**: `--xf-mode=`, `--xf-sort=` (unique to xf)

**NOTE**: This supersedes bd-1osrc which proposed a different interface. This bead is the canonical implementation.

## Command Interface

```bash
# Basic search (uses --query= modifier, NOT inline value)
ntm --robot-xf-search --query="error handling patterns"

# With search mode
ntm --robot-xf-search --query="rust async" --xf-mode=semantic --limit=10

# With date range filter
ntm --robot-xf-search --query="claude code" --since=2024-01-01 --until=2024-06-30

# With pagination
ntm --robot-xf-search --query="ai agents" --limit=20 --offset=20

# Sort by date (newest first)
ntm --robot-xf-search --query="llm" --xf-sort=date
```

## Output Schema

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "timestamp": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z",
  "query": "error handling patterns",
  "mode": "hybrid",
  "sort": "relevance",
  "count": 5,
  "offset": 0,
  "hits": [
    {
      "type": "tweet",
      "date": "2023-06-15",
      "content": "Been thinking about error handling patterns in Rust...",
      "score": 0.95,
      "url": "https://x.com/user/status/123456",
      "author": "rustacean",
      "thread_id": "123456"
    }
  ],
  "total_matches": 150,
  "has_more": true,
  "_agent_hints": {
    "next_offset": 5,
    "pages_remaining": 29,
    "suggested_query_refinement": null
  }
}
```

## Error Response

```json
{
  "success": false,
  "timestamp": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z",
  "error": "xf not found in PATH",
  "error_code": "TOOL_NOT_FOUND",
  "hint": "Install xf: go install github.com/.../xf@latest"
}
```

## Modifier Flags

| Flag | Description | Default | Scope |
|------|-------------|---------|-------|
| `--query=Q` | Search query (required) | - | **Required** |
| `--xf-mode=M` | Search mode: keyword, semantic, hybrid | hybrid | Tool-specific |
| `--xf-sort=S` | Sort order: relevance, date, date-asc | relevance | Tool-specific |
| `--limit=N` | Max results to return | 20 | Global shared |
| `--offset=N` | Skip first N results (pagination) | 0 | Global shared |

- Tool-specific flags (`--xf-mode`, `--xf-sort`) ARE tool-prefixed

This matches the established JFP and CASS patterns.

title: [HIGH] verbose author_model fallback still routes to same-family pane
description:
Review of 91056510 ([bug-fix][bd-8wu4e] prefer canonical family over raw author_model in pane strategy) found that the fallback path still treats raw author_model values as if they were already canonical model families.

Current behavior:
- foreachAuthorModelFamily first checks model_family/family/type.
- If those are absent, it returns author_model/model unchanged.
- byModelFamilyDifference compares pane.ModelFamily directly against that raw string.

Reproducer shape:
- item: {author_model: "claude-sonnet-4"}
- available pane families in order: [{id:p1, family:cc}, {id:p2, family:cod}]
- foreachAuthorModelFamily returns "claude-sonnet-4".
- byModelFamilyDifference sees p1.ModelFamily "cc" != "claude-sonnet-4" and selects p1, even though semantically that is the same Claude/cc family as the author.

Impact: by_model_family_difference can silently collapse adversarial/cross-family routing whenever iteration items carry only a verbose author_model, defeating the strategy and assigning critique work to the same model family.

Expected: normalize author_model/model fallback values to canonical pane families before comparison (for example claude* -> cc, codex/openai* -> cod, gemini* -> gmi), and add a regression where author_model is verbose and model_family is absent.

No code fix was applied in this review pass because the requested CRITICAL/HIGH auto-fix scope is restricted to NEW files only, while the production fix requires changing the existing pane-assignment helper or strategy comparison.

title: EPIC: Progressive CLI Discovery System - Tiered Command Visibility
description:
## Overview
Implement a proficiency-tiered command discovery system that progressively reveals NTM commands as users gain experience. This reduces cognitive overload for new users while preserving full power for experts.

## Problem Statement
NTM has 40+ commands and flags. New users face a wall of options in --help, making the tool feel overwhelming. Meanwhile, power users need quick access to advanced features. Current flat --help listing serves neither audience well.

## Design Philosophy
- Tier 1 (Apprentice): Core workflow commands only (spawn, send, status, kill, help)
- Tier 2 (Journeyman): Full standard commands (all current public commands)
- Tier 3 (Master): Advanced/experimental features (robot mode, internal debugging)

## Key Features
1. Tiered help output: Commands filtered by proficiency level
2. Automatic tier promotion: Track usage patterns to suggest promotions
3. ntm level command: View/change proficiency tier
4. Contextual suggestions: Suggest relevant commands based on current state
5. Progressive disclosure in dashboard: Show only tier-appropriate controls

## Configuration
- Store tier in ~/.config/ntm/proficiency.json
- Support NTM_PROFICIENCY_TIER env var override
- Default new users to Tier 1

## Success Criteria
- New users see only 5-7 essential commands initially
- Help output adapts to proficiency tier
- Users can manually upgrade/downgrade tier
- Dashboard respects tier for keybinding hints
- Contextual suggestions appear for common next actions

## Files Likely Affected
- internal/cli/help.go (new file for tiered help)
- internal/cli/root.go (tier-aware command registration)
- internal/config/proficiency.go (new file for tier management)
- internal/tui/dashboard/help.go (tier-aware hints)

## Implementation Phases
1. Define tier taxonomy and command categorization
2. Implement proficiency config storage
3. Create tiered help renderer
4. Add usage tracking for auto-promotion
5. Implement contextual suggestions
6. Update dashboard help to respect tiers
notes: Closed as dropped: only keep help --minimal/--full + contextual suggestions; no tier gating.
close_reason: Completed Progressive CLI Discovery System implementation. All 6 child tasks done: taxonomy defined (3 tiers with command categorization), proficiency config storage (JSON-based with env override), ntm level command (show/up/down/set tiers), usage tracking (commands, sessions, advanced attempts), unit tests (56+ tests), E2E tests (12 tests). System reduces cognitive overload for new users while preserving full power for experts.

title: Pipeline Phase B: comprehensive test suite + e2e harness
description:
# Epic: Lock in correctness with tests

## Background

Phase A added ~600 LOC of schema/parser/executor changes with **zero new tests**. As we wire execution semantics for E1/E2/E3/E5, the surface area for subtle bugs (variable scoping, pane assignment race conditions, command exit propagation, custom UnmarshalYAML edge cases) explodes. Tests-first lets us refactor confidently and catches regressions immediately.

The existing pipeline tests (parser_test.go, executor_test.go, etc.) test the v2.0 canonical schema. They need extension to cover all the new types and behaviors.

## Goal

1. **Unit tests** for every new custom UnmarshalYAML method:
   - PaneSpec (int, expr, null, empty)
   - ParallelSpec (bool, list)
   - OnFailureSpec (string, retry:N, struct)
   - IntOrExpr (int, expr)
   - AfterRef (string, list)
   - StringOrList (string, list)
   - OutputDecl (bare-string, full-struct, single-key shorthand)
2. **Workflow.Normalize() idempotency** — second call equals first across all alias collapses (After→DependsOn dedup, OnFailure→OnError mapping, Loop.Body→Loop.Steps, TemplateParams→Params merge).
3. **Validator rules** — assert each new mutual-exclusivity check fires (prompt+command, prompt+template, command+template) and the no-work check fires only when truly empty.
4. **Mock tmux + mock agent harness** — deterministic in-memory tmux state + scriptable agent responses. Lets executor tests run without a real tmux session.
5. **End-to-end integration test**: the mock harness runs brennerbot-incident.yaml (smallest, 8 steps) end-to-end, verifying command-step exit codes propagate, template substitution happens, foreach iteration covers expected items, dispatch logs go to the right place. Golden-file comparison for dispatch logs.
6. **TOML round-trip tests** for all new types.

## Why #4 priority (and why early)

Phase A's 600 LOC has no test coverage. Before adding 1500+ more LOC for E1/E2/E3/E5, lock in current behavior. Tests-first matters here because orchestration semantics are subtle.

## Sub-tasks

10 sub-beads: 7 unmarshal-method tests, normalize idempotency, validator rules, mock tmux harness, e2e harness, golden-file comparison, TOML round-trip.

## Dependencies

None — can start immediately after Phase A.

## Why future-self should care

Without tests we won't know we got it right. A real brennerbot session is hours long; a buggy executor wastes that. The harness lets us iterate fast.

## Files likely to change

- internal/pipeline/schema_test.go — extend
- internal/pipeline/parser_test.go — extend
- internal/pipeline/executor_test.go — extend
- internal/pipeline/mock_tmux.go — NEW; in-memory tmux harness
- internal/pipeline/mock_agent.go — NEW; scriptable agent
- internal/pipeline/e2e_test.go — NEW; end-to-end integration
- internal/pipeline/testdata/brennerbot-incident-golden.txt — NEW; golden output
- internal/pipeline/toml_test.go — NEW or extend; TOML round-trip
design: Consolidated file plan: keep parser/schema tests in existing parser_test.go and schema_test.go when they fit; use internal/pipeline/mock.go and internal/pipeline/mock_test.go for tmux and agent test doubles instead of tmux_iface.go, mock_tmux.go, mock_agent.go, or separate mock-agent files. E2E/golden assets belong under e2e/pipeline/ with shared helpers, capped by the bd-z5lv3 plan. Race/fuzz targets may use dedicated *_test.go files only where Go's testing model requires them.

description:

title: E4.10: Mock agent harness — scriptable agent responses
description:
Build a scriptable agent simulator so executor tests can verify dispatched prompts get expected responses.

## Spec
- AgentScripter: fixture interface that the mock tmux uses to simulate agent behavior. Caller pre-seeds (prompt-pattern → response) pairs.
- When mock tmux receives PasteKeys, it consults the scripter; if a pattern matches the prompt, the scripter appends the response to the pane's output buffer (after a configurable delay).

- Scripter pattern-matching works with substring AND regex.
- Multiple sequential dispatches to the same pane get sequential scripted responses.
- Tests don't deadlock if the script runs out (default response or clear error).

- internal/pipeline/mock_agent_test.go — NEW

title: E4.15: Logging conventions + slog event schema (foundation for all observability)
description:
## Why this bead exists FIRST in E4

Every other bead's 'use slog with these fields' instruction needs an established convention. This bead defines that convention and provides the helper functions every implementation will call.

## Spec

### Stable event names

Define const event names as strings (NOT enums to keep slog fields simple):

```go
const (
    EventRunStart        = "pipeline.run.start"
    EventRunComplete     = "pipeline.run.complete"
    EventRunError        = "pipeline.run.error"
    EventStepStart       = "pipeline.step.start"
    EventStepComplete    = "pipeline.step.complete"
    EventStepError       = "pipeline.step.error"
    EventStepSkip        = "pipeline.step.skip"
    EventStepRetry       = "pipeline.step.retry"
    EventDispatch        = "pipeline.dispatch"
    EventCommandExec     = "pipeline.command.exec"
    EventCommandResult   = "pipeline.command.result"
    EventTemplateRender  = "pipeline.template.render"
    EventForeachStart    = "pipeline.foreach.start"
    EventForeachIter     = "pipeline.foreach.iteration"
    EventForeachComplete = "pipeline.foreach.complete"
    EventBranchEval      = "pipeline.branch.eval"
    EventBranchDispatch  = "pipeline.branch.dispatch"
    EventOnFailureFire   = "pipeline.on_failure.fire"
    EventOnSuccessFire   = "pipeline.on_success.fire"
    EventSubstResolve    = "pipeline.subst.resolve"
    EventSubstWarn       = "pipeline.subst.warn"
    EventLoopIterStart   = "pipeline.loop.iteration.start"
    EventLoopExit        = "pipeline.loop.exit"
)
```

### Stable field names

Every relevant event includes these where applicable:

| Field | Type | Required when |
|-------|------|---------------|
| run_id | string | always |
| workflow | string | always |
| step_id | string | always (per-step events) |
| step_kind | string | always (prompt|command|template|foreach|branch|...) |
| pane_id | string | post-pane-selection |
| pane_index | int | post-pane-selection |
| agent_type | string | for prompt steps |
| iteration | int | inside foreach (0-based) |
| iteration_total | int | inside foreach |
| item_summary | string | inside foreach (truncated representation of the iteration item) |
| duration_ms | int64 | step.complete + step.error |
| status | string | step.complete |
| exit_code | int | command.result for non-zero exit |
| substitution_key | string | subst.resolve |
| substitution_resolved | bool | subst.resolve |
| recovery_pane | int | on_failure.fire when structured form |

title: E4.16: Race-detector test suite (go test -race) for parallel + foreach + nested
description:
## Background

Standard `go test ./internal/pipeline/...` doesn't enable Go's race detector. With Phase B's parallel + foreach concurrency, race conditions are likely without explicit testing.

## Spec

Add a CI-and-local target that runs `go test -race ./internal/pipeline/...` and `go test -race ./e2e/pipeline/...`. Race detector should pass.

Specific test scenarios to add:
1. `concurrency_test.go::TestRace_ParallelInline_50steps` — parallel:[50 inline steps] under -race.
2. `TestRace_ForeachParallel_100items` — 100-item foreach + parallel:true + max_concurrent:16.
3. `TestRace_NestedForeachParallel` — outer:parallel + inner:parallel.
4. `TestRace_PostPipelineDuringMain` — tight overlap scenario where main step finishes just as post-pipeline starts.
5. `TestRace_VariableScopeStackUnderForeach` — concurrent ${item.X} substitutions across goroutines.

title: E4.17: Fuzz tests for parser + substituteVariables + filter expression evaluator
description:
## Background

The user has a `testing-fuzzing` skill — they value fuzz testing. The pipeline package has several attack surfaces:
- YAML parser (parser.go) — malformed YAML, deeply-nested structures, alternation-type edge cases
- Substitution layer (executor.go substituteVariables) — recursive ${X}, escape edge cases, malformed refs
- Filter expression evaluator (foreach.go from E2.6) — malformed expressions, deeply-nested parens, operator precedence

## Spec

Use Go's native fuzz testing framework (Go 1.18+). Three fuzz targets:

### FuzzParseWorkflow
- Input: arbitrary bytes.
- Action: ParseFile equivalent that takes []byte.
- Goal: never panic. Errors are fine; panics are bugs.
- Seed corpus: every brennerbot pipeline + canonical example + a few minimal valid pipelines.

### FuzzSubstituteVariables
- Input: arbitrary string + a fixed Vars/Defaults/Pane fixture.
- Action: substituteVariables.
- Goal: never panic; recursion always terminates within max-depth; output is well-formed (no half-substituted ${X} unless original had one).
- Seed corpus: the known-good test cases from E3.6.

### FuzzFilterExpr
- Input: arbitrary string + a fixed Item fixture.
- Action: filter expression eval.
- Goal: never panic; rejects malformed inputs cleanly; doesn't infinite-loop on weird inputs.
- Seed corpus: the test cases from E2.6.

## Run policy

- Fuzz targets run for `-fuzztime=30s` in CI.
- Local devs can run for longer.
- Discovered crashes get committed as testdata/fuzz/ entries that turn into regression tests.

## Acceptance
- 3 fuzz functions exist and are registered.
- Each runs for 30s in CI without finding new crashes.
- Initial corpus seeded from existing tests.
- Documentation: how to run fuzz locally, where seed corpus lives.

title: E4.18: Benchmark tests for substitution + foreach + dispatch hot paths
description:
## Background

Hot paths in the pipeline package:
- substituteVariables (called per-step + per-iteration; potentially thousands of calls per pipeline)
- Foreach iteration loop (overhead per iteration)
- Step dispatch (channel ops, goroutine creation)
- Pane metadata lookup (cached but cache-miss path matters)

Without benchmarks, performance regressions land silently.

## Spec

Standard Go benchmarks for:

### BenchmarkSubstituteVariables
- Variants: 1 var / 5 vars / 50 vars / nested-path / pane.X / item.X / no-substitution-needed.
- Establish baseline; document budget (e.g., <1µs for no-subst, <10µs for 5 vars).

### BenchmarkForeachIteration_Sequential
- 100 iterations with a simple sleep-step.
- Measures iteration overhead.

### BenchmarkForeachIteration_Parallel
- Same 100 iterations with parallel:true, max_concurrent:8.
- Compare to sequential.

### BenchmarkPaneMetadataLookup
- Cache-hit + cache-miss paths.

## Run policy

- `go test -bench=. -benchmem ./internal/pipeline/...` locally.
- CI runs benchmarks on a stable hardware profile and compares against checked-in baseline (testdata/benchmarks/baseline.txt).
- Regression > 25% fails CI; <25% logs a warning.

- Baseline file generated.
- Documentation: how to run + how to update baseline.

title: dry-run command banner doesn't sanitize ANSI/OSC bytes from substituted Command/Stdin
description:
## Problem
The dry-run output for command steps in \`internal/pipeline/executor.go\` (executeCommand DryRun branch at ~line 1203) renders \`expandedCmd\` and \`expandedStdin\` through \`truncatePrompt(s, n)\` only. \`truncatePrompt\` normalizes \\n / \\t to spaces but does NOT strip ANSI/OSC escape sequences or C0 control bytes the way \`SanitizeDescriptionForTerminal\` (introduced by bd-lqz30) does for description fields.

Both fields are expanded via \`substituteVariablesStrictCtx\`, which interpolates \`\${steps.X.output}\`, \`\${vars.X}\`, \`\${defaults.X}\`, \`\${env.X}\`, etc. The interpolated value can contain arbitrary attacker-controlled bytes:
- Resumed dry-run via \`--from-state\` pulls real prior \`steps.X.output\` (an agent or command that emitted ANSI bytes).
- \`vars\` come from a var-file (JSON/YAML) that can contain control bytes.
- \`env.X\` / \`defaults.X\` similarly.

Result: a workflow run with \`ntm pipeline run --dry-run\` can hijack the operator's terminal — \`ESC[2J\` (clear screen), OSC 52 (clipboard), BEL, etc. — analogous to the bd-lqz30 attack on description fields, but via a different field path that bd-lqz30 did not patch.

## Reproduce
1. Workflow has step\`agent\` whose output contains \`\\x1b[2J\\x1b[H\` (or run resumed dry-run with state file containing such bytes).
2. Workflow has \`step2\` with \`stdin: \${steps.agent.output}\` and \`command: cat\`.
3. \`ntm pipeline run --dry-run\`.
4. Operator's terminal is cleared by the dry-run banner output.

## Fix
Wrap \`expandedCmd\` and \`expandedStdin\` with \`SanitizeDescriptionForTerminal\` before passing to \`truncatePrompt\` in the dry-run branch (executor.go ~line 1208–1211). Add a regression test that asserts the dry-run output for a step with control bytes in Stdin emits no C0 / ESC bytes.

## Severity
[MEDIUM] — operator-affecting terminal hijack reachable through legitimate workflow shape; only triggers in --dry-run plus attacker-controlled bytes in substituted variables. Same severity class as bd-lqz30 which patched description fields.

## Related
- bd-lqz30 (1c1fa26f) — pioneered SanitizeDescriptionForTerminal; this is a parity gap.
- bd-ziavr (76113228) — added expandedStdin to dry-run output without applying the sanitizer.
close_reason: Wrapped expandedCmd + expandedStdin with SanitizeDescriptionForTerminal before truncatePrompt in executeCommand DryRun branch (internal/pipeline/executor.go:1205-1219). Regression test TestExecuteCommand_DryRun_SanitizesControlBytes asserts no ESC/BEL/NUL bytes survive into dry-run output while payload text round-trips. Commit af9ecc47.

title: [MEDIUM] foreach models source skips variable substitution
description:
Review of e0293f86 (feat(pipeline): resolve foreach models iteration source) found that foreach.models is never passed through the foreach substitution path before ResolveModels runs. In internal/pipeline/foreach.go, substituteForeachStepFieldsProtected substitutes config.Items, Beads, Pairs, Debates, Filter, Template, Params, and nested body fields, but omits config.Models. ResolveForeachItems then calls resolver.ResolveModels(ctx, config.Models) on the raw parsed StringOrList.

Impact: workflows cannot drive the models iteration source from otherwise supported pipeline variables/defaults/runtime values, and shell model sources containing variables are executed with unresolved ${...} text. For example, a models shell source containing ${vars.model_family} does not receive the same substitution treatment as items/beads/pairs/debates/filter. This makes the models source inconsistent with the rest of foreach source resolution and with normal step string fields.

Expected: foreach.models entries should be substituted with the same protected-root semantics as other foreach source strings before ResolveModels, with regression coverage for a variable-backed literal list entry and a shell source containing ${vars.*}.

No production fix applied in this review pass because severity is MEDIUM; the narrow fix belongs in existing foreach substitution code, while current auto-fix scope is CRITICAL/HIGH only and NEW-file-only.
close_reason: substituteForeachStepFieldsProtected now iterates config.Models and applies substituteForeachString to each entry, matching the protected-root semantics already used for items/beads/pairs/debates/filter. Workflow vars in models entries (e.g. {model_family} -> 'claude') resolve before ResolveModels runs. Added TestSubstituteForeachFieldsResolvesModelsList covering two var-backed entries plus a literal pin.

This makes filters unusable for scalar item lists even though scalar foreach items are otherwise supported. Expected: exact item and ${item} resolve to ctx.Item, and exact pane/${pane} resolve to ctx.Pane; item.X/pane.X should keep current path behavior. Source commit: 6a20120d feat(pipeline): add foreach filter evaluator (bd-2ubxp.6).

Scalar foreach lists can now be filtered with item==value or ${item}==value. Tests cover string-equal, string-not-equal, ${item} form, false case, and bare pane scalar.

title: [LOW] PID-recycle race in waitCommandWithProcessGroupCleanup between ctx.Done and SIGTERM send
description:
Review of a7abefe2 found a tight race window where the cancel path may signal a recycled PID/process-group.

In internal/pipeline/process_group.go waitCommandWithProcessGroupCleanup:

  done := make(chan error, 1)
  go func() { done <- cmd.Wait() }()
  select {
  case err := <-done: ...
  case <-ctx.Done():
      ...
      _ = signalCommandProcessGroup(cmd, syscall.SIGTERM)
      ...
  }

If the child exits naturally between the moment ctx.Done() fires (selected) and signalCommandProcessGroup runs (a few microseconds later), the goroutine's cmd.Wait may have already returned and reaped the PID. The kernel can then assign that PID to a different process. Our subsequent Kill(-old_pid, SIGTERM) targets a process group that the OS now associates with an unrelated process, so we can SIGTERM/SIGKILL a stranger.

The previous implementation (removed by this commit) used exec.CommandContext + cmd.Cancel + cmd.WaitDelay, which the standard library coordinates internally — Go ensures the signal is sent before Wait reaps. Switching to exec.Command + a goroutine reintroduced the classic pattern hazard.

Practical exploitability: extremely low — requires the canceled command to exit on its own within microseconds of cancel, AND the kernel to recycle that PID quickly, AND that PID to lead a new process group. Almost never observed.

Mitigations:
- Restore exec.CommandContext + cmd.Cancel for SIGTERM, layer the SIGKILL fallback via cmd.WaitDelay
- Or hold the Process via cmd.Process and call cmd.Process.Signal(SIGTERM) instead of bare syscall.Kill, since Process.Signal returns os.ErrProcessDone if Wait already reaped (closing the race more cleanly)

Source commit: a7abefe2 fix(pipeline): clean up command process groups on cancel (bd-e2z38)
close_reason: waitCommandWithProcessGroupCleanup now does a non-blocking <-done check before SIGTERM and again before SIGKILL. If Wait has already reaped the child between the ctx.Done() firing and us reaching the signal call, we skip the signal entirely so we cannot SIGTERM/SIGKILL a recycled PID's unrelated process group. The pre-existing TestExecuteCommand_CancelKillsProcessGroupChild still verifies the happy-path cleanup; the race is hard to deterministically reproduce in a unit test, but the new guards close the window without changing observable behavior on the normal cancel path.

title: CAAM Integration: Coding Agent Account Manager for Rate Limit Recovery
description:
Integrate CAAM (coding_agent_account_manager) for instant account switching when agents hit rate limits.

## Project Location
/dp/coding_agent_account_manager (Rust CLI)

## Problem Being Solved

Rate limits are the #1 operational pain point in multi-agent workflows:
- Claude Code: 5-minute to multi-hour cooldowns
- OpenAI Codex: Per-minute/per-day limits
- Gemini: Regional and tier-based limits

Current workaround: Wait, or manually switch browser profiles. This kills productivity.

## What CAAM Does

CAAM is an OAuth token vault with instant profile switching:
- Stores encrypted OAuth tokens for multiple accounts per provider
- Detects rate limit responses automatically
- Switches to next available account in <100ms
- Tracks usage per account to predict limits
- Supports: Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, Anthropic API, etc.

### Key CAAM Commands
```bash
caam list                    # List all accounts
caam switch claude account2  # Switch to specific account
caam status                  # Show current account and usage
caam auto-rotate             # Enable automatic rotation on rate limit
```

## Integration Strategy for NTM

### 1. Rate Limit Detection
NTM monitors agent output for rate limit signals:
- "Rate limit exceeded"
- HTTP 429 responses
- Provider-specific messages

### 2. Automatic Recovery
When rate limit detected:
1. Pause agent activity
2. Call: caam switch <provider> --next
3. Update environment variables for agent
4. Resume agent

### 3. Robot Mode Commands
- --robot-switch-account: Manually trigger switch
- --robot-account-status: Get current account info
- --robot-accounts-list: List available accounts

### 4. Dashboard Integration
- Show current account per agent
- Show usage/limit percentages
- Alert when approaching 80% of limit

## Considerations
- Security: CAAM handles encryption, NTM just invokes CLI
- Atomicity: Account switch must be atomic (no half-switched state)
- Recovery: If CAAM fails, agent should continue with current account
- Latency: <100ms target for account switch

title: [HIGH] Foreach completion guard can replay already-executed iteration after cancellation
description:
Review of 7c302816 ([bug-fix][bd-xreqm]) found a regression in internal/pipeline/loops.go executeForEach: completion persistence changed from iterationSucceeded(...) to ctx.Err()==nil && iterationSucceeded(...).

If cancellation arrives after nested steps complete but before markForeachIterationCompleted runs, ctx.Err()!=nil and the iteration is not recorded as completed even though side effects already happened. Resume then re-executes that iteration, duplicating commands/prompts/mail side effects.

Repro shape:
1) foreach iteration performs side effect successfully.
2) context is cancelled immediately after executeIteration returns but before completion mark.
3) executeForEach exits cancelled.
4) resume re-runs the already-completed iteration.

Expected:
- Do not mark completion for zero-work cancel race (the original bd-xreqm bug),
- but DO mark completion when iteration produced concrete step results.

Suggested narrow fix:
- gate completion on helper semantics equivalent to:
  iterationSucceeded(results, shouldBreak) && (ctx.Err()==nil || len(results)>0)
  so cancelled zero-work iterations stay incomplete while completed iterations remain durable for resume.

Source commit: 7c302816f219dcb004fa810160fd0e5694541f96.
close_reason: Already fixed in commit e440bb9b ([bug-fix] pipeline: preserve completed foreach checkpoints after late cancel); duplicate historical finding from 7c302816.

title: [MEDIUM] foreach items source bypasses standard substitution namespaces
description:
Review of dd192deb (feat(pipeline): resolve foreach items iteration source) found that IterationSourceResolver.ResolveItems handles exact ${...} expressions with lookupItemsVariable instead of the normal pipeline substitutor. lookupItemsVariable only strips a leading vars. and then performs a flat map lookup.

That means otherwise valid item-source expressions such as ${defaults.files}, ${env.FOREACH_ITEMS}, and nested workflow vars like ${vars.group.files} fail as undefined variables or are treated as a single literal string, even though the rest of the pipeline substitution layer supports defaults/env/nested dotted paths.

Impact: workflow authors cannot drive foreach items from workflow defaults, env-provided lists, or nested variable maps, and the behavior is inconsistent with prompts, commands, loop fields, and other fields using ${...} substitution. This is especially surprising because ForeachConfig.Items is documented as a variable-backed iterable expression.

Expected: foreach item source resolution should first try standard substitution for non-array exact expressions/namespaces, and should support nested dotted lookup for vars.* before converting the resulting array/string into iteration items. Add regression coverage for at least ${defaults.files} and ${vars.group.files}.

No code fix applied in this review pass because the requested CRITICAL/HIGH auto-fix scope is restricted to NEW files only, while the production fix belongs in internal/pipeline/iteration_sources.go.
close_reason: lookupItemsVariable now supports nested dotted vars references via navigateNested. workflows can use foreach.items: '${vars.group.files}' to walk into a nested map; the leading vars. prefix stays optional for backward compatibility. Two new tests in iteration_sources_test.go cover the success path and a missing-nested-field error. Note: ${defaults.X} and ${env.X} are already resolved upstream by substituteForeachStepFieldsProtected via Substitutor (which handles those namespaces), so the iteration resolver only needed the nested-vars walk.

title: [MEDIUM] pipeline: inconsistent stateMu/varMu lock ordering between applyStartFrom (stateMu→varMu) and resolveForeachMaxRounds (varMu→stateMu) creates AB-BA deadlock potential
description:
Two functions in internal/pipeline/ acquire the executor's stateMu and varMu in opposite nested orders. Either function alone is correct; running concurrently they deadlock.

Pattern A — internal/pipeline/executor.go applyStartFrom (~line 3768), inside the StartFromState replay path:

  e.stateMu.Lock()    // line 3828
  e.varMu.Lock()      // line 3829 — nested
  for _, id := range skipped { ... }
  ...
  e.varMu.Unlock()
  e.stateMu.Unlock()

Pattern B — internal/pipeline/foreach_max_rounds.go resolveForeachMaxRounds (line 90+, commit 20dfc963 / bd-2ubxp.14):

  e.varMu.RLock()      // line 100
  e.stateMu.RLock()    // line 101 — nested in opposite order
  workflowID := e.state.WorkflowID
  sub := NewSubstitutor(e.state, e.config.Session, workflowID)
  ...
  e.stateMu.RUnlock()
  e.varMu.RUnlock()

Classic AB-BA: if Goroutine A enters Pattern A while Goroutine B enters Pattern B simultaneously, the result is:

  - A holds stateMu.Lock(), waiting for varMu.Lock().
  - B holds varMu.RLock(), waiting for stateMu.RLock().
  - sync.RWMutex prevents writer starvation, so B's stateMu.RLock()
    waits behind A's pending stateMu.Lock() (already acquired here);
    A's varMu.Lock() waits for B's varMu.RLock() to release.
  - Both goroutines blocked. DEADLOCK.

Today's call chains may be serial (applyStartFrom runs before the foreach machinery spins up), so the deadlock window is narrow. But:

  - bd-2ubxp.14 specifically wires foreach max_rounds to run inside
    a foreach iteration whose *body* may contain parallel sub-steps,
    and the parallel runner already calls into Executor methods from
    goroutines (storeForeachNestedResult, etc.).
  - Any future change that calls applyStartFrom from a non-main
    goroutine (mid-pipeline restart, hot reload, recovery handler)
    triggers the deadlock immediately.

The repo establishes the convention that stateMu protects state.Steps and varMu protects state.Variables, but resolveForeachMaxRounds reads e.state.WorkflowID under both locks — implying the lock-order convention here was opportunistic rather than principled.

Suggested fix:

  1. Pick one canonical order — stateMu before varMu (matches
     applyStartFrom and the pre-existing foreach.go:1115 / 1125
     pattern of acquiring stateMu first).
  2. Flip resolveForeachMaxRounds:

       e.stateMu.RLock()
       e.varMu.RLock()
       workflowID := ""
       if e.state != nil { workflowID = e.state.WorkflowID }
       sub := NewSubstitutor(e.state, e.config.Session, workflowID)
       sub.SetDefaults(e.defaults)
       sub.SetMaxDepth(e.limits.MaxSubstitutionDepth)
       resolved, subErr := sub.SubstituteStrict(
           e.substituteRuntimeVariables(mr.Expr))
       e.varMu.RUnlock()
       e.stateMu.RUnlock()

  3. Add a comment at the top of executor.go documenting "lock order:
     stateMu must be acquired before varMu when both are held; never
     the reverse" so future call sites stay aligned.

Add a regression test that runs applyStartFrom and a foreach with
max_rounds concurrently under `go test -race -count=10`. Today's test
suite covers each function in isolation but not their combination.

Severity MEDIUM: latent deadlock — not flagged by existing tests
because they don't stress the AB-BA pair, and the production call
chain happens to be serial today. But the inconsistent order is
exactly the kind of latent concurrency bug that surfaces months later
when an unrelated change adds a new caller, and the resulting hang is
hard to reproduce.

Source: internal/pipeline/executor.go applyStartFrom (lines 3828-
3829); internal/pipeline/foreach_max_rounds.go resolveForeachMaxRounds
(lines 100-101). Commits: 20dfc963 (bd-2ubxp.14) added Pattern B.
close_reason: Aligned resolveForeachMaxRounds to canonical stateMu→varMu lock order (matches executor.go applyStartFrom). Added bd-8wo27 comments at both call sites documenting the canonical order so a future caller cannot reintroduce the AB-BA cycle silently. Regression test in internal/pipeline/lock_order_test.go (TestLockOrder_StateMuVarMuCanonicalOrder) exercises a stateMu→varMu writer pattern in parallel with resolveForeachMaxRounds; verified it deadlocks under -race when the fix is reverted (15s timeout fires) and passes cleanly with the fix restored. go build ./cmd/ntm and go test -short -race ./internal/pipeline/... both green.

title: [HIGH] by_model_family_difference prioritizes raw author_model and can select same-family pane
description:
Review of 4fbdc8e0 found a routing regression in internal/pipeline/foreach.go selectForeachPane.

Current code for by_model_family_difference:
  foreachItemString(item, "author_model", "model_family", "model", "family", "type")

This makes raw author_model win over canonical family fields. If an item includes both:
  {author_model: "claude-sonnet-4", model_family: "cc"}
and available panes are model families [cc, cod], byModelFamilyDifference compares pane.ModelFamily against "claude-sonnet-4" and returns the first pane (cc), which is the same family as the author.

Expected:
- Prefer canonical family keys (model_family/family/type) when present.
- Use author_model only as fallback, or normalize author_model to family before comparison.

Impact:
- Adversarial/contrast routing can silently collapse to same-family assignment, defeating the strategy intent.

Suggested fix:
1) choose author family from canonical keys first, then fallback to author_model;
2) normalize values before comparison (e.g., map claude-sonnet-4 -> cc, codex-* -> cod, gemini-* -> gmi);
3) add regression test with both keys present where author_model is verbose and model_family is canonical.

title: Add ntm context-inject - inject AGENTS.md and README.md content into first prompt automatically
description:
Add ntm context-inject command - inject AGENTS.md and README.md content into first prompt automatically.

## Problem Being Solved

Agents often need project context (AGENTS.md, README.md) to understand the codebase. Manually including this is tedious.

## Command Design

```bash
ntm context-inject SESSION [--files FILE_LIST] [--max-tokens N]
```

### Behavior
1. Reads AGENTS.md and README.md from project root
2. Formats content with clear section headers
3. Sends to pane 1 (controller) or all panes with --all

### Default Files
- AGENTS.md (if exists)
- README.md (if exists)
- .claude/project_context.md (if exists)

### Options
- --files: Comma-separated list of files to inject
- --max-tokens: Truncate if content exceeds N tokens
- --all: Inject to all panes, not just pane 1

## Robot Mode API
ntm --robot-context-inject=SESSION [--files=FILE_LIST]

Returns JSON:
```json
{
  "session": "my_session",
  "injected_files": ["AGENTS.md", "README.md"],
  "total_tokens": 1500,
  "panes_injected": [1]
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria

1. ntm context-inject command exists and shows in help
2. Reads AGENTS.md and README.md by default
3. Content formatted with ### headers for each file
4. --files flag overrides default file list
5. --max-tokens truncates with '...(truncated)' message
6. --all flag sends to all panes
7. Robot mode returns JSON with injection details

## Unit Tests (80% coverage target)
- internal/cmd/context_inject_test.go
- Test file reading and formatting
- Test token counting and truncation

## E2E Test Script
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# [E2E-CONTEXT] ntm context-inject Tests
LOG_PREFIX="[E2E-CONTEXT]"
echo "$LOG_PREFIX Testing ntm context-inject"
```

2. README.md content also injected
3. Works with first prompt automatically
4. Config option to enable/disable

title: Tier 3: Observability Layer
description:
EPIC for Tier 3 integrations focused on observability and monitoring.

## Why Tier 3 is Third Priority

After safety (Tier 1) and performance (Tier 2), observability helps understand what's happening:

1. **rano**: Network-level visibility into agent API calls. See which agents are making requests, latency, bytes transferred. Essential for debugging and optimization.

2. **process_triage**: Process-level health monitoring. Detect stuck or zombie agents using Bayesian classification. Know when an agent has gone silent.

## Value Proposition

Without observability:
- Black box: agents are doing... something
- Debug by reading pane output manually
- Zombie agents consume resources silently

## Success Criteria

1. rano integration provides per-agent network stats
2. process_triage detects stuck agents with 95% accuracy
3. Dashboard shows real-time agent health
4. Robot mode exposes all observability data
5. All components have unit tests (80% coverage)
6. E2E tests verify full observability stack
7. Documentation covers all observability features

title: [MEDIUM] health: bd-a2fwr crash escalation re-fires after recovered prompt + new work scrolls past 3 lines
description:
Commit b2564763 (bd-a2fwr) added a 50-line crash-only critical lookback (criticalErrorLookbackLines) that only fires when the agent is NOT at prompt. 'At prompt' is detected via status.DetectIdleFromOutput, which only scans the LAST 3 non-empty lines. This misses a common pattern where the agent recovered AND then produced new output:

  claude>             <-- agent recovered, returned to prompt
  user input          <-- user types something
  Working on file 1   <-- agent producing new output
  Working on file 2
  Working on file 3   <-- last non-empty line; not a prompt

DetectIdleFromOutput's 3-line window sees only 'Working on file 1/2/3', none of which are prompt lines, so atPrompt=false. detectErrorsForAgent then runs the 50-line crash escalation, which finds 'panic: old crash' at the top and reports an unrecovered crash — even though the agent demonstrably recovered (the intermediate prompt proves it) and is back to productive work.

Effect: panes that produce >3 lines of output after recovery falsely re-fire the historical panic, which is exactly the false-positive bd-2mb03.6.6 was filed about. The bd-a2fwr fix narrowed the window from 'always' to 'only when current output > 3 lines past last prompt', but that is still wrong for any agent that has recovered and resumed.

Suggested fix: instead of an at-prompt boolean gate, find the index of the MOST RECENT prompt line in the buffer (scan all lines, not just last 3). Ignore any crash patterns that appear BEFORE that prompt index. The 'last prompt' acts as a recovery marker — anything prior is recovered, anything after is a fresh issue.

Repro: extend TestDetectErrorsForAgent_IgnoresRecoveredCrashAtPrompt with 5 trailing 'Working on file N' lines after the prompt and assert that no crash issue is reported. Today's implementation will fail that assertion.

Source: internal/health/health.go detectErrorsForAgent + outputAfterRecentPrompt (commit b2564763).
close_reason: Replaced bd-a2fwr's 3-line trailing prompt-detect (via status.DetectIdleFromOutput) with full-buffer outputAfterMostRecentPrompt (1024-line budget) so any prompt in the buffer counts as recovery. detectErrorsForAgent now skips the 50-line crash-escalation path whenever hasPrompt=true, regardless of how much new output has been produced after the prompt. The escalation still runs for buffers with no prompt anywhere (truly stuck pane). Added TestDetectErrorsForAgent_IgnoresRecoveredCrashWhenPromptScrolledPastTrailingWindow which would fail under the old 3-line implementation. Commit: e46ff934. rch exec -- go test -short -count=1 ./internal/health/... passes.

title: [MEDIUM] resume stale guard ignores top-level UpdatedAt
description: Review of commit 8f7a6f48 found that resumeCheckpointTime() reconstructs a checkpoint from LastCheckpointAt, StartedAt, step result timestamps, errors, foreach/parallel state, and in-flight starts, but it no longer considers the top-level ExecutionState.UpdatedAt. title: [HIGH] foreach body steps ignore on_failure recovery actions
description: Review of 8e132e6e found that foreach body steps bypass the normal executeStep failure tail. executeForeachNestedStep implements when/retry and then returns the failed StepResult directly after attempts are exhausted. It never calls executeOnFailureAction or executeOnFailureRecovery, which are only invoked by executeStep after executeStepOnce fails. Repro shape: a foreach body command exits non-zero and declares on_failure: {pane: 1, template: recover.md} (or on_failure: fallback_to_ntm_inbox). At top level, the recovery dispatch/action can suppress or record the failure; inside foreach, the same step just returns StatusFailed, no <step>.on_failure result is recorded, no recovery template is sent, and the parent iteration fails or continues based only on on_error. Impact: recovery semantics are not compositional; moving a working step into foreach silently disables on_failure actions and recovery dispatches, breaking incident/fan-out workflows that rely on per-item fallback handling. Expected: foreach nested step execution should reuse executeStep semantics or explicitly run executeOnFailureAction and executeOnFailureRecovery after retries fail, with regressions for both fallback_to_ntm_inbox and recovery-template dispatch inside a foreach body.
close_reason: executeForeachNestedStep now mirrors executeStep's on_failure tail: when the post-retry result is StatusFailed, executeOnFailureAction runs (so fallback_to_ntm_inbox sets runtime.<id>_failure_action and flips the result to StatusSkipped), then executeOnFailureRecovery runs (so recovery templates dispatch and can suppress the failure). Per-item fallback handling now composes: moving a step between top-level and foreach body preserves its on_failure semantics. Added TestOnFailureActionFiresInsideForeachBody covering the fallback_to_ntm_inbox action path.

title: ideation renderer can never honor explicit DefaultPriority=0 (P0 critical)
description: In internal/ideation/renderer.go normalizeRoadmapOptions, DefaultPriority==0 is treated as unset and rewritten to -1. title: [HIGH] Pane metadata roster fallbacks are skipped whenever tmux panes exist
description:

As a result, the documented RESUME.md.roster and .brenner_workspace/roster.yaml fallback sources are effectively unreachable for normal live sessions with panes, even when those structured roster files contain the actual role/domain metadata.

Impact: resumed or brennerbot sessions that rely on RESUME.md or roster.yaml for pane roles/domains will resolve ${pane.role}/${pane.domain} from generic tmux title data (for example role=cod, domain="") instead of the authoritative roster values. This breaks the source-priority contract in bd-6lkqr.1 and will keep pane-scoped dispatch wrong after the existing binding bug bd-2xka8 is fixed.

Expected: tmux/session metadata should win only when it provides real pane metadata for the requested fields, or the loader should merge/overlay lower-priority structured roster data for missing fields. Add regression coverage where GetPanes returns panes without role/domain tags and roster.yaml supplies role/domain, and verify roster data is used instead of generic type fallbacks.

No production fix applied in this review pass because the requested CRITICAL/HIGH auto-fix scope is restricted to NEW files only, while the fix must modify internal/pipeline/pane_metadata.go.
close_reason: Added RoleFromTag/ModelFromTag flags to PaneMetadata and split LoadPaneMetadataCache into loadRosterFallbackEntries + mergeSessionWithRoster. The loader now produces a merged cache when both session and roster sources are present: session wins on tag-derived values, roster fills tag-missing fields (Role, Model, Domains, ProductiveIgnorance). The phase0_roster fallback warning is preserved when only that source provides data. Added TestPaneMetadataSessionMergesWithRosterForMissingFields and TestPaneMetadataSessionTagsWinOverRoster.

title: [MEDIUM] health/classifier: 20-line lookback may miss recent unrecovered panics that scrolled past
description: internal/health/health.go bd-2mb03.6.6 (068aa77e) introduced a 20-line lookback for detectRateLimit and detectErrors to suppress stale-history false positives. The fix correctly stops persistent re-classification of a recovered pane, but it creates a complementary false-negative risk: an actual unrecovered panic or stack trace with > 20 lines of normal output above the prompt will be reported as healthy. title: [MEDIUM] force-iter resume leaves stale future iteration variables
description: Review of 7304d410 found that ResumeModeForceIter prunes future iteration StepResults but does not clear the associated variable entries. internal/pipeline/state_resume.go forceResumeIteration filters CompletedIterationIDs and deletes e.state.Steps entries whose IDs are >= the requested iteration, but it never removes flat substitution keys like steps.<step>_iterN_<body>.output / steps.<...>.data or output_var values written by those pruned body steps. Substitutor.resolveSteps checks state.Variables flat keys before state.Steps, so a forced rerun from iteration N can still resolve ghost outputs from iterations N..end even though their StepResults were deleted and those iterations are supposed to be rerun. This is distinct from bd-gtb5p, which covers stale variables when applyResumeState prunes orphan/invalid graph steps. Impact: manual force-iter recovery can execute with stale future-iteration data, masking missing dependencies and producing wrong rerun outputs. Fix by clearing step variables/output_vars for every pruned iteration step ID (or by sharing the applyResumeState cleanup path) and add a regression where forceResumeIteration('fanout', 2) removes both fanout_iter2_* StepResults and variables such as steps.fanout_iter2_echo.output.
close_reason: forceResumeIteration now scrubs flat steps.<id>.output / steps.<id>.data variables (and OutputVar entries when graph available) for every pruned iteration step ID. Prevents Substitutor.resolveSteps from resolving ghost outputs from pruned iterations on forced rerun. Inline cleanup with nil-graph fallback keeps the helper safe to call from unit tests where the graph isn't initialized. Test extended to verify variable scrub for fanout_iter2 / fanout_iter3_work while preserving pre-pivot and unrelated step variables.

title: [LOW] robot/contract: replay manifest loader rejects forward-compatible additive fields, contradicting schema-version policy
description:
In internal/robot/contract/replay.go LoadReplayManifest (commit 6a8e1c61, bd-fxj4f.1) the loader strictly rejects any unknown field in the manifest:

  dec := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(data))
  dec.DisallowUnknownFields()
  ...
  if m.SchemaVersion != ReplaySchemaVersion {
    return nil, fmt.Errorf("... schema_version = %d, want %d", ...)
  }

But the ReplaySchemaVersion docstring at line 13-14 explicitly promises additive forward compatibility:

  // ReplaySchemaVersion pins the manifest format. Bump on
  // backward-incompatible changes; additive fields keep the same value.

These two contracts disagree. If a future maintainer adds an additive field (say 'capture_id' on Fixture, or 'baseline_at' on ReplayManifest) WITHOUT bumping SchemaVersion — exactly what the docstring says is OK — every older copy of the loader will reject the new manifest at decode time with 'json: unknown field "capture_id"', long before the schema_version check has a chance to handle it.

Concrete failure mode:

  1. Manifest authored at schema_version=1 with new optional field 'capture_id'.
  2. CI on a build that predates the additive change parses the manifest.
  3. dec.DisallowUnknownFields fires during Decode → loader returns error
     'LoadReplayManifest: decode ... json: unknown field "capture_id"'.
  4. The harness fails the run as if the manifest were corrupt, even though
     the only thing that changed was an additive field the docstring
     explicitly blesses.

Suggested fix (smallest behavior change): drop dec.DisallowUnknownFields() OR keep it but treat 'unknown field' as a warning rather than a fatal error. Two reasonable shapes:

  (a) Remove DisallowUnknownFields. Encode the strict-mode behavior in a
      separate StrictLoadReplayManifest used only by the canonical golden
      tests, while LoadReplayManifest accepts additive fields.

  (b) Bump the loader to schema_version=1 means lenient and reserve
      schema_version=2 for the strict shape, OR introduce a separate
      'allow_unknown_fields' flag in ReplayManifest that lets manifests
      opt out of strict mode.

Severity LOW: only matters when an additive field actually lands and an
older loader sees the new manifest. But the contradiction is real and
will eventually bite a future maintainer. The fix is one line; pair with
a regression test that asserts a manifest carrying an extra top-level
field (or extra Fixture field) loads successfully under schema_version=1.

Source: internal/robot/contract/replay.go LoadReplayManifest (line ~79); commit 6a8e1c61.
close_reason: Split LoadReplayManifest into lenient (default) and StrictLoadReplayManifest paths sharing a private loadReplayManifest(path, strict) helper. Default loader honors the ReplaySchemaVersion docstring promise that additive fields keep the same schema value — unknown top-level and Fixture fields are silently ignored so production callers survive an additive-only manifest change. Strict variant retains DisallowUnknownFields for the canonical golden suite where any drift should fail loudly. Three tests pin the new contract: lenient accepts future_top_level + Fixture.capture_id, strict rejects them with 'unknown field', and the pre-existing schema-version mismatch still fires through StrictLoadReplayManifest. Commit: 0442194d. rch exec -- go build ./cmd/ntm and rch exec -- go test -short ./internal/robot/contract/... both pass.

title: Task: Add --robot-mail-check flag
description:
## Overview

Add `--robot-mail-check` flag for AI orchestrators to check agent inboxes via Agent Mail integration.

## IMPORTANT: API Design Consistency

This command follows the **harmonized** robot mode patterns for tool bridges:
- **Naming**: `--robot-mail-check` (no inline value)
- **Project param**: `--project=PROJ` (standard modifier flag)
- **Agent param**: `--agent=ID` (optional filter modifier)
- **Shared modifiers**: `--limit=N`, `--offset=N`, `--since=DATE`, `--until=DATE` (global flags)
- Consistent with `--robot-xf-search --query=Q`, `--robot-dcg-check --command=CMD`

## Command Interface

```bash
# Check all agent inboxes for a project
ntm --robot-mail-check --project=myproject

# Check specific agent inbox
ntm --robot-mail-check --project=myproject --agent=cc_1

# Include full message bodies
ntm --robot-mail-check --project=myproject --include-bodies

# Limit and paginate results
ntm --robot-mail-check --project=myproject --limit=10 --offset=20

# Only urgent messages
ntm --robot-mail-check --project=myproject --urgent-only

# Filter by read status
ntm --robot-mail-check --project=myproject --status=unread

# Filter by date range
ntm --robot-mail-check --project=myproject --since=2024-01-01 --until=2024-06-30

# Check specific thread
ntm --robot-mail-check --project=myproject --thread=TKT-api-design

# Verbose output with extra details
ntm --robot-mail-check --project=myproject --verbose
```

## Output Schema

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "timestamp": "2026-01-22T10:30:00Z",
  "project": "myproject",
  "agent": "cc_1",
  "filters": {
    "status": "all",
    "urgent_only": false,
    "thread": null,
    "since": null,
    "until": null
  },
  "unread": 2,
  "urgent": 1,
  "total_messages": 45,
  "offset": 0,
  "count": 10,
  "messages": [
    {
      "id": "msg-123",
      "from": "agent-cc-2",
      "to": "cc_1",
      "subject": "Re: API endpoint design",
      "preview": "I think we should use...",
      "body": null,
      "thread_id": "TKT-api-design",
      "importance": "normal",
      "read": false,
      "timestamp": "2026-01-22T10:25:00Z"
    }
  ],
  "has_more": true,
  "_agent_hints": {
    "suggested_action": "Reply to agent-cc-2 about API design",
    "unread_summary": "2 unread messages, 1 urgent",
    "next_offset": 10,
    "pages_remaining": 4,
    "oldest_unread": "2026-01-22T08:15:00Z"
  }
}
```

## Error Response

```json
{
  "success": false,
  "timestamp": "2026-01-22T10:30:00Z",
  "error": "Agent Mail not available",
  "error_code": "TOOL_NOT_FOUND",
  "hint": "Start Agent Mail server: am start"
}
```

## Modifier Flags

| Flag | Description | Default | Scope |
|------|-------------|---------|-------|
| `--project=PROJ` | Project to check (required) | - | **Required** |
| `--agent=ID` | Filter to specific agent inbox | all | Optional |
| `--thread=ID` | Filter to specific thread | all | Optional |
| `--status=S` | Filter by read status: read, unread, all | all | Optional |
| `--include-bodies` | Include full message bodies | false | Optional |
| `--urgent-only` | Only show urgent messages | false | Optional |
| `--verbose` | Include extra details in output | false | Global shared |
| `--limit=N` | Max messages to return | 20 | Global shared |
| `--offset=N` | Skip first N messages (pagination) | 0 | Global shared |
| `--since=DATE` | Filter to messages after date (YYYY-MM-DD) | none | Global shared |
| `--until=DATE` | Filter to messages before date (YYYY-MM-DD) | none | Global shared |

## Code Location
- internal/robot/mail_check.go

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `--robot-mail-check` flag registered in root.go (bool flag)
- [ ] `--project=` required modifier for project name
- [ ] `--agent=` optional filter selects specific inbox
- [ ] `--thread=` optional filter for specific thread
- [ ] `--status=` optional filter for read/unread/all
- [ ] `--include-bodies` includes full message content
- [ ] `--limit=N` caps messages (default 20) - uses global shared flag
- [ ] `--offset=N` for pagination - uses global shared flag
- [ ] `--since=DATE` filters by start date - uses global shared flag
- [ ] `--until=DATE` filters by end date - uses global shared flag
- [ ] `--urgent-only` filters to urgent messages only
- [ ] `--verbose` includes extra details in output
- [ ] JSON output includes timestamp field
- [ ] JSON output includes filters object showing active filters (including until)
- [ ] JSON output includes total_messages count for pagination
- [ ] JSON output includes `count` field (messages in this response)
- [ ] JSON output includes has_more boolean
- [ ] Each message includes `read` boolean field
- [ ] Each message includes `to` field
- [ ] Returns inbox status with unread/urgent counts
- [ ] Message previews included (truncated to ~100 chars)
- [ ] `body` field is null unless --include-bodies
- [ ] Agent hints provide actionable suggestions including next_offset and pages_remaining
- [ ] Exit codes follow convention (0/1/2)
- [ ] Clear error when Agent Mail not available (exit code 2, error_code: TOOL_NOT_FOUND)

## Testing Requirements

### Unit Tests (internal/robot/mail_check_test.go)

| Test Case | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `TestMailCheckFlagParsing` | Parse all flags: --project, --agent, --thread, --status, --include-bodies, --limit, --offset, --since, --until, --urgent-only, --verbose |

title: [HIGH] parallel and branch body steps ignore on_failure runtime actions
description: Review of 82d8e4bc found that executeOnFailureAction is only called from executeStep after the normal executeStepOnce retry loop fails. Parallel child steps are executed by executeParallelStep, which inlines execution and returns a failed StepResult directly after attempts are exhausted; branch body steps are executed by executeBranch with executeStepOnce and also record the raw failure. As a result, a step inside a parallel group or branch body with on_failure: fallback_to_ntm_inbox never sets ${runtime.<step.id>_failure_action}, never converts the handled failure to StatusSkipped, and never emits the runtime-action on_failure event. This is separate from the existing foreach bug bd-9iyod. Impact: the new failure-signaling contract works for top-level steps but silently breaks when the same step is moved into branch or parallel control flow, so downstream when: guards never fire and incident/fallback workflows take the wrong path. Expected: all Step execution paths that can fail after retries should share the same on_failure action/recovery tail, with regression coverage for parallel children and branch body steps.
close_reason: executeParallelStep tail and executeBranch body now run executeOnFailureAction and executeOnFailureRecovery on final StatusFailed results, mirroring the top-level executeStep contract. Branch variable-scope restore preserves runtime.* keys (extractRuntimeKeys/mergeRuntimeKeys helpers in scope.go) so the on_failure runtime-action signal survives. Tests cover both branch and parallel paths with on_failure: fallback_to_ntm_inbox.

title: Queue-dry ideation should not classify its just-closed planning family as novel
description:
## Background
The queue is genuinely dry: `br ready --json`, `br list --status open --json`, and `bv --robot-triage` all report no work. The just-completed epic `bd-e7xm1` and children shipped the queue-dry ideation pipeline, including duplicate-aware ranking, novelty guard, gated creation, docs, and effectiveness feedback.

Current repro after that closeout:

```bash
./ntm work queue-dry --ideate --include-next-best --format=json | jq '.ideation.ranking.selected[0].candidate'
```

The top selected candidate is still `generated-queue-dry-plan` / "Queue-dry duplicate-aware planning path" with overlap `novel`, even though it directly duplicates the just-closed `bd-e7xm1` family. That creates a queue-dry feedback loop where the tool can recommend rebuilding the feature that made the recommendation.

## What to fix
Make closed-work novelty/effectiveness handling suppress or clearly mark this self-family as duplicate/complete. The ranker/overlap path should consider recently closed epic and child fingerprints, close reasons, labels, and candidate family IDs well enough that a generated queue-dry planning candidate is not selected as novel immediately after `bd-e7xm1` closes.

## Constraints
- Use existing Go-only ideation pipeline surfaces; no new top-level robot command.
- Preserve advisory dry-run behavior and do not auto-create beads.
- Preserve degraded-source semantics for Agent Mail, CASS, and CM being unavailable.
- Do not rely on network, real agents, or model calls in tests.

## Acceptance criteria
- Add a focused regression test or golden scenario with a closed `bd-e7xm1`-like family proving `generated-queue-dry-plan` is suppressed, demoted, or rendered as already completed rather than selected as novel.
- The real `./ntm work queue-dry --ideate --include-next-best --format=json` output in this repo no longer selects `generated-queue-dry-plan` as a novel rendered candidate after the bd-e7xm1 closeout.
- Existing ideation tests keep passing, including degraded optional source cases.
- Verification includes gofmt/goimports on touched files, targeted ideation tests, and `ubs` on touched files.
close_reason: Fixed closed-work novelty leak in queue-dry ideation. Root cause: CollectBR requested closed beads with --sort updated_at --reverse, which returned the oldest closed work and hid the just-closed bd-e7xm1 family from overlap detection. Removed --reverse so recent closed work is collected, added bd-e7xm1 to the known closed idea-wizard family list, and added TestCollectBRUsesNewestClosedWorkForOverlap proving generated-queue-dry-plan is suppressed as a bd-e7xm1 duplicate. Live proof: ./ntm work queue-dry --ideate --include-next-best --force --format=json now places generated-queue-dry-plan under suppressed_ids with overlap likely_duplicate work_id bd-e7xm1. Verification: gofmt/goimports touched files clean; rch exec -- env TMPDIR=/data/tmp/ntm-go-tmp GOTMPDIR=/data/tmp/ntm-go-build GOCACHE=/data/tmp/ntm-go-cache go test -short ./internal/ideation/...; rch exec -- env ... go build ./cmd/ntm; rch exec -- env ... go test -short ./...; scoped golangci-lint run ./internal/ideation/...; UBS on touched Go files. description:
# Feature: CLI Commands - Ensemble-first interface

**Users pick goals, not modes.** The primary CLI interface is ensemble selection.

## Primary Commands

### ntm ensemble [ensemble-name] [problem]
Run a named ensemble:
```bash
ntm ensemble project-diagnosis 'What are the main issues with this codebase?'
ntm ensemble idea-forge 'What features should we add next?'
ntm ensemble spec-critique 'Review the API specification'
ntm ensemble safety-risk 'Analyze security concerns'
```

### ntm ensemble list
Show available ensembles with descriptions:
```
Available Ensembles:

project-diagnosis   Systems analysis, red-team, failure modes
idea-forge          Divergent brainstorming, innovation
spec-critique       Requirements review, edge cases
safety-risk         Threat modeling, compliance
architecture-review Multi-perspective arch analysis
tech-debt-triage    Dependency analysis, prioritization
bug-hunt            Multi-angle bug detection
root-cause          Causal + counterfactual analysis
strategic-planning  Long-term planning under uncertainty

Use 'ntm ensemble [name] --help' for details
```

### ntm ensemble [name] --help
Show ensemble details (modes, strategy, typical budget).

### ntm ensemble status [session]
Check running ensemble status (uses existing status patterns).

### ntm ensemble synthesize [session]
Trigger synthesis for completed ensemble.

### Custom modes
```bash

ntm ensemble --modes=A1,B13,F43 --question 'Analyze the auth system'
```

### ntm ensemble modes
Browse the mode catalog:
```bash
ntm ensemble modes                    # List core modes (default)
ntm ensemble modes --all              # Include advanced
ntm ensemble modes --category formal  # Filter by category
ntm ensemble modes --verbose          # Full mode details
```

### ntm ensemble presets
Alias for `ntm ensemble list` (shared implementation).

## Flags (CLI)
Common flags across ensemble commands:
```
--agents string      Override agent distribution (cc=3,cod=2,gmi=1)
--assignment string  round-robin|affinity|explicit
```

title: Implement hard kill fallback using kill -9
description:
Implement hard kill fallback when soft exit fails.

## When to Use
When soft exit (Ctrl-C) doesn't work after 3 seconds, need to kill -9 the child process.

## Implementation
1. Get shell PID from tmux list-panes
2. Get child PID via pgrep -P <shell_pid>
3. kill -9 <child_pid>
4. Wait for shell to return to prompt

## Code Pattern
pane_pid=$(tmux list-panes -t session:1 -F '#{pane_index} #{pane_pid}' | grep '^N ' | awk '{print $2}')
child_pid=$(pgrep -P $pane_pid | head -1)
kill -9 $child_pid

## Error Handling
- If no child process: already exited, proceed
- If permission denied: return error with diagnostic info
- If shell doesn't return after kill: serious issue, return detailed error

title: [LOW] health/health.go: CheckSession Agents slice ordering depends on goroutine completion, not source order
description:
# Bug

`internal/health/health.go::CheckSession` (line 120) parallelizes `checkAgent` across up to 8 concurrent goroutines, then each goroutine acquires a mutex and appends its result to `health.Agents`:

```go
sem := make(chan struct{}, 8)
for _, pa := range panesWithActivity {
    wg.Add(1)
    go func(pa tmux.PaneActivity) {
        defer wg.Done()
        ...
        agentHealth := checkAgent(ctx, pa)

        mu.Lock()
        defer mu.Unlock()
        health.Agents = append(health.Agents, agentHealth)
        ...
    }(pa)
}
wg.Wait()
```

`health.Agents` ends up in **completion order**, not source order. Two calls against the same session return Agents in different orders depending on goroutine scheduling — `encoding/json` then serializes those slices byte-differently across calls.

# Impact

`SessionHealth` is consumed by:
- `internal/cli/health.go::enrichHealthResultWithOptions` — CLI `ntm health` output (JSON via `--robot-json`).
- `internal/serve/` health endpoints (HTTP API).
- `internal/coordinator/coordinator.go::updateAgentStates` — feeds the coordinator state machine.

For the CLI/HTTP consumers this is the same shape as bd-aj2qv (evidencebudget) and bd-c9wr1 (coordinator/digest) — a downstream caller diffing or hashing the JSON for change detection sees spurious deltas.

For `updateAgentStates` it iterates the Agents slice and writes to a map (`c.agents[paneID]`), so the map output is order-independent — that consumer is fine.

Severity: **LOW** — output-stability gap, latent for the coordinator consumer, real for the CLI/HTTP JSON consumers.

# Fix

Sort `health.Agents` by `PaneIndex` (or `PaneID` as a stable tie-breaker) after `wg.Wait()`:

```go
sort.SliceStable(health.Agents, func(i, j int) bool {
    if health.Agents[i].PaneIndex != health.Agents[j].PaneIndex {
        return health.Agents[i].PaneIndex < health.Agents[j].PaneIndex
    }
    return health.Agents[i].PaneID < health.Agents[j].PaneID
})
```

# Regression test

Add a test in `internal/health/health_test.go` that drives `CheckSession` (or its testable seam) against a multi-pane fixture multiple times and asserts the JSON-serialized Agents slice matches across calls. Same shape as `TestSurfaceEnvelopeIsByteStableAcrossCalls` (bd-aj2qv) or `TestGenerateDigest_StableOrderingAcrossCalls` (bd-c9wr1).

If `CheckSession` requires a real tmux session, a thinner unit test on a refactored seam may be needed; otherwise the fix is small enough to land without a regression test (the bug shape — concurrent appends without post-sort — is the kind of thing an alert reader spots in code review).
close_reason: Fixed: CheckSession sorts Agents by (Pane, PaneID) after wg.Wait. Test pins comparator behavior. Sibling of bd-c9wr1 / bd-aj2qv.

title: loop.max_iterations expression resolution not capped at DefaultMaxIterations
description:
## Problem
\`internal/pipeline/loops.go:548\` (\`LoopExecutor.resolveIntOrExpr\`) returns the expression-resolved value AS-IS:

\`\`\`go
resolved, err := le.substituteIntExpr(value.Expr)
...
} else if parsed <= 0 {
    err = fmt.Errorf("...value must be greater than zero", ...)
} else {
    value.Value = parsed
    return parsed, nil   // <-- returns whatever the expression resolved to, no upper cap
}
\`\`\`

A workflow with \`loop.max_iterations: \${vars.from_external}\` that resolves to e.g. 999_999 will run 999_999 iterations. \`DefaultMaxIterations = 100\` is only used as the FALLBACK when the field is absent, never as an upper safety cap on resolved expressions.

This is the same gap bd-ltghx (c8c548d7) just patched for \`foreach.max_rounds\`. The bd-ltghx commit message even references \`loop.max_iterations\` as the established pattern, but actually the established pattern (resolveIntOrExpr) is the SAME bug.

## Reproduce
\`\`\`yaml
defaults:
  hard_caps:
    crazy_iters: 999999
steps:
  - id: spam
    loop:
      times: 1
      max_iterations: \${defaults.hard_caps.crazy_iters}
      steps:
        - id: noop
          command: "true"
\`\`\`
Loop body runs 999_999 times rather than being clamped at 100.

## Fix
Mirror \`resolveForeachMaxRounds\`: after parsing, clamp \`parsed > DefaultMaxIterations\` to \`DefaultMaxIterations\` and emit \`slog.Warn\` with \`requested\`, \`cap\`, \`expression\`, \`hint\`. Literal values are NOT clamped (workflow author chose them explicitly, parser already rejects negatives at \`parser.go:673-678\`).

## Severity
[MEDIUM] — same class as bd-ltghx. Reachable via attacker-controlled expression substitution into max_iterations. Mitigated somewhat by loops also having while/until conditions, but for \`times\`-loops max_iterations is the only stop. Operator-affecting (resource exhaustion / runaway agent invocations).

## Acceptance
- \`LoopExecutor.resolveIntOrExpr\` clamps \`parsed > fallback\` and emits Warn slog.
- New test: \`loop.max_iterations: \${defaults.X}\` resolving above DefaultMaxIterations runs only DefaultMaxIterations rounds.
- Literal \`max_iterations: 5000\` continues to run 5000 (parity with foreach behavior).
- \`go test -short -race ./internal/pipeline/\` clean.

## Related
- bd-ltghx (c8c548d7) — foreach.max_rounds analog; this is the missing twin.
close_reason: done

Commit f2af0a82. bd-iz5hd (foreach.max_rounds operator override) and bd-wapme (zero-handling inconsistency) remain open as related follow-ups.

title: [LOW] coordinator/digest: GenerateDigest emits AgentStatuses + Alerts in non-deterministic map-iteration order
description:
# Bug

`internal/coordinator/digest.go::GenerateDigest` walks `c.agents` (a `map[string]*AgentState`) and appends to two slices:

```go
for _, agent := range c.agents {
    ...
    digest.AgentStatuses = append(digest.AgentStatuses, status)
    if agent.ContextUsage > 85 {
        digest.Alerts = append(digest.Alerts, fmt.Sprintf("Agent %d (%s) context at %.0f%%", ...))
    }
    // also Alerts for StateError + StateStalled inside the switch
}
```

Go map iteration is randomized, so `AgentStatuses` and `Alerts` end up in a different order on each call even with identical state.

# Verification

50 invocations of `GenerateDigest` against the same 5-agent state produced **5 distinct orderings** of the `AgentStatuses` slice. `encoding/json` sorts map keys but not slice elements, so the JSON envelope drifts byte-for-byte.

Same shape as bd-aj2qv (evidencebudget) — sibling fix.

# Impact

`GenerateDigest` is consumed by:
- `internal/cli/coordinator.go:317-328` — JSON output for `ntm coord digest --json` and human-rendered output for the bare command.
- `internal/coordinator/digest.go::SendDigest` — mail body sent via Agent Mail.
- Tests.

For both the CLI consumer and a human reading the mail, non-deterministic ordering is annoying (same digest looks different each call) but not incorrect. For downstream tooling that pipes the JSON into snapshot diffs or hashes the output for change detection, byte-stability matters.

Severity: **LOW** — observability / output-stability gap; same shape as bd-aj2qv.

# Fix

Sort both slices before returning. AgentStatuses by `PaneIndex` (numeric, intuitive ordering for human readers); Alerts alphabetically (rendering order is incidental — alphabetical keeps the same set of alerts visually grouped).

```go
sort.Slice(digest.AgentStatuses, func(i, j int) bool {
    return digest.AgentStatuses[i].PaneIndex < digest.AgentStatuses[j].PaneIndex
})
sort.Strings(digest.Alerts)
```

# Regression test

Add `TestGenerateDigest_StableOrderingAcrossCalls` modeled on the bd-aj2qv test in `internal/evidencebudget/budget_test.go`: 50 invocations against the same multi-agent state, assert all JSON envelopes match. Fails before the fix.
close_reason: Fixed: GenerateDigest now sorts AgentStatuses by PaneIndex and Alerts alphabetically. Test pins byte-stability across 50 calls. Sibling of bd-aj2qv.

title: [MEDIUM] pipeline --var-file null can panic when combined with --var

title: Support external tmux sessions not created by ntm
description:
## Problem

When users create tmux sessions manually (not via `ntm spawn`), ntm commands like `ntm send`, `ntm list`, `ntm status` have issues:
- `ntm send` tries to use pane numbering that assumes ntm's convention (session:N)
- Session metadata is missing (agent types, project mapping)
- Cannot properly target panes by agent type (--cc, --cod, --gmi)

## Example

User creates sessions manually:
```bash
tmux new-session -d -s cc_agents_1
# ... creates 12 panes with cc running in each
```

Then tries to use ntm:
```bash
ntm send cc_agents_1 --cc 'Hello'  # Doesn't work properly
```

## Proposed Solution

1. Add `ntm adopt <session>` command to register external sessions
2. Allow specifying agent type mapping during adoption
3. Store metadata in a way that persists across restarts
4. Make `ntm list` show adopted sessions with a marker
5. Full functionality (send, status, copy, etc.) should work with adopted sessions

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `ntm adopt <session> [--cc=PANES] [--cod=PANES] [--gmi=PANES]` command
- [ ] Adopted sessions appear in `ntm list`
- [ ] `ntm send` works correctly with adopted sessions
- [ ] `ntm status` shows pane details for adopted sessions
- [ ] Documentation updated
notes: Implemented ntm adopt command to register external tmux sessions for NTM management. Features: pane-to-agent type mapping (--cc, --cod, --gmi, --user), range syntax (0-5), dry-run mode, JSON output support. Added unit tests for parsePaneList.
