title: bd-7ramj.1 sibling: notifyMacOS uses unbounded exec.Command, can hang pipeline thread
description:
## Summary

bd-7ramj.1 (b680154b) wrapped \`notifyLinux\` in a 2-second
\`context.WithTimeout\`-bounded \`exec.CommandContext\` so the pipeline
thread couldn't be wedged by a hung \`notify-send\` (e.g. minimal cloud
VMs without dbus/libnotify, a wedged notification daemon). The macOS
sibling at \`internal/pipeline/notify.go:169\` is still bare
\`exec.Command\`:

\`\`\`go
func notifyMacOS(title, body string) error {
    script := fmt.Sprintf(\`display notification %q with title %q\`, body, title)
    cmd := exec.Command("osascript", "-e", script)
    return cmd.Run()
}
\`\`\`

\`osascript\` can block indefinitely under several real-world conditions:

- A modal Apple permission dialog (e.g. the first time a binary tries to
  post a notification or use the System Events bridge) — \`osascript\`
  waits on the dialog response with no caller-side timeout.
- A wedged or terminating \`launchd\` / \`NotificationCenter\` agent (less
  common than Linux's notify-send hangs but documented in Apple
  developer threads).
- Sandbox / TCC interactions that pause the script while authorization is
  evaluated.

Same failure mode bd-7ramj.1 closes for Linux: the pipeline thread
blocks on the OS-level notification call, and there's no caller-side
deadline.

## Severity

P3 — same severity as the Linux fix. macOS users are less likely to
hit it (Apple's notification stack is more reliable than Linux's
optional dbus chain), but the symptom is identical: \`pipeline run\`
freezes mid-step on a side-effect that doesn't matter to the
workflow.

## Suggested fix

Mirror the Linux pattern verbatim:

\`\`\`go
func notifyMacOS(title, body string) error {
    ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
    defer cancel()
    script := fmt.Sprintf(\`display notification %q with title %q\`, body, title)
    cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "osascript", "-e", script)
    return cmd.Run()
}
\`\`\`

The 2 s ceiling matches notifyLinux. \`osascript\` will return
\`ETIMEDOUT\` (via the killed-cmd error path) and the caller's existing
log-and-continue contract still holds.

## Acceptance

- A unit test that swaps \`exec.LookPath\` or invokes notifyMacOS with a
  simulated long-running script and asserts the call returns within
  ~2.1 s with a non-nil error. (Test runs only on darwin via
  \`runtime.GOOS\` gate; Linux/Windows skip.)
- \`grep -n "exec.Command(" internal/pipeline/notify.go\` should be empty
  for any line whose enclosing function does not also wrap a
  context-with-timeout — locks the parity contract.

## Files

- internal/pipeline/notify.go (notifyMacOS — line ~169)
- internal/pipeline/notify_test.go (regression test if a darwin test
  file exists; otherwise the existing test scaffold needs a
  GOOS-gated case).

## Related

- bd-7ramj.1 (b680154b) — original fix for Linux notify-send.
- 385132f2 — companion supervisor procattr_windows fix; the commit
  message describes the Linux notify-send fix landing alongside the
  Windows process-group fix, but the diff only contains the supervisor
  change. The Linux fix actually landed separately in b680154b. Same
  unmodified macOS path remains in both. (Cosmetic commit-message
  hygiene issue, not a defect — flagging here for context.)
close_reason: notifyMacOS now wraps osascript in a 2 s context.WithTimeout-bounded exec.CommandContext, mirroring bd-7ramj.1's notifyLinux pattern verbatim. Test TestNotifyMacOS_BoundedByContextTimeout overrides PATH with a sleep-30 osascript stub and asserts notifyMacOS returns within 5 s (2 s ceiling + CI slack); skips on Windows where the PATH-stub approach doesn't apply cleanly. Pipeline -race -short clean in fresh HEAD worktree at 28.795 s. Commit a27a1f17.

title: [MEDIUM] conflicting parallel output_var_mode values are silently ignored
description:
Review of 0c8151b0 found that colliding inline parallel substeps can declare different output_var_mode values for the same output_var and validation accepts the workflow without warning. storeParallelOutputVars calls parallelGroupOutputVarMode, which returns the first non-empty mode among the colliding steps and silently ignores any later conflicting modes.

Reproducer shape:

  parallel:
    - id: left
      prompt: left
      output_var: shared
      output_var_mode: collect
    - id: right
      prompt: right
      output_var: shared
      output_var_mode: last

Current behavior: Validate emits only the duplicate-output warning and execution uses whichever non-empty mode appears first in declaration order. Swapping the two substeps changes the storage shape between map/string/list semantics even though both substeps still claim the same shared output variable.

Expected behavior: a colliding output_var group should have one unambiguous effective mode. Validation should either reject conflicting non-empty modes on the same output_var group or emit a clear warning and require the mode to be set on the parent/group instead of silently discarding later values.

Impact: pipeline authors can believe a substep-specific mode is active when it is ignored, causing downstream variable substitutions to observe a different type or value than configured. This is separate from bd-ijryv, which covers foreach output_var_mode being ignored entirely, and bd-i3eah, which covers aggregate mode dropping failed/cancelled slots.

Source commit: 0c8151b0 feat(pipeline): aggregate colliding output vars (bd-mepnp)

title: Concurrency-safety contract for parallel + foreach + nested executions (cross-cutting)
description:
## Background

Phase B introduces multiple concurrency scenarios:

1. `parallel: [<step>, ...]` — N inline steps run concurrently in goroutines.
2. `foreach: ... parallel: true` — N iterations run concurrently.
3. `nested foreach + parallel:true` — combinatorial concurrency.
4. `post_pipeline_steps: ` running sequentially while main steps may still be wrapping up.

Each goroutine touches:
- `Executor.state` (StepResult map per step ID)
- `Executor.state.Variables` (workflow + scope vars)
- `Executor.graph` (dependency-graph state)
- The slog logger (slog handlers are concurrency-safe IF the underlying Handler is)

## Spec

Establish + enforce these contracts:

### Executor.state mutex
- All reads/writes to `state.Steps` map go through `e.stateMu` (already exists in Phase A executor).
- `state.Variables` map already has its own `varMu`.
- Verify NO field in ExecutionState is mutated without holding the appropriate mutex.

### Variable scope stack
- The scope stack (E7) is per-iteration (inside foreach goroutine) — each goroutine gets its OWN scope stack copy.
- The OUTER (workflow-global) Variables map is shared but mutex-protected.
- Document: scope frames are GOROUTINE-LOCAL; workflow vars are SHARED + locked.

### foreach iteration goroutines
- Each goroutine takes ownership of its iteration's loop variable.
- The goroutines do NOT share a single mutable Step struct — each gets a deep-copy via copyStep().
- StepResults from each iteration go through `stateMu` to the parent foreach's aggregated result.

### Race-detector tests
- `go test -race ./internal/pipeline/...` must pass.
- Add specifically targeted tests in `concurrency_test.go` that hammer:
  - 50-item foreach with parallel:true and max_concurrent=8
  - parallel:[10 inline steps]
  - Nested foreach with parallel at both levels
  - Mixed parallel + sequential within the same workflow

### Documentation
- Add a §Concurrency section to PIPELINES.md documenting the contract.
- Document that custom output_parse functions (Pattern: regex etc.) MUST be pure / re-entrant.

## Acceptance
- `go test -race ./internal/pipeline/...` passes.
- All concurrency_test.go scenarios above pass under -race.
- Documentation reflects the actual behavior.

## Files
- internal/pipeline/executor.go — audit all state.* mutations for mutex coverage
- internal/pipeline/foreach.go — deep-copy steps before per-iteration goroutines
- internal/pipeline/concurrency_test.go — NEW; race-targeted scenarios
- /home/ubuntu/.claude/skills/ntm/references/PIPELINES.md — add §Concurrency
design: Consolidated file plan: extend existing implementation files unless the concern is one of bd-z5lv3's justified modules. Shared concurrency/race tests may live in internal/pipeline/concurrency_test.go; resource-limit tests should prefer existing executor/foreach/schema test files unless a dedicated limits_test.go is justified by size. Documentation must be repo-local (for example references/ or docs/); do not edit ~/.claude or ~/.codex paths from a bead file list.

title: [MEDIUM] plugins/sdk: AdapterRegistry.Register adds plugin to map before Init completes — concurrent Get/List/Shutdown can observe and invoke a plugin that has not finished Init
description:
In internal/plugins/sdk.go AdapterRegistry.Register (commit d4971f66, bd-2mb03.6.7), the plugin is inserted into r.plugins under the registry lock, the lock is released, and only THEN is Plugin.Init invoked:

  r.mu.Lock()
  if _, ok := r.plugins[name]; ok {
      r.mu.Unlock()
      return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", ErrPluginAlreadyRegistered, name)
  }
  r.plugins[name] = p          // <-- visible to other goroutines
  r.mu.Unlock()

  if err := p.Init(r.hostCtx); err != nil {
      r.mu.Lock()
      delete(r.plugins, name)  // <-- rollback
      r.mu.Unlock()
      return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: %v", ErrPluginInitFailed, name, err)
  }
  return nil

This pattern violates the documented Plugin contract:

  // Implementations must be safe to call from multiple goroutines
  // after Init returns nil.

So before Init returns, the plugin is NOT safe to invoke. But during the window between r.mu.Unlock() and p.Init() returning, the plugin is observable via:

  - Get(name) → returns the plugin even though Init may not have run.
  - List() → includes the plugin in the deterministic snapshot.
  - FindByCapability(cap) → matches on Capabilities() (which Init may not yet have set up state for) and returns the plugin.
  - Shutdown() → iterates r.plugins, acquires lock, calls p.Shutdown() while p.Init() is in progress in another goroutine. Plugin contract says "After Shutdown returns, no further calls into the plugin are made"; pairing Shutdown with an Init-in-flight is the inverse problem.
  - Unregister(name) → also calls p.Shutdown() while Init is in flight.

Concrete repro of the Init/Shutdown overlap:

  // Goroutine A.
  go func() {
      reg.Register(slowInitPlugin{})  // Init blocks on I/O for 200ms.
  }()
  time.Sleep(10 * time.Millisecond) // window where p is in r.plugins, Init still running.

  // Goroutine B.
  reg.Shutdown()  // Acquires lock, sees p, calls p.Shutdown(),
                  // deletes from map. p.Init() is still running.

  // Goroutine A's p.Init() returns nil; Register returns no error.
  // The registry now has a plugin Init'd-then-Shutdown with the
  // host expecting it to be live.

  // OR: p.Init() returns an error; Register's rollback delete
  // is a no-op (B already deleted), and B's Shutdown ran on a
  // plugin whose Init never completed.

The 14-test suite covers concurrent Register/List but not Register-overlapping-with-Shutdown or Register-overlapping-with-Unregister. The doc says "Init must return promptly" — but for any plugin doing I/O (network handshakes, file scanning, subprocess setup), the race window is wide enough to hit in production.

Two reasonable fixes:

  (a) Init outside the lock with an "initializing" placeholder so
      other registry ops can skip in-flight registrations:

        r.mu.Lock()
        if _, ok := r.plugins[name]; ok { ... duplicate ... }
        r.plugins[name] = nil       // sentinel: name claimed, plugin
                                    // not yet usable
        r.mu.Unlock()

        if err := p.Init(...); err != nil {
            r.mu.Lock()
            delete(r.plugins, name)
            r.mu.Unlock()
            return ...
        }

        r.mu.Lock()
        r.plugins[name] = p           // promote to live
        r.mu.Unlock()
        return nil

      Get / List / FindByCapability / Shutdown skip the nil entry; the
      name slot is reserved so a concurrent Register sees ErrPluginAlready
      Registered correctly. (Or use a separate `inFlight` set instead
      of nil entries to keep map types clean.)

  (b) Run Init inside the registry-write lock. Trades parallelism
      for correctness. Acceptable when Init is documented to be
      "promptly" — slow plugins are rare enough that serializing
      registrations is fine. The doc would need updating to note
      that concurrent Register/List etc. blocks until each Init
      completes.

Either fix should ship with a regression test that runs Register on
a plugin whose Init blocks on a channel, concurrently calls Shutdown,
asserts plugin.Shutdown() is NOT called until plugin.Init() completes
(or completes-with-error and is rolled out before Shutdown sees it).

Severity MEDIUM: only manifests under concurrent Register-vs-Shutdown
or Register-vs-Unregister, both of which are admittedly uncommon
during normal operation. But the registry's stated mission is "fail-
closed registration semantics" — invoking a plugin before Init
returns nil is exactly the not-fail-closed leak the contract is
trying to prevent. The race is also exposed by errors-during-Init:
a plugin that fails Init can have Shutdown called on it (via
Shutdown() or Unregister()) before its in-flight Init even has a
chance to return.

Source: internal/plugins/sdk.go (Register lines ~190-205, Shutdown
lines ~310-330, Unregister ~210-230); commit d4971f66 (bd-2mb03.6.7).
close_reason: Replaced map[string]Plugin with map[string]*pluginEntry where pluginEntry tracks {p, ready}. Register reserves the slot with ready=false, runs Init OUTSIDE the registry lock, then re-acquires to flip ready=true (success) or delete (failure). Get/List/FindByCapability filter to ready=true so observers cannot invoke a not-yet-init'd plugin. Unregister treats not-ready as not-found. Added closed bool; Shutdown sets it under the lock and iterates only ready entries — subsequent Register fails with new ErrRegistryClosed, and any in-flight Init that completes AFTER Shutdown observes closed=true, removes its entry, and calls p.Shutdown() on the freshly-init'd plugin so no orphan leaks. Five regression tests cover the contract: in-flight invisibility, Shutdown skips not-ready, post-Shutdown Register fail-close, Unregister of in-flight returns not-found, and a 24-goroutine race-detector test on Register+List+FindByCapability+Get+Shutdown. Existing 14 tests stay green. Commit: 09473a1d. rch exec -- go build ./cmd/ntm and rch exec -- go test -short -race -count=1 ./internal/plugins/... both pass.

title: executeParallel hardcodes substep concurrency at 8 — not configurable, no LimitsConfig knob
description:
## Summary

`internal/pipeline/executor.go:1894` hard-codes a fan-out semaphore for parallel sub-steps:

```go
// Semaphore to limit concurrency (max 8 parallel steps)
sem := make(chan struct{}, 8)
```

The codebase has `LimitsConfig.MaxConcurrentForeach` for foreach iterations, but parallel sub-step concurrency has no config knob — it is silently fixed at 8. A workflow with `parallel.steps: [...]` of length > 8 will only run 8 substeps at a time, with no surface-level error or log explaining why the rest are queued.

## Severity

P3. Functionally correct (work eventually completes), but surprising and undocumented. Operators tuning workflow throughput on large parallel groups will hit this wall and have no obvious lever.

## Suggested approach

Either:
1. Honour an existing limit (e.g. `MaxConcurrentForeach`), since both shapes are "parallel work fan-out".
2. Introduce a new `LimitsConfig.MaxConcurrentParallelSubsteps` (default 8 for back-compat).

Option 2 keeps semantics distinct (foreach vs explicit parallel block); option 1 reduces the config surface.

## Acceptance

- The `8` in executor.go:1894 is replaced with a configurable value sourced from `LimitsConfig`.
- `LimitsConfig` defaults preserve the current behavior for unconfigured workflows.
- A unit test asserts that `parallel.steps` of length N > limit is correctly fan-out-limited and eventually completes all N.
- Schema doc for the new (or repurposed) limit documents the cap.

## Files

- internal/pipeline/executor.go (executeParallel semaphore)
- internal/pipeline/schema.go (LimitsConfig + defaults)
close_reason: done

title: policy/Compile: first-error abort silently disables remaining rules in same category
description: internal/policy/policy.go (*Policy).compile() returns on the FIRST regex.Compile error in Blocked/ApprovalRequired/Allowed. Effect: if a user loads a YAML policy where Blocked[0].Pattern is malformed, every other Blocked rule in the policy never has its regex set, and Check() silently skips uncompiled rules ('if rule.regex != nil && rule.regex.MatchString'). SimulatePlan registers a single 'policy compilation failed' note but still calls Check, treating dangerous-but-uncompiled rules as allow. Real-world impact: a user with a typo in their first blocked pattern gets a degraded fail-open policy, with no indication beyond one terse note. Fix: compile() should attempt every rule, mark each compile failure on the rule itself, and return errors.Join of all failures. Check() can then either: (a) skip uncompiled rules but log/warn each one, (b) treat any compile failure in Blocked/ApprovalRequired as fail-closed (block everything not on Allowed list). Recommend (a) plus a SimulationReport field that lists every failed pattern so consumers see the full damage.
close_reason: Changed (*Policy).compile() to attempt every rule across all three slices (Blocked/ApprovalRequired/Allowed), collecting failures via errors.Join and continuing past each error. Successful patterns still get their regex set; failed patterns leave nil regex and are skipped by Check. A typo in Blocked[0] no longer silently disables Blocked[1..N]. New tests: TestCompile_MalformedPatternDoesNotDisableLaterRules verifies the regression specifically (bad regex + good regex in Blocked, good rule still matches via Check); TestCompile_AllErrorsJoinedAcrossSlices verifies failures from all three slices are surfaced together. policy short-mode suite passes.

title: EPIC: Automatic File Reservation via Agent Mail
description:
**IDEA #5 - INVISIBLE SAFETY NET (87% confidence)**

## What It Does
When NTM detects an agent is editing a file (from pane output analysis), it automatically reserves that file in Agent Mail, preventing other agents from conflicting edits.

## Why This Matters
- Conflicts between agents are a major pain point
- Currently: Users must remember to manually reserve files
- After: It just works; conflicts are prevented automatically
- Users don't even notice until they get a conflict warning (which is now rare)

## How It Works
Detection triggers:

title: [HIGH] JSON pipeline run ignores start-from and from-state flags
description: Review of bb4fceca found that ntm --json pipeline run accepts --start-from and --from-state flags but the JSON-mode branch constructs PipelineRunOptions without carrying either value, and PipelineRunOptions has no start-from/from-state fields. The human path wires execCfg.StartFromStep and loads StartFromState, but --json mode calls pipeline.PrintPipelineRun with only WorkflowFile, Session, ProjectDir, Variables, DryRun, and Background. title: [CRITICAL] approval.WaitForApproval misses notification if decision arrives between Check and waiter registration
close_reason: Fixed in internal/approval/engine.go::WaitForApproval: register the wait channel BEFORE checking status, then re-check. Pre-fix Check-then-register had a race window where Approve()/Deny() running between the Check and the register-waitCh step would call notifyWaiters with this channel not yet in e.waiters[id] — the decision was lost and the caller blocked for the full timeout despite the decision having been made. With register-then-check, either (a) the second Check catches the recent decision, or (b) any future decision arrives via the now-registered channel — no race window. Soak test TestWaitForApproval_NoRaceWithApproveBetweenCheckAndRegister runs 200 iterations with no-delay Approve goroutines and asserts each WaitForApproval call returns within 50ms (well below the 200ms timeout). The race window is narrow enough that pre-fix didn't deterministically fail in 200 iterations even under race detector, but the fix is correctness-by-inspection: register-then-check is the standard double-check pattern for waiter races and matches the implementation in cond-variable code throughout the standard library.

title: Kill subprocess process group on cancellation (Setpgid + signal -pgid)
description:
## Background

A `command:` step that runs `./scripts/spawn-helpers.sh` may itself spawn background processes. On Ctrl-C, Go's exec.Cmd kills only the direct child. The grandchildren orphan + leak.

This is partially covered by E_CANCEL (cancellation contract) but warrants its own bead because the implementation requires platform-specific syscalls (Setpgid on Linux/macOS, JobObject on Windows).

## Spec

### Linux / macOS
- exec.Cmd.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{Setpgid: true} when starting the command.
- On ctx.Done() or timeout: syscall.Kill(-pid, syscall.SIGTERM); wait 5s; if still alive, syscall.Kill(-pid, syscall.SIGKILL).
- The negative pid signals the entire process group.

### Windows
- exec.Cmd.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{CreationFlags: CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP}
- On cancel: send CTRL_BREAK_EVENT to the process group ID.
- Wait + force-kill via TerminateJobObject if needed.

### Documentation
- Note that some workloads spawn processes that intentionally detach (nohup, setsid). These can't be killed via group signal — operator's problem.

## Acceptance
- Unit test (Linux/macOS): a command spawning a child sleep, killed mid-flight, both die.
- Unit test (Windows-skip): same but using PowerShell's Start-Process pattern.
- Cross-platform: verify the command's process group is set up correctly.

## Files
- internal/pipeline/executor.go — extend executeCommand with platform-specific syscall wiring (use build tags or runtime checks)
- internal/pipeline/process_group_linux_test.go — Linux-specific test
- internal/pipeline/process_group_windows_test.go — Windows-specific test (or skip if not supported now)

- Every event MUST include these stable fields where applicable: `run_id`, `workflow`, `step_id`, `pane_id`, `agent_type`, `iteration` (for foreach).
- Levels: Info for normal lifecycle events, Warn for recoverable issues, Error for failures, Debug for verbose tracing.

## File proliferation discipline (per AGENTS.md § No File Proliferation)

- New files justified only when the module is genuinely a separate concern AND would bloat an existing file beyond ~1500 LOC.

title: [LOW] executeParallel adoption branch appends to completionOrder/results without mu (asymmetric lock pairing)
description:
## Severity: [LOW]

Commit 7afe3a97 (bd-qbymk) added an adoption branch to `executeParallel` that runs in the main dispatch loop:

```go
for i, pStep := range step.Parallel.Steps {
    e.stateMu.RLock()
    existing, hasExisting := e.state.Steps[pStep.ID]
    e.stateMu.RUnlock()
    if hasExisting && !shouldRerunStep(existing) && existing.Status == StatusCompleted {
        results[i] = existing
        completionOrder = append(completionOrder, existing.StepID)   // no mu
        e.markParallelSubstepFinished(step.ID, pStep.ID, existing.Status)
        continue
    }

    wg.Add(1)
    go func(idx int, ps Step) {
        ...
        mu.Lock()
        results[idx] = pResult
        completionOrder = append(completionOrder, pResult.StepID)    // mu held
        ...
        mu.Unlock()
    }(i, pStep)
}
```

The dispatch goroutines synchronise their `completionOrder` append via `mu`, but the new adoption-branch append on the main thread does not take `mu`. When dispatched goroutines for prior fresh children are still running (they acquire `sem`, do work, then acquire `mu`), and the main thread iterates to the next step and hits the adoption branch, the two appends race on the slice header. A race-induced lost append silently corrupts `completionOrder` — which is the source for downstream ordering.

## Empirical note

I tried 20 iterations of an interleaved fresh/adopted test under `-race` without triggering the detector, because:
- The main-loop iteration is very fast (microseconds).
- Dispatched goroutines need to acquire `sem`, then execute, before reaching their append.

So the timing rarely aligns. Still, the lock pairing is wrong by code review and the contract violation is real (one append could be lost on reallocation). Heavier loads (longer chains, slower goroutines, GC pressure) make the window plausibly reachable.

## Fix sketch

Take `mu` around the adoption-branch writes:
```go
if hasExisting && !shouldRerunStep(existing) && existing.Status == StatusCompleted {
    mu.Lock()
    results[i] = existing
    completionOrder = append(completionOrder, existing.StepID)
    mu.Unlock()
    e.markParallelSubstepFinished(step.ID, pStep.ID, existing.Status)
    continue
}
```

`results[i] = existing` is technically race-free because each goroutine writes a distinct index, but defending it under `mu` matches the goroutine's contract and avoids future maintenance hazards.

## Files
- internal/pipeline/executor.go:1870-1885 (executeParallel adoption branch)
close_reason: Fixed: adoption branch now takes mu around results[i]/completionOrder appends, matching the goroutine append contract. Build green, parallel tests -race clean. Files: internal/pipeline/executor.go:1880-1888

title: Idea Wizard: queue-dry ideation pipeline vNext
description:
Queue-dry idea-wizard roadmap for the next tranche after bd-2mb03, bd-3v1gs, bd-fxj4f, and bd-8kglp are closed. The previous programs covered swarm-scale pressure/backpressure, operator assurance, recovery drills, robot contract replay, allocation, closeout proof bundles, and reservation/worktree risk advisors. This epic focuses on the remaining operator gap: when br ready and bv robot triage are genuinely dry, NTM should help an agent or human produce duplicate-aware, evidence-backed, self-contained candidate beads instead of relying on an ad hoc manual brainstorming session.

Goal: build a Go-only, safe-by-default planning loop that reads current queue state, closed bead history, docs, optional CASS/CM context, support-bundle/closeout evidence, and code-surface signals; generates candidate improvements; detects overlap with existing open and recently closed work; renders a dry-run roadmap; and only creates beads when an explicit gated mode is requested.

Non-goals: do not add a new top-level robot surface unless the robot surface taxonomy justifies it; prefer work/queue-dry integration and JSON output on existing work commands. Do not auto-create beads by default. Do not require network, real agents, or real model calls for tests. Do not duplicate already-closed adaptive-ops, operator-assurance, recovery-drill, robot-contract, and pressure/backpressure work.

Acceptance: child beads are independently shippable, self-contained, and dependency-linked. The resulting feature lets a future queue-dry operator run a dry-run ideation command, inspect ranked candidates with duplicate evidence, and optionally create/refine beads with br while preserving dry-run behavior, auditability, and degraded-source semantics.

title: Queue-dry ideation evidence model and overlap rubric

The model must support missing optional sources without failing the run.

Required outputs: IdeaEvidenceSnapshot, CandidateSource, ExistingWorkFingerprint, OverlapVerdict, NoveltySignal, and ValidationNote structs with stable JSON tags. Every candidate must carry enough evidence for a future agent to see why it exists and what it might duplicate.

Overlap rubric: compare against open beads, in-progress beads, and recently closed idea-wizard families including bd-2mb03, bd-3v1gs, bd-fxj4f, and bd-8kglp. The rubric must classify exact duplicate, likely duplicate, adjacent follow-up, and novel. It must preserve evidence strings rather than only emitting scores.

title: Queue-dry novelty guard and review-first fallback
description:

Signals: recent closed-bead volume, recent bug density, failed or skipped verification in closeout proof bundles, dirty worktree, active reservations, stale in-progress history, duplicate-heavy candidate set, and current graph health. The guard must explain its decision with stable reason codes and evidence.

Output: Recommendation values such as ideate, review_recent_work, validate_closeout, stand_down, or wait_for_coordination. These recommendations feed bd-e7xm1.4 CLI output and bd-e7xm1.5 create gating.

title: Duplicate-aware 30-to-5 and 15-candidate ranker
description:
Build the deterministic candidate generation and winnowing core for bd-e7xm1. The engine should mimic the idea-wizard workflow shape without requiring a model call: generate a broader candidate set from evidence categories, score each candidate against the project rubric, winnow to the best five, then retain the next ten complementary candidates for roadmap breadth.

Scoring factors must be explicit and inspectable: robustness, reliability, performance, ergonomics, usefulness, user-visible value, implementation cost, testability, degraded-source risk, and overlap verdict from bd-e7xm1.1. A likely duplicate must lose to an adjacent novel follow-up unless the candidate has clear evidence that the prior closed work left a gap.

Output requirements: stable ordering, reasons for inclusion/exclusion, per-candidate source evidence, overlap evidence, and a reasoned final rank. The engine must be pure and fixture-friendly so tests can assert byte-stable JSON.

description:
bd-8wo27 picked stateMu before varMu as the canonical lock order across the pipeline executor, flipped resolveForeachMaxRounds to match, and added a regression test. But internal/pipeline/loops.go LoopExecutor.substituteIntExpr (commit 399e5b0f, bd-6lkqr.5) has the SAME inverted order:

  func (le *LoopExecutor) substituteIntExpr(expr string) (string, error) {
      le.executor.varMu.RLock()
      defer le.executor.varMu.RUnlock()
      le.executor.stateMu.RLock()
      defer le.executor.stateMu.RUnlock()

      workflowID := ""
      if le.executor.state != nil {
          workflowID = le.executor.state.WorkflowID
      }
      sub := NewSubstitutor(le.executor.state, le.executor.config.Session, workflowID)
      sub.SetDefaults(le.executor.defaults)
      return sub.SubstituteStrict(le.executor.substituteRuntimeVariables(expr))
  }

This call site shipped four months before bd-8wo27 and uses the `defer` form of the inverted nesting, which a naive grep for "varMu.RLock then stateMu.RLock without an unlock between them" misses (because the `defer le.executor.varMu.RUnlock()` line sits between them and a regex-only scan thinks the lock is already released). The deadlock potential is identical to bd-8wo27:

  Goroutine A: applyStartFrom holds stateMu.Lock(), waits for varMu.Lock().
  Goroutine B: substituteIntExpr holds varMu.RLock(), waits for stateMu.RLock().
  Both blocked. AB-BA deadlock.

substituteIntExpr is called from resolveIntOrExpr (also in loops.go), which the LoopExecutor uses for executeForEach/executeWhile/executeTimes max_iterations resolution. Any loop body that runs concurrent foreach iterations through the parallel runner has at least the same exposure as resolveForeachMaxRounds — likely more, since resolveIntOrExpr fires on every loop step entry.

Suggested fix:

  1. Flip the acquisition order to stateMu before varMu, mirroring the
     bd-8wo27 fix in foreach_max_rounds.go and applyStartFrom in
     executor.go:

       le.executor.stateMu.RLock()
       defer le.executor.stateMu.RUnlock()
       le.executor.varMu.RLock()
       defer le.executor.varMu.RUnlock()

  2. Add a comment referencing bd-8wo27 + this finding so the
     canonical-order convention covers both call sites.

  3. Audit the rest of internal/pipeline for any other deferred-form
     varMu→stateMu nesting (the original bd-8wo27 review missed this
     site because of the defer pattern). One reliable way is `grep -B
     1 -A 4 'varMu\.RLock'` looking for a stateMu.RLock within four
     following lines, with or without intervening defers.

Add a regression test in internal/pipeline/lock_order_test.go that
exercises this call path concurrently with the existing applyStartFrom
writer pattern. The existing TestLockOrder_StateMuVarMuCanonicalOrder
covers resolveForeachMaxRounds; the new test should cover
substituteIntExpr (and ideally any further call sites the audit
finds).

Severity MEDIUM: same risk and rationale as bd-8wo27 — latent AB-BA
deadlock, narrow trigger window today, broad future exposure.
Unblocks the lock-order convention bd-8wo27 was supposed to
establish.

Source: internal/pipeline/loops.go LoopExecutor.substituteIntExpr
(~line 603); commit 399e5b0f (bd-6lkqr.5). Related: bd-8wo27 (this
file's foreach_max_rounds.go counterpart fix).
close_reason: Flipped LoopExecutor.substituteIntExpr to stateMu→varMu canonical order matching bd-8wo27. Added bd-eslpu comment block documenting the deferred-form audit gap so a future review can't miss the same pattern. Regression test TestLockOrder_LoopSubstituteIntExprCanonicalOrder runs substituteIntExpr concurrently with stateMu→varMu writers; verified the test fires its 15s deadlock timeout when the fix is reverted, passes cleanly with the fix restored. Audit surfaced four MORE inverted call sites (substituteStrict, substituteVariablesStrictCtx, evaluateConditionCtx, snapshotState) plus loops.go::resolveItems; filed as a follow-up bead since snapshotState's order has a documented bd-xuxev rationale that needs separate analysis.

title: [HIGH] step bracket access only works at first field segment
description:
[HIGH] Review of ea6c697a found that splitBracketAccess is applied only to the second steps segment (`field := parts[1]`) inside Substitutor.resolveSteps. The commit advertises `${steps.fetch.output.items[0].title}`, `${steps.fetch.data[user][profile][name]}`, and `${steps.fetch.parsed_data.list[3]}`, but the tokenizer passes deeper bracketed tokens such as `items[0]` or `list[3]` through `rest := parts[2:]` unchanged. navigateNested does not understand bracket suffixes on map keys, so it looks for a literal key named `items[0]` and fails even when ParsedData has `items: [...]`.

Working shape today: `${steps.fetch.output[0]}` because the bracket is attached to the first field token (`output[0]`). Broken documented shape: `${steps.fetch.output.items[0].title}`.

Expected: bracket expansion should be applied to every path segment before navigateNested, or navigateNested should split bracket suffixes itself. Add regression coverage for a parsed JSON step result with `items: [{title: "ok"}]` and `${steps.fetch.output.items[0].title}` resolving to `ok`.

No code fix was applied in this review pass because the requested CRITICAL/HIGH auto-fix scope is restricted to NEW files only, while the production fix requires wiring the existing variables.go path expansion before nested traversal.
close_reason: navigateNested now expands bracket suffixes on every path segment via new helper expandBracketParts, so steps.fetch.output.items[0].title, steps.fetch.data[user][profile][name], and steps.fetch.parsed_data.list[3] resolve as documented. Added TestResolveSteps_OutputBracketAccessOnDeeperSegment for the four documented shapes; existing tests stay green.

title: Fix Fleet count inconsistency (0/17 vs 17 panes)
description:
## Problem
The dashboard shows inconsistent fleet counts: "Fleet: 0/17" in status bar vs "17 panes" in the stats bar.

## Screenshot Evidence
- Status bar: "Fleet: 0/17 (C:16)"
- Stats bar badge: "17 panes"

This suggests 0 active agents out of 17 panes, with 16 Claude instances - but the "0" is likely incorrect.

## Code Locations
- internal/tui/dashboard/dashboard.go:2112-2180 - renderStatsBar()
- internal/tui/dashboard/panels/ticker.go - Fleet count in ticker
- Model fields: panes, claudeCount, codexCount, geminiCount

## Possible Causes
1. **Different data sources** - Stats bar uses len(m.panes), ticker uses different count
2. **Async update race** - Pane count updated but agent count not yet
3. **Filter mismatch** - Active vs total panes counted differently
4. **Status detection lag** - Agent status not yet determined for some panes

## Investigation
\`\`\`go
// Check these fields are consistent:
log.Debug("fleet counts",
    "total_panes", len(m.panes),
    "claude_count", m.claudeCount,
    "codex_count", m.codexCount,
    "gemini_count", m.geminiCount,
    "user_count", m.userCount,
    "agent_statuses", len(m.agentStatuses))
\`\`\`

## Fix Pattern
\`\`\`go
// Ensure consistent counting
func (m *Model) updateCounts() {
    m.claudeCount = 0
    m.codexCount = 0
    m.geminiCount = 0
    m.userCount = 0
    
    for _, pane := range m.panes {
        switch pane.AgentType {
        case "claude":
            m.claudeCount++
        case "codex":
            m.codexCount++
        case "gemini":
            m.geminiCount++
        default:
            m.userCount++
        }
    }
    
    // Active = has known status
    m.activeCount = 0
    for _, pane := range m.panes {
        if status, ok := m.agentStatuses[pane.ID]; ok && status.State != "unknown" {
            m.activeCount++
        }
    }
}

// Ticker should use same source
func (t *TickerPanel) SetFleetData(active, total int) {
    t.activeAgents = active
    t.totalAgents = total
}
\`\`\`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Fleet count shows consistent X/Y across all UI locations
- [ ] "X" represents agents with known status
- [ ] "Y" represents total panes
- [ ] Counts update atomically (no partial updates visible)

## Unit Tests
1. TestFleetCount_Consistent - stats bar and ticker show same totals
2. TestFleetCount_ActiveDefinition - active = has non-unknown status
3. TestFleetCount_UpdateAtomic - counts update together
4. TestFleetCount_AgentTypes - Claude/Codex/Gemini counts sum correctly

## Logging
- DEBUG: Log count calculations with breakdown
- INFO: Log fleet count changes
- WARN: Log inconsistencies between counts
close_reason: Fixed: Removed incorrect len(m.paneStatus)==0 condition that prevented fallback from triggering when paneStatus map has entries with empty State values

title: [HIGH] robot/causality: pipeline state size cap is TOCTOU — Stat-then-ReadFile lets file grow past limit
description:
Commit e7387292 (bd-w3ft1) caps pipeline state file size in internal/robot/causality.go readPipelineStateFileWithLimit:

  if maxBytes > 0 {
    info, err := os.Stat(path)
    ...
    if info.Size() > maxBytes {
      return nil, fmt.Errorf('pipeline state file exceeds limit: ...')
    }
  }
  data, err := os.ReadFile(path)

This is TOCTOU. The Stat() result and the ReadFile() result are not from the same file descriptor or the same instant. Concrete failure modes:

1. Concurrent writer growth: between Stat and ReadFile the file is appended to (or atomically replaced via rename). Stat sees 1MB, ReadFile sees 100MB and allocates the full buffer. The 16MB cap is bypassed; memory exhaustion in the --robot-causality command path.

2. Symlink swap: os.Stat follows symlinks. If path is a symlink that points to a small file at Stat time and a large file at ReadFile time (process-controlled by another local user, or by a buggy NTM writer), the cap is bypassed.

3. Pipe / sparse file: os.Stat on a sparse file or named pipe can report size != bytes-readable; ReadFile may consume more than reported.

os.ReadFile internally calls Stat again on the FD it opened, so the second Stat may show the new size and ReadFile will allocate that much. The code's outer check is decorative: it cannot bound the actual read.

Fix: open the file once, then use io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(f, maxBytes+1)) and reject if read returned > maxBytes. Single FD, single read, hard upper bound.

Severity: HIGH — DoS via memory exhaustion in the causality command path. .ntm/pipelines/ is user-owned but NTM itself can produce runaway files (e.g., a workflow that dumps unbounded variable data), and the silent-error swallow in loadPipelineCausalityEvents (line 612-614 of internal/robot/causality.go: 'st, err := readPipelineStateFile(...); if err != nil { continue }') masks any sign of the problem until OOM hits.

Source: internal/robot/causality.go readPipelineStateFileWithLimit (line ~707), loadPipelineCausalityEvents (line ~583).
close_reason: Replaced os.Stat-then-os.ReadFile with single-FD os.Open + io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(f, maxBytes+1)) in internal/robot/causality.go readPipelineStateFileWithLimit. The read is now bounded by the open FD itself, so a concurrent writer growing the file or a symlink-swap between size-check and read cannot bypass the cap. Added TestReadPipelineStateFileWithLimit_BoundsReadEvenWhenStatLies (5KiB file, 1KiB cap, confirms rejection without full-file allocation) and TestReadPipelineStateFileWithLimit_AcceptsExactlyMaxBytes (boundary). Commit: 68976edd. rch exec -- go test -short -count=1 -run TestReadPipelineStateFileWithLimit ./internal/robot/ passes.

title: EPIC: Agent Activity Timeline Visualization
description:
## Overview
Add a Gantt-chart style timeline visualization showing agent state transitions over time. This provides crucial historical context for understanding what agents did and when, enabling better debugging and optimization.

## Problem Statement
Current NTM status shows only instantaneous state. Users can't see:
- When an agent started/stopped working
- How long tasks took
- Overlapping activity patterns
- Idle time vs busy time
- Historical state for debugging

## Key Features
1. Timeline panel in dashboard showing horizontal bars per agent
2. Color-coded states: idle (gray), working (green), waiting (yellow), error (red)
3. Scrollable time window with zoom controls
4. Event markers for prompts sent, errors, completions
5. Export timeline to SVG/PNG for reports

## Technical Design
1. State tracking:
   - Record state transitions with timestamps
   - Store in memory during session
   - Optionally persist to file for post-session analysis

2. Timeline rendering:
   - Use lipgloss for colored blocks
   - Calculate time scale based on window width
   - Support minute/hour/day scales

3. Data model:
   type AgentEvent struct {
     AgentID   string
     State     AgentState  // idle, working, waiting, error
     Timestamp time.Time
     Details   string      // prompt sent, error message, etc.
   }

## Success Criteria
- Timeline panel shows agent activity over time
- States are clearly color-coded
- Time scale adapts to session duration
- Can scroll through history
- Export works for offline analysis

## Files Likely Affected
- internal/state/timeline.go (new - event tracking)
- internal/tui/dashboard/panels/timeline.go (new - visualization)
- internal/tui/dashboard/model.go (add timeline panel)
- internal/export/timeline.go (new - SVG/PNG export)
notes:
## Testing Requirements
- Unit tests: core logic, error paths, edge cases.
- E2E scripts: full CLI/robot flow with detailed log/slog prefixes (e.g., [E2E-<AREA>]) and include session/agent/bead IDs.
- If structured outputs are affected, assert schema stability + deterministic ordering.

title: Task: Implement contextual command suggestions
description:
## Overview
Provide intelligent, context-aware command suggestions based on current NTM state.

## Deliverables
1. Create internal/cli/suggestions/contextual.go:
   - SuggestNextCommand(state State) Suggestion
   - State struct capturing current NTM status
   - Suggestion struct with command, reason, example

2. Context detection:
   - No sessions running -> suggest spawn
   - Sessions running, none busy -> suggest send
   - Sessions running, all busy -> suggest status or dashboard
   - Recent errors -> suggest tail or logs
   - Many sessions -> suggest dashboard
   - Beads available -> suggest assign or swarm

3. Suggestion display:
   - Show at end of command output (non-intrusive)
   - Format: 'Next: ntm send myproject --msg="Start task"'
   - Make dismissible via config (suggestions_enabled: false)

4. Integration points:
   - After ntm status: suggest send if agents idle
   - After ntm spawn: suggest send
   - After ntm send: suggest status or tail
   - After error: suggest relevant recovery command

## Implementation Notes
- Keep suggestions brief (one line)
- Don't show suggestion if user seems to know what they're doing
- Rate limit to avoid being annoying

## Acceptance Criteria
- Suggestions appear in appropriate contexts
- Suggestions are actionable and relevant
- Can be disabled via config
- Unit tests for each context scenario
notes: Optional, non-intrusive suggestions. Do NOT depend on tiers or usage tracking.

## Origin
Four parallel read-only audits swept the codebase on 2026-07-24 (robot, session/tmux/status, pipeline/state/checkpoint/audit, serve/auth/webhook). Every finding below was verified by the auditing agent against real code, and several were reproduced empirically (live tmux 3.5a, -race runs, standalone regex probes).

## Already fixed in this sweep
Landed in commits 810bee1b, cf4c25a1, 53167788, aa5b908b, 286ef537, c6f6762a:
- encryption: keyring decrypt order nondeterministic; keyring without active_key_id made writes undecryptable; key-resolution failure silently degraded to plaintext; `ntm analytics` read the event log raw so encrypted logs reported zero events; e2e coverage added.
- serve/beads: `POST /beads/sync` ran a bare `br sync` (proven to regress 191 issues in this repo); argv injection via bead IDs/titles/filters; non-atomic claim.
- agy launch: robot spawn and restart rendered `--model ''` so Antigravity never started; AliasesFor did not normalize `oc`.
- dead regexes: `^error:` in status detection and six file-detection patterns lacked `(?m)`.
- file-edit detection reserved prose tokens (`e.g`, `Object.assign`, `node.js`) as exclusive locks.
- robot JSON contract: `alerts`/`sessions`/`active_incidents` emitted null; `agents` omitempty on degraded mail/wait paths.
- `--robot-interrupt --no-wait` dropped already-idle panes from the follow-up message.
- `--robot-errors`: malformed `--panes` silently scanned pane 0; leading context lines dropped near the top of the buffer.
- pipeline: `snapshotState` shallow-copied `ForeachIterationState`, risking a fatal concurrent map write.

## Scope of this epic
The children are the findings NOT yet fixed. Each carries file:line, the concrete trigger, and the proposed minimal fix. Verify before fixing — a few are design questions rather than defects.

title: [HIGH] Foreach beads structured queries silently truncate br results
description:
Review of 98215809 (feat(pipeline): resolve foreach beads iteration source) found that parseStructuredBeadsQuery builds br list --json without an explicit --limit. In this repository br list defaults to a finite page size, so a foreach step using the structured beads form, for example beads: hypothesis,state:active, silently receives only the first page of matching bead records.

Impact: large hypothesis/debate/backlog pipelines can skip all matching beads beyond the default br list limit with no error. This is especially dangerous for foreach fan-out because the truncated result becomes the complete iteration set, so downstream templates simply never run for the omitted beads.

This is distinct from the already-fixed bead_query truncation bug bd-0e3el: internal/pipeline/bead_query.go now uses br list --json --limit 0, but internal/pipeline/iteration_sources.go parseStructuredBeadsQuery still starts with []string{"list", "--json"}.

Expected: structured foreach beads queries should request unlimited results, e.g. add --limit 0 to parseStructuredBeadsQuery, and add a regression test asserting the generated br args include the unlimited limit.

No code fix applied in this review pass because the requested CRITICAL/HIGH auto-fix scope is restricted to NEW files only, while the production fix belongs in internal/pipeline/iteration_sources.go.
close_reason: Added --limit 0 to parseStructuredBeadsQuery so structured foreach beads queries request unlimited results. Updated all parseStructuredBeadsQuery test fixtures and added TestParseStructuredBeadsQuery_AlwaysIncludesUnlimitedLimit regression test that asserts --limit 0 is present regardless of expr.

title: Task: Implement real-time synthesis streaming
description:
## Implementation
Add streaming synthesis without altering non-stream behavior:

1. Add `SynthesisChunk` + stream method in existing synthesis code (prefer extending `internal/ensemble/synthesis.go`; only add a new file if unavoidable):
   - `StreamSynthesize(ctx, inputs) (<-chan SynthesisChunk, <-chan error)`
   - Chunk fields: type, content, mode_id, index, timestamp

2. Emission rules:
   - Deterministic ordering (monotonic index)
   - Progress/status chunks at key milestones
   - Backpressure-safe channel usage

3. CLI:
   - `ntm ensemble synthesize --stream` (human-readable incremental output)
   - `--stream --json` emits JSONL events + final summary
   - Ctrl+C cancels, writes checkpoint, prints resume command

4. Checkpoint integration:
   - On cancel/error, write partial checkpoint (bd-3didt)
   - On resume, continue emitting chunks from last index

## Logging
- Log stream start/end, chunk_count, time_to_first_chunk, cancel reason

## Tests
- Unit: chunk ordering + deterministic emission
- Integration: stream + synthesis fixture
- E2E: CLI streaming output and resume path

## Dependencies
- Synthesis System (bd-2qwm8)
- Synthesis strategies (bd-2ztw9)
- Partial recovery (bd-3didt)
close_reason: Completed (streaming synth + checkpoints + E2E tests)

title: Implement --dry-run and explicit allocation
description:
Implement --dry-run and explicit allocation modes.

## --dry-run Mode

Show allocation plan without executing:
```json
{
  "dry_run": true,
  "planned_assignments": [
    {
      "pane": 2,
      "would_assign": "bd-92e1",
      "reason": "highest_unblocks (9)"
    }
  ]
}
```

Useful for:
- Reviewing before executing
- Integration testing
- What-if analysis

## Explicit Allocation (--allocation)

Accept JSON mapping of pane to bead:
```bash
ntm --robot-bulk-assign myproject --allocation='{"2":"bd-92e1","3":"bd-55pm"}'
```

Bypasses bv triage, uses exactly what user specifies.

## --skip-panes Flag

Exclude specific panes from allocation:
```bash
ntm --robot-bulk-assign myproject --from-bv --skip-panes=4,10
```

Useful when some panes are:
- Already working on something
- Rate limited (leave them alone)
- Reserved for manual control
close_reason: Implemented --dry-run and --allocation flags for bulk assign

title: Implement --fix auto-remediation
description:
Implement --fix flag for automatic remediation.

## Behavior

When --fix is provided:
1. Run normal diagnosis
2. For each auto_fixable recommendation, execute fix_command
3. Report results of each fix attempt

## What Gets Fixed

- crashed: Restart agent via --robot-restart-pane
- unresponsive: Kill and restart via --robot-restart-pane

## What Does NOT Get Fixed

- rate_limited: Requires human decision (wait vs caam)
- unknown: Not enough info to act safely

## Output Enhancement

Add fix_results to response:
```json
{
  "recommendations": [...],
  "fix_results": [
    {
      "pane": 15,
```

title: bd-82zsc/bd-g40ad sibling: bead_query dry-run banner skips SanitizeDescriptionForTerminal on substituted args
description:
## Summary

bd-82zsc (af9ecc47) and bd-g40ad (656c4ffa) wrapped every dry-run banner that
prints a post-substitution string with `SanitizeDescriptionForTerminal` so an
upstream agent cannot inject ANSI/OSC/C0 control sequences (clear-screen, OSC
52 clipboard hijack, BEL, ESC c) into the operator's terminal during
`pipeline run --dry-run`. One sibling site was missed:

### `internal/pipeline/bead_query.go:64` — `executeBeadQuery` dry-run banner

```go
resolvedQuery, err := e.substituteBeadQueryFields(step.BeadQuery)
// ...
args := resolvedQuery.brListArgs()
if e.config.DryRun {
    result.Status = StatusCompleted
    result.Output = dryRunOutput(step, "Would run br "+strings.Join(args, " "))
    // ↑ args contain post-substitution strings — same attack class as bd-82zsc
    return result
}
```

`substituteBeadQueryFields` (bead_query.go:144) supports `${vars.X}`,
`${steps.X.output}`, `${defaults.X}`, etc. on every scalar field
(`status`, `state`, `type`, `priority`, `assignee`, `filter`) and on each
label entry. A workflow with:

```yaml
- id: collect_ids
  agent: claude
  prompt: "List bead IDs..."

- id: filter_query
  bead_query:
    filter: "${steps.collect_ids.output}"
```

…lets the upstream agent's output flow into `q.Filter` after substitution.
That string then becomes one of `args`, joined into "Would run br ..." and
written to the operator's terminal during `--dry-run` without sanitization.

The `bead_query` namespace is sealed-terminal at the substitutor layer
(prevents recursive expansion of `${env.SECRET}` inside upstream output —
bd-447se), but sealing only blocks recursion. The single first-level
substitution still places upstream bytes verbatim into the field, and the
dry-run banner has no separate sanitize step.

## Severity

P3 — same severity / same attack class as bd-82zsc and bd-g40ad. Real-world
risk is bounded by how often `${steps.X.output}` reaches a `bead_query`
field, but the silent-failure mode (a malicious agent output corrupting the
operator's terminal during a routine `--dry-run`) is a parity gap with a
recently-patched class of vector.

## Suggested fix

Mirror the bd-82zsc / bd-g40ad pattern — sanitize before joining:

```go
sanitized := make([]string, len(args))
for i, a := range args {
    sanitized[i] = SanitizeDescriptionForTerminal(a)
}
result.Output = dryRunOutput(step, "Would run br "+strings.Join(sanitized, " "))
```

(or wrap the joined string once, depending on whether arg-boundary integrity
matters for the banner — wrapping once is simpler and matches bd-82zsc's
"sanitize the displayed payload" framing).

## Acceptance

- New `TestExecuteBeadQuery_DryRun_SanitizesControlBytes` mirroring
  `TestExecuteCommand_DryRun_SanitizesControlBytes` (bd-82zsc) and
  `TestExecuteStepOnce_DryRun_SanitizesAgentPrompt` (bd-g40ad): pre-seed
  `state.Steps["upstream"].Output` with ESC/BEL/NUL bytes, run a dry-run
  bead_query whose filter references `\${steps.upstream.output}`, assert
  the rendered banner replaces ESC bytes with `?` and preserves payload
  text round-trip.
- Audit: `grep -n 'dryRunOutput\|truncatePrompt' internal/pipeline/*.go |
  grep -v Sanitize` should be empty for any line that prints a
  post-substitution string.

## Files

- internal/pipeline/bead_query.go (line 64 — wrap with SanitizeDescriptionForTerminal)
- internal/pipeline/bead_query_test.go (new sanitize regression)

## Related

- bd-82zsc (af9ecc47) — original dry-run command banner sanitize
- bd-g40ad (656c4ffa) — agent / parallel / branch dry-run banner sanitize
- bd-zc034 / bd-lqz30 — workflow & step description sanitize
- bd-447se — bead_query namespace sealing (orthogonal: prevents recursive
  expansion, does not address terminal control sequences in the first-pass
  substitution)
close_reason: Wrapped each substituted arg with SanitizeDescriptionForTerminal before joining the dry-run banner in bead_query.go. Test TestExecuteBeadQuery_DryRun_SanitizesControlBytes pre-seeds steps.evil.output with ESC[2J + ESC[H + BEL bytes, references it via Status: ${steps.evil.output}, and asserts the banner scrubs control bytes while preserving payload + 'Would run br' prefix. Pipeline -race -short green at 32.992s. Commit b0c0ce6c.

title: bd-82zsc parity gap: agent + parallel-substep dry-run banners still print unsanitized prompt bytes
description:
## Summary

bd-82zsc (af9ecc47) wrapped expandedCmd and expandedStdin with `SanitizeDescriptionForTerminal` before `truncatePrompt` in the dry-run banner of `executeCommand` (executor.go:1214-1216). Three sibling dry-run banners still call `truncatePrompt(prompt, ...)` directly on a post-substitution string and can leak the same ANSI/OSC/C0 bytes the bd-82zsc fix scrubbed:

1. `internal/pipeline/executor.go:994` — `executeStepOnce` agent step:
   ```go
   result.Output = dryRunOutput(step, "Would execute: "+truncatePrompt(prompt, 100))
   ```
   `prompt` is the post-substituted agent prompt (resolved at line 951, substituted via `substituteVariablesStrictCtx(ctx, prompt)` at line 966). Same attack class — `${steps.X.output}` from an upstream agent can inject ESC[2J / OSC 52 / BEL.

2. `internal/pipeline/executor.go:2263` — `executeParallelStep` agent retry path:
   ```go
   result.Output = dryRunOutput(step, "Would execute: "+truncatePrompt(prompt, 100))
   ```
   Mirror of site #1 inside the parallel substep retry loop.

3. `internal/pipeline/control_flow.go:111` — `executeBranch` predicate dry-run:
   ```go
   result.Output = dryRunOutput(step, "Would evaluate branch predicate: "+truncatePrompt(step.Branch, 80))
   ```
   Lower risk than #1/#2 because `step.Branch` is raw author config (not yet substituted), but inconsistent with the surrounding contract — once Branch substitution is added or the field is fed from `${vars.X}`, the same gap reopens.

## Severity

P3. Same severity bd-82zsc was filed at — operator-terminal hijack via agent-controlled output during `--dry-run`. Sites #1 and #2 are the agent-prompt analogue of bd-82zsc's command path; site #3 is a defense-in-depth consistency fix.

## Suggested approach

Wrap each `truncatePrompt(prompt, ...)` and `truncatePrompt(step.Branch, ...)` call in dry-run banners with `SanitizeDescriptionForTerminal` first. Mirrors the bd-82zsc shape:

```go
result.Output = dryRunOutput(step, "Would execute: "+truncatePrompt(SanitizeDescriptionForTerminal(prompt), 100))
```

Consider extracting a helper (e.g. `sanitizedTruncate(s, n int) string`) so future dry-run banners get the right contract by default. The static analysis equivalent: `grep -n 'truncatePrompt(' internal/pipeline/*.go internal/pipeline/control_flow.go | grep -v Sanitize` should be empty for any line that feeds into operator-visible dry-run output.

## Acceptance

- A regression test for each site, mirroring `TestExecuteCommand_DryRun_SanitizesControlBytes` (af9ecc47): pre-stage a payload containing `\x1b[2J\x1b[H\x07payload`, run the relevant code path with `e.config.DryRun = true`, assert no raw ESC/BEL/NUL bytes survive while the trailing data round-trips.
- Audit pattern above shows no remaining unsanitized dry-run banners.

## Files

- internal/pipeline/executor.go (lines 994, 2263)
- internal/pipeline/control_flow.go (line 111)
- Optional: helper extraction site (anywhere)

## Related

- bd-82zsc (af9ecc47) — original sanitize fix for `executeCommand` dry-run; this is the parity sweep.
- bd-lqz30 — original `SanitizeDescriptionForTerminal` introduction for description fields.
close_reason: Wrapped post-substitution prompt with SanitizeDescriptionForTerminal in executeStepOnce dry-run (executor.go:1000), executeParallelStep retry dry-run (executor.go:2272), and step.Branch in executeBranch dry-run (control_flow.go:114). Regression test TestExecuteStepOnce_DryRun_SanitizesAgentPrompt asserts no control bytes survive into agent dry-run banner. Commit 656c4ffa.

title: [MEDIUM] LimitsConfig stderr and total-step caps are not enforced
description: Review of f8c9d940 found that LimitsConfig adds MaxCommandStderrBytes and MaxStepCountTotal as resource caps, with defaults in EffectiveLimits(), but the executor never checks either value. executeCommand allocates stderrBuf when output_parse is enabled and never truncates or bounds it; when output_parse is disabled stderr is merged into stdout and only the combined captured output is truncated after cmd.Wait() has already buffered it all. MaxStepCountTotal is likewise defaulted but not consulted when building/running workflow graphs or materializing foreach/loop/parallel body steps. Impact: workflows can still consume unbounded memory via stderr-heavy commands or oversized expanded step graphs despite configured limits. Add enforcement and regression tests for stderr truncation/failure behavior and total-step-count rejection.
close_reason: Added cappedWriter (capped_writer.go) that bounds in-memory captured payload while exec.Cmd is still running. executeCommand now uses cappedWriter for both stdout (replacing post-hoc string-slice truncation) and stderr (when output_parse routes them separately) — MaxCommandStderrBytes is now actually enforced. Slog warning emitted for stderr truncation alongside the existing stdout warning. Tests cover unit-level cappedWriter contract, stderr-only cap with output_parse, and merged stream behavior. MaxStepCountTotal enforcement deferred to a follow-up bead since it requires materialized-graph counting that bridges the foreach/loop/parallel runtime expansion.

title: [MEDIUM] policy/simulate: worktree-add HEAD suggestion does not preserve uncommitted changes
description:
Commit 88a78ac2 (bd-60ing) replaced a stash-based suggestion with 'git worktree add /tmp/safety-backup HEAD' in internal/policy/simulate.go saferAlternatives() for the destructive-reset branch. The replacement is mechanically broken in the same scenario the suggestion is meant to protect.

The destructive-reset command's primary danger is destroying UNCOMMITTED working-tree changes. The new suggestion creates a worktree at the HEAD commit — it captures only the committed state, NOT the uncommitted changes the user is about to lose. After the user runs the suggested worktree-add and then proceeds with the destructive reset, their working-tree edits are gone and the safety-backup worktree contains only what was already in HEAD.

Concrete scenario:
  1. User edits 5 files (uncommitted)
  2. Plans to run a hard reset to a previous commit
  3. ntm policy simulator suggests the worktree-add as safer alternative
  4. User runs the suggestion, then proceeds with the reset
  5. Working-tree edits lost; /tmp/safety-backup contains a clean checkout of HEAD with no trace of the lost edits

The bead's own description anticipated this: 'git worktree add or cp -r backup pattern'. The cp -r half is what captures uncommitted state. The implementation took only the worktree half.

Secondary issue: '/tmp/safety-backup' is a hardcoded fixed path. A second invocation (e.g., another agent in another pane) fails with 'fatal: /tmp/safety-backup already exists' — the suggestion is broken on the second use.

Suggested fix: emit a two-step suggestion that actually backs up the working tree, e.g. cp -r working tree to a unique timestamped directory, or save 'git diff' and 'git diff --cached' to a backup directory, then proceed. Or document that the worktree suggestion is for committed-state recovery only, and add a separate suggestion for working-tree preservation.

Source: internal/policy/simulate.go saferAlternatives() destructive-reset branch (~line 157-165).
close_reason: Replaced 'git worktree add /tmp/safety-backup HEAD' (which only captures committed state, missing the uncommitted edits the destructive operation actually destroys) with 'cp -a . /tmp/ntm-safety-backup-$(date +%s)' (working-tree backup with timestamped path so parallel agents do not collide). Inline comment in internal/policy/simulate.go saferAlternatives explains why worktree-HEAD and stash are unsuitable. Added TestSimulatePlanResetHardSuggestsWorkingTreeBackup pinning three invariants: no stash (policy), no fixed /tmp/safety-backup path (collision), at least one cp/tar/rsync working-tree backup offered. Commit: 075adfb0. rch exec -- go test -short -count=1 ./internal/policy/... passes.

title: [HIGH] foreach items drift unprotected — bd-3awat fingerprint only covers legacy loop:items, not foreach:
description:
## Severity: [HIGH]

Commit b6a2285f added an items-fingerprint check to the legacy `loop:` items path (internal/pipeline/loops.go::executeForEach). The newer `foreach:` syntax — handled by `internal/pipeline/foreach.go::executeForeach` and persisted to the same `ForeachState` map — was not extended. So the same drift bug bd-3awat fixed for `loop:` still exists for `foreach:`.

## Reproducer (conceptual)

```yaml
steps:
  - id: produce
    command: "ls scratch/*.txt"
  - id: fanout
    foreach:
      items: "${steps.produce.output}"  # dynamic, can drift
      steps:
        - command: "process ${item}"
```

1. First run: items resolves to `[a.txt, b.txt, c.txt]`. iter0 completes (a.txt processed). Workflow cancelled.
2. Operator deletes a.txt before resuming.
3. Resume: items resolves to `[b.txt, c.txt]`. CompletedIterationIDs records `fanout_iter0` as done. Resume skips iter0 — which is now b.txt. b.txt is silently skipped, and c.txt at index 1 gets processed twice (once as iter1 in original resolution, once as iter1 in the new resolution that points at it).

`grep -n "computeForeachItemsFingerprint\|ItemsFingerprint" internal/pipeline/foreach.go` returns nothing — the newer path has no fingerprint guard.

## Fix

Mirror the bd-3awat pattern in `executeForeach` (foreach.go) right after items resolution and before the iteration loops:

```go
itemsFingerprint := computeForeachItemsFingerprint(items)
if err := e.verifyForeachItemsFingerprint(step.ID, itemsFingerprint); err != nil {
    return finishForeachFailure(result, "foreach", err.Error())
}
e.recordForeachItemsFingerprint(step.ID, itemsFingerprint)
```

Both verifyForeachItemsFingerprint and recordForeachItemsFingerprint already exist on Executor (added by bd-3awat) and operate on the same ForeachState map foreach.go already uses, so the surface change is small.

## Acceptance

- A test mirroring TestForeachItemsDriftDetected for the `foreach:` syntax: same scenario, same expected error.
- Existing bd-3awat tests still pass.
- Sweep: `grep -n CompletedIterationIDs internal/pipeline/*.go` shows every consumer is paired with a fingerprint verify call.

## Files
- internal/pipeline/foreach.go::executeForeach
- internal/pipeline/foreach_test.go (new regression)
close_reason: Fixed: extended bd-3awat fingerprint protection to foreach: syntax. computeForeachItemsFingerprint now runs on plan items at executeForeach entry, with verifyForeachItemsFingerprint refusing drift and recordForeachItemsFingerprint persisting the hash. Tests TestForeach_ItemsDriftDetectedOnResume and TestForeach_FingerprintRecordedOnFirstRun pass; full pipeline -race -short suite green. Files: internal/pipeline/foreach.go:104-126, internal/pipeline/foreach_drift_regression_test.go (new)

title: [MEDIUM] resume pruning leaves stale steps.* variables for removed steps
description: Review of f97f184c found that applyResumeState deletes persisted step results when graph.MarkExecuted(stepID) fails, but it does not call clearStepVariables for those removed/orphan step IDs. Substitutor.resolveSteps checks state.Variables["steps.<id>.<field>"] before consulting state.Steps, so a removed step can still resolve through stale flat variables such as steps.old.output or steps.old.data. Impact: after resuming a changed workflow, prompts/conditions can consume ghost outputs from steps no longer present in the dependency graph, masking missing-step errors and driving execution with stale data. Existing bd-98sd7 tracks the silent deletion/audit issue; this bead is the behavioral stale-variable leak. Fix by adding MarkExecuted-failed step IDs to the cleanup list (or otherwise clearing their steps.* variables) and add a regression where an orphan completed step with steps.orphan.output is pruned and ${steps.orphan.output} no longer resolves.
close_reason: applyResumeState now tracks orphan step IDs (those failing graph.MarkExecuted) separately and calls clearStepVariables on them so the flat steps.<id>.output and steps.<id>.data variables are purged alongside the StepResult itself. Downstream substitutions can no longer resolve through ghost outputs from steps removed by a workflow rename. Added TestApplyResumeStateClearsOrphanStepVariables.

title: Add ntm respawn command to kill-and-restart worker agents by pane number
[HIGH] by_model_family_difference treats Gemini pane variants as cross-family
description:
Review of 144a013a ([bug-fix][bd-7k7ie] normalize verbose author_model to pane family vocabulary) found that the new model-family normalization still compares exact pane ModelFamily strings after mapping the author's family to one token. pane metadata can store Gemini panes as the bare variant "pro" when no model tag is present (see internal/pipeline/pane_metadata_test.go), but modelFamilyGroup only recognizes gmi/gemini/google-style names.

Repro shape:
- strategyPanes: [{ID:"p1", ModelFamily:"pro"}, {ID:"p2", ModelFamily:"cod"}]
- item: {author_model:"gemini-pro"}
- foreachAuthorModelFamilyForPanes maps the item to canonical "gmi" because no pane ModelFamily groups as Gemini.
- byModelFamilyDifference exact-compares pane.ModelFamily != "gmi" and selects p1, even though p1 is the same Gemini family.

Impact: by_model_family_difference can silently assign Gemini-authored debate/devil's-advocate work back to a Gemini pane, defeating the cross-family routing contract and biasing fan-out results. This is separate from the Claude-specific variant gap in bd-2sk2c.

Expected: compare normalized model-family groups instead of exact strings, or classify common Gemini pane variants such as pro/flash/ultra consistently with gmi. Add a regression where author_model=gemini-pro with panes {pro,cod} selects the cod pane.
close_reason: Extended modelFamilyGroup to recognize Gemini variant names (pro, flash, ultra) and prefixes (flash*, ultra*) as the gemini family. mapModelFamilyToPaneVocabulary now resolves an item with author_model='gemini-pro' against panes [pro, cod] to the matching pane vocabulary 'pro', so byModelFamilyDifference correctly routes to the cod pane instead of returning the same-family Gemini-variant pane. Added TestSelectForeachPaneModelFamilyDifferenceTreatsGeminiVariantsAsSameFamily covering all three variants.

title: [LOW] swarmslo: computeAckLatencies counts pending acks but discards the count via '_ = pending', contradicting docstring promise to surface them in Warnings
description:
In internal/swarmslo/swarmslo.go computeAckLatencies (commit f6740fa6, bd-3v1gs.7), the function counts unacked ack-required messages but never surfaces the count anywhere:

  func computeAckLatencies(events []MailEvent) Distribution {
    var seconds []float64
    pending := 0
    for _, m := range events {
      if !m.AckRequired { continue }
      if m.AckedAt == nil {
        pending++
        continue
      }
      ...
    }
    d := distributionFromSeconds(seconds)
    // Pending is recorded out-of-band in the metric; surfacing it as
    // a Distribution field would be misleading because it is a count
    // of *unobserved* latencies, not a sample.
    _ = pending
    return d
  }

The comment says 'recorded out-of-band' but there is no out-of-band recording — pending is computed and explicitly discarded. The Compute caller has no way to learn it. The package's own docstring on this branch (visible in the commit body for f6740fa6) describes the contract as 'Unacked ack-required messages are surfaced as count-of-pending in Warnings.' That promise is unfulfilled: Summary.Warnings only carries missing-source notices, never the pending-ack count.

Failure mode: an operator dashboard rendering swarmslo's output sees TimeToFirstAck.Count=N (acks measured) and assumes N is the full population. Pending-ack messages — exactly the ones the operator most needs to see, because they represent unanswered coordination — are invisible. A swarm with 0 acked + 50 pending reports an identical envelope to a swarm with 0 messages at all.

Suggested fix (smallest behavior change):

  - Add Pending int field on Distribution (json:'pending,omitempty'),
    set on the TimeToFirstAck distribution from the pending counter
    here. Other distributions stay zero. The 'pending' name stays
    semantically narrow to acks; it doesn't apply to ready→claim or
    claim→close.

  - OR append a warning when pending > 0 so the existing Warnings
    surface carries it: 'time_to_first_ack: %d ack-required
    messages still pending'. Honors the docstring's existing
    'surfaced ... in Warnings' phrasing without expanding the
    Distribution shape.

Either fix should ship with a regression test that asserts a fixture
with 3 acked + 5 pending produces a non-zero pending count (or a
matching warning) — the existing pending counter is currently
untestable because the value never escapes the function.

Severity LOW: no false numbers — the count and percentiles for
acked messages are accurate. But the dropped pending count is the
exact signal the SLO surface exists to expose, and the docstring
already promises it.

Source: internal/swarmslo/swarmslo.go computeAckLatencies (~line 141), commit f6740fa6 (bd-3v1gs.7).
close_reason: Added Distribution.Pending int (json:'pending,omitempty') and threaded the previously-discarded pending counter from computeAckLatencies onto the returned distribution. Removed the misleading '_ = pending' discard and the stale 'recorded out-of-band' comment so a future maintainer doesn't reintroduce the loss. Three regression tests pin the contract: TimeToFirstAck.Pending equals ack-required+nil count (excludes non-ack-required pending), zero Pending omits the JSON field entirely (back-compat for existing consumers), all-pending fixture distinguishes itself from empty-input via Count=0/Pending=N. Other distributions stay at Pending=0 (no pending concept). Existing tests stay green. Commit: 9887491d. rch exec -- go build ./cmd/ntm and rch exec -- go test -short ./internal/swarmslo/... both pass.

title: Add ntm send --randomize - randomize order of individualized prompts to avoid thundering herd on same files
description:
## Overview
Add --randomize flag to ntm send to randomize the order of individualized prompts, avoiding thundering herd problems when multiple agents start working on overlapping files.

## Problem
When sending individualized prompts (e.g., each agent gets a different bead), agents often start simultaneously on related files. This causes:
- Git conflicts when multiple agents edit the same area
- File reservation conflicts in Agent Mail
- Wasted work from merge conflicts

## Solution
`ntm send myproject --randomize` shuffles the order of prompts before sending.

## Implementation
```go
func randomizePrompts(prompts []Prompt) []Prompt {
    shuffled := make([]Prompt, len(prompts))
    copy(shuffled, prompts)
    rand.Shuffle(len(shuffled), func(i, j int) {
        shuffled[i], shuffled[j] = shuffled[j], shuffled[i]
    })
    return shuffled
}
```

## CLI Examples
```bash
# Randomize prompt order
ntm send myproject --randomize

# Combine with batch
ntm send myproject --batch prompts.txt --randomize

# Combine with delay for extra staggering  
ntm send myproject --randomize --delay 2s
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Prompts shuffled before sending
- [ ] Deterministic seed option for reproducibility (--seed=N)
- [ ] Works with --batch and --distribute
- [ ] Logging shows shuffle order
- [ ] No effect if only one prompt

## Tests Required
- Unit test: Shuffle produces different order
- Unit test: Seed produces reproducible order
- E2E test: Randomized batch send
notes:
## Testing Requirements
- Unit tests: core logic, error paths, edge cases.
- E2E scripts: full CLI/robot flow with detailed log/slog prefixes (e.g., [E2E-<AREA>]) and include session/agent/bead IDs.
- If structured outputs are affected, assert schema stability + deterministic ordering.

title: ideation ranker normalizeRankOptions cannot express NextLimit=0
description: In internal/ideation/ranker.go normalizeRankOptions, NextLimit==0 is treated as 'unset' and rewritten to DefaultRankOptions().NextLimit (10). A caller who wants the ranker to emit only the top selected slice and no NextBest candidates cannot express that — passing 0 silently bumps to 10. (Same shape as bd-9vp55 for DefaultPriority.) Fix: use a sentinel outside [0, top of int] for unset (e.g., < 0) and only override when negative; treat 0 as a valid user request.
close_reason: Removed the second 'NextLimit==0 → default' coercion in normalizeRankOptions. Now NextLimit < 0 is the only 'unset' sentinel and 0 is honored verbatim, so callers can request top-only output. All existing call sites (DefaultRankOptions, ranker_test.go, corpus_test.go) either use the default 10 or pass an explicit positive value, so the behavior change is contained. Added TestNormalizeRankOptionsHonorsExplicitNextLimitZero.
