comments.text: Sensitivity follow-up: the normative example corpus must now include visible, preview_only, redacted, withheld, and hashed-evidence scenarios across snapshot, digest, attention, inspect, streaming, and replay so disclosure behavior is just as concrete as freshness or boundedness behavior.

title: robot-redesign/contracts: define deterministic ordering, truncation, pagination, and payload-budget semantics
description: Define how robot surfaces stay deterministic, bounded, and token-efficient when the underlying system gets large or noisy. This task exists because the redesign only improves real user experience if snapshot, status, digest, attention, and inspect outputs remain predictable and explainable instead of silently growing without bound or changing order run to run.
design:
The contract should specify stable ordering keys for major collections, explicit truncation markers, pagination or continuation semantics for large sections, default and maximum detail limits per surface, and how surfaces point operators toward inspect drill-down instead of stuffing everything into bootstrap payloads. It should also define payload-size and latency guardrails that downstream implementation and validation can treat as design budgets, plus how omission or compression is signaled across JSON, TOON, markdown, terse, REST, and streaming views.

The goal is not to hard-code arbitrary tiny limits. The goal is to make boundedness, determinism, and explainable omission part of the product contract rather than accidental behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
Produce a self-contained contract for ordering, truncation, pagination, and payload budgeting that downstream surface, registry, transport, and validation tasks can implement directly.

The result must make it obvious how consumers should interpret incomplete or compressed views, how large result sets are continued safely, and how future regressions in size or ordering will be detected.
notes: Fast, bounded, diff-friendly output is part of correctness for robot mode. If a surface can silently reorder items, silently drop context, or explode in size under routine use, this task is incomplete.

title: robot-redesign/contracts: define action-handoff, remediation, and error semantics
description: Define how robot surfaces communicate machine-actionable follow-up steps and recoverable failure modes. This task exists because the redesign only becomes truly agent-ergonomic if consumers can move from snapshot or attention to the right next command, and can recover from invalid cursor, expired replay window, invalid inspect target, unavailable source, or bounded-result conditions without guesswork.
design: The contract should define a stable machine-readable shape for next_actions or remediation hints across success and failure paths, plus an error taxonomy for conditions such as invalid cursor, expired replay window, invalid inspect target, unavailable source, unsupported transport feature, truncated or paginated result, duplicate or ambiguous request, and partial or degraded data. It should specify which failures are retryable, which require resync or a different follow-up surface, how structured follow-up commands or action descriptors are expressed, when a client should reuse an existing request or idempotency key versus mint a new one, and how these semantics stay aligned across CLI JSON, REST, SSE, WebSocket, and alternate renderers. The goal is not to wrap every response in bureaucracy. The goal is to make recovery, drill-down, and actuation handoff explicit enough that an agent does not have to reverse-engineer what to do next from human prose.
acceptance_criteria: Produce a self-contained contract for action handoff, remediation hints, recoverable error semantics, and safe retry expectations that downstream surfaces, transports, registry metadata, and validation tasks can implement directly. The result must make it obvious how consumers recover from common failure modes, how they move from summary to drill-down or actuation, and how those follow-up semantics remain stable across transports and formats.
notes: If an agent still has to guess whether to retry, resync, paginate, inspect, or switch commands after reading a response, this task is incomplete.

title: robot-redesign/contracts: define explainability, evidence, and diagnostic semantics
description: Define how robot surfaces explain why data are stale, degraded, truncated, prioritized, or escalated so operators can trust and debug the system without source-code archaeology. This task exists because freshness metadata and remediation hints tell consumers what is wrong and what to do next, but the redesign still needs a first-class way to explain why the system reached that state.
design:
The contract should define stable machine-readable explanation and evidence shapes at section and item granularity. It should cover degraded-source reasons, last successful collection context, omission and truncation causes, cursor invalidation or resync evidence, incident-promotion evidence, attention-prioritization evidence, and how compact explanation handles link to deeper inspect flows.

The goal is not raw debug spam or per-field provenance. The goal is targeted operational explainability: enough structured evidence that an agent or human can answer why is this stale, degraded, truncated, open, or prioritized and can see where deeper evidence lives without grepping logs.
acceptance_criteria:
Produce a self-contained explainability and evidence contract that downstream surfaces, registry metadata, docs, and validation tasks can implement directly.

The result must make it obvious how consumers learn why a robot surface made a claim or hid detail, how shallow explanation handles differ from deeper drill-down, and how these semantics stay stable across transports and renderers.
notes: Explainability here means operational clarity, not hand-wavy AI rationalization. If a future operator still has to inspect raw logs or read code to understand a first-class surface decision, this task is incomplete.

title: robot-redesign/contracts: define stable resource references and cross-surface identity semantics
description: Define stable resource-reference and cross-surface identity semantics so agents can correlate sessions, panes, agents, work items, incidents, attention items, diagnostic handles, and action targets across snapshot, digest, attention, inspect, REST, and streaming transports without guessing from display text. This task exists because the redesign still lacks an explicit contract for how machine consumers join one surface to another or hold onto a target across retries, pagination, truncation, and follow-up actions.
design:
The contract should define canonical machine-readable references for major operator-facing entities such as sessions, panes, agents, work items, coordination items, incidents, attention items, diagnostic handles, and actuation targets. It should specify which references are durable versus ephemeral, how references relate to schema payloads and inspect lookup keys, how they behave when an entity disappears or is superseded, and how inline summary surfaces carry enough reference material to let consumers drill down or act without text matching.

The goal is not to invent a baroque URI framework. The goal is to ensure agents can safely correlate data across surfaces, transports, truncation boundaries, and action loops using stable references instead of brittle titles, labels, or positional assumptions.
acceptance_criteria:
Produce a self-contained reference and identity contract that downstream action-handoff, diagnostics, surfaces, registry metadata, parity work, docs, and validation tasks can implement directly.

The result must make it obvious how consumers correlate one payload with another, how follow-up commands target the correct entity, how references survive bounded-output behavior, and how invalid or stale references are reported.
notes: If a future agent still has to join snapshot, attention, inspect, and actuation flows using human-readable names or positional indexes, this task is incomplete.

title: robot-redesign/sqlite: runtime projection and persistence layer
description: Extend ntm's existing SQLite state layer to persist derived robot-mode facts such as runtime projections, source health, attention events, incidents, and output watermarks. This epic exists because the redesign needs restart-safe, replay-safe, projection-driven state without abandoning SQLite or creating a parallel storage story.
design: The key design principle is that SQLite stores derived and cached robot facts, not the ultimate ground truth of tmux or external tools. The persistent layer must therefore be explicit about freshness, provenance mode, recomputation, and invalidation.\n\nThis epic also owns write-amplification discipline: the redesign should not win nicer outputs at the cost of a noisy or fragile state store.
acceptance_criteria: This epic is complete when ntm has durable tables, migrations, store APIs, recomputation paths, and retention rules that can support the shared projection model, persistent attention journal, and incident system.
notes: Do not import ideas from vibe_cockpit's DuckDB layer. The transferable lesson is normalized projections and freshness semantics, not the underlying engine.
close_reason: All sqlite/runtime-store child beads bd-j9jo3.2.1 through bd-j9jo3.2.5 are closed; the epic is implementation-complete and should not stay open as a faux actionable item.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Future self: if a problem seems easier to solve by dropping a separate analytical database into ntm, assume that instinct is wrong until proven otherwise.

title: robot-redesign/sqlite: design runtime tables and migration plan
description: Design the SQLite schema that will hold runtime projections, source health, persistent attention events, incidents, and output watermarks. This task exists to make the persistent layer intentional rather than letting tables accrete around the first implementation that happens to work.
design: The schema should separate durable source-of-truth state from derived robot-facing runtime state. It should describe table purposes, keys, indexes, retention boundaries, and the relationship between projection rows, source_health rows, attention events, incidents, and watermark/baseline tables.\n\nIt should also explain how migrations will be introduced safely into ntm's existing SQLite state store without pretending the new runtime data are equivalent to tmux truth.
acceptance_criteria: Produce a concrete migration-ready table design with clear ownership for runtime_sessions, runtime_agents, runtime_work, runtime_coordination, runtime_quota, source_health, attention_events, incidents, and output_watermarks or equivalent structures.\n\nThe result must be explicit enough for store APIs and tests to proceed without re-litigating the data model.
notes: Be conservative about schema complexity, but not simplistic. The goal is a durable projection substrate that can survive restart, replay, and parity work without needing a second database later.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Future self: this is where the SQLite-only constraint gets turned into a real architecture instead of a slogan.

title: robot-redesign/sqlite: implement store APIs and migration plumbing for runtime state
description: Implement the store and migration plumbing needed to read and write the new runtime projection tables. This task exists so later builders and surfaces talk to typed storage APIs instead of writing SQL ad hoc throughout the codebase.
design: The store layer should make projection writes, source-health updates, watermark persistence, incident persistence, and journal appends feel like first-class ntm operations. It should also enforce transactional boundaries that let projection recompute and event publication happen coherently.\n\nThe design should avoid leaking SQL details into unrelated robot packages.
acceptance_criteria: This task is complete when ntm has typed store methods and migrations for the new runtime state, and downstream tasks can persist and query projections without inventing their own schema access patterns.
notes: A good outcome here reduces future drift and makes restart-safe behavior testable. A bad outcome spreads SQL around the robot and server packages and recreates today's duplication in a different form.
close_reason: Verified implemented in runtime_store.go (1956 lines) + 007_runtime.sql migration. Store APIs: Session (Upsert/Get/Delete), Agent (Upsert/GetBySession/Delete), Work (Upsert/Get/List), Coordination (Upsert/Get/List), Quota (Upsert/Get/List), SourceHealth (Upsert/Get/GetDegraded), AttentionEvent (Append/GetSince/ReplayWindow), Incident (Create/Get/List/UpdateStatus), Watermark (Get/Set), Audit (Record/History/Trace). Both Store and Tx transaction variants. Full projection persistence layer with typed APIs.

title: robot-redesign/sqlite: build projection recompute/orchestration pipeline
description: Build the orchestration path that takes normalized adapter outputs and writes a coherent runtime projection into SQLite. This task exists because the projection model only helps if ntm has one disciplined place where derived state is assembled and committed.
design: The projection pipeline should define when recomputation happens, what counts as a full versus partial refresh, how related sections are committed transactionally, and how downstream consumers find a coherent latest view.\n\nThis is also the task that should decide whether some sections are materialized eagerly, lazily, or on-demand, provided the external contract remains crisp.
acceptance_criteria: This task is complete when ntm can build and persist a coherent runtime projection from normalized inputs, with clear recompute semantics and atomic visibility for consumers.
notes: The builder should make later surfaces thinner, not more magical. If surface code still has to reconstruct core relationships, this task is incomplete.
close_reason: Implemented normalized projection refresh/orchestration with transactional persistence for runtime_work, runtime_coordination, runtime_quota, source_health, runtime_sessions, and runtime_agents; verified with focused robot tests and targeted compile probes.

title: robot-redesign/sqlite: define retention, pruning, and read/write amplification guardrails
description: Define the retention, pruning, update-frequency, and read-path cost rules that keep the SQLite runtime layer healthy under continuous robot and server use. This task exists to ensure the redesign stays operationally cheap rather than quietly turning the state DB into a churny log sink or a slow query bottleneck.
design:
The task should address which runtime sections are snapshots versus append-only journals, how long attention events and incidents are retained, how watermarks are compacted, how projection recompute avoids rewriting everything on every poll, and what indexing or query-shape guardrails keep frequent summary and replay reads efficient.

The goal is not premature micro-optimization; it is preventing obvious write amplification, pathological read fanout, and unbounded growth.
acceptance_criteria: This task is complete when future implementers have explicit rules for pruning, bounded retention, update cadence, and read-path expectations, and when the SQLite layer has a documented stance on avoiding unnecessary rewrites and expensive routine queries.
notes: Guardrails belong in the design, not as an afterthought discovered after the DB has already become noisy or slow under realistic operator polling.
close_reason: Completed: codified runtime retention and pruning guardrails with RunGC(DefaultRuntimeGCConfig()), added bounded stale snapshot/source-health cleanup, documented the operational cadence/read-path rules, and made runtime_quota usage percentages explicit via used_pct_known plus used_pct_source.

title: robot-redesign/sqlite: persist audit trail, actor attribution, and decision-history primitives
description: Persist the audit primitives that let ntm reconstruct who changed what, when, and why across operator overrides, actuation loops, incident lifecycle changes, and disclosure-control decisions.
design: The implementation should extend the SQLite runtime layer with a bounded, queryable audit trail keyed strongly enough to join with stable entity references, request IDs, incident fingerprints, and disclosure metadata. It should decide what gets persisted as full audit events versus compact summaries, how actor identifiers and origin classes are stored, how retention and pruning behave, how sensitive content is excluded or transformed inside the audit trail, and how store APIs make audit writes a normal part of attention-state changes, actuation outcomes, incident transitions, and redaction or disclosure decisions rather than an optional afterthought. This work should preserve trust and replay utility without creating an unbounded append-only swamp.
acceptance_criteria: This task is complete when ntm has typed SQLite primitives and retention-aware persistence for actor-attributed audit events and decision history, and downstream tasks can attach trustworthy audit records to operator overrides, actuation loops, incident changes, replay flows, and disclosure-control behavior without inventing their own side logs.
notes: A useful audit trail is concise, queryable, and correlated. If it is so vague that it cannot answer who changed this and why, or so noisy that nobody will consult it, this task is incomplete.
close_reason: Verified implemented. AuditEvent struct (runtime_schema.go:467-506) has full actor attribution (ActorType, ActorID, ActorOrigin), request correlation (RequestID, CorrelationID), event classification (Category, EventType, Severity), entity tracking (EntityType, EntityID), state changes (PreviousState, NewState, ChangeSummary), decision context (Reason, Evidence, DisclosureState), retention (RetentionClass, ExpiresAt). Store APIs: RecordAuditEvent, GetActorActivity, GetAuditHistory, GetRequestTrace, GCExpiredAuditEvents. AuditActor for actor correlation. Full audit trail implementation.

title: robot-redesign/adapters: normalize live sources into shared projections
description: Build the source adapters that translate tmux state, process telemetry, beads/bv, Agent Mail, conflicts, handoff data, quota, alerts, and health signals into the canonical projection model. This epic exists because the shared projection layer only helps if all major robot-relevant inputs are normalized consistently.
design: Adapters should hide source-specific weirdness and emit section-shaped data plus freshness/degraded metadata. They should not leak the old command-local assembly model upward.\n\nThe intent is to make later surfaces project the same underlying model regardless of whether they are rendered as JSON, TOON, markdown, terse summaries, REST payloads, or dashboard sections.
acceptance_criteria: This epic is complete when the projection builder can consume normalized adapter outputs for all major robot-relevant domains and populate source_health deterministically.
notes: Adapters are where we keep ntm tmux-first: tmux and session reality still drive the system, but every consumer sees that reality through a stable normalized shape.
close_reason: All adapter child beads bd-j9jo3.3.1 through bd-j9jo3.3.5 are closed; keeping the epic open was only polluting planning views.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Future self: adapter code should absorb source idiosyncrasies so the rest of the system does not have to memorize how each upstream tool misbehaves.

title: robot-redesign/adapters: build tmux/session/agent/process normalization adapter
description: Normalize tmux session, pane, agent, process, and output-activity data into the canonical projection shape. This task exists because tmux is still the core source of truth for ntm, but consumers should no longer have to understand tmux's raw quirks directly.
design: The adapter should unify pane/session inspection, process telemetry, activity signals, context telemetry, and agent-type detection into one stable shape. It should also define how raw pane identifiers, output timestamps, and process-derived fields map into runtime_sessions and runtime_agents.\n\nThis task should explicitly preserve ntm's tmux-first nature while insulating the rest of the robot stack from tmux-specific mechanics.
acceptance_criteria: This task is complete when tmux-derived runtime session and agent data can be produced in the canonical projection shape, with enough fidelity to drive snapshot, status, and attention surfaces.
notes: If later surfaces still reach directly into tmux packages for core state assembly, this adapter task has not gone far enough.
close_reason: Verified implemented in tmux_adapter.go (references bd-j9jo3.3.1 in header). TmuxAdapter normalizes tmux data to RuntimeSession/RuntimeAgent. Key methods: NormalizeSession(tmux.Session→RuntimeSession, line 84), NormalizeSessions (line 149), NormalizeAgent(Agent→RuntimeAgent, line 164), NormalizeAgents (line 214). Classifies agent state, maps pane identifiers, handles output timestamps and process fields. Acceptance criteria met: tmux-derived data in canonical projection shape.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: This adapter is the spine of the redesign. If it stays ad hoc, everything above it will stay ad hoc too.

title: robot-redesign/adapters: build work and coordination normalization adapter
description: Normalize work and coordination signals such as beads/bv state, Agent Mail unread/backlog state, file conflicts, reservation conflicts, and handoff context into shared projection sections. This task exists because operator pain often comes from coordination state rather than from tmux state alone.
design: The adapter should produce stable work and coordination sections that can answer questions like: what is ready, what is blocked, who has unread mail, where are reservation conflicts, what is the current handoff summary, and which coordination problems deserve attention.\n\nThe implementation should hide the peculiarities of each source tool so later surfaces can reason about coordination with one vocabulary.
acceptance_criteria: This task is complete when work and coordination sections can be populated from beads/bv, Agent Mail, tracker/conflict data, and handoff data without leaking each tool's bespoke output model upward.
notes: This adapter is where the redesign becomes more agent-intuitive than today's scattered bridge commands.
close_reason: Verified implemented in work_coordination.go. WorkSection (lines 28-62) normalizes beads/bv with Ready/Blocked/InProgress/Summary/Triage. CoordinationSection (lines 91-140) normalizes: MailSummary (Agent Mail unread/backlog), ReservationsSummary (file reservation pressure), HandoffSummary (handoff context). Adapter methods: summarizeMail, summarizeReservations, summarizeHandoff, collectCoordinationProblems. All acceptance criteria met: beads/bv, Agent Mail, tracker/conflict data, handoff data unified under one vocabulary.

title: robot-redesign/adapters: build system, quota, alert, and health normalization adapter
description: Normalize non-tmux operational signals such as quota pressure, health checks, alerts, and system-level warnings into shared projection sections. This task exists because operator decisions require a coherent operational picture, not just pane state plus occasional bespoke warnings.
design: The adapter should define how health summaries, rate-limit signals, quota warnings, crash/restart state, and system degradation are represented in stable sections and reason codes.\n\nIt should also ensure those signals can later promote into incidents instead of remaining forever as disconnected ephemeral warnings.
acceptance_criteria: This task is complete when global operational signals can be surfaced in the projection model with stable section names and reason-code-friendly data.
notes: If a future consumer has to parse free-form alert text to understand quota or health state, this adapter task has failed.

title: robot-redesign/adapters: compute source_health, freshness, and degraded feature state
description: Compute source_health and degraded-feature information from all major adapters so every later surface can explain what is fresh, stale, partial, or unavailable. This task exists because freshness semantics must be produced systematically, not improvised by each renderer.
design: The implementation should take adapter outputs plus failure states and emit section-level freshness and degradation metadata according to the contract defined earlier. It should decide how partial refreshes are represented, how source outages affect downstream sections, and how degraded features are advertised without drowning the response in noise.\n\nThis task is the bridge between adapter mechanics and trustworthy operator-facing semantics.
acceptance_criteria: This task is complete when runtime projections carry deterministic source_health and degraded feature state for all major sections and when later surfaces can reuse that data verbatim.
notes: A surface should not have to decide on its own whether data are fresh or degraded. That decision belongs here.
close_reason: Implemented in normalize.go: ComputeSourceHealth() for deterministic freshness/degradation from adapter results, ComputeDegradedFeatures() for feature impact mapping. SignalAggregator.Collect() now auto-computes source health. 7 tests added and passing.

title: robot-redesign/adapters: implement redaction, safe previews, and disclosure metadata across normalized sources
description: Implement the source-side and projection-side redaction path that lets ntm expose richer robot data without leaking secrets or sensitive text into live surfaces, durable projections, or replay artifacts.
design: The implementation should introduce a disciplined disclosure-control layer in the normalization pipeline. It should decide where text and structured payloads are classified and sanitized before persistence or projection, how pane tails, mail snippets, diagnostic evidence, actuation arguments or outcomes, and replay snapshots produce safe previews instead of raw sensitive blobs, and how disclosure metadata such as redaction markers, rule versions, hashed evidence handles, and counts of hidden material are carried into the shared model. It should also decide whether and how ntm keeps a lightweight redaction audit trail in SQLite so diagnostics, docs, and tests can verify that sensitive material was transformed rather than silently dropped. This work should preserve operator usefulness: evidence should remain explainable and correlatable even when the raw content is hidden.
acceptance_criteria: This task is complete when normalized robot-visible source data can flow through ntm with deterministic redaction or disclosure-control behavior, safe previews where appropriate, explicit machine-readable markers for hidden or transformed content, and enough auditability that replay, diagnostics, and validation can prove the system did the safe thing rather than merely omitting data.
notes: If secrets can still slip from tmux output, mail content, diagnostic evidence, or replay artifacts into robot surfaces without an explicit and testable disclosure decision, this task is incomplete.
close_reason: Completed after follow-up fix: persisted sanitized handoff summary plus disclosure metadata in runtime_handoff, surfaced it through projection-backed status, and added runtime/status persistence coverage.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Reopened: Reopened after fresh review: handoff disclosure metadata is still adapter-only and not durably projected or surfaced via projection-backed status.

title: robot-redesign/attention: persistent journal, replay, and cursor semantics
description: Persist the attention journal and related output/activity watermarks so ntm's operator loop survives process restarts and exposes replay-safe, cursor-safe deltas across CLI and server transports. This epic exists because the attention loop is already the best direction in ntm, but it still needs durable mechanics to become the true center of the robot interface.
design: The intended outcome is a durable event stream with stable cursor semantics, bounded retention, deterministic replay, explicit resync behavior, and enough persisted output/activity context to compute deltas even after ntm restarts.\n\nThis epic also owns transport parity: replay semantics should not diverge between CLI JSON, REST, SSE, and WebSocket consumers.
acceptance_criteria: This epic is complete when events, digest, and attention can operate over durable journal state instead of volatile in-memory-only assumptions.
notes: The attention feed should become more central, not more magical. It remains a sensing and triage surface, not a hidden planner.
close_reason: All child tasks completed by swarm

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Future self: the operator loop is the product. Treat any cursor ambiguity, replay drift, or restart breakage as a first-order defect.

title: robot-redesign/attention: implement SQLite-backed attention event store and cursor model
description: Implement the durable event store and cursor model that back ntm's replay-safe attention loop. This task exists because a central product promise of the redesign is that attention, events, and digest survive process restarts and expose stable delta semantics.
design: The design should define event identity, cursor generation, retention windows, replay ordering, and how durable journal state relates to runtime projections and source health. The implementation should make cursor expiration and resync explicit instead of leaving them as accidental behavior.\n\nThis task should also preserve the existing attention-feed intent while upgrading its durability and transport neutrality.
acceptance_criteria: This task is complete when ntm can append and replay durable attention events from SQLite with stable ordering and explicit cursor semantics that later digest/attention/transport tasks can rely on.
notes: Treat the cursor model as contract-critical. If it is vague, every delta consumer becomes brittle.
close_reason: Verified already implemented. AttentionStore interface (attention_feed.go:21-34) with AppendAttentionEvent, GetAttentionEventsSince, GetAttentionReplayWindow, GetLatestEventCursor, GCExpiredEvents. SQLite implementation (runtime_store.go:1024-1163) with INSERT INTO attention_events, cursor model, replay window queries, GC. CursorAllocator for monotonic cursors. AttentionFeedConfig with JournalSize, RetentionPeriod, HeartbeatInterval.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Future self: this task is where the current good attention-feed direction becomes restart-safe infrastructure instead of a clever in-memory convenience.

title: robot-redesign/attention: publish durable events from adapters and monitors
description: Emit durable attention events from the normalized adapters and monitoring logic instead of synthesizing them only in ad hoc surface code. This task exists because the durable journal only matters if source changes and operator-significant events are published consistently at the right seam.
design: The publication model should define which normalized changes become events, which categories and reason codes they carry, how duplicate/noisy events are suppressed, and which events remain background versus action-required.\n\nThis is where we make event production systematic rather than letting each renderer invent its own idea of what changed.
acceptance_criteria: This task is complete when major normalized sources can publish durable attention events with stable categories, reason codes, and actionability semantics into the SQLite journal.
notes: If event meaning still depends on where you read it from, this task is incomplete.
close_reason: Normalized adapters already published durable attention; PT monitor callbacks now bridge into the durable attention journal with stable PT reason codes, actionability, dedup windows, and repo-wide verification (go build ./cmd/ntm, go test -short ./..., golangci-lint run).

title: robot-redesign/attention: persist output/activity watermarks for restart-safe deltas
description: Persist the output and activity baselines needed to compute deltas across restarts and refresh boundaries. This task exists because output-derived activity and stall semantics are much less trustworthy if they reset whenever ntm itself restarts.
design: The design should specify what is persisted per pane/agent, how hash or line-count baselines are maintained, how buffer wrap/reset is handled, and how those baselines feed both runtime projections and event publication.\n\nThis task should also make explicit which baselines are durable versus ephemeral cache-only accelerators.
acceptance_criteria: This task is complete when output/activity delta computation can survive ntm process restarts without collapsing into unknown state or spurious activity transitions.
notes: The purpose is restart-safe semantics, not perfect eternal scrollback knowledge. Persist only what materially improves delta correctness.
close_reason: Implemented restart-safe output/activity baselines: WatermarkStore interface, WithWatermarkStore option, first-sample baseline (charsAdded=0), post-restart hash-match (uses stored rune count), post-restart hash-mismatch (buffer reset, charsAdded=0), velocity=0 across restart boundary. 11 focused tests pass.

title: robot-redesign/attention: align replay, resync, and degraded semantics across transports
description: Make sure CLI replay, REST replay, SSE streams, and WebSocket event delivery all share the same cursor, resync, and degraded-state semantics. This task exists because transport-specific drift would undermine trust in the operator loop even if the core event store is correct.
design: The work should describe and implement how cursor expiry, replay windows, degraded event publication, deduplicated or suppressed item semantics, resurfacing after cooldown, operator acknowledgment or snooze state, pin or escalation state, request-correlation or retry semantics, resync hints, and recoverable error semantics appear across transports. Consumers should be able to switch transport without re-learning what a cursor means, how a degraded source is reported, how an aggregated or snoozed attention item behaves, or how to recover from a stale, duplicated, or unsupported request. This task makes the event-store contract portable rather than CLI-only.
acceptance_criteria: This task is complete when replay, resync, degraded-state, aggregation, operator-attention-state, and request-correlation behavior are semantically aligned across all supported transports and documented strongly enough for parity tests to pin them down.
notes: Operator loop moved here after closing bd-j9jo3.4.7. Starting bounded parity pass across CLI/REST/SSE/WebSocket replay-resync-degraded semantics.
close_reason: Aligned attention replay cursor-expired semantics across REST/SSE with the robot contract by replacing legacy resync_hint payloads with machine-readable resync_command sourced from CursorExpiredDetails; focused serve tests, go build ./cmd/ntm, go test -short ./..., golangci-lint run, and touched-file format/import checks are green.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Watch-semantics follow-up: transport alignment explicitly includes heartbeat cadence, replay-to-live transition markers, filtered subscription behavior, unsupported-selector handling, and the distinction between durable material events and ephemeral keepalives.

title: robot-redesign/attention: publish actuation outcomes and closed-loop verification events
description: Publish durable actuation-outcome and reconciliation events so the operator loop becomes closed-loop rather than hopeful. This task exists because once ntm points agents toward existing control commands, the system also needs a first-class way to tell them whether a request started, succeeded, partially applied, timed out, was superseded, or still needs verification.
design: The work should define how existing robot control commands emit or correlate durable events representing request receipt, request or correlation ID and idempotency semantics where applicable, target reference, expected effect, observed effect, timeout or supersession, and final verification state. It should distinguish direct command execution results from later observed convergence in runtime state, define pending versus confirmed versus failed versus unknown outcomes, and explain how these outcome events appear in digest, attention, diagnostics, and parity transports. This task should improve operator confidence without inventing hidden planner behavior. The system already has explicit actuation commands; the missing piece is trustworthy feedback and reconciliation.
acceptance_criteria: This task is complete when the attention journal and related surfaces can represent actuation requests plus later outcome or reconciliation evidence strongly enough that consumers know whether to proceed, wait, retry, inspect, or escalate, and can correlate that evidence back to the originating request without guesswork. The result must make write-loop verification a first-class part of the operator story rather than a side effect inferred from unrelated state diffs.
notes: If an agent still has to grep output or manually diff snapshots to decide whether its own command actually worked, this task is incomplete.
close_reason: Completed: added first-class actuation requested/outcome/verified attention events with request/correlation/idempotency metadata across send, send+ack, interrupt, and REST propagation; verified with targeted tests plus go build ./cmd/ntm, go test -short ./..., and golangci-lint run.

title: robot-redesign/attention: implement deduplication, aggregation, cooldown, and saturation policies
description: Implement the attention-hygiene layer that turns durable events into an operator-usable queue instead of a stream of repetitive churn. This task exists because even a correct durable journal will feel hostile if repeated source flaps, restarts, unread-mail bursts, or ongoing degraded states spam digest and attention with near-duplicate items.
design: The work should define and implement how repeated events are deduplicated or rolled up, how cooldown and resurfacing windows work, how persistent conditions escalate from repeated attention items into incidents, how actuation-outcome events and diagnostic evidence are merged into existing items, how operator acknowledgment, snooze, mute, and pin state interact with automatic ranking, and how bounded attention budgets prefer the most decision-relevant items without hiding important recurrence. It should make suppression, aggregation, and operator overrides explainable rather than silent so operators can still tell why an item appeared once, changed severity, stayed hidden, or re-emerged after cooldown or snooze expiry. This is not about hiding bad news. It is about preserving signal-to-noise and operator trust.
acceptance_criteria: This task is complete when attention and digest can present a concise, prioritized queue that resists duplicate churn, surfaces recurrence intentionally, and makes suppression, aggregation, and operator override rules inspectable.
notes: If a transient flapping source can drown out real action items or if repeated retries create visually separate clutter instead of a coherent thread, this task is incomplete.
close_reason: Completed: automatic attention cooldown/resurfacing is now inspectable and ranking-aware. Ingress dedup tracks suppressed recurrence, resurfaces the next event with explicit cooldown evidence, and digest prioritization/trace now preserve recurrence under bounded budgets. Verified with focused internal/robot tests, go build ./cmd/ntm, golangci-lint run, and go test -short ./... .

title: robot-redesign/attention: persist operator attention state and re-emergence rules
description: Implement the durable operator-attention state that lets users and agents intentionally shape the queue over time. This task exists because the redesign should not force consumers to passively accept automatic ranking forever; they need durable semantics for acknowledged, snoozed, muted, pinned, and manually escalated items so the attention loop becomes collaborative rather than naggy.
design: The implementation should persist operator attention state in SQLite, keyed strongly enough to survive restarts and correlate with stable item identities or incident fingerprints rather than brittle presentation text. It should define how acknowledged, snoozed, muted, pinned, and manually escalated items influence ranking, visibility, resurfacing, and incident promotion; how manual state interacts with automatic deduplication and cooldown; what happens when an item changes materially while snoozed or acknowledged; and how expired snoozes or changed conditions reintroduce items into digest and attention. It should also expose enough evidence that diagnostics and parity surfaces can explain why an item was hidden, resurfaced, pinned, or force-escalated. This task is where the attention loop becomes collaborative rather than one-way.
acceptance_criteria: This task is complete when operator attention state is durably persisted and the system can consistently honor acknowledgment, snooze, mute, pin, and manual escalation semantics across restart, replay, resurfacing, and prioritization behavior.
notes: If users still have no durable way to say not now, keep this visible, or this matters more than the default ranking thinks, this task is incomplete.
close_reason: Implemented durable operator attention item state with restart/replay/digest/wait semantics plus POST /api/v1/attention/items/{cursor}/state for acknowledge, snooze, dismiss, restore, pin, unpin, mute, unmute, and escalate; build, lint, state/serve targeted tests, and focused reviews are green.

title: robot-redesign/attention: implement watch subscriptions, heartbeats, and adaptive cadence semantics
description: Implement the long-lived watch semantics that make ntm's event loop safe and pleasant to consume over time: typed event publication, heartbeats, filtered subscriptions, idle-vs-stuck liveness, and adaptive cadence. This task exists because the current redesign is strong on durable replay and operator prioritization, but it still leaves too much ambiguity around what continuous consumers should see when nothing material changes, when sources are slow, or when a consumer only wants a narrow slice of the event stream.
design:
The implementation should define and build how the durable attention journal, transport layer, and source-health logic cooperate to emit typed watch events and explicit keepalive behavior without flooding the system with meaningless churn. It should decide which signals are durably persisted versus emitted only as ephemeral transport keepalives, how heartbeat cadence and liveness deadlines are derived, how filtered subscriptions are evaluated against stable references and event classes, how replay hands off cleanly to live updates, and how source-progress or projection-status annotations tell consumers whether quiet means healthy idle, narrow filtering, temporary source slowness, or a real stuck condition.

This work should also implement adaptive cadence or similar pressure control so high-churn periods stay responsive while low-churn or degraded periods remain operationally cheap. The goal is not a complex scheduler. The goal is to keep long-lived watch consumers trustworthy, bounded, and intelligible. The implementation should reuse existing cursor, identity, explainability, request-correlation, source-health, and boundedness semantics rather than inventing a parallel model just for streaming.
acceptance_criteria: This task is complete when ntm can support long-lived filtered watch or streaming consumption with explicit typed events, trustworthy heartbeats, clear idle-vs-stuck semantics, replay-to-live handoff, and adaptive cadence behavior that stays aligned with the shared attention and transport contracts.

title: robot-redesign/incidents: durable escalation model for recurring operator pain

title: robot-redesign/incidents: define incident taxonomy and promotion rules
description: Define which operator-visible problems stay as transient alerts and which ones should promote into durable incidents. This task exists so recurring or high-cost operational problems acquire lifecycle and memory instead of reappearing forever as disconnected warnings.
design: The taxonomy should classify incident families such as crash loops, chronic quota pressure, repeated reservation conflicts, sustained stalls, unhealthy source outages, and broken coordination patterns. It should specify severity, promotion thresholds, deduplication/fingerprinting factors, resolution semantics, and how incidents relate to reason codes already used by attention and alerting.\n\nThe result should make incident behavior boring and predictable rather than heuristic folklore hidden in code.

title: robot-redesign/incidents: implement bounded incident replay and as-of reconstruction
description: Implement the bounded historical-replay capability that lets ntm reconstruct or serve a recent operator picture around an incident or requested timestamp without making operators manually stitch raw event history. This task exists because durable incidents and attention events are much more useful if ntm can replay them into a coherent as-of view for debugging, explanation, and post-mortem sharing.
design:
The implementation should build a bounded replay path on top of SQLite-backed projections, incidents, and attention events. It should decide when an as-of or incident replay is reconstructed from durable inputs versus served from a cached replay snapshot, what replay windows are kept, how cache invalidation and retention behave, how missing historical inputs are surfaced, and how replay outputs preserve stable identities, diagnostics handles, evidence links, and explicit degraded or partial markers.

This should stay tightly scoped to recent operational debugging and incident archaeology. It is not a general analytics engine. The product value is that an operator or agent can ask what ntm knew around this incident or timestamp and get a coherent, bounded, machine-readable answer quickly enough to use in live debugging and post-mortem work.
acceptance_criteria: This task is complete when ntm can provide bounded incident replay or recent as-of reconstruction with clear limits, stable references, explicit degraded markers, and enough caching or reconstruction discipline that the feature is practical rather than theoretical.

Added GetEventsForIncident and GetAttentionEventsInTimeRange with focused state verification green. design: The new status surface should present a compact summary derived from the shared runtime projection, with stable semantics around freshness and degraded state, and without silently omitting context in ways that mislead consumers into thinking they saw the whole world.\n\nThe design should make the relationship between status and snapshot obvious and intentional.

title: robot-redesign/surfaces: rewrite digest and attention as the prioritized action queue
description: Rewrite digest and attention so they form the heart of the ongoing operator loop rather than acting like separate vaguely-related summaries. This task exists because ntm's strongest agent-native idea is the attention feed, and the redesign should put that at the center.
design: Digest should answer what changed since a cursor in grouped, replay-safe form, including correlated actuation outcomes, operator attention-state changes, and intentional resurfacing of previously cooled-down or snoozed issues. Attention should answer what deserves action now, with reason codes, freshness, severity, stable resource references, request or outcome correlation handles where relevant, structured next_actions or equivalent remediation descriptors, compact evidence summaries or explanation handles, explicit aggregation or suppression markers when items represent rolled-up churn rather than raw event volume, and clear indicators when an item is pinned, snoozed, acknowledged, muted, or manually escalated. The two surfaces should feel like adjacent views over the same durable state rather than unrelated features, and they should bridge cleanly into inspect and diagnostics flows when an operator needs to understand why an item is present or absent. This task is where ntm steals the derived-actionability lesson from vibe_cockpit without adopting its fleet or analytics posture.
acceptance_criteria: This task is complete when digest and attention are coherent, prioritized, cursor-aware surfaces that help an agent tend the system over time instead of repeatedly rescanning the entire world, while still supporting safe retries, verified outcomes, durable operator control, and a concise signal-to-noise ratio.
notes: If agents still need to reconstruct the next action from raw dumps, the redesign has missed its main ergonomic payoff.
close_reason: Completed: digest now exposes a bounded prioritized_queue in source and CLI surfaces, with ordering/cap semantics covered by focused tests and verified by clean review.

title: robot-redesign/surfaces: rationalize targeted inspect surfaces for session and agent drill-down

The work should decide which session and agent inspect views remain distinct commands or modes, how they key into sessions, agents, and panes, how invalid or stale lookup requests are reported with machine-actionable follow-up guidance, and how they expose detail that is too verbose for snapshot, status, or attention. It should also make explicit how output, activity, context, and process detail is presented without leaking raw tmux mechanics back into the surface contract, and where these views deliberately hand off to the shared diagnostics flow when deeper why, evidence, truncation, or replay context is needed.

The goal is disciplined drill-down for session and agent state, not a generic debug dump.

notes: A useful heuristic: a session or agent inspect surface should answer a focused follow-up question raised by snapshot or attention, not replace them.

title: [MEDIUM] watch assignment limit stops after the first planned assignment
description: Reviewing commit 965ac957. WatchLoop.handleCompletion respects --limit inside the for _, assigned := range result.Assignments loop by checking len(result.Assignments) >= w.limit. That condition is independent of how many assignments have actually been emitted, so when the planner returns exactly the limit or more assignments the loop breaks after logging/dispatching the first one. The check should count assignments processed in the current cycle, not the total result slice length, so --limit=3 can emit three assignments and only then stop.
close_reason: handleCompletion now counts assignments emitted in the current cycle (processed counter) instead of comparing the planner slice length to limit. --limit=3 with three planned assignments now emits all three before the cycle stops. No existing WatchLoop test fixture covers handleCompletion; bug fix is a one-line semantic change with comment pointing at the previous regression.

title: Add ntm assign command - combines bv triage with ntm send in one step
description:
## Overview
Canonical work distribution command: `ntm assign`. Combines BV triage with ntm send.

## Supported Strategies
- **balanced** (default): Balance workload across idle agents, consider current assignment counts
- **speed**: Prioritize agents with low context usage for fast completion
- **quality**: Match agent type to bead type using capability matrix
- **dependency**: Prioritize beads that unblock the most downstream work (high PageRank/betweenness)
- **round-robin**: Deterministic even distribution (bead[i] -> agent[i % N])

## Command Design
```bash
# Preview assignments (default - no sending)
ntm assign myproject

# Execute assignments immediately
ntm assign myproject --auto

# With strategy
ntm assign myproject --strategy=quality --auto

# Limit number of assignments
ntm assign myproject --limit=5 --auto

# Assign specific beads
ntm assign myproject --beads=bd-123,bd-456 --auto

# Filter agent types (two naming styles for convenience)
ntm assign myproject --cc-only --auto
ntm assign myproject --agent=claude --auto    # Equivalent
ntm assign myproject --agent=codex --auto
ntm assign myproject --agent=gemini --auto
```

## Common Flags (all ntm commands)
```bash
--json           # Machine-readable JSON output
-v, --verbose    # Show detailed scoring/decision logs
-q, --quiet      # Suppress non-essential output
--timeout=30s    # Timeout for external calls (bv, br, Agent Mail)
--dry-run        # Alias for no --auto (preview mode)
--no-color       # Disable colored output
```

## Prompt Template System
Built-in templates:
- **impl**: "Work on bead {BEAD_ID}: {TITLE}. Check dependencies first with br dep tree {BEAD_ID}."
- **review**: "Review and verify bead {BEAD_ID}: {TITLE}. Run tests if applicable."
- **custom**: User provides template file

Variables available: {BEAD_ID}, {TITLE}, {DESCRIPTION}, {PRIORITY}, {TAGS}, {BLOCKED_BY}

## Agent Capability Matrix (for quality strategy)
```go
var AgentCapabilities = map[string]map[string]float64{
    "claude": {
        "refactoring": 0.95, "architecture": 0.95, "analysis": 0.90,
        "documentation": 0.85, "bug_fix": 0.85, "feature": 0.85,
        "testing": 0.75,
    },
    "codex": {
        "feature": 0.90, "bug_fix": 0.90, "testing": 0.85,
        "refactoring": 0.75, "documentation": 0.70,
    },
    "gemini": {
        "documentation": 0.90, "analysis": 0.85, "review": 0.90,
        "feature": 0.80, "testing": 0.80,
    },
}
```

## Algorithm
1. Get idle agents (context < 80%, no active assignment)
2. Get actionable beads from BV (not blocked)
3. Apply strategy scoring:
   - balanced: score = 1.0 / (current_assignments + 1)
   - speed: score = 1.0 - (context_usage / 100)
   - quality: score = capability_matrix[agent_type][bead_type]
   - dependency: score = unblocks_count * 0.5 + pagerank * 0.5
   - round-robin: deterministic index assignment
4. Generate (bead, agent) pairs sorted by score
5. If --auto: Send prompts, update assignment store
6. Emit JSON output

## Output Format
```json
{
  "strategy": "balanced",
  "assigned": [
    {
      "bead_id": "bd-abc1",
      "bead_title": "Implement feature X",
      "pane": 2,
      "agent_type": "claude",
      "agent_name": "GreenCastle",
      "score": 0.85,
      "prompt_sent": true
    }
  ],
  "skipped": [
    {
      "bead_id": "bd-def2",
      "reason": "blocked_by bd-abc1"
    }
  ],
  "summary": {
    "total_beads": 10,
    "assigned": 4,
    "skipped": 6,
    "idle_agents": 4
  }
}
```

## Error Handling
- No idle agents: Return with "no_idle_agents" in output, suggest wait or spawn more
- No actionable beads: Return with "no_ready_beads" in output
- BV unavailable: Fall back to br ready list, warn user
- Send failure: Mark as failed in assignment store, include in output

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All 5 strategies work correctly
- [ ] --auto sends prompts via ntm send
- [ ] --limit caps assignments
- [ ] --beads allows explicit bead list
- [ ] Agent type filters work (--cc-only and --agent=claude)
- [ ] Prompt templates expand correctly
- [ ] Assignment store updated
- [ ] JSON output is complete and stable
- [ ] Clear error messages for edge cases
- [ ] Logging shows scoring decisions (with --verbose)
- [ ] Common flags implemented (--json, --verbose, --quiet, --timeout)

## Tests Required
- Unit test: Each strategy scoring algorithm
- Unit test: Agent filtering logic (both styles)
- Unit test: Prompt template expansion
- Unit test: Output JSON format
- Unit test: Common flags (--json, --verbose, --quiet)
- E2E test: Full assign workflow with real agents
- E2E test: Error cases (no agents, no beads)
notes: Canonical assignment entry. Strategy list must stay in sync with code: balanced|speed|quality|dependency (+ round-robin if added). Supersedes send --distribute, swarm, and YAML swarm config.

title: [MEDIUM] TOML filter suppresses [steps.parallel] child-step keys, masking config errors
description:
Review of commit 77c89524 found parser.filterUndecodedTOMLKeys() now discards undecoded TOML keys under steps.parallel when key[2] matches knownStepTOMLFields (id, prompt, command, etc.). This was intended to allow schema-level handling of inline parallel step arrays, but it also drops malformed table-style child-step keys and hides the real authoring error.

Repro:
1) Create TOML:

   schema_version = "2.0"
   name = "probe"

   [[steps]]
   id = "p"

   [steps.parallel]
   id = "child"
   prompt = "hello"

2) Run: go run ./cmd/ntm pipeline lint /tmp/ntm_inline_parallel_probe.toml

Current behavior:
- ParseFile succeeds.
- Validation later reports generic "steps[0]: step must have prompt, prompt_file, command, template, parallel, loop, foreach, branch, or bead_query" because id/prompt under [steps.parallel] were silently discarded.

Expected behavior:
- Parser should not suppress this shape as if it were valid inline-step syntax.
- Return a precise parse/validation error that points to invalid [steps.parallel] child-step keys (or explicit unsupported TOML inline-step form), not a misleading missing-step-kind error.

Likely fix:
- Narrow filterUndecodedTOMLKeys() so it only ignores undecoded keys for the exact inline-array limitation signatures, not all steps.parallel.<known-step-field> keys.
- Add regression coverage for malformed [steps.parallel] id/prompt table entries so they fail with actionable errors.
close_reason: ParallelSpec.UnmarshalTOML now rejects [steps.parallel] tables that contain step-shaped fields (id/prompt/command/etc.) with a clear hint pointing at the canonical [[steps.parallel.steps]] array form. Narrowed filterUndecodedTOMLKeys to only suppress legitimate steps.parallel.steps.<step-field> leftovers from inline-array decoding.

title: EPIC: Context Continuity System - Compound Dont Compact
description:
## Philosophy: "Compound, Don't Compact"

This EPIC implements a context management system inspired by [Continuous-Claude-v3](https://github.com/parcadei/Continuous-Claude-v3). The core insight: **each compaction is lossy compression**—after several compactions, agents work with degraded context. Instead of fighting compaction, we:

1. **Extract state before compaction** - Pre-compact hook captures context
2. **Clear and reload fresh** - Start new session with full signal from handoff
3. **Use token-efficient YAML** - ~400 tokens vs ~2000 markdown
4. **Show status in real-time** - Dashboard displays goal/now from latest handoff

## Why This Approach Is Superior

**Current approach problems:**
- Agents suddenly hit context limits, lose mid-work context
- Each compaction degrades signal quality
- No structured way to preserve decisions, learnings, next steps
- Users never know "where did we leave off?"

**CC-v3 approach benefits:**
- Handoffs preserve 100% of key information
- Fresh context = full signal, no degradation
- Structured format ensures nothing is lost
- Status line shows current goal/now at a glance
- Works with multiple concurrent sessions

## YAML Handoff Format (~400 tokens)

```yaml
---
session: {session-name}
date: YYYY-MM-DD
status: complete|partial|blocked
outcome: SUCCEEDED|PARTIAL_PLUS|PARTIAL_MINUS|FAILED
---

goal: {What this session accomplished - shown in statusline}
now: {What next session should do first - shown in statusline}
test: {Command to verify this work}

done_this_session:
  - task: {First completed task}
    files: [{file1.go}, {file2.go}]

blockers: [{any blocking issues}]
questions: [{unresolved questions for next session}]

decisions:
  - {decision_name}: {rationale}

findings:
  - {key_finding}: {details}

worked: [{approaches that worked}]
failed: [{approaches that failed and why}]

next:
  - {First next step}
  - {Second next step}

files:
  created: [{new files}]
  modified: [{changed files}]
```

## Key Fields

- **goal + now**: REQUIRED, shown in status line/dashboard
- **done_this_session**: What was accomplished with file references
- **decisions**: Important choices and rationale for "future self"
- **findings**: Key learnings discovered
- **worked/failed**: What to repeat vs avoid
- **next**: Action items for resuming

## Directory Structure

```
.ntm/
├── handoffs/
│   ├── {session-name}/
│   │   ├── 2026-01-19_14-30_auth-complete.yaml
│   │   └── auto-handoff-{timestamp}.yaml
│   └── general/
└── ledgers/
    └── CONTINUITY_{session}.md
```

## Lifecycle Hooks Integration

1. **Pre-Compact Hook**: When agent approaches context limit (70%+) or manual /clear
   - Parse recent output/transcript
   - Generate YAML handoff automatically
   - Save to handoffs directory

2. **Session-Start Hook**: When spawning new session
   - Find most recent handoff for this session
   - Extract goal/now fields
   - Inject into initial agent context

3. **Session-End Hook**: On kill/exit
   - Prompt for handoff creation if work in progress

## CLI Commands

- `ntm handoff [session]` - Create manual handoff for session
- `ntm resume [session|path]` - Resume from handoff
- `ntm context status` - Show context and handoff status

## Integration Points

- **Dashboard**: Show goal/now/context% in top status bar
- **BV**: Include active bead IDs in handoffs
- **Agent Mail**: Thread IDs for related conversations
- **CM**: Query relevant memories on resume

## Success Criteria

- Agents can be cleared and resumed with zero context loss
- Status line shows current goal/now from latest handoff
- Automatic handoffs triggered before context exhaustion
- YAML format uses ~400 tokens (95% reduction from raw)
- Works with multiple concurrent sessions

## Relationship to Existing Beads

This EPIC subsumes and improves upon:
- bd-ljrn (Proactive Context Window Management)
- bd-2i44 (Structured Handoff Protocol)
- bd-3dxk (End-of-Session Summarization)

Complements:
- bd-38kx (Smart Session Recovery) - provides handoff data
- bd-2n9s (Cross-Session Memory via CM) - procedural memory
notes:
## Testing Requirements
- Unit tests: core logic, error paths, edge cases.
- E2E scripts: full CLI/robot flow with detailed log/slog prefixes (e.g., [E2E-<AREA>]) and include session/agent/bead IDs.
- If structured outputs are affected, assert schema stability + deterministic ordering.

title: Implement recommendation generator

Implement recommendation generator for diagnosed issues.

## Recommendations per Status

### rate_limited
- action: wait_or_caam
- reason: 'Output contains rate limit pattern'
- Parse reset_time if available
- auto_fixable: false (requires human decision)

### unresponsive
- action: kill_restart
- reason: 'No output for N seconds, process state: X'
- auto_fixable: true
- fix_command: 'ntm --robot-restart-pane <session> <pane>'

title: SanitizeMachineFingerprint not idempotent for 'machine:unknown' sentinel — silent drift on reload
description:
## Defect

internal/pressure/profile_trend.go SanitizeMachineFingerprint is non-idempotent for empty/unknown input. The function returns 'machine:unknown' when raw is empty, but on the next call (e.g. via MigrateHostProfileTrendRecord on a reloaded record), it does NOT recognize 'machine:unknown' as already-sanitized — len('unknown') != 16 so isSanitizedMachineFingerprint returns false. The string then gets sha256-hashed into 'machine:14bb8699b3f42d60'.

## Repro

  sanitize('')                 -> 'machine:unknown'
  sanitize('machine:unknown')  -> 'machine:14bb8699b3f42d60'  (changed!)
  sanitize('machine:14bb8699b3f42d60') -> stable

## Impact

MigrateHostProfileTrendRecord rewrites the fingerprint on every reload of a record that was originally stored without machine info. After one reload, comparisons against a freshly-built 'unknown' record will show a phantom fingerprint drift even though no actual machine info changed.

## Fix

Treat 'machine:unknown' as a valid sanitized sentinel: short-circuit return it from SanitizeMachineFingerprint before hashing.

## Regression test

Add idempotency test asserting sanitize(sanitize('')) == sanitize('') and that 'machine:unknown' round-trips through MigrateHostProfileTrendRecord unchanged.
close_reason: SanitizeMachineFingerprint now treats 'machine:unknown' as a valid sanitized sentinel; added TestSanitizeMachineFingerprintIsIdempotentForUnknownSentinel that fails pre-fix and passes post-fix.

description:
Add ntm health --auto-restart-stuck - detect and restart agents that appear stuck (no output for N minutes).

## Problem Being Solved

Agents sometimes hang or get stuck. Currently requires manual detection and restart.

## Command Design

```bash
ntm health SESSION --auto-restart-stuck [--threshold DURATION] [--dry-run]
```

1. Monitors all agent panes for output activity
2. Detects panes with no output for threshold duration
3. Automatically restarts stuck panes

- Track last output timestamp per pane
- Pane is 'stuck' if no output for threshold (default: 5m)
- Ignore panes that are intentionally idle (awaiting user input)

- --dry-run: Report stuck panes without restarting

ntm --robot-health-restart-stuck=SESSION [--threshold=DURATION]

title: [HIGH] git/worktree safeSessionPrefix truncation aliases distinct session-agent IDs (cleanup/status/worktree collisions)
description:
[REVIEW FINDING]

Commit f016b204 updates sessionMatchesWorktree to compare branch session IDs against safeSessionPrefix(sessionName+"-"+agentType+"-"). This codifies an 8-char truncation that is not unique and can alias distinct work items.

Root cause:
- safeSessionPrefix(sessionID) in internal/git/worktree.go returns only the first 8 characters (or zero-padded).
- For session names >=8 chars, the prefix contains only session-name bytes and drops agentType/agentNum from the key.
- ProvisionWorktree uses this truncated key in both worktreeName and branchName.

Concrete collisions:
1) Same session, same agent type, multiple panes:
   sessionID alpha-team-claude-1 and alpha-team-claude-2 both prefix to "alpha-te" => same worktree/branch identity.
2) Different sessions with same first 8 chars:
   alpha-team-x and alpha-team-y map to the same prefix => cross-session alias in cleanup/status matching.

Impact:
- worktree/status/cleanup can target the wrong logical pane/session because identity is lossy.
- potential data-loss/confusion when cleanup removes or reuses a worktree that belongs to a different logical session/pane.

Expected fix direction:
- Stop using an 8-char truncation as the persisted identity key.
- Persist a collision-resistant key (full sanitized ID or hashed suffix) that preserves agentType+agentNum uniqueness, and match on that canonical key in cleanup/status.

title: [LOW] parity: indexByKindID silently overwrites duplicate Kind:ID views, hiding a class of drift the harness exists to surface
description:
In internal/parity/parity.go indexByKindID (commit 45999d27, bd-fxj4f.13), duplicate (Kind, ID) pairs are silently overwritten:

  func indexByKindID(views []SnapshotView) map[string]SnapshotView {
    out := make(map[string]SnapshotView, len(views))
    for _, v := range views {
      k := strings.TrimSpace(v.Kind) + ":" + strings.TrimSpace(v.ID)
      if k == ":" { continue }
      out[k] = v   // <-- silent overwrite
    }
    return out
  }

Two failure modes both invisible to the report:

(a) A surface (robot or TUI) emits two views with the same Kind:ID. The second overwrites the first — Compare runs against only one of the two, the other is silently dropped from comparison. This contradicts the package's stated mission ('any drift indicates a rendering bug, a stale field, or a contract violation that would otherwise reach an operator as a confusing UI inconsistency') because a duplicate-ID is itself a contract violation and should be surfaced as a drift, not swallowed.

(b) The 'k == ":"' guard only catches Kind+ID both empty. A view with Kind="session" and ID="" produces key "session:", as does any other empty-ID session view; all of them silently collapse to one entry. A nonempty ID with empty Kind has the same shape (":id").

Suggested fix (smallest behavior change):

  - Detect collisions in the loop: if out[k] already exists, append a Drift with Kind, ID, Field="duplicate_id", Severity=SeverityCritical, Detail="two views share the same Kind:ID on this surface". Keep the FIRST view (so legitimate caller errors surface deterministically).
  - Tighten the empty-key guard: skip when ID=="" OR Kind=="", not only when both are empty. Empty Kind without ID, or empty ID without Kind, are invalid surface inputs and should produce a 'missing_id' or 'missing_kind' info-severity drift instead of being silently absorbed.

Severity LOW: requires malformed surface input to manifest, and Compare itself is correct for well-formed input. But the harness's job is to surface rendering bugs, and silently dropping inputs is the opposite. Easy fix; should ship with a regression test that asserts duplicate-ID collisions surface as a drift.

Source: internal/parity/parity.go indexByKindID (line ~195); commit 45999d27 (bd-fxj4f.13).
close_reason: Fixed silent overwrite in indexByKindID. Now: (1) duplicate Kind:ID emits SeverityCritical 'duplicate_id' drift (keeps FIRST view deterministically), (2) empty Kind emits SeverityInfo 'missing_kind' drift, (3) empty ID emits SeverityInfo 'missing_id' drift. Surface drifts attributed via Robot/TUI field. Two regression tests added: TestCompare_DuplicateKindIDIsCritical, TestCompare_MalformedIdentityFieldsAreInfoDrifts.

title: EPIC: Proactive Context Window Management with Predictive Compaction
description:
**IDEA #4 - ELIMINATES SURPRISES (88% confidence)**

## What It Does
Instead of reacting when an agent hits context exhaustion (80-95% full), NTM predicts when exhaustion will occur and proactively triggers compaction before the agent's work is interrupted.

## Why This Matters
- Currently: Agents suddenly hit context limits, lose mid-work context
- After: NTM handles it proactively; work continues smoothly
- Users never see 'Conversation compacted - lost context' mid-task
- Transforms context limits from a constant worry to a non-issue

## How It Works
Continuous monitoring:
1. Track token velocity: Characters per minute → estimated tokens per minute
2. Model context growth: Based on recent velocity, project time-to-exhaustion
3. Predict exhaustion: 'At current rate, agent will exhaust context in 12 minutes'
4. Proactive action: At 70% + high velocity, suggest compaction; at 75% with continued high velocity, trigger automatically

## Prediction Model
tokens_remaining = context_limit - current_tokens
time_to_exhaustion = tokens_remaining / token_velocity_per_minute

if time_to_exhaustion < threshold_minutes:
    trigger_proactive_compaction()

## Flywheel Alignment
- Enhances existing context rotation feature
- Pairs perfectly with Smart Session Recovery
- Compaction + recovery = seamless context management

- ContextPredictor struct with velocity sampling

title: [HIGH] Foreach parent on_error=continue does not keep later body steps running
description:
Review of c2803ea7 ([bug-fix] foreach honors workflow continue in body steps) found that the fix applies workflow.Settings.OnError inside executeForeachIteration, but still ignores the parent foreach step OnError when deciding whether to continue later body steps after a nested failure.

Current flow:

1. executeForeach resolves parent-level onError := resolveErrorAction(step.OnError, workflow.Settings.OnError) and uses it only after an iteration has already returned.
2. executeForeachIteration sees a failed/cancelled nested body step and checks resolveErrorAction(nestedStep.OnError, workflow.Settings.OnError).
3. If the parent foreach step has on_error: continue, the nested step has no on_error, and workflow default is fail, this resolves to fail and returns immediately.
4. Later body steps in the same iteration never run, even though the parent foreach step explicitly requested continue semantics.

The c2803ea7 regression test covers workflow-level settings.on_error=continue, so it misses the equivalent parent-step case:

  - id: fanout
    on_error: continue
    foreach:
      items: [one]
      steps:
        - id: fail
          command: "exit 7"
        - id: after
          command: "printf after"

Expected: the failed body step is recorded and after runs, matching the workflow-level behavior c2803ea7 just fixed. Actual: executeForeachIteration returns after fail and after is skipped.

Impact: pipelines that scope error policy to a foreach step cannot reliably run cleanup/follow-up body steps after a tolerable per-item failure. This is user-visible control-flow loss and can skip side effects the pipeline author explicitly placed after the failing body step.

Likely fix: carry the parent foreach resolved error action into executeForeachIteration and use it as the fallback for nested body steps, e.g. resolveErrorAction(nestedStep.OnError, parentOnError), while preserving nested-step overrides. Add a regression test mirroring TestExecuteForeachWorkflowContinueKeepsBodyStepsAfterFailure with step.OnError=continue and workflow default fail.

No direct fix applied in this review pass because the requested CRITICAL/HIGH fix policy restricts fixes to NEW files only, while the production fix requires changing internal/pipeline/foreach.go.
close_reason: Threaded parent foreach step's resolved on_error into executeForeachIteration as parentOnError. Nested body steps without their own on_error now inherit the parent foreach's continue policy instead of falling through to workflow.Settings.OnError. Regression test added: TestExecuteForeachParentStepContinueKeepsBodyStepsAfterFailure with workflow default fail + parent on_error=continue + nested fail step + nested follow-up step asserting the follow-up still runs.

      iterResult.SkipReason = result.SkipReason
      ...
      return iterResult                                  // ← halts the rest of the iteration body
  }

Practical impact: a foreach body with multiple steps cannot have an optional middle step gated by 'when:' without aborting the whole iteration. Example:

  foreach:
    items: ${rows}
    steps:
      - id: setup
        command: ./setup
      - id: maybe
        when: ${item.dry_run} == false
        command: ./run-real
      - id: cleanup
        command: ./cleanup

Pre-daefceb9 behavior (intuitive): setup → maybe (skipped) → cleanup runs.
Post-daefceb9 behavior: setup → maybe (skipped) → iteration returned, cleanup never runs.

Workaround: the user must wrap optional logic in a LoopControl step (continue/break with when), but the early-return-on-Skipped is undocumented. The new test TestExecuteForeachSkippedBodyStepSkipsIteration only covers a single-body-step case, so the multi-step body footgun is not exercised.

Recommended:
- Document the semantic clearly: 'a body step returning Skipped halts the rest of the iteration body and marks the iteration skipped; use LoopControl=continue with when to skip just one step'
- Or: make halting opt-in via a per-step or per-foreach setting (skip_aborts_iteration: true|false), defaulting to the more intuitive behavior of skipping just the one step

Source commit: daefceb9 feat(pipeline): propagate skipped foreach iterations (bd-2ubxp.16)
close_reason: Already fixed by c6b961e6 ([bug-fix] pipeline: continue foreach after optional skip); current executeForeachIteration continues after non-control StatusSkipped body steps and TestExecuteForeachSkippedOptionalBodyStepContinuesIteration covers the multi-step optional skip case.
