title: [MEDIUM] by_model_family strategy skips author_model normalization, diverging from by_model_family_difference
description:
Review of 144a013a [bug-fix][bd-7k7ie] normalize verbose author_model to pane family vocabulary found that the normalization layer is wired into only one of two sibling foreach pane-assignment strategies, producing inconsistent routing for the same input.

In internal/pipeline/foreach.go selectForeachPane (line 1207-1217 after the commit):

  case 'by_model_family':
      paneID, err = byModelFamily(strategyPanes, foreachItemString(item, 'model_family', 'model', 'family', 'type'))
  case 'by_model_family_difference':
      paneID, warned, err = byModelFamilyDifference(strategyPanes, foreachAuthorModelFamilyForPanes(item, strategyPanes))

The 'by_model_family_difference' branch now routes the item value through foreachAuthorModelFamilyForPanes -> mapModelFamilyToPaneVocabulary, which (a) prefers a case-insensitive pane.ModelFamily match, (b) maps verbose Anthropic/OpenAI/Google model names (e.g. 'claude-sonnet-4', 'openai-codex', 'gpt-4', 'gemini-2.0-pro') to a recognized family group, and (c) falls back to the canonical short token ('cc'/'cod'/'gmi'). The 'by_model_family' branch still consumes the raw foreachItemString value and feeds it into byModelFamily, which compares with strict pane.ModelFamily == modelFamily.

Reproducer:
  strategy: by_model_family
  panes: [{ModelFamily: 'cc'}, {ModelFamily: 'cod'}]
  item: {author_model: 'claude-sonnet-4'} (or model_family: 'claude')

  Current behavior: foreachItemString returns 'claude-sonnet-4' (or 'claude'); byModelFamily compares with 'cc' and 'cod', neither matches, returns errNoModelFamilyPane.
  Expected behavior: routing should pick the 'cc' pane, the same way 'by_model_family_difference' would now classify the item as belonging to the 'cc' family.

Impact: pipeline authors who upgrade to a config that names verbose Anthropic/OpenAI/Google model strings cannot rely on 'by_model_family' even though the parallel 'by_model_family_difference' was just fixed for them. Users who write a config that works under one strategy and try the other (e.g. while debugging) will see surprising errNoModelFamilyPane / different pane selections.

Fix: extract the normalization into a shared helper used by both strategies, e.g.

  case 'by_model_family':
      paneID, err = byModelFamily(strategyPanes, foreachAuthorModelFamilyForPanes(item, strategyPanes))

Or, equivalently, have byModelFamily call mapModelFamilyToPaneVocabulary internally. Add a regression test analogous to TestSelectForeachPaneModelFamilyDifferencePrefersCanonicalOverVerboseAuthor for 'by_model_family'.

Source commit: 144a013a [bug-fix][bd-7k7ie] normalize verbose author_model to pane family vocabulary
close_reason: duplicate of bd-i5ax1 — same root cause (by_model_family strategy doesn't apply the family normalization that 144a013a only wired into by_model_family_difference). bd-i5ax1 was filed ~38 seconds earlier with a more concrete pane.ModelFamily=opus repro. Closing this one to avoid duplicated triage.

title: [HIGH] parallel resume reruns completed substeps
description:
[HIGH] Commit 7304d410 adds ParallelState bookkeeping in executeParallel(), but Resume/applyResumeState never consumes ParallelState.CompletedStepIDs or skips completed child steps when the parent parallel step lacks a final StepResult. If ntm is interrupted after one or more parallel children finish and persist their child StepResults, but before the parent parallel result is stored, resume marks the child graph nodes executed and then runs the parent parallel step again from scratch. That re-dispatches already completed child commands/prompts, duplicating side effects despite the persisted parallel progress contract.

Expected: resume should use persisted parallel substep state to avoid re-running completed parallel children, or it should not claim mid-parallel resume support.

Evidence: 7304d410 records beginParallelState/markParallelSubstepFinished in internal/pipeline/executor.go and state_resume.go, but executeParallel always iterates all step.Parallel.Steps and applyResumeState only prunes failed/running StepResult entries; ParallelState.CompletedStepIDs is never read during execution.
close_reason: executeParallel now reads e.state.Steps before dispatching each child; if the child persisted StatusCompleted from a prior run (and isn't flagged for rerun), it adopts the result and records it in ParallelState.CompletedStepIDs instead of re-dispatching. Regression test pre-populates step1 with a sentinel and asserts that re-running the parallel group preserves it while step2/step3 dispatch fresh.

title: [HIGH] step-level foreach resume reruns completed iterations from scratch
description:
Review of 7304d410 (feat: persist resumable execution state) found that the new resume bookkeeping is only wired into LoopExecutor.executeForEach for legacy loop: items. The newer step-level foreach: executor in internal/pipeline/foreach.go never calls beginForeachState, markForeachIterationStarted, markForeachIterationCompleted, or markStepInFlight for individual iterations.

Current behavior:
1. executeStepWithRetry marks the parent foreach step in InFlightSteps.
2. executeForeach runs iterations and stores nested results via storeForeachNestedResult, but it does not persist a completed-iteration set for the foreach step.
3. If cancellation or timeout happens after some iterations completed, applyResumeState sees the parent step as in-flight, deletes the parent step result, clears InFlightSteps, and removes dynamic nested step results that are not in the dependency graph.
4. Resume executes the whole foreach step from iteration 0 again.

Impact: step-level foreach resume can duplicate side effects for iterations that already completed before cancellation. This violates the bd-3nebw contract for foreach/parallel mid-step resume and is distinct from the legacy loop: collect bug because it affects the primary ForeachConfig path added under bd-2ubxp.

Expected: executeForeach should persist per-iteration progress for the step-level foreach path and skip completed iterations on resume, or explicitly refuse/resume-restart foreach steps instead of silently pretending mid-step resume is supported. Add a regression with a foreach: step over multiple items, cancel after the first iteration completes, resume, and assert the first iteration command is not run twice.

No code fix was applied in this review pass because the requested CRITICAL/HIGH auto-fix scope is restricted to NEW files only, while the production fix requires changing internal/pipeline/foreach.go and resume handling.
close_reason: executeForeach now calls beginForeachState upfront and reads ForeachState.CompletedIterationIDs to suppress re-dispatch of iterations that completed in a prior run; iteration loops mark each successful iteration via markForeachIterationCompleted so the persisted set stays current. New SkipKindResumeAlreadyCompleted classifies the skip. Regression seeds CompletedIterationIDs with iter0, points the body at a side-effect counter file, and asserts the counter records exactly the iter1/iter2 runs (no iter0 re-dispatch).

title: [MEDIUM] cli/work/queue-dry: 10s Agent Mail context timeout makes interactive diagnostic feel hung
description: internal/cli/work.go collectQueueDryReservations uses context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Second) when fetching active reservations from Agent Mail. queue-dry is interactive — operator runs 'ntm work queue-dry' expecting sub-second feedback. If Agent Mail is hung, the operator waits 10s for the diagnostic to even start rendering. Fix: (1) drop the timeout to 2s for the live diagnostic, since a hung/slow Agent Mail is itself a signal the queue may be dry due to lock contention; (2) emit a 'reservations_unavailable' warning immediately when the timeout trips so the operator sees fast feedback even when AM is down; (3) consider running the AM call in a goroutine so other evidence sources (br summary, bv triage, git commits) can be rendered while AM is queried.
close_reason: Reduced collectQueueDryReservations Agent Mail context timeout from 10s to 2s via new queueDryReservationTimeout const, and added appendQueueDryReservationWarning to surface the timeout/unavailability in the diagnostic output. Interactive 'ntm work queue-dry' now returns within ~2s even when Agent Mail is slow or hung; the timeout itself is a useful signal the operator can see in Warnings. queue-dry tests still pass; cmd/ntm builds clean.

title: [MEDIUM] pressure: Governor.SetMode writes g.mode under lock but Gate/Mode read g.mode without lock — data race per Go memory model
description:
In internal/pressure/governor.go (commit 3c01a51e, bd-2mb03.1), the Governor field `mode Mode` is mutated by SetMode under the write lock but read by Gate and Mode() with no lock at all:

  func (g *Governor) Mode() Mode { return g.mode }

  func (g *Governor) SetMode(m Mode) {
      g.mu.Lock()
      defer g.mu.Unlock()
      if m != ModeEnforce { m = ModeObserve }
      g.mode = m
  }

  func (g *Governor) Gate(action Action, session string, urgent bool) Result {
      snap := g.Latest()                  // RLock-protected ✓
      budget := g.budgetFor(session)
      res := Result{
          ...
          Mode: g.mode,                   // <-- racy read
          ...
      }
      ...
      if g.mode == ModeObserve && res.Decision != DecisionAllow {  // <-- racy read
          ...
      } else if res.Decision != DecisionAllow {
          ...
      }
      return res
  }

The Go memory model gives no happens-before between SetMode's locked store and Gate's unlocked load. Two concrete failure modes:

  1. Operator flips ModeObserve → ModeEnforce. A concurrent Gate call
     may observe ModeObserve even after SetMode returns, so a critical-
     pressure spawn that should have been Denied is silently Allowed
     for that one decision (and the Result.Mode field reports
     "observe", further misleading the caller's logs).

  2. The race detector (`go test -race ./internal/pressure/...`)
     flags this on any test that exercises SetMode + Gate
     concurrently. The pressure_test.go suite covers observe-only
     and enforce paths separately but does not stress the transition.

This same pattern likely applies to any future dynamic field on Governor; the fix should establish a discipline that all g-state reads in Gate go through the lock.

Suggested fix (smallest change):

  func (g *Governor) currentMode() Mode {
      g.mu.RLock()
      defer g.mu.RUnlock()
      return g.mode
  }

  func (g *Governor) Mode() Mode { return g.currentMode() }

  func (g *Governor) Gate(action Action, session string, urgent bool) Result {
      mode := g.currentMode()             // single locked read
      ...
      Mode: mode,                          // use captured value
      ...
      if mode == ModeObserve && res.Decision != DecisionAllow { ... }
  }

Alternative: store mode as `atomic.Value` (since Mode is a string) or
sync/atomic.Pointer[Mode]. Avoids the lock contention but changes the
SetMode boilerplate.

Add a regression test that runs SetMode + Gate concurrently and
asserts no race (the test passes today only because no goroutines
exercise the pair simultaneously). Run `go test -race -run
TestGovernorMode -count=10 ./internal/pressure/...` to confirm the
fix.

Severity MEDIUM: race window is small (single field load/store),
production callers may rarely flip mode dynamically, and even when
they hit the race the wrong decision is at most one Gate call out
of date. But the race IS a Go-spec data race — the race detector
will flag it on any future test that stresses mode transitions, and
operators relying on SetMode for incident response (toggle to
enforce when a swarm misbehaves) get a one-call grace window where
their flip is invisible.

Source: internal/pressure/governor.go (Mode/SetMode lines ~98-110,
Gate ~187-205); commit 3c01a51e (bd-2mb03.1).
close_reason: Closed the Governor.mode + last data race. Mode() now takes RLock; Gate() takes a single RLock at the top, snapshots both g.mode and g.last (with empty-snapshot fallback when nil) into locals, releases the lock, and operates on the locals through the remainder of the function — so the decision branch and Result.Mode reference the same snapshotted view. Other Governor fields (providers, thresholds, global, sessions, now, logger) are immutable after New, so no additional locking needed. Added TestGovernor_ModeAndGateAreRaceFreeUnderConcurrentAccess: 4 SetMode flippers + 4 Gate readers + 4 Mode readers + 4 Refresh writers × 200 iterations, with a post-flight assertion that Gate still returns a canonical Mode value. Pre-fix this test reports unsynchronized writes/reads under -race; post-fix the run is clean. Commit: 7e66d47f. rch exec -- go build ./cmd/ntm and rch exec -- go test -short -race -count=1 ./internal/pressure/... both pass.

title: foreach resume can rerun fully completed iteration when cancel lands before completion mark
description:
[HIGH] Review of 7c302816 ([bug-fix][bd-xreqm] guard markForeachIterationCompleted against ctx cancel race) found a new duplicate-work regression in foreach resume semantics.

In internal/pipeline/loops.go, completion marking changed from:
  if iterationSucceeded(iterResult, shouldBreak) { markForeachIterationCompleted(...) }

to:
  if ctx.Err() == nil && iterationSucceeded(iterResult, shouldBreak) { ... }

This prevents the empty-iteration race, but it also drops completion for iterations that actually finished all nested steps when cancellation arrives just after executeIteration returns and before the completion check.

Repro shape:
1. Foreach iteration executes all body steps successfully and returns non-empty iterResult.
2. External cancel triggers between executeIteration return and completion check.
3. ctx.Err() != nil, so markForeachIterationCompleted is skipped.
4. State is persisted without this iteration in CompletedIterationIDs.
5. Resume starts from firstIncompleteIteration and reruns that already-finished iteration, duplicating side effects/output.

Impact: resume can re-execute already-applied work (duplicate command execution, duplicate writes/messages), which is a functional correctness issue on happy-path cancel/resume flows.

Expected: completion decision should distinguish empty-cancel race from fully-successful iteration completion (for example, allow completion on cancel when the iteration conclusively finished all planned nested steps, not merely based on ctx.Err()).

Scope pointers:
- internal/pipeline/loops.go around the completion check in executeForEach.
- internal/pipeline/state_resume.go helper logic (shouldCompleteForeachIteration / iterationSucceeded) for centralized policy.

Testing gap:
- Add regression proving cancellation after successful iteration completion does not cause duplicate rerun on resume.
close_reason: Duplicate of bd-4vqx3 (same cancel-after-success foreach resume rerun defect)

title: [LOW] commitlint/lint.go: pathMatchesReservation skips bare "**" catch-all (mirror of bd-6286k / bd-397fv)
description:
# Bug

`internal/commitlint/lint.go::pathMatchesReservation` recognizes a `/**` suffix but does NOT special-case bare `"**"`:

```go
if strings.HasSuffix(pattern, "/**") {
    prefix := strings.TrimSuffix(pattern, "/**")
    if prefix == "" {
        return true
    }
    return p == prefix || strings.HasPrefix(p, prefix+"/")
}
```

`strings.HasSuffix("**", "/**")` is false (the candidate is shorter than the suffix), so a bare `"**"` reservation pattern falls through both the `/**` and `/*` branches and reaches `path.Match("**", p)`. Because `path.Match`s `*` cannot cross `/`, `path.Match("**", "internal/foo.go") == false` — the catch-all silently fails to cover any path containing a slash.

# Verification

- `pathMatchesReservation("internal/foo.go", "**") = false` ❌ (must be true — catch-all)
- `pathMatchesReservation("deep/nested/file.go", "**") = false` ❌
- `pathMatchesReservation("internal/foo.go", "/**") = true` ✓ (existing prefix=="" handles `/**`)

# Impact

`commitlint.Evaluate` is a pre-commit/pre-handoff readiness lint. `pathMatchesReservation` runs over `Inputs.Reservations` to decide:

1. **`foreign_reservation` finding (Critical)**: another agents `**` exclusive reservation should block the operator from committing over their lock. Pre-fix it does not — the operators touched paths silently appear "unreserved by anyone foreign".
2. **`missing_reservation` finding (Warning)**: the operators OWN `**` reservation should cover any touched path. Pre-fix it does not — the lint emits a "no matching reservation" warning even when the operator legitimately holds `**`.
3. **`stale_own_reservation` finding (Warning)**: stale `**` reservations are missed for the same reason.

So the commit-readiness gate has a blind spot for the catch-all reservation pattern.

This is the third instance of the same bug shape across the codebase (after bd-6286k in reservationsim and bd-397fv in contentionforecast); the underlying cause is identical (`HasSuffix("**", "/**")` is false). Worth running an audit pass for the remaining `HasSuffix("/**")` sites — `internal/scanner/autoscan.go::matchRecursivePattern` looks like a fourth instance.

# Fix

Add an explicit catch-all short-circuit at the top of `pathMatchesReservation`:

```go
if pattern == "**" {
    return true
}
```

Same shape as bd-6286k and bd-397fv.

# Regression test

Add a `TestPathMatchesReservation_CatchAllAndBoundaries` table-driven test that pins:
- `pathMatchesReservation("foo/bar.go", "**") == true`
- `pathMatchesReservation("deep/nested/file.go", "**") == true`
- `pathMatchesReservation("anyfile.go", "**") == true`
- `pathMatchesReservation("foo/bar.go", "/**") == true` (pin existing behavior)
- positive and negative existing cases (prefixed `/**`, prefixed `/*`, exact match, miss).

Severity: **LOW** — pre-commit lint blind spot for the broadest reservation pattern; advisory output and no current production caller using `"**"` reservations, but the lint contract is what gates commit safety so it should be correct.
close_reason: Fixed: bare ** treated as catch-all in pathMatchesReservation; mirrors bd-6286k / bd-397fv. Test pins all 4 catch-all cases plus existing patterns.

title: max_rounds resume re-runs already-completed rounds within an interrupted iteration
description:
## Severity: [LOW]

bd-qeatk (6af8c8f9) added iteration-level resume skip via \`ForeachState.CompletedIterationIDs\`: a foreach iteration whose ID is on the completed set is skipped on resume. An iteration is added to the set only when it FULLY completes — i.e., all body steps for all rounds finish.

bd-2ubxp.14 (20dfc963) introduced \`max_rounds\` so each iteration's body can run N times. Per-round state.Steps keys are suffixed \`_round<N>\` so each round's results don't clobber. But there is no per-round resume bookkeeping.

## Problem

If a workflow with \`max_rounds: 3\` is cancelled while iteration 0 is in round 2:
1. iter0 has run round 1 fully and round 2 partially.
2. iter0 is NOT in \`CompletedIterationIDs\` (still incomplete).
3. On resume, iter0 re-dispatches from round 1.
4. Round 1's nested step results in \`state.Steps\[fanout_iter0_<child>_round1\]\` are overwritten as the body re-executes round 1 from scratch.

For idempotent bodies this is benign. For non-idempotent bodies (\`agent\` steps that send messages, \`command\` steps with file/network side effects, CM/CASS writes), round 1's side effects are duplicated.

## Reproduce

\`\`\`yaml
steps:
  - id: fanout
    foreach:
      items: ["A"]
      max_rounds: 3
      steps:
        - id: counter
          command: echo "round=\${round}" >> /tmp/counter.log
\`\`\`

Cancel after round 2 starts but before it finishes; resume.
- Expected: rounds 2-3 run.
- Actual: rounds 1-3 all run, /tmp/counter.log has "round=1" twice.

## Fix sketch

Mirror bd-qeatk's pattern at the round level. Two options:

1. **Track completed rounds per iteration.** Extend \`ForeachIterationState\` with \`CompletedRounds map[string]int\` keyed by iteration ID; \`runForeachIterationRound\` skips rounds <= completed-round-watermark on resume. Cheap, deterministic, no extra state.Steps reads.

2. **Inspect \`state.Steps[<roundN-key>].Status\` at round entry.** If all body steps for round N are recorded \`completed\`, skip that round. Reuses existing keys, no schema change, but more work per round.

Option 1 is preferred for clarity and to keep the contract under \`-race\` like bd-qeatk's approach.

## Acceptance

- A test cancels a max_rounds=3 foreach mid-round-2 (e.g., body that writes a file and then returns ErrTimeout on round 2 attempt 1) and verifies on resume that rounds 1's body steps DO NOT re-execute (single line in counter file).
- Existing TestForeachMaxRounds_* tests still pass.
- ForeachState schema migration: a missing \`CompletedRounds\` map on legacy state files defaults to empty (zero rounds completed → re-run all rounds of any incomplete iteration), preserving today's behavior.

## Related
- bd-qeatk (6af8c8f9) — iteration-level resume skip
- bd-2ubxp.14 (20dfc963) — max_rounds feature
- bd-2ubxp.15 — integration test scaffolding
- bd-2ubxp.20 (5edbb6e6) — race fix for round vars

## Files
- internal/pipeline/foreach.go (executeForeachIteration / runForeachIterationRound)
- internal/pipeline/schema.go (ForeachIterationState if option 1)
close_reason: Added CompletedRounds map[string]int to ForeachIterationState (state_resume.go:80) keyed by iterID → highest fully-completed round. executeForeachIteration starts the round loop at watermark+1 (foreach.go:629-643) instead of round 1, and markForeachIterationRoundCompleted bumps the watermark after every clean runForeachIterationRound return. Single-round iterations don't write here so legacy state files stay byte-identical. Regressions TestForeachMaxRounds_ResumeSkipsAlreadyCompletedRounds and TestForeachMaxRounds_FreshRunRecordsRoundWatermark cover the resume-skip and fresh-record paths. Pipeline -race -short green. Commit 7dcbe087.

```bash
#\!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

LOG=/tmp/ntm-e2e-spawn-assign-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).log
exec > >(tee -a $LOG) 2>&1

echo "[INFO] Starting ntm spawn --assign E2E test at $(date)"

# Setup
echo "[STEP 1] Creating test workspace..."
TEST_DIR=/tmp/ntm-spawn-assign-test-$$
mkdir -p $TEST_DIR
cd $TEST_DIR
br init
for i in {1..4}; do br create "Test bead $i" --type task; done
echo "[OK] Created 4 test beads"

# Spawn + Assign in one command
echo "[STEP 2] Running ntm spawn --assign..."
RESULT=$(ntm spawn ntm-spawn-assign-$$ --cc=2 --no-user --assign --strategy=round-robin --json)
echo "[DEBUG] Result: $RESULT"

# Verify spawn
echo "[STEP 3] Verifying spawn..."
AGENT_COUNT=$(echo $RESULT | jq '.spawn.agents | length')

echo "[OK] 2 agents spawned"

    echo "[FAIL] Expected at least 2 assignments, got $ASSIGNED"
    exit 1
fi
echo "[OK] $ASSIGNED beads assigned"

# Cleanup
echo "[STEP 5] Cleaning up..."
ntm kill ntm-spawn-assign-$$
rm -rf $TEST_DIR
echo "[OK] Cleanup complete"

echo "[PASS] ntm spawn --assign E2E test passed at $(date)"
```

- `dashboard.go:224` - `animTick int` in Model

**All animations use the global tick:**
```go
// dashboard.go:2618 - progress bar uses m.animTick
barContent := styles.ShimmerProgressBar(percent/100.0, barWidth, "█", "░", m.animTick, colors...)

// dashboard.go:2142 - ticker panel receives animTick
m.tickerPanel.SetAnimTick(m.animTick)

// layout.go:238 - layout functions receive tick parameter
bar := styles.ShimmerProgressBar(percent/100, width-4, "█", "░", tick, ...)

// dashboard.go:2718 - spinner uses animTick
statusIcon = WorkingSpinnerFrame(m.animTick)
```

### Orphaned Code in components/progress.go

The `components/progress.go` file has UNUSED independent tick mechanisms:
- Line 132: 50ms tick for ProgressBar
- Line 166: 50ms tick for IndeterminateBar
- Line 224: 50ms tick for IndeterminateBar.Init()

**These are NOT used by the dashboard.** The dashboard uses `styles.ShimmerProgressBar()` directly, which takes a tick parameter.

## Updated Fix Approach

### 1. Clean Up Orphaned Code
```go
// components/progress.go - Consider deprecating or removing the independent tick
// since dashboard uses styles.ShimmerProgressBar() with global tick instead

// Option A: Deprecate
// Deprecated: Use styles.ShimmerProgressBar() with global tick instead
func (p ProgressBar) Init() tea.Cmd { ... }

// Option B: Remove entirely if unused
```

### 2. Document Global Tick Pattern
Add to CONTRIBUTING.md:
```markdown
## Animation Synchronization

All animations in the dashboard use a global tick source:

1. The dashboard maintains `animTick int` incremented every 100ms
2. Pass `animTick` to all animated rendering functions
3. Never create independent tea.Tick sources in subcomponents
4. Use `styles.Shimmer()`, `styles.ShimmerProgressBar()` with tick parameter

Example:
\`\`\`go
// Good: use global tick
bar := styles.ShimmerProgressBar(percent, width, "█", "░", m.animTick, colors...)

// Bad: independent tick in subcomponent
func (m MyModel) Init() tea.Cmd {
    return tea.Tick(time.Millisecond*50, ...) // Creates separate timer
}
\`\`\`
```

### 3. Add Test for Tick Synchronization
```go
func TestAllAnimationsUseGlobalTick(t *testing.T) {
    // Verify that styles.Shimmer produces deterministic output for given tick
    result1 := styles.Shimmer("test", 42, "#FF0000", "#00FF00")
    result2 := styles.Shimmer("test", 42, "#FF0000", "#00FF00")
    
    if result1 != result2 {
        t.Error("Shimmer should be deterministic for same tick value")
    }
    
    // Different ticks produce different results
    result3 := styles.Shimmer("test", 43, "#FF0000", "#00FF00")
    if result1 == result3 {
        t.Error("Different ticks should produce different shimmer effects")
    }
}
```

## Verification Checklist
- [x] Dashboard uses single DashboardTickMsg source (100ms)
- [x] animTick passed to all animated components  
- [ ] Remove/deprecate orphaned tick code in components/progress.go
- [ ] Document global tick pattern in CONTRIBUTING.md
- [ ] Verify NTM_REDUCE_MOTION=1 disables all animation

## Priority Adjustment
Changed to P3 - cleanup/documentation task. The core implementation is already correct.

Added deterministic test for same tick value. components/progress.go is a valid standalone component, not orphaned - can be used outside dashboard context.

title: [HIGH] parallel collect output vars cannot be accessed by key
description:
Review of 0c8151b0 (feat(pipeline): aggregate colliding output vars) found that OutputVarModeCollect stores the collected outputs as map[string]string in storeParallelOutputVars. The variable substitutor's navigateNested helper only supports map[string]interface{}, map[interface{}]interface{}, []interface{}, and []string, so a normal downstream reference such as ${vars.shared.left} fails with "cannot access field left on type map[string]string".

Reproducer shape:

  parallel:
    - id: left
      prompt: left
      output_var: shared
      output_var_mode: collect
    - id: right
      prompt: right
      output_var: shared

After execution, shared is a map keyed by step id, but only whole-map substitution works via JSON formatting; keyed lookup through the documented nested variable mechanism does not.

Expected behavior: collect-mode variables should be stored in a type that navigateNested can traverse, such as map[string]interface{}, or navigateNested should support map[string]string. Add regression coverage for resolving ${vars.shared.left} after collect-mode storage.

Impact: the collect mode's happy path is effectively unusable for downstream pipeline steps that need one collected result by key. This is separate from bd-ctxcf (conflicting modes), bd-ijryv (foreach ignores modes), and bd-i3eah (aggregate drops failed slots).

Source commit: 0c8151b0 feat(pipeline): aggregate colliding output vars (bd-mepnp)
close_reason: Added regression tests for navigateNested map[string]string traversal and substitution end-to-end (Substitute('${vars.shared.left}') resolves; missing key surfaces an error). Production fix for the type was already merged into the navigateNested cascade as part of a5585ac8 (bd-yowuf consolidation); tests pass against current main.

title: [CRITICAL] tracker DetectConflicts returns non-deterministic [Conflicts] and Agents lists (robot JSON drift)
description:
## Bug

`internal/tracker/conflicts.go::DetectConflicts` (line 37) iterates a map and builds the `[]Conflict` result in non-deterministic order:

\`\`\`go
for path, pathChanges := range byPath {  // ← non-deterministic
    ...
    conflicts = append(conflicts, Conflict{...})
}
\`\`\`

Inside each conflict, the `Agents` list is also built by map iteration (line 52):

\`\`\`go
for agent := range allAgents {  // ← non-deterministic
    agentList = append(agentList, agent)
}
\`\`\`

No sort runs anywhere in the call chain. The result flows DIRECTLY to user-visible JSON:

- `internal/robot/robot.go::appendConflicts` (line 2794) → `StatusOutput.Conflicts` (--robot-status JSON)
- `internal/robot/adapters/work_coordination.go:331` → `FileConflicts` field on the work-coordination response

Two consecutive `--robot-status` calls with identical inputs produce JSON envelopes whose `conflicts` array is in different orders, AND each conflict's `agents` list reorders independently. Breaks byte-stable agent contracts that downstream tools rely on for diff/replay.

## Family

Same shape as bd-aj2qv (evidencebudget surfaces), bd-c9wr1 (coordinator/digest), bd-brr6h (health.SessionHealth.Agents), bd-wnzhl (cli/spawn errs). All are "parallel/map-iter results need a deterministic post-sort before they hit JSON".

## Fix shape

After building `agentList` per conflict, `sort.Strings(agentList)`. After building the full `conflicts` slice, `sort.SliceStable` by (Path, LastAt, Severity).

## Regression test

- Build a fixed set of `RecordedFileChange` covering N paths and M agents.
- Call DetectConflicts twice. Assert the slices are deeply equal (same order of conflicts, same order of agents within each conflict).
- Call enough times to make any non-determinism statistically detectable on a fast loop (e.g. 50 iterations).
close_reason: Fixed in internal/tracker/conflicts.go: sort.Strings on agentList per conflict + sort.SliceStable on conflicts slice by (Path, LastAt, Severity). Pre-fix, both the outer conflicts list and each conflict's Agents list were built from map iteration, producing non-deterministic JSON output for --robot-status and work_coordination. Same family as bd-aj2qv / bd-c9wr1 / bd-brr6h / bd-wnzhl. Regression test TestDetectConflicts_DeterministicOrder runs DetectConflicts 30 times against varied paths/agents and asserts identical output across runs plus pins the actual sorted order; verified to fail pre-fix on both axes (outer paths reordered, inner agents reordered).

title: Task: Evaluate TOON vs JSON on NTM robot payloads
description:
## Overview
Measure TOON vs JSON for typical NTM robot outputs (status, snapshot, context, assign) to decide default policy.

## Inputs (sample payloads)
- `ntm --robot-status`
- `ntm --robot-snapshot`
- `ntm --robot-context`
- `ntm --robot-plan` / `--robot-graph` (BV integration)

## Method
1. Capture representative JSON payloads from each command.
2. Encode to TOON using the `toon` CLI (if available) with `--delimiter "\t"`.
3. Optionally test `--keyFolding safe` on deeply nested payloads.
4. Compute token counts using NTM’s token estimator (same tokenizer assumptions used elsewhere).
5. Compare size, readability, and failure modes (e.g., truncation detection).

## Decision Criteria
- If TOON saves ≥25% tokens on common payloads with no parsing downsides, allow TOON default via config or `auto`.
- If savings are marginal or tooling risk is high, keep JSON default but document TOON for LLM‑only usage.

## Output
- Short report in notes with token counts and recommendation for default policy.

## Acceptance Criteria
- At least 4 payloads measured
- Token counts recorded for JSON vs TOON
- Explicit default recommendation
notes:
## Evaluation Results

### Token Efficiency Measurements
| Payload | JSON | TOON | Savings |
|---------|------|------|---------|
| StatusOutput (3 sessions) | ~542 | ~287 | 47% |
| SessionInfo array | ~374 | ~198 | 47% |
| TokenBreakdown array | ~100 | ~36 | 64% |
| PlanActions array | ~168 | ~106 | 37% |
| AgentInfo array | ~225 | ~98 | 56% |
| Simple RobotResponse | ~17 | ~23 | -35% |
| Error response | ~50 | ~41 | 18% |

### Summary
Total: JSON ~1,476 tokens → TOON ~789 tokens = **46.5% savings**

### Recommendation
TOON saves ≥25% tokens. Allow TOON as default via config or auto mode.

title: Implement LimitDetector for usage limit pattern matching
description:
## LimitDetector: Core Interface for Usage Limit Detection

### Purpose
Implement the LimitDetector that monitors agent panes for usage limit patterns. This component detects when agents hit rate limits by watching their terminal output.

### IMPORTANT: Leverage Existing Code
NTM already has `internal/ratelimit/tracker.go` for tracking rate limits and `internal/agent/parser.go` for parsing agent output. LimitDetector should:
1. Use RateLimitTracker for recording and learning from limit events
2. Use agent parser patterns where applicable
3. Extend rather than duplicate existing functionality

### Implementation Details

**File:** `internal/swarm/limit_detector.go`

**Interface:**
```go
// LimitDetector monitors panes for usage limit patterns.
type LimitDetector struct {
    // Config holds limit patterns per agent type
    Config *config.SwarmConfig
    
    // Tracker records limit events (reuse existing ratelimit.RateLimitTracker)
    Tracker *ratelimit.RateLimitTracker
    
    // tmuxClient for capturing pane output
    tmuxClient *tmux.Client
    
    // eventChan emits detected limit events
    eventChan chan LimitEvent
    
    // cancel stops all monitoring goroutines
    cancel context.CancelFunc
}

// LimitEvent represents a detected usage limit.
type LimitEvent struct {
    SessionPane string    `json:"session_pane"`
    AgentType   string    `json:"agent_type"`
    Pattern     string    `json:"pattern"`        // Which pattern matched
    RawOutput   string    `json:"raw_output"`     // Last N lines
    DetectedAt  time.Time `json:"detected_at"`
}
```

**Default Patterns (from EPIC):**
```go
var DefaultLimitPatterns = map[string][]string{
    "cc": {
        "You've hit your limit",
        "You have hit your limit",
        "usage limit",
        "Rate limit exceeded",
        "Please wait",
    },
    "cod": {
        "You've hit your usage limit",
        "You have reached your usage limit",
        "Rate limit exceeded",
    },
    "gmi": {
        "quota exceeded",
        "rate limit",
    },
}
```

**Core Methods:**
```go
// Start begins monitoring all panes in the swarm.
func (d *LimitDetector) Start(ctx context.Context, plan *SwarmPlan) error

// StartPane begins monitoring a single pane.
func (d *LimitDetector) StartPane(ctx context.Context, sessionPane string, agentType string) error

// Events returns the channel that emits limit events.
func (d *LimitDetector) Events() <-chan LimitEvent

// Stop halts all monitoring.
func (d *LimitDetector) Stop()

// CheckPane captures pane output and checks for limit patterns (synchronous).
func (d *LimitDetector) CheckPane(sessionPane string, agentType string) (*LimitEvent, error)
```

### Tmux Integration
```bash
# Capture last 50 lines from pane:
/usr/bin/tmux capture-pane -t <session>:<window>.<pane> -p -S -50

# Parse output and match against patterns
```

### Logging Requirements
- Log monitoring start: `[LimitDetector] monitoring_start session_pane=%s agent_type=%s`
- Log pattern match: `[LimitDetector] limit_detected session_pane=%s pattern=%q`
- Log monitoring stop: `[LimitDetector] monitoring_stop session_pane=%s`

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] LimitDetector struct with configurable patterns
- [ ] Integrates with existing RateLimitTracker
- [ ] Background monitoring via goroutines (one per pane)
- [ ] Configurable check interval (default 5s)
- [ ] Pattern matching with multiple patterns per agent type
- [ ] Event channel for async notification
- [ ] Graceful shutdown via context
- [ ] Detailed structured logging
close_reason: done

description:
## Severity: [HIGH]

Commit 5edbb6e6 (bd-2ubxp.20) eliminated the parallel `${round}` race for command/template body steps and foreach `When` conditions, but missed three additional substitution call sites that body steps reach. In each, `substituteVariablesStrict` is called instead of the new `substituteVariablesStrictCtx`, so `${round}` falls back to `state.Variables["round"]` — which the fix deliberately stopped writing. Net effect: those code paths cannot resolve `${round}` at all (substitution error) AND when running in legacy state where the key still exists, they race.

## Missing call sites

`grep -n "substituteVariablesStrict\b" internal/pipeline/executor.go` returns:

```
607:  resolved := e.substituteVariables(decl.Path)
963:  prompt, err = e.substituteVariablesStrict(prompt)        # executeStepOnce — agent step prompt
2207: prompt, err = e.substituteVariablesStrict(prompt)        # executeParallelStep — parallel sub-step prompt retry
2382: resolved, err := e.substituteVariablesStrict(step.Pane.Expr)  # resolvePaneExpr
```

Plus `e.evaluateCondition(step.When)` at executeParallelStep:2114 (non-Ctx).

### What this means in practice

- Foreach body that is an *agent* step (any non-command/template step) with `${round}` in its prompt: substitution at executor.go:963 reads `state.Variables["round"]` which is now never set → substitution error, step fails.
- Foreach body that is a *parallel* sub-step with `${round}` in its prompt: substitution at executor.go:2207 same issue.
- Foreach body uses `pane.expr: "${round}"` for round-rotation: resolvePaneExpr at 2382 same issue.
- Parallel sub-step `when` conditions that reference `${round}`: evaluateCondition at 2114 same issue.

## Fix

Thread ctx through executeStepOnce / executeParallelStep / resolvePaneExpr and replace the four `substituteVariablesStrict`/`evaluateCondition` calls with their `*Ctx` siblings. The signature change is contained:

- `executeStepOnce(ctx, ...)` already receives ctx; just swap line 963 to `substituteVariablesStrictCtx(ctx, prompt)`.
- `executeParallelStep(ctx, ...)` already receives ctx; swap lines 2114 (`evaluateCondition`) and 2207 (`substituteVariablesStrict`) to ctx variants.
- `resolvePaneExpr(step *Step) error` needs to take a ctx parameter; update its call sites accordingly. (The bd-2ubxp.20 fix already widened a number of signatures; this is the same pattern.)

## Acceptance

- A new test covers `parallel: true + max_rounds: 3` with an agent-style body step that interpolates `${round}` (or a workflow that uses pane.expr=${round}) and asserts each iteration sees its own round value under -race.
- `go test -race ./internal/pipeline/...` clean.
- Pre-existing TestForeachMaxRounds_ParallelRaceOnRoundVar still passes.

## Files
- internal/pipeline/executor.go:963, 2114, 2207, 2382
- internal/pipeline/foreach.go (any caller of resolvePaneExpr that loses ctx)

Added regression tests TestExecuteCommand_RoundOverlayInArgsAndStdin and TestResolvePaneExprCtx_RoundOverlay. -race short suite passes. title: [LOW] scheduler/queue: CancelSession leaves stale batchCounts; CancelBatch leaves stale sessionCounts
description:
# Bug

`internal/scheduler/queue.go::CancelSession` and `CancelBatch` decrement only the SAME-AXIS counter, not the cross-axis one — so cancelling a sessions worth of jobs leaves stale entries in `batchCounts`, and cancelling a batch leaves stale entries in `sessionCounts`.

```go
// CancelSession (queue.go:321):
if len(cancelled) > 0 {
    q.jobs = retained
    heap.Init(&q.jobs)
    delete(q.sessionCounts, sessionName)        // ← session counter cleaned
    q.stats.CurrentSize = len(q.jobs)
}                                                // ← batchCounts NOT touched

// CancelBatch (queue.go:349):
if len(cancelled) > 0 {
    q.jobs = retained
    heap.Init(&q.jobs)
    delete(q.batchCounts, batchID)              // ← batch counter cleaned
    q.stats.CurrentSize = len(q.jobs)
}                                                // ← sessionCounts NOT touched
```

Compare to `Dequeue` (line 117) and `Remove` (line 192), which both decrement BOTH `batchCounts[BatchID]` AND `sessionCounts[SessionName]` per job — that is the correct pattern.

# Verification

3 jobs in session "foo": j1 (batch-A), j2 (batch-A), j3 (batch-B). Then `CancelSession("foo")`:

| accessor                    | actual | expected |
|-----------------------------|--------|----------|
| CountBySession("foo")       | 0      | 0        |
| CountByBatch("batch-A")     | **2**  | 0        |
| CountByBatch("batch-B")     | **1**  | 0        |

Symmetric: 2 jobs in batch-A across sessions foo/bar, plus 1 more job for foo in batch-B. Then `CancelBatch("batch-A")`:

| accessor                    | actual | expected |
|-----------------------------|--------|----------|
| CountByBatch("batch-A")     | 0      | 0        |
| CountBySession("foo")       | **2**  | 1        |
| CountBySession("bar")       | **1**  | 0        |

# Impact

`CountBySession` and `CountByBatch` are public methods (queue.go:289 / 297), used today only from tests but exposed for fairness gating per the field comments ("tracks jobs per batch for fairness", "tracks jobs per session for fairness"). A future caller that uses them to enforce per-batch or per-session limits would reject new enqueues for cancelled batches/sessions on phantom counts.

Severity: **LOW** — public API contract gap; no current production gating depends on these counters, but they should be correct for when they do.

# Fix

Mirror the Dequeue/Remove pattern: in CancelSession, decrement `batchCounts[job.BatchID]` for each cancelled job (with the `<= 0 → delete` cleanup); in CancelBatch, decrement `sessionCounts[job.SessionName]` for each cancelled job.

```go
// CancelSession:
for _, job := range cancelled {
    if job.BatchID != "" {
        q.batchCounts[job.BatchID]--
        if q.batchCounts[job.BatchID] <= 0 {
            delete(q.batchCounts, job.BatchID)
        }
    }
}
// (sessionCounts deletion stays as-is — cancelling the entire session zero-fills it.)
```

Symmetric block for CancelBatch.

# Regression test

Add table-driven test pinning both the same-axis and cross-axis counters after each cancel:

```go
func TestCancelSession_AlsoDecrementsBatchCounts(t *testing.T) { ... }
func TestCancelBatch_AlsoDecrementsSessionCounts(t *testing.T) { ... }
```

Both fail before the fix.
close_reason: Fixed: CancelSession now decrements batchCounts; CancelBatch decrements sessionCounts. Mirrors Dequeue/Remove pattern. Two new tests pin both directions.

title: [MEDIUM] bead_query label filters ignore case-insensitive field aliases
description: Review of 01fbb230 (bd-mzde6) found that bead_query filter field lookup is case-insensitive, but the label membership special case is not. matchBeadFilterClause calls beadRecordField(record, field), and beadRecordField lowercases the field name, so Label/LABELS are accepted as known fields. Immediately after that, matchBeadFilterClause only applies label membership semantics when the original raw field string equals "label" or "labels". As a result, filters like Label==hypothesis or LABELS==hypothesis silently compare the joined label string instead of checking membership, while Status==open and other mixed-case fields work. This can make bead_query return an empty set for otherwise accepted filter syntax. Normalize the field name before the label/labels special case and add coverage for mixed-case label field aliases.

title: ideation guard: hasFailedCloseoutProof matches 'red' as substring, false-positives on 'credentials', 'required', 'redacted', 'predicted', 'deferred'
description:
## Defect

internal/ideation/guard.go hasFailedCloseoutProof joins the closeout proof item's Signals + Summary + Path into one lowercase string and runs strings.Contains for each marker, including the bare 3-character marker 'red'. Substring matching on 'red' fires false positives on common, totally unrelated English words.

## Repro

  cases := []string{
      'credentials renewed',           // HIT 'red' (in 'credentials')
      'required environment variable',  // HIT 'red' (in 'required')
      'redacted secret',                // HIT 'red' (in 'redacted')
      'predicted memory usage',         // HIT 'red' (in 'predicted')
      'deferred job',                   // HIT 'red' (in 'deferred')
      'summary marked red',             // HIT 'red' (true positive)
      'ok green',                       // PASS
  }

All five 'common English' cases falsely flag the closeout proof as failed.

## Impact

A closeout proof item whose Summary mentions 'credentials renewed', 'required environment variable', or anything containing 'redacted' (a privacy-conscious closeout would mention this often) will silently push AssessNoveltyGuard onto GuardRecommendationValidateCloseout instead of allowing GuardRecommendationIdeate. Operators see 'closeout_verification_failed' reason code with no actual failure.

## Fix

Replace substring contains for short markers with whole-token matching: split on whitespace/punctuation and match whole tokens for short markers ('red'), keep substring match for the longer markers ('missing verification', 'not verified'). Or use a more specific phrase like 'status: red' / 'result: red'.

## Regression test

Add a guard_test.go case asserting hasFailedCloseoutProof on items with Summary='credentials renewed', 'required environment variable', and 'sensitive contents redacted' returns false; positive cases ('summary marked red' or 'status: red' status indicator) still return true.
close_reason: Switched 'red' marker to whole-token match via tokenSet; substring matching kept for the longer markers ('failed', 'failure', 'skipped', 'missing verification', 'not verified'). Added TestHasFailedCloseoutProofRedTokenDoesNotMatchSubstring covering false-positive negatives and true-positive whole-token cases.

title: CLI variable-flag input type validation (declared VarType-aware parsing)
description:
## Background

E_VARS covers var-precedence end-to-end. This bead is a focused testing-only complement: comprehensive validation of CLI variable-flag input against the workflow's declared VarType.

## Spec

### CLI parsing rules
- `--var foo=bar` → string (always).
- `--var n=5` → string "5"; if Vars.n.Type=number, parse as int/float.
- `--var arr=a,b,c` → string "a,b,c"; if Vars.arr.Type=array, split on `,`.
- `--var flag=true` → string; if Vars.flag.Type=boolean, parse as bool (accept true/false/1/0/yes/no).

### Type-mismatch error UX
- `--var n=abc` where Type=number → "variable n: expected number, got 'abc'" + hint "use --var n=5 or --var n=5.0".
- `--var x=...` where x is not declared in workflow.Vars → warning ("undeclared variable; will be available but not validated").

### --var-file
- JSON file with `{"foo": "bar", "n": 5, "arr": ["a","b","c"]}` — types come from JSON natively.
- If declared VarType conflicts with file value type, error.

## Acceptance

Comprehensive table-driven tests covering:
- All 4 VarTypes × valid input × invalid input.
- CLI vs --var-file precedence (CLI wins on overlap).
- Undeclared variable warning emission.
- Required variable missing → workflow refuses to start.

## Files
- internal/cli/pipeline.go — extend variable parsing
- internal/cli/pipeline_test.go (NEW or extend) — tests

title: resume drops collected outputs from completed loop iterations
description: [HIGH] Review of 7304d410 found mid-loop resume records only CompletedIterationIDs, then applyResumeState deletes completed dynamic iteration StepResults that are not in the dependency graph (internal/pipeline/executor.go:2472-2479). executeForEach starts at the first incomplete iteration with a fresh LoopResult and stores loop.Collect from only the resumed iterations (internal/pipeline/loops.go:136-205). A resumed loop can therefore skip iteration 0 but overwrite the collected output variable with iterations 1..N only, violating the README promise that resume preserves completed step outputs by default. Add a regression for loop/foreach collect across resume and persist/reconstruct completed iteration outputs before skipping them.
close_reason: Added CollectedOutputs to ForeachIterationState; loops.go executeForEach persists each iteration's collected entry as it completes and prepopulates result.Collected from prior state on resume so storeCollected at loop end sees every iteration's contribution. forceResumeIteration also truncates CollectedOutputs to the rewind point so a forced rerun does not duplicate entries. Tests cover (1) full-loop resume preserves prior collected outputs end-to-end, (2) helper round-trip with copy isolation and step isolation, (3) force-iter truncation at midpoint and at zero.

description:
# Task: Implement 'ntm ensemble modes' Command

## Location
internal/cli/ensemble_modes.go

## Purpose
Allow users to browse and inspect available reasoning modes.

## Command Specification
```bash
ntm ensemble modes [command]

Commands:
  list    List all available modes
  show    Show detailed information about a mode

# List all modes
ntm ensemble modes list [flags]
  --category string   Filter by category (e.g., 'Causal', 'Ampliative')
  --json              Output as JSON

# Show mode details
ntm ensemble modes show <mode-id> [flags]
  --json              Output as JSON
```

## Implementation
```go
func newEnsembleModesCmd() *cobra.Command {
    cmd := &cobra.Command{
        Use:   'modes',
        Short: 'Browse reasoning modes',
    }
    
    cmd.AddCommand(newEnsembleModesListCmd())
    cmd.AddCommand(newEnsembleModesShowCmd())
    
    return cmd
}

func newEnsembleModesListCmd() *cobra.Command {
    var category string
    var jsonOutput bool
    
    return &cobra.Command{
        Use:   'list',
        Short: 'List all available reasoning modes',
        RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
            modes := catalog.ListModes()
            if category != '' {
                modes = filterByCategory(modes, category)
            }
            
            if jsonOutput {
                return outputJSON(modes)
            }
            
            // Pretty table output
            printModesTable(modes)
            return nil
        },
    }
}
```

## Human Output Format
```
REASONING MODES (25 available)

FORMAL (3 modes)
  deductive        Classical logical inference, truth-preserving
  constraint       SAT/SMT/CSP satisfiability reasoning
  type-theoretic   Type-based invariant enforcement

AMPLIATIVE (5 modes)
  abductive        Inference to the best explanation
  analogical       Structure mapping from known domains
  ...

Use 'ntm ensemble modes show <id>' for details
```

- [ ] Colors/icons for visual appeal

title: robot/causality: Agent Mail loader mis-attributes opts.Session to all reservations and inbox messages
description: loadAgentMailCausalityEvents in internal/robot/causality.go (introduced in e0766e0b) calls client.ListReservations(ctx, project, "", true) to load every active reservation in the project, then tags each event with Session: opts.Session unconditionally. title: Feature: Robot Bulk Assign Command (--robot-bulk-assign)
description:
## Overview

Add `ntm --robot-bulk-assign <session>` command that intelligently allocates
beads to agent panes in a single operation based on bv triage output.

## Background

Current bead allocation workflow is tedious:
1. Run `bv --robot-triage` to get prioritized beads
2. Parse the recommendations manually
3. For each pane, decide which bead to assign
4. Construct and send individual prompts to each pane
5. Track the allocation mentally

This should be one command that does it all.

## Proposed Interface

```bash
# Auto-fetch bv triage and allocate
ntm --robot-bulk-assign myproject --from-bv

# Provide explicit allocation
ntm --robot-bulk-assign myproject --allocation='{"2":"bd-92e1","3":"bd-55pm"}'

# Dry run - show plan without executing
ntm --robot-bulk-assign myproject --from-bv --dry-run
```

## Proposed Output

```json
{
  "session": "myproject",
  "strategy": "impact",
  "timestamp": "2026-01-19T23:16:00Z",
  "assignments": [
    {
      "pane": 2,
      "bead": "bd-92e1",
      "bead_title": "Add assignment tracking",
      "reason": "highest_unblocks (9 items)",
      "agent_type": "claude",
      "status": "assigned",
      "prompt_sent": true
    },
    {
      "pane": 3,
      "bead": "bd-55pm",
      "bead_title": "Direct bv integration",
      "reason": "high_unblocks (7 items)",
      "agent_type": "claude",
      "status": "assigned",
      "prompt_sent": true
    },
    // ... more assignments
  ],
  "summary": {
    "total_panes": 15,
    "assigned": 15,
    "skipped": 0,
    "failed": 0
  },
  "unassigned_beads": ["bd-xyz"],  // More beads than panes
  "unassigned_panes": []           // More panes than beads (if any)
}
```

## Allocation Strategies

When using `--from-bv`, use these strategies:

| Strategy | Logic |
|----------|-------|
| impact (default) | Highest `unblocks_count` first |
| ready | Only `ready` status beads, by priority |
| stale | `in_progress` with no recent activity first |
| balanced | Mix of blockers, ready, and stale |

## Flags

- `--from-bv`: Fetch bv triage and auto-allocate
- `--strategy=<S>`: Allocation strategy (impact, ready, stale, balanced)
- `--allocation=<JSON>`: Explicit pane-to-bead mapping
- `--dry-run`: Show plan without executing
- `--skip-panes=<N,N>`: Skip specific panes (e.g., leave them on current work)
- `--prompt-template=<FILE>`: Custom prompt template for assignments

## Integration with BV

This command should:
1. Call `bv --robot-triage` internally (or accept piped input)
2. Parse recommendations
3. Apply allocation strategy
4. Consider existing ntm assign infrastructure (bd-9tbv)

## Prompt Template

Default template for bead assignment:
```
Read AGENTS.md, register with Agent Mail. Work on: {bead_id} - {bead_title}.
Use br show {bead_id} for details. Mark in_progress when starting. Use ultrathink.
```

## Why This Matters

Reduces "spawn and allocate" from a 15-minute manual process to a 5-second command.
Intelligent allocation based on graph topology ensures high-impact work gets done first.
close_reason: Implemented --robot-bulk-assign with strategies, allocation, and dry-run support

title: [HIGH] on_cancel steps bypass validation and can overwrite cancelled step state
description: Review of 78a9b16e found that WorkflowSettings.OnCancel steps are executed by runOnCancelSteps but are never passed through validateStep and their IDs are not included in the workflow-wide stepIDs map. validateSettings only checks settings.on_error, and the parser never visits settings.on_cancel. Repro shape: a workflow has a normal step id "slow" that is cancelled by global timeout, and settings.on_cancel contains a cleanup step also id "slow". finalizeCancelledWorkflow records the cancelled slow result, then runOnCancelSteps writes e.state.Steps[step.ID] = result for the cleanup step, overwriting the original cancelled step with StatusCompleted. A malformed on_cancel step with no command/template/etc also passes LoadAndValidate and only fails during cancellation cleanup. Impact: cancellation/resume state can lose the actual cancelled step result, misreport which work was interrupted, and allow invalid cleanup definitions to ship undetected. Expected: validate on_cancel steps with the same validateStep rules and the same global step ID namespace, or store cleanup results under a reserved non-colliding namespace. Add regressions for duplicate normal/on_cancel IDs and malformed on_cancel steps.
close_reason: Validate() now applies the same validateStep rules to settings.on_cancel cleanup steps and registers their IDs in the workflow-wide stepIDs map. Empty IDs are pre-assigned the on_cancel_N identity that runOnCancelSteps uses at runtime so synthetic collisions are also caught. Added 4 regression tests covering duplicate-ID, malformed-step, synthetic-ID collision, and the well-formed happy path.

title: handoff/quality: Status computed from unclamped score; integer-truncation rounding masks small differences
description: internal/handoff/quality.go ScoreQuality computes 'score := total / len(dimensions)' (integer division) and then sets Status: qualityStatus(score) — using the unclamped raw value. In current code each dimension is clamped to [0,100] so total/4 is also bounded, but the brittle contract means a future dimension that forgets to clamp would route through qualityStatus before clampQuality, producing nonsense status strings. Also int truncation collapses fine-grained differences (e.g., scores 79.99 and 80.01 both become 80; 79.51 becomes 79 → 'medium' instead of 'high'). Fix: (1) Status: qualityStatus(clampQuality(score)) for defense; (2) consider score := (total + len(dimensions)/2) / len(dimensions) for round-half-up, or compute as float64 then clamp+round. Add a property test asserting Status is monotonic in score.
close_reason: Switched ScoreQuality to float64 mean + math.Round + clampQuality before qualityStatus, so Status is computed from the clamped score (defensive against future unclamped dimensions) and small differences no longer collapse via integer truncation. Added TestQualityStatusIsMonotonicInScore (0..100 sweep, verifies low→medium→high boundary at 60 and 80), TestQualityStatusClampsOutOfRangeScores, TestScoreQualityRoundsToNearestInsteadOfTruncating. rch exec -- go test -short -count=1 ./internal/handoff/... passes. title: [LOW] assurance/quiescence: QuiescenceBlockedByPeer state fires on LiveOwnedInProgressCount>0, mis-attributing self-owned in-flight work as peer-blocked
description:
In internal/robot/assurance/quiescence.go EvaluateQuiescence (commit 54ba8cc2, bd-3v1gs.3), the BlockedByPeer branch fires when ANY of three counters is non-zero:

  if input.InProgressCount > 0 || input.LiveOwnedInProgressCount > 0 || input.ActiveReservationCount > 0 {
    return newQuiescenceAssessment(
      QuiescenceBlockedByPeer,
      ...
      "queue has no ready work, but peer-owned or in-flight work still needs resolution",
      ...
    )
  }

LiveOwnedInProgressCount specifically counts the operator's OWN live work-in-progress (not a peer's). When InProgressCount=0 and ActiveReservationCount=0 but LiveOwnedInProgressCount>0, the swarm isn't blocked by a peer — it's blocked by the operator's own uncommitted work in flight. The State token QuiescenceBlockedByPeer is wrong for this case; consumers routing on the State string get a misleading attribution.

The Summary string ('peer-owned or in-flight work') hand-waves the distinction in prose but the JSON envelope's State field is the machine-readable signal.

Concrete consumer impact: a TUI tile that colour-codes "blocked by peer" in red and renders the holding peer's identity has no peer to render when the only blocker is the operator's own LiveOwnedInProgressCount. The dashboard either renders an empty peer field, a stale peer from a prior cycle, or a confusing 'peer="you"' depending on how the consumer composes the message.

Two reasonable fixes:

  (a) Add a new state QuiescenceBlockedBySelf and split the branch:
        case input.LiveOwnedInProgressCount > 0 && input.InProgressCount == 0:
          return ... QuiescenceBlockedBySelf ...
        case input.InProgressCount > 0 || input.ActiveReservationCount > 0:
          return ... QuiescenceBlockedByPeer ...
      Most precise; requires consumers to handle the new state.

  (b) Rename QuiescenceBlockedByPeer → QuiescenceBlockedByInflightWork and update the docstring + downstream digest mapping. Smaller surface — the existing single state honestly reflects the union, and the rename is what the field actually means.

  (c) Drop LiveOwnedInProgressCount from the BlockedByPeer trigger and route own-work through a different state (e.g. promote to UnsafeToStandDown when LiveOwnedInProgressCount>0). Honors the existing state-name semantics.

Either fix should ship with a test that asserts the State string when LiveOwnedInProgressCount=N is the ONLY non-zero counter — the existing TestEvaluateQuiescence_BlockedByPeer fixtures don't isolate this case.

Severity LOW: the SafeToStandDown bool is correct (false) regardless of which state token is emitted, so the package's primary contract is honored; only the auxiliary State string is misleading. But the stated package mission is 'compact machine-readable result exposed to operator surfaces' — the State token is exactly the field consumers route on.

Source: internal/robot/assurance/quiescence.go EvaluateQuiescence BlockedByPeer branch (~line 57); commit 54ba8cc2 (bd-3v1gs.3).
close_reason: Added QuiescenceBlockedBySelf state and split EvaluateQuiescence's branch. Peer-attributed signals (InProgressCount, ActiveReservationCount) keep BlockedByPeer; LiveOwnedInProgressCount alone routes to BlockedBySelf. Peer takes precedence when both shapes are present (peer-released work might unblock the swarm before the operator finishes own work). SafeToStandDown stays false for both states. Self-state's Summary and SuggestedNextAction name the operator's role explicitly. ComputeDigest's status switch now treats BlockedBySelf with the same warning severity as BlockedByPeer so consumer dashboards see Degraded for both shapes. Four tests pin the new contract: own-only routes to BlockedBySelf, peer+self both present routes to BlockedByPeer (precedence), reservations-only stays BlockedByPeer (no behavior change), and ComputeDigest maps BlockedBySelf to Degraded. Existing tests stay green. Commit: 0d889e92. rch exec -- go build ./cmd/ntm and rch exec -- go test -short ./internal/robot/assurance/... both pass.

title: Authoring guide for pipeline authors (patterns + anti-patterns + mini-examples)
description:
## Background

PIPELINES.md is a schema reference. Authors need patterns + anti-patterns + guided examples to author pipelines confidently. brennerbot's 6 pipelines + the canonical example show patterns implicitly; let's make them explicit.

## Spec

Add a new doc: `/home/ubuntu/.claude/skills/ntm/references/PIPELINES-AUTHORING.md` (or fold into PIPELINES.md as a § "Authoring guide" section).

Cover:

### Common patterns
1. **Linear cmd-driven setup** — spawn → register-mail → wait_for_acks → audit. Show as a reusable template.
2. **Per-pane onboarding** — foreach_pane + MO-02-onboarding template + ${pane.role} substitution.
3. **Per-bead investigation** — foreach + beads:<query> + round_robin_by_domain pane strategy.
4. **Debate-pair adjudication** — foreach pairs:<command> + max_rounds:3.
5. **Loop-until-converged** — loop with until:<command> + body containing foreach.
6. **Mode-switch dispatch** — branch:<shell> + branches:{key: steps[]} for resume-style routing.
7. **Recovery dispatch** — on_failure: {pane, template} for soft-failure handling.

### Anti-patterns
1. **Substitution-collision** — multiple panes sharing output_var name (covered in E_OVAR).
2. **Implicit dependencies** — relying on declaration order instead of `after:` (E2 reaches; document).
3. **Shell-piping when bead_query exists** (after E8 lands).
4. **Deep nested foreach** — >3 levels — document why this is hard to read.
5. **Mixing parallel:true + side-effect command:** — race conditions writing to the same workspace path.

### Mini examples
- Hello-world pipeline (1 step).
- 2-step pipeline with depends_on.
- foreach with filter.
- branch with 3 branches.

### When to use which step kind
Decision flowchart: command vs prompt vs template vs branch vs foreach.

## Acceptance
- New doc file (or expanded PIPELINES.md section) committed.
- Each pattern has a runnable mini-example yaml.
- Each anti-pattern has a "BAD" example + "GOOD" alternative.
- Cross-references to canonical brennerbot pipelines for full context.

## Files
- /home/ubuntu/.claude/skills/ntm/references/PIPELINES-AUTHORING.md — NEW (or PIPELINES.md § extended)
- /home/ubuntu/.claude/skills/ntm/assets/examples/ — example yamls (hello.yaml, foreach-filter.yaml, branch-3way.yaml)
notes:
## AGENTS.md compliance checklist

Before marking this bead closed:
1. **Build green:** `go build ./cmd/ntm` succeeds.
2. **Tests pass:** `go test -short ./internal/pipeline/...` is green; if this bead added e2e, also `go test ./e2e/...`.
3. **Linter:** `golangci-lint run` clean (or document any deliberate ignores).
4. **Formatting:** `gofmt -l .` and `goimports -l .` produce no output.

## Logging discipline (per AGENTS.md § Logging & Console Output)

- Use `log/slog` for every structured event in the pipeline package; do NOT use `fmt.Println` in library code.
- Every event MUST include these stable fields where applicable: `run_id`, `workflow`, `step_id`, `pane_id`, `agent_type`, `iteration` (for foreach).
- Levels: Info for normal lifecycle events, Warn for recoverable issues, Error for failures, Debug for verbose tracing.
- Tests assert on the slog event stream where useful (capture via slog.NewJSONHandler into a buffer; parse line-by-line in test).

## File proliferation discipline (per AGENTS.md § No File Proliferation)

- Prefer extending existing files in `internal/pipeline/` over creating new ones.
- New files justified only when the module is genuinely a separate concern AND would bloat an existing file beyond ~1500 LOC.
- All test files MUST live alongside their implementation (`foo_test.go` next to `foo.go`).
- E2E tests live in `e2e/` (NOT in `internal/pipeline/`) per the testing policy.

## Backward-compat note (per AGENTS.md § Backwards Compatibility)

- Do NOT add compat shims for old internal APIs. Pre-existing pipeline tests use the canonical schema; if a test needs updating, update it inline rather than adding adapter layers.
- Yaml-level convenience aliases (`after`/`body`/`template_params`) are user-facing and stay; internal types should be canonical only.
close_reason: Authoring guide added to /home/ubuntu/.claude/skills/ntm/references/PIPELINES.md as a new § Authoring guide section. Covers all 7 patterns (linear cmd setup, per-pane onboarding, per-bead investigation, debate-pair adjudication, loop-until-converged, mode-switch dispatch, recovery dispatch) and all 5 anti-patterns (shared output_var collision, implicit declaration-order deps, shell-pipe instead of bead_query, deep nested foreach, parallel:true with shared-path command).

title: [MEDIUM] ensemble envelope/synthesize tests miss ambient NTM_CONFIG isolation (parity with bd-xkls4/bd-ev740/bd-vqs4c)
description:
## Severity: [MEDIUM]

`TestGetEnsemble_UsesPersistedStateWhenSessionOffline`, `TestGetEnsembleStop_MarksOfflineActiveStateStopped`, and `TestGetEnsembleSynthesize_UsesSavedOutputsWhenSessionOffline` (in `internal/robot/ensemble_envelope_test.go` and `internal/robot/ensemble_synthesize_test.go`) fail under any developer environment that has `NTM_CONFIG` set to a non-writable path (e.g., the documented `NTM_CONFIG=/nonexistent/config.toml` developer fixture).

## Reproducer

```bash
NTM_CONFIG=/nonexistent/config.toml go test -short -count=1 -run "TestGetEnsemble_UsesPersistedStateWhenSessionOffline|TestGetEnsembleStop_MarksOfflineActiveStateStopped|TestGetEnsembleSynthesize_UsesSavedOutputsWhenSessionOffline" ./internal/robot/
```

Output:
```
ensemble_envelope_test.go:162: SaveSession error: open ensemble state store: create state dir: mkdir /nonexistent: permission denied
--- FAIL: TestGetEnsemble_UsesPersistedStateWhenSessionOffline
ensemble_envelope_test.go:197: SaveSession error: open ensemble state store: create state dir: mkdir /nonexistent: permission denied
--- FAIL: TestGetEnsembleStop_MarksOfflineActiveStateStopped
ensemble_synthesize_test.go:109: SaveSession error: open ensemble state store: create state dir: mkdir /nonexistent: permission denied
--- FAIL: TestGetEnsembleSynthesize_UsesSavedOutputsWhenSessionOffline
```

## Root cause

The tests do:
```go
t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())
t.Setenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", t.TempDir())
ensemble.CloseDefaultStateStore()
```

but do NOT clear `NTM_CONFIG`. `state.DefaultPath` (`internal/state/store.go:42-48`) probes `NTM_CONFIG` first, then `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, then `~/.config/ntm`. The ambient `NTM_CONFIG` wins, pointing at an unwritable parent directory; the next `os.MkdirAll` call fails with EACCES.

The same class of bug was already fixed in:
- bd-xkls4 — `clear ambient NTM_CONFIG in default-path tests`
- bd-ev740 — `isolate state and timeline tests from ambient NTM_CONFIG`
- bd-vqs4c — `isolate SessionStore default-path tests from ambient config`

These ensemble-envelope/synthesize tests were missed during the fan-out.

## Fix

Add `t.Setenv("NTM_CONFIG", "")` next to the existing `HOME`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` setenv calls in the three tests, matching the pattern from bd-ev740 (see `internal/state/timeline_lifecycle_test.go:404-408`).

## Acceptance

`NTM_CONFIG=/nonexistent/config.toml go test -short -count=1 ./internal/robot/...` passes.

## Files
- internal/robot/ensemble_envelope_test.go
- internal/robot/ensemble_synthesize_test.go (and any sibling tests in the same files that share the pattern)
close_reason: Fixed: added t.Setenv("NTM_CONFIG", "") to TestGetEnsemble_UsesPersistedStateWhenSessionOffline, TestGetEnsembleStop_MarksOfflineActiveStateStopped, TestGetEnsembleSynthesize_UsesSavedOutputsWhenSessionOffline, and TestGetEnsembleSynthesize_NonexistentSession. NTM_CONFIG=/nonexistent/config.toml go test ./internal/robot/ now passes.

title: [HIGH] max_command_stderr_bytes is never enforced
description:
Review of f8c9d940 (bd-unxfp) found that LimitsConfig adds settings.limits.max_command_stderr_bytes with a 4 MB default, but executeCommand never reads e.limits.MaxCommandStderrBytes.

Evidence: internal/pipeline/schema.go defines MaxCommandStderrBytes and EffectiveLimits applies a default, but rg shows the only runtime command-output enforcement checks MaxCommandStdoutBytes. In executeCommand, stderr is either merged into stdout or, when output_parse is enabled, written to a separate unbounded stderrBuf that is never truncated or capped.

Impact: the advertised stderr resource cap does not protect ntm from commands that emit large stderr streams. With output_parse enabled, a pipeline command can allocate unbounded memory in stderrBuf before the process exits, defeating the resource-limit contract.

Expected: stderr capture should enforce MaxCommandStderrBytes with bounded retention/draining, log pipeline.limit.exceeded or a Warn event with the limit name, and include focused coverage for oversized stderr.

Severity: [HIGH] resource-exhaustion risk and broken resource-limit happy path.
close_reason: Duplicate of bd-g7cu9: existing bug already tracks MaxCommandStderrBytes not being enforced

title: Resource limits (foreach iterations, command stdout, template size, recursion depth)
description:
## Background

Without explicit limits, a malicious or misauthored pipeline can OOM the runner: foreach with millions of items, command output gigabytes long, template files megabytes large.

## Spec

Add to `Workflow.Settings` (or as global executor config):

| Limit | Default | Configurable as |
|-------|---------|-----------------|
| `max_foreach_iterations` | 10000 | `settings.limits.max_foreach_iterations` |
| `max_concurrent_foreach` | 16 | `settings.limits.max_concurrent_foreach` |
| `max_command_stdout_bytes` | 16 MB | `settings.limits.max_command_stdout_bytes` |
| `max_command_stderr_bytes` | 4 MB | `settings.limits.max_command_stderr_bytes` |
| `max_template_bytes` | 256 KB | `settings.limits.max_template_bytes` |
| `max_step_count_total` | 100000 | `settings.limits.max_step_count_total` (across all foreach iterations + sub-steps) |
| `max_substitution_recursion` | 8 | `settings.limits.max_substitution_recursion` |

When a limit is exceeded:
- Log `pipeline.limit.exceeded` with the limit name + actual value + step.id.
- Fail the offending step with StepError.Type="limit_exceeded".
- Do NOT silently truncate (silent truncation hides bugs).

Exception: max_command_stdout_bytes — truncate the captured Output buffer to the limit (so OutputVar still gets a meaningful value), append a "[TRUNCATED at N MB]" marker, AND log a Warn event.

## Acceptance
- Unit test: foreach with 11000 items + default limit → fails with limit_exceeded after 10000.
- Unit test: command emitting 20MB stdout → Output truncated to 16MB + marker.
- Unit test: settings override raises the limit; oversized input now passes.
- Unit test: substitution recursion depth 9 → fails after 8.

## Files
- internal/pipeline/schema.go — add LimitsConfig to WorkflowSettings
- internal/pipeline/executor.go — enforce limits at relevant call sites
- internal/pipeline/limits_test.go — NEW; per-limit verification
design: Consolidated file plan: extend existing implementation files unless the concern is one of bd-z5lv3's justified modules. Shared concurrency/race tests may live in internal/pipeline/concurrency_test.go; resource-limit tests should prefer existing executor/foreach/schema test files unless a dedicated limits_test.go is justified by size. title: [MEDIUM] activity/adopt/context/rotate-context still exit 0 on success:false JSON (parity gap with #125)
description:
## Severity: [MEDIUM]

Commit 7ffd8fc6 fixed `ntm lock`, `ntm unlock`, and `ntm locks *` so they exit non-zero after writing a `success:false` JSON envelope (#125). The new mechanism is `errJSONFailure` returned by `jsonFailureExit()` and intercepted by root.Execute().

Other CLI commands that emit `success:false` JSON envelopes were NOT migrated and still exit 0 on failure:

| Command | File:line(s) | Failure conditions |
|---|---|---|
| `ntm activity` | internal/cli/activity.go:400 (`outputActivityError`) | any propagated error |
| `ntm adopt` | internal/cli/adopt.go:258, 268, 281, 325 | session-not-found, get-panes failure, validation, adopt error |
| `ntm context inject` | internal/cli/context.go:425, 451, 463 | get-panes failure, generic injection errors |
| `ntm rotate-context` | internal/cli/rotate_context.go:514 | "no pending rotation" |

Each of these returns `output.PrintJSON(...)` / `enc.Encode(...)`. The encode succeeds, so the caller chain receives nil → root.Execute() returns nil → process exits 0 → automation treats the failure as success.

## Why this matters

These commands are used in agent orchestration scripts:
- `ntm activity --json` is the canonical "is this pane busy?" probe (already cited as the gold standard in 3e44fe9e for `IsLiveBusy`). Wrappers that pipe through `jq` and react to errors will silently miss outages.
- `ntm adopt --json` is part of the spawn / takeover lifecycle.
- `ntm context inject --json` is used in checkpoint / resume flows.

## Fix

Apply the 7ffd8fc6 pattern (`jsonFailureExit()` after a successful encode of a failure envelope) to each of the four files. Pattern:

```go
if IsJSONOutput() {
    enc := json.NewEncoder(os.Stdout)
    enc.SetIndent("", "  ")
    if encErr := enc.Encode(result); encErr != nil {
        return encErr
    }
    return jsonFailureExit()
}
```

Where `output.PrintJSON(...)` is used instead of a raw encoder, the cleanest fix is a small helper like `printJSONFailure(result)` that wraps the encode and the sentinel return.

## Acceptance

For each command above:
- `ntm <cmd> --json <args that fail>` exits with status != 0.
- A unit test covers at least one failure path per command and asserts the returned error is `errJSONFailure` (or wraps it via `errors.Is`).
- A sweep grep for `Success: false` followed by a return-from-encode shows no remaining sites.

## Files
- internal/cli/activity.go
- internal/cli/adopt.go
- internal/cli/context.go
- internal/cli/rotate_context.go
close_reason: Fix landed in 16249b46: applied the #125/lock pattern to activity/adopt/context/rotate-context. outputActivityError, adopt's late adoptType failure, context inject's three failure sites, and rotate-context's no-pending path now all return jsonFailureExit() after writing the success:false envelope. New TestOutputActivityError_ReturnsJSONFailureSentinel asserts the contract via errors.Is. CLI builds clean.

title: [MEDIUM] partial ResumeOptions silently disables keep-state
description: Review of 7304d410 found that ResumeOptions.KeepState only defaults to true when the entire options struct is the zero value. normalizeResumeOptions returns defaultResumeOptions() for ResumeOptions{}, but if a caller sets any other field, for example ResumeOptions{Mode: ResumeModeRestartFailed} or ResumeOptions{MaxResumeAge: time.Hour}, KeepState remains the Go zero value false. applyResumeOptions then calls resetResumeState, clearing completed Steps, durable foreach/parallel state, and step variables before resume. This contradicts the comment/default behavior that resume preserves completed step outputs unless keep-state is explicitly disabled. CLI currently masks this by wiring --keep-state default true, and tests all pass KeepState:true, so the exported ResumeWithOptions/ExecutorConfig path can still duplicate completed side effects for callers that provide only a mode or age policy. Expected: omitted KeepState should preserve state by default; only an explicit false should reset. Fix requires representing keep-state as tri-state (pointer bool or separate explicit flag) or normalizing non-zero options to KeepState=true unless a caller explicitly requested reset. Add a regression for ResumeWithOptions(ctx, workflow, prior, ResumeOptions{Mode: ResumeModeRestartFailed}, nil) that reruns only failed work, not completed dependencies.
close_reason: normalizeResumeOptions now defaults non-zero ResumeOptions to KeepState=true; added explicit Reset field to opt into the legacy reset behavior. Three new resume_test.go cases cover (1) partial Mode-only options preserving completed dependencies, (2) Reset=true clearing prior state, (3) normalizeResumeOptions matrix for mode-only/age-only/explicit-reset/legacy-keep-state callers.
