`internal/robot/events.go:293-304`. `feed.Replay(SinceCursor, limit+1)` returns the oldest `limit+1` events. If `filterEventsForRobot` drops them all, `len(filtered)==0` and `nextCursor = newestCursor` (the whole-feed max).

Trigger: 500 events with the only `alert` at cursor 300. `--since-cursor=0 --events-limit=100 --events-category=alert` returns `events:[], next_cursor:500, has_more:false`; the loop resumes at 500 and never sees cursor 300. `hasMore := len(filtered) > limit` also under-reports whenever anything is filtered. The same code backs HTTP (`internal/serve/server.go:5414`).

Fix: `hasMore := len(events) > limit`; when `filtered` is empty but `events` is not, use `events[len(events)-1].Cursor`.
close_reason: hasMore is now judged on the replayed page rather than the filtered subset, and next_cursor advances to the last event of the page actually consumed instead of jumping to the whole feed's newest cursor. Previously a page whose every event was filtered out reported next_cursor = newestCursor, so a loop resumed past everything in between: with 500 events and the only alert at cursor 300, --since-cursor=0 --events-limit=100 --events-category=alert returned an empty page with next_cursor 500 and the match was never returned. Same code backs the HTTP surface at internal/serve/server.go:5414.

title: robot: multi-window pane index collisions corrupt --robot-diagnose --fix and project health
description:
Two sites key maps by a window-local pane index on sessions that span windows.

`internal/robot/diagnose.go:478` and `:613`: `paneIDByIndex := map[int]string{}` and `typesByIndex := make(map[int]string, ...)` are keyed only by `p.Index`. With windows 0 and 1 both holding a pane 1, the later entry overwrites the earlier, so a crashed pane 1 in window 0 is respawned at window 1's pane 1, and `validateDiagnoseFixTargets` checks `ValidateAutomatedRelaunch` against the other pane's agent type (letting a grok pane through, or blocking a supported one). The `p.Index == opts.Pane` filter at `:190-196` matches multiple panes for the same reason, producing `"crashed":[1,1]`.

`internal/robot/health.go:280`: `paneKey := fmt.Sprintf("%d", pane.Index)` then `sessHealth.Agents[paneKey] = agentHealth`. Window 1's pane 0 overwrites window 0's pane 0, so `sessions[].agents` reports fewer agents than exist and the survivor's health is attributed to the wrong pane. Reachable via `ntm serve` (`internal/serve/server.go:2792`). The `!agentHealth.Responsive` alert at `:288` also names an ambiguous pane.

Fix: key both maps by canonical `W.P` / pane ID (`tmux.PaneTargetKey(pane, multiWindow)`) and carry that identity in `DiagnoseRecommendation`.
close_reason: Both index-collision sites now key on the unambiguous pane target. DiagnoseRecommendation gained PaneTarget (%ID or W.P), populated at all six construction sites including buildRateLimitRecommendation; the --fix path's paneIDByIndex became paneIDByTarget and validateDiagnoseFixTargets' typesByIndex became typesByTarget, so --fix can no longer respawn a pane in an unrelated window or validate the wrong pane's agent type. GetProjectHealth's sessHealth.Agents map moved from fmt.Sprintf("%d", pane.Index) to tmux.PaneTargetKey, so window 1's pane 0 no longer overwrites window 0's pane 0 (which under-reported the agent count and attributed the survivor's health to the wrong pane), and the derived alert now names an unambiguous pane. diagnoseRecommendationKey falls back to the bare index when PaneTarget is absent, which is safe because that is exactly what paneTargetKey yields for a single-window session — the only topology where an index is unambiguous. Covered by TestValidateDiagnoseFixTargetsDistinguishesPanesAcrossWindows (two windows each holding a pane 1: window 0's claude allowed, window 1's grok refused, error naming 1.1) and TestDiagnoseRecommendationKeyFallsBackToIndex. Note DiagnosePanes still reports []int index lists, which remains ambiguous on multi-window sessions but is the published JSON shape; the harmful actuation path is what is fixed here.

title: status: multi-line recovery prompts are delivered to the agent in fragments
description:
`internal/status/recovery.go:234`. `sendRecoveryPrompt` calls `tmux.SendKeys(target, prompt, enter)` — raw `send-keys -l`. But `BuildContextAwarePrompt` (`:176`) appends `"

# Project Context from Beads
"` plus per-bullet `
`s whenever `bv` is installed (`IncludeBeadContext` defaults to true), so the payload is always multi-line.

Verified on tmux 3.5a: `send-keys -l -- $'line1
line2
line3'` delivers each `
` to the pane as a real Enter, so the agent receives roughly 15 separate partial prompts instead of one. `sendRecoveryPromptByIDForAgent` already resolved and holds `agentType` but never uses it for the send mechanism.

Fix: thread `agentType` into `sendRecoveryPrompt` and call `tmux.SendKeysForAgent(target, prompt, enter, tmux.AgentType(agentType))` so `needsBufferSend` routes newline-containing prompts through `load-buffer`/`paste-buffer`.
close_reason: sendRecoveryPrompt now takes the agent type and calls tmux.SendKeysForAgent instead of raw tmux.SendKeys, so needsBufferSend routes newline-containing prompts through load-buffer/paste-buffer. sendRecoveryPromptByIDForAgent had already resolved agentType at its top but never used it for the send mechanism. This matters on every recovery because BuildContextAwarePrompt appends a '# Project Context from Beads' block plus a newline per bullet whenever bv is installed and IncludeBeadContext defaults to true — so the payload is essentially always multi-line, and send-keys -l delivers each newline as a real Enter, giving the agent roughly a dozen partial prompts instead of one. Covered by TestSendRecoveryPromptForwardsAgentTypeForBufferRouting; needsBufferSend's routing is already covered in the tmux package.

title: tmux: send-keys silently strips a trailing semicolon, and chunking makes it data-dependent
description:
`internal/tmux/session.go:1544,1565`. tmux's `cmd_parse_from_arguments` treats any argument ending in an unescaped `;` as a command terminator, and `--` does not protect it.

Verified on tmux 3.5a: `send-keys -l -- 'A=x;'` delivers `A=x`; `'C=y;;'` delivers `C=y;`; a payload of exactly `';'` sends nothing at all. This corrupts any prompt or command ending in `;`, and the 4096-byte chunk loop at `:1553-1567` makes it data-dependent: any chunk boundary landing right after a `;` silently drops that byte mid-prompt.

Fix: escape a trailing semicolon before invoking `send-keys -l` (verified working: `'D=x\;'` delivers `D=x;`), or route payloads containing `;` through `SendBufferWithDelayContext` (`load-buffer` reads stdin and is unaffected).
close_reason: SendKeysWithDelayContext now escapes a trailing semicolon on every payload and on every chunk, via the new escapeTrailingSemicolon. Verified empirically on tmux 3.5a before the fix: send-keys -l -- 'A=x;' delivered 'A=x', 'C=y;;' delivered 'C=y;', and 'D=z\;' delivered 'D=z;' — so -- does not protect a trailing semicolon from cmd_parse_from_arguments. Verified again after the fix through the real send path: 'A=x;' now delivers 'A=x;', 'C=y;;' delivers 'C=y;;', and 'run this; and that;' arrives intact. Escaping per chunk matters because the 4096-byte chunk loop made the truncation data-dependent: any boundary landing right after a semicolon dropped that byte from mid-prompt. Interior semicolons are untouched and an already-escaped trailing semicolon is left alone (odd/even backslash count). Covered by TestEscapeTrailingSemicolon.

title: state: Tx.DeleteRuntimeHandoff runs an unscoped DELETE, destroying other sessions' handoff rows
description:
`internal/state/runtime_store.go:1138-1139` executes `DELETE FROM runtime_handoff` with no WHERE clause. Migration ntm#135 re-keyed this table on `(session_name, working_dir)`, and a correctly scoped `Tx.DeleteRuntimeHandoffByScope` sits 11 lines below at `:1149`, but the unscoped version is what the projection path calls: `internal/robot/robot.go:7742` does `if handoffRow == nil { tx.DeleteRuntimeHandoff() }`.

`buildRuntimeHandoffRow` (`robot.go:8085-8095`) returns nil whenever the coordination section is absent OR `Session`/`Goal`/`Now`/`Status` are all blank — e.g. a transient Agent Mail outage. So one handoff-less projection tick deletes every persisted handoff row, and `GetRuntimeHandoff` then returns nil.

Design question to settle first: `persistNormalizedProjection` reconciles globally (every sibling loop deletes existing rows absent from the new snapshot), so "delete all when the new set is empty" may be the intended contract. But the same function never removes stale rows from OTHER scopes when `handoffRow != nil`, so the two directions are inconsistent, and treating an absent coordination section as authoritative emptiness destroys durable state on a degraded tick. Note `buildRuntimeCoordinationRows` has the same degradation shape.

Fix: decide whether the handoff projection is global-authoritative or per-scope. If per-scope, call `tx.DeleteRuntimeHandoffByScope(sessionName, workingDir)`. Either way, distinguish "no handoff" from "coordination source unavailable" so a degraded tick cannot wipe durable rows.
close_reason: Resolved the design question from the code itself: CoordinationSection carries an explicit Available flag (plus Reason) precisely because Agent Mail and friends can be unreachable, and the runtime_handoff projection is a freshness-bounded cache rebuilt from signals each tick (readers filter stale_after > now). So the projection IS global-authoritative, and an unscoped truncation is correct when the source reported successfully — the actual defect was truncating when it had NOT. persistNormalizedProjection now branches three ways: upsert when a handoff row exists; truncate only when coordinationSectionIsAuthoritative (section present and Available) reports no handoff; otherwise leave the projection alone and let stale_after expire it, so a transient outage no longer blanks every session's handoff surface. Corrected the DeleteRuntimeHandoff doc, which claimed to preserve pre-#135 singleton semantics after the table was re-keyed on (session_name, working_dir); it now states the authoritative-caller precondition and points at DeleteRuntimeHandoffByScope. Made the existing TestPersistNormalizedProjection_ReplacesRows fixture explicit (Available: true) since it relied on the zero value, and added TestPersistNormalizedProjectionKeepsHandoffWhenCoordinationUnavailable covering absent section, unavailable section, and the authoritative-empty case. Note the same degradation shape exists for coordination rows via buildRuntimeCoordinationRows and is not addressed here.

title: health: every idle shell/user pane is reported as a crashed process
description:
`internal/health/health.go:661-667`. `detectProcessStatusForAgent` returns `ProcessExited` whenever `shellPID > 0` and the pane's shell has no live child. An idle user pane (bash/zsh at a prompt) has zero children — verified: `/proc/<pane_pid>/task/*/children` is empty for a pane running `/bin/sh`.

`calculateStatus` checks `ProcessExited` (`:707`) before activity, so the pane becomes `StatusError` and `SessionHealth.OverallStatus` goes red. `CheckSession` iterates all panes with no user-pane filter, and neither `renderHealthTUI` nor `filterHealthResult` (`internal/cli/health.go:358`) excludes them — so `ntm health` and the dashboard show an ERROR for the user pane of every session. Corroborating evidence that this data is known-bad: `internal/robot/robot.go:5723` hand-filters `agent.AgentType == "user"` with the comment "ignore any user panes if present".

Fix: gate the PID verdict on an agent pane — when `agent.AgentType(agentType).Canonical()` is `user` or `unknown`, fall through to the idle-prompt check at `:671` instead of returning `ProcessExited`.
close_reason: detectProcessStatusForAgent now gates the PID verdict on paneRunsAgent(agentType). A user or plain-shell pane at a prompt legitimately has zero children, so 'shell has no live child' is not evidence of a crash there — but calculateStatus checks ProcessExited before activity, so the pane became StatusError and SessionHealth.OverallStatus went red, making ntm health and the dashboard show an ERROR for the user pane of every session. Non-agent panes now fall through to the idle-prompt check instead. An empty agentType keeps the historical PID-based behavior so detectProcessStatus is unchanged, and an agent pane with no live child is still ProcessExited. Covered by TestDetectProcessStatusForAgentIgnoresPIDForNonAgentPanes.

title: audit: the append-only log takes no file lock, so concurrent processes fork the hash chain
description:
`internal/audit/logger.go:317-318`. The comment says "exclusive locking intent" but `os.OpenFile(..., O_APPEND, ...)` locks nothing (contrast `internal/session/lock_unix.go`, which flocks). Chain state is read once at open (`loadLastHash` -> `:363-366`) and each process increments its own counter (`:483`).

Trigger: two processes both read `seq=N`/`lastHash=H` and both append `SequenceNum=N+1, PrevHash=H`. `VerifyIntegrity` then hard-fails at `:613` ("sequence number mismatch"). This happens on every concurrent invocation, because `startCommandAudit` (`internal/cli/root.go:496,627`) logs from every ntm process into the shared `global-<date>.jsonl` (`logger.go:202`). Net effect: tamper-evidence is permanently red, so real tampering is indistinguishable from normal use.

## Why the obvious fix does not work (investigated 2026-07-24)

Wrapping the append in `syscall.Flock` is NOT sufficient, because writes are buffered. `Log()` computes each entry's hash from the in-memory `al.lastHash` and writes into a `bufio.Writer`; the flush happens later, once `entriesWritten >= bufferSize`. So a lock held only around the append does not cover the read-modify-write of the chain state, and holding it from the first buffered entry until flush would serialize whole segments — with `BufferSize: 1000` (used by `logger_perf_test.go`) that starves other processes for a long time.

Buffering is also a tested, intentional contract: `TestAuditLogger_FlushesOnBufferSize` pins it and the perf test depends on it. So it cannot simply be removed.

## Options, needing a maintainer decision

1. **One writer per file (recommended).** A hash chain requires a single writer by construction. Give the shared `global-<date>.jsonl` a per-process discriminator (PID, or the random run ID) so each process owns its own chain. Buffering stays intact, no locking is needed, and `VerifyIntegrity` verifies each file's own chain soundly. Cost: more files, and `audit list`/`export`/aggregation must treat a day as a set of files (the query layer already reads multiple files, so this is mostly naming and docs).

2. **Lock-serialized segments.** Take an exclusive `flock` on first buffered entry, re-read the file tail to derive `PrevHash`/`SequenceNum`, and hold it through flush. Correct, but couples throughput to `bufferSize` and can block other processes for a long time.

3. **Make verification multi-writer aware.** Keep writes as they are and teach `VerifyIntegrity` to verify per-writer subchains, distinguishing an interleaved-append fork from genuine tampering. Preserves the file layout but weakens the guarantee and is the most subtle to get right.

Option 1 is the only one that makes the guarantee true rather than tolerated. It was not implemented unilaterally because it changes the on-disk audit layout, which is an operator-visible contract.
close_reason: Implemented the bead's recommended option 1 (one writer per file), which makes the tamper-evidence guarantee TRUE rather than tolerated. A hash chain requires a single writer by construction; the audit filename now carries a per-process discriminator (PID): SESSION-PID-YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl. Key design point that made this cheap: the discriminator goes BEFORE the date, so every existing reader keeps working untouched — query.go matches sessions with HasPrefix(session+'-') and extracts the date from the LAST 10 characters of the name (putting the PID last would have silently broken date filtering), and 'ntm audit verify SESSION' already globs SESSION-*.jsonl so it picks up all per-writer files automatically. Buffering is preserved (the tested BufferSize contract and the perf test are untouched) and no locking is introduced — the bead correctly notes a lock could not fix this anyway, since the chain's read-modify-write spans until flush. The misleading 'exclusive locking intent' comment on O_APPEND is replaced with the real rationale. Legacy SESSION-YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl files remain readable and verifiable. EVIDENCE (both directions, through the real CLI): with the fix, 6 concurrent ntm processes produced 6 files and 'ntm audit verify global' reported PASS for every chain; after temporarily restoring the old shared-file naming, 6 concurrent processes reproduced the exact reported failure — 'sequence number mismatch: expected 2, got 1' — then the fix was restored and re-verified. New test TestAuditLogger_ConcurrentWritersDoNotForkTheHashChain pins the chain soundness AND the filename invariants the query layer depends on (session prefix, date in the last 10 chars, discriminator present). audit+cli suites green. Note: this changes the on-disk audit layout (more files per day), which the bead flagged as operator-visible; reads, search, list, and verify were all confirmed to handle it.

title: audit: the day-file filter compares a local-date filename against a UTC-parsed date, dropping matching files
description:
`internal/audit/query.go:406-415`. Filenames are stamped with the local date (`logger.go:313-314`), entry timestamps are UTC (`logger.go:480`), and the filter does `time.Parse("2006-01-02", ...)` (UTC midnight) against `query.Since.Truncate(24*time.Hour)`.

Trigger on a UTC-4 host: entries written at local 2026-07-22 21:00 land in `...-2026-07-22.jsonl` with UTC timestamps of `2026-07-23T01:00Z`; a `--since 2026-07-23T00:00Z` query computes `fileDate = 2026-07-22T00:00Z`, sees `.Before(...)`, and skips the file. Those records silently never appear in `ntm audit show --since`, `audit search --days N`, or `robot causality`.

Fix: `time.ParseInLocation("2006-01-02", datePart, time.Local)` and widen the bound to a whole day — skip only when `fileDate.Add(24*time.Hour).Before(*query.Since)` or `fileDate.After(*query.Until)`.
close_reason: getLogFiles now parses the filename date with time.ParseInLocation in time.Local, matching how logger.go stamps it, and widens the bound to a whole day: a file named for day D holds entries anywhere in that local day, so it is excluded only when the entire day precedes Since or the day starts after Until. Previously the filename was parsed as UTC while entry timestamps are UTC-normalized from local wall time, so on a UTC-4 host entries written at local 21:00 on the 22nd carry UTC timestamps on the 23rd, and a --since of the 23rd computed a file date of the 22nd, saw Before, and skipped the file — those records silently never appeared in ntm audit show --since, audit search --days N, or robot causality. Covered by TestQueryDateFilterHonorsLocalFilenameDates.

title: pipeline: --keep-state=false is silently a no-op; the reset path is unreachable
description:
`internal/pipeline/state_resume.go:150`. `normalizeResumeOptions` ends with `opts.KeepState = !opts.Reset`, clobbering whatever the caller passed. The CLI (`internal/cli/pipeline.go:627-633`) sets `KeepState: keepState` and never sets `Reset`, so `--keep-state=false` always normalizes back to true and `resetResumeState` never runs. `Reset: true` appears only in `resume_test.go:225,254`.

`README.md:353` explicitly tells operators to use `--keep-state=false` "to deliberately re-run work"; instead the resume reuses all completed outputs.

Fix: have the CLI set `Reset: !keepState` when the user explicitly passed the flag (`cmd.Flags().Changed("keep-state")`), or honor an explicitly-false `KeepState` in `normalizeResumeOptions` instead of deriving it solely from `Reset`.
close_reason: The CLI now sets Reset when --keep-state was explicitly passed as false. normalizeResumeOptions derives KeepState from Reset (bd-uyjdn, so that callers who set only Mode still get keep-state), which clobbered the CLI's KeepState:false — so --keep-state=false always normalized back to true and resetResumeState never ran, despite README.md:353 documenting that flag as the way to deliberately re-run work. Gating on cmd.Flags().Changed("keep-state") preserves the bd-uyjdn default for every caller that does not pass the flag.

title: pipeline: a top-level foreach step's output_var is overwritten with the human summary line
description:
`internal/pipeline/executor.go:710-718`. `storeForeachOutputVars` (`foreach.go:149`) computes the declared shape (`[]string` for the default `aggregate` mode, `map[string]string` for `collect`) and writes `Variables[parent.OutputVar]`. `executeWorkflow` then unconditionally does `e.state.Variables[step.OutputVar] = result.Output`, and for a foreach `result.Output` is `"Foreach completed: 2/2 dispatched, 0 skipped, 0 failed"`.

Verified: `collected` ends up as that string (type `string`, not `[]string`), and a downstream `${vars.collected}` consumer received `saw=Foreach completed: 2/2 dispatched, 0 skipped, 0 failed`. `output_var_mode` is therefore dead for every top-level foreach, and for one nested in a foreach body via the identical overwrite in `storeForeachNestedResult` (`foreach.go:1148-1153`).

Fix: skip the `OutputVar` write in `executeWorkflow`/`storeForeachNestedResult` when the step is a foreach container (`step.Foreach != nil || step.ForeachPane != nil`), since `storeForeachOutputVars` already owns that key.
close_reason: The generic step-result path no longer overwrites a foreach container's output_var. storeForeachOutputVars already writes the shape declared by output_var_mode ([]string for aggregate, map[string]string for collect); executeWorkflow then unconditionally assigned result.Output, which for a foreach is the human summary 'Foreach completed: N/N dispatched, ...', so output_var_mode was dead for every top-level foreach and for one nested in a foreach body via the identical overwrite in storeForeachNestedResult. Both sites now skip the OutputVar write when the new stepOwnsForeachOutputVar reports a foreach container, while still recording steps.<id>.output for observability. Also moved the unsynchronized e.state.UpdatedAt write in executeWorkflow under stateMu, since snapshotState reads that field under RLock (the second item of bead .66). Covered by TestStepOwnsForeachOutputVar and TestForeachAggregateOutputVarKeepsDeclaredShape; pipeline suite green under -race.

title: serve: server-wide write mutex held across a 1.25s network probe, stalling every request
description:
`internal/serve/mail.go:376-393` takes `s.mu.Lock()` with `defer Unlock`, then calls `client.IsAvailable()`, which runs up to 3 probes bounded by `availabilityProbeBudget = 1250ms` (`internal/agentmail/client.go:42`). It returns early at `:389` when unavailable and only caches the client on the success path (`:393`).

`redactionMiddleware` takes `s.mu.RLock()` on every request (`redact.go:42-44`), as does `corsMiddlewareFunc` for any request with an Origin. Go's RWMutex is writer-preferring, so a pending `Lock()` stalls all subsequent readers. Because the client is only cached when available, the 30s availability cache never applies — each mail/reservations request builds a fresh client and re-probes. With Agent Mail down, serial requests to `/api/v1/mail/*` stall the entire HTTP server continuously. (`err` is also never non-nil, making roughly 20 "failed to create mail client" branches dead.)

Fix: build and probe the client outside the lock, then store the verdict — including "unavailable" — under it.
close_reason: getMailClient now builds and probes the client outside s.mu and caches the verdict — including the negative one — under it. IsAvailable makes up to three probes bounded by agentmail's 1250ms budget, while redactionMiddleware takes s.mu for reading on every request (as does the CORS middleware for any request with an Origin); Go's RWMutex is writer-preferring, so a pending write lock stalled every subsequent reader. Because only successful probes were cached, an unreachable Agent Mail server meant every mail request rebuilt a client and re-probed, stalling the whole HTTP server continuously. A new mu-guarded mailUnavailableUntil caches the unavailable verdict for 30s (matching the client's own availability cache, which never applied), is cleared when PATCH /config repoints projectDir, and the post-probe critical section re-checks both the cached client and the project directory so a concurrent winner or a repointed project is honored. Covered by TestGetMailClientDoesNotBlockReadersDuringProbe, which asserts readers keep acquiring the lock during a probe and that a second call uses the cached verdict; serve suite green under -race.

title: serve: REST-started pipelines are permanently unlistable, ungettable, and uncancellable
description:
`internal/serve/pipelines.go:107,266,307`. `GetAllPipelines()`/`GetPipelineExecution()` read only the in-process `pipelineRegistry`, whose sole writer is `registerPipeline` via `StartBackgroundPipeline` (`internal/pipeline/robot.go:224`) — never called from `internal/serve`, which builds its own `pipeline.NewExecutor(...)` inline (`:588,:719,:853`). The registry is always empty in `ntm serve`.

Trigger: `POST /api/v1/pipelines/run {"background":true}` returns `200 {"run_id":"run-X"}`; then `GET /api/v1/pipelines` reports `count:0`, `GET /api/v1/pipelines/run-X` returns 404, and `POST /api/v1/pipelines/run-X/cancel` returns 404 (so `pipeline.CancelPipeline` at `:325` is unreachable). Background runs also swap in `context.Background()` (`:606`) with no cancel handle stored anywhere, so they keep driving tmux to completion.

Fix: use `GetAllPipelineSnapshots()`/`GetPipelineSnapshot()` (they merge the registry with `.ntm/pipelines/*.json`) and start runs through `StartBackgroundPipeline` so cancel resolves.
close_reason: Confirmed and fixed on both halves. READ side: the three serve handlers now use GetAllPipelineSnapshots()/GetPipelineSnapshot() instead of the bare in-process registry, so list/get/cancel see both this process's live runs and the runs persisted under .ntm/pipelines — the registry was always empty in 'ntm serve' because it builds its own executor inline and never calls registerPipeline. WRITE side: background runs now publish themselves to the registry BEFORE the response returns, via the new pipeline.NewTrackedExecution(runID, workflowID, session, totalSteps, executor, cancel) + RegisterPipeline, and call UpdatePipelineFromState when the run finishes — so the run_id handed to the caller resolves on GET and POST /cancel, and CancelPipeline reaches a real cancel handle. StartBackgroundPipeline could not be reused directly because it owns its own progress channel while serve must forward progress to WebSocket subscribers; NewTrackedExecution is the minimal seam that gives an externally-driven run the same registry identity and cancel wiring. Also fixed the detached-context half the bead flagged: background runs used a bare context.Background() with no cancel stored anywhere, so they kept driving tmux to completion with nothing able to stop them; each run now gets a cancellable context whose cancel is both stored in the registry and deferred by the run goroutine. Applied to BOTH background paths (/pipelines/run and the inline /pipelines/exec). go vet caught a genuine context-leak on the synchronous branch during this work, now structured so each branch owns its cancel unconditionally (vet clean). New test TestNewTrackedExecution_IsVisibleAndCancellable pins visibility in snapshot+list and that CancelPipeline invokes the handle, cancels the context, and marks the run cancelled. pipeline+policy+serve suites green.

title: serve: idempotent replay on /api/v1/jobs bypasses the RBAC check
description:
`internal/serve/server.go:1051-1057`:

    r.Route("/jobs", func(r chi.Router) {
        r.Use(s.idempotencyMiddleware)
        r.With(s.RequirePermission(PermWriteJobs)).Post("/", s.handleCreateJob)

Chi applies a sub-router's `Use` middlewares in `updateRouteHandler` before routing, so they run before the inline `With` chain (`chi/v5@v5.2.5/mux.go:430,514`). `idempotencyMiddleware` (`:1397-1402`) serves the cached body and status and returns, so `RequirePermission` never executes. The cache key (`scopedIdempotencyKey`, `:1439`) is method+path+query+key with no principal, so a caller lacking `jobs:write` who reuses a key an authorized caller already used receives that caller's response with `X-Idempotent-Replay: true`.

Fix: move `idempotencyMiddleware` after `RequirePermission` in each route's chain, and include the authenticated principal in the cache key.
close_reason: Two fixes. idempotencyMiddleware moved off the /jobs sub-router into each mutating route's With chain, positioned after RequirePermission: chi applies a sub-router's Use middlewares before routing and therefore before an inline With chain, and a cached replay returns from the middleware without calling next, so RequirePermission never ran for a replayed request. It is also no longer attached to the read routes, where it did nothing. Second, scopedIdempotencyKey now includes the authenticated principal (role plus user ID, or 'anonymous' when no RBAC context is attached), so one caller's cached response can no longer be served to a different caller who reuses the same Idempotency-Key on the same method and path. Covered by TestIdempotencyReplayStillEnforcesPermission (authorized call caches, same principal replays from cache, a viewer reusing the key gets 403 and never sees the cached body) and TestScopedIdempotencyKeyIncludesPrincipal.

title: serve: data race on s.projectDir across roughly 60 unlocked reads
description:
`internal/serve/server.go:2507`. `handlePatchConfigV1` writes `s.projectDir` (and nils `s.mailClient`) under `s.mu.Lock()`, and `handleGetConfigV1:2471` correctly snapshots it under RLock — but it is read with no lock in roughly 60 places: `mail.go:475,505,547,588,625,707,755,806,1096,1138,1196,1263,1309,1356,1430,1487,1533,1576,1649,1717`; `beads.go:130,193,233,...,770`; `scanner.go:457,806,824`; `cass.go:720,862,872,997,1081,1243,1285,1334`; `pipelines.go:173,949`.

Trigger: concurrent `PATCH /api/v1/config {"project_dir":"/x"}` and `GET /api/v1/beads`. In default local mode every caller is `RoleAdmin`, which holds `PermSystemConfig`. A torn string (ptr+len are two words) means `br`/`ubs`/`cm` run with a garbage cwd.

Fix: add a `projectDirSnapshot()` accessor that takes `s.mu.RLock()`, and use it everywhere.

title: serve: POST /api/v1/pipelines/validate reads arbitrary paths with only pipelines:read
description:
`internal/serve/pipelines.go:422`. `pipeline.ParseFile` does `os.ReadFile(path)` before the extension check (`internal/pipeline/parser.go:237-243`), with no confinement to `s.projectDir`. The route is gated on `PermReadPipelines`, which `RoleViewer` holds (`rbac.go:101`).

Trigger: `{"workflow_file":"/root/.ssh/id_rsa"}` returns 400 whose `load_error` distinguishes "permission denied" from "no such file" (an existence oracle); for `.yaml`/`.toml` targets, `buildYAMLParseError`/`buildTOMLParseError` (`parser.go:58-97`) surface `field <key> not found in type pipeline.Workflow` / `LastKey`, leaking the file's key names. Nothing in the handler validates the path — contrast `pipeline.LoadState`, which does call `validateRunID`.

Fix: resolve with `filepath.Abs` and require an `s.projectDir` prefix (or an allowlist from `discoverPipelineTemplates()`); do not echo raw parse errors.
close_reason: Added Server.resolveWorkflowPath, which confines a caller-supplied workflow path to s.projectDir: relative paths are joined to the project root, absolute paths must lie within it, EvalSymlinks is applied to both root and target so a link inside the project cannot point outside, and an unconfigured project directory is refused outright. Wired into POST /api/v1/pipelines/validate and also into runPipelineWithResult, which had the same exposure (it only ran filepath.Abs before handing the path to LoadAndValidate). This matters because pipeline.ParseFile os.ReadFile's the path BEFORE checking the extension, and /validate is gated on PermReadPipelines which RoleViewer holds — so the least-privileged role could probe arbitrary paths, with the echoed load error distinguishing permission-denied from not-found and .yaml/.toml parse errors leaking a file's key names. Covered by TestResolveWorkflowPathConfinesToProjectDir (accepts inside and relative; rejects absolute-outside, ../ traversal, /root/.ssh/id_rsa, empty, an escaping symlink, and a server with no project dir). Adjusted TestRunPipelineWithResult_InvalidWorkflowDoesNotPanic, whose fixture lived outside the project and would otherwise fail on the path rather than on the schema.

title: state: timeline checkpointing rewrites the whole file from a 48h retention window, deleting older persisted history
description:
`internal/state/timeline_persist.go:428` and `:462`. Both the 5-minute checkpoint goroutine and `FinalizeSession` call `tracker.GetEventsForSession(id, time.Time{})`. A zero `since` does not mean "everything": `timeline.go:335-337` rewrites it to `now - RetentionDuration`, which is 48h for the global tracker (`timeline.go:785`; 24h by default at `:156`). `SaveTimeline` then fully replaces the file via `writeTimelineFileLocked` -> `os.Rename`.

Trigger: a swarm session alive past 48h. The hour-49 checkpoint overwrites the on-disk JSONL with only the trailing 48h, and `Prune()` has already evicted those events from memory, so durably-written hour-1 history is unrecoverable. `FinalizeSession` does the same on the final save, defeating post-session analysis — the stated purpose of the file.

Fix: add a tracker getter returning all retained events for a session (or pass an explicit epoch `since`), and merge with the existing on-disk events instead of a windowed full rewrite.
close_reason: Split the two write contracts. SaveTimeline keeps replace semantics (it backs user-facing export at internal/cli/timeline.go:587, where an exact write is correct). New CheckpointTimeline merges with what is already on disk and is what the 5-minute checkpoint goroutine and FinalizeSession now call, so a windowed view can no longer narrow the durable record. mergeTimelineEvents dedupes on (agent, timestamp, state, previous_state) since AgentEvent has no unique ID, and returns timestamp order, so repeat checkpoints converge instead of appending. Also added TimelineTracker.GetAllEventsForSession, because GetEventsForSession treats a zero since as the retention window rather than everything. Covered by TestCheckpointTimelinePreservesHistoryOutsideRetentionWindow and TestGetAllEventsForSessionIgnoresRetentionWindow; existing TestSaveTimelineOverwrite still passes, confirming export semantics are unchanged.

title: serve: PUT /api/v1/policy/automation can replace the effective safety policy with built-in defaults
description:
`internal/serve/safety.go:851-864,899-900`. The handler hardcodes `$HOME/.ntm/policy.yaml` and, when that file is absent, starts from `policy.DefaultPolicy()` — but every reader in the file uses `policy.LoadOrDefault()` (`:91,:211,:444,:797,:1278`), which prefers `$HOME/.ntm/policy.yaml` else the CWD-relative `.ntm/policy.yaml` (`internal/policy/policy.go:97-118`). `ntm setup` creates the project-local file (`internal/cli/setup.go:138-145`), so the vulnerable state is the default.

Trigger: `PUT /policy/automation {"auto_push":true}` writes a fresh home policy containing only defaults and returns `200 {"modified":true}`. `LoadOrDefault` now prefers it, so the project's `blocked`/`approval_required` rules stop being enforced — including by the installed `git`/`rm` wrappers and the Claude `PreToolUse` hook.

Fix: resolve the target path with the same `LoadOrDefault` precedence and read-modify-write that file.
close_reason: Confirmed and fixed. New policy.ResolveEffectivePath() encodes the SAME precedence LoadOrDefault uses (home $HOME/.ntm/policy.yaml if present, else CWD-relative .ntm/policy.yaml, else the home path as the creation target) and LoadOrDefault was refactored to call it, so reader and writer can no longer drift apart. handlePolicyAutomationUpdateV1 now read-modify-writes the file that is actually ENFORCED instead of hardcoding the home path: previously, in the default post-'ntm setup' state (project-local policy exists, home policy does not), toggling a single automation flag wrote a fresh home policy containing nothing but defaults, and because LoadOrDefault prefers the home file that new file immediately took precedence — silently disabling the project's blocked/approval_required rules for the installed git/rm wrappers and the Claude PreToolUse hook. Two regression tests: TestResolveEffectivePath_PrefersProjectPolicyWhenNoHomePolicy walks all three states (nothing exists -> creation target is home and exists=false; project-only -> resolves to the project file; home present -> home wins, matching LoadOrDefault), and TestResolveEffectivePath_AgreesWithLoadOrDefault asserts the resolver and the enforcement reader never disagree. policy+serve suites green. Separately filed bd-7hcy1 for two PRE-EXISTING UBS taint criticals in the same file (request-derived id reaching an os.WriteFile(0755) sink via the approvals/wrapper install path) — verified not introduced by this change, whose diff is confined to the policy handler.

title: serve: the audit subsystem is dead code, so no mutating REST/WS action is ever logged
description:
`internal/serve/audit.go:129,590`. `NewAuditStore` and `AuditMiddleware` have no callers outside tests, so `AuditMiddleware` is never in the chain and no audit record is ever written — even though handlers dutifully call `SetAuditResource`/`SetAuditSession`/`SetAuditAction` (e.g. `server.go:5926-5929`) and `handleAttentionItemStateV1` records DB-level audit rows.

Fix: construct the store in `internal/cli/serve.go` and add `r.Use(s.AuditMiddleware(store))` to `buildRouter`.

title: pipeline: a branch step's deferred variable restore destroys concurrent sibling steps' outputs
description:
`internal/pipeline/control_flow.go:197-206`. `executeBranch` snapshots the entire `state.Variables` map, then on return calls `restoreAllVariables(e.state, varSnapshot)`, which replaces the whole map (`scope.go:92`). A `branch` step is reachable inside a foreach body (`executeForeachNestedStepOnce` -> `executeStepOnce` -> `executeBranch`), and `parallel: true` foreach runs iterations concurrently. Iteration A's restore therefore discards every `output_var` and `steps.<id>.output` key that iterations B..N wrote while A's branch body ran.

Verified by the auditor with an 8-item parallel foreach whose body is `produce` (with `output_var`) plus `route` (a branch): only 2 of 8 `output_var` values and 7 of 16 `steps.*` keys survived. Silent — a downstream `${vars.produced_c}` then fails or resolves stale.

Fix: scope branch-locally instead of whole-map. Capture and restore only the keys the branch body actually shadows (`CaptureVariableScope`/`Restore`, as `pushLoopVars` already does) rather than snapshot-and-replace the map.
close_reason: executeBranch no longer snapshot-and-replaces state.Variables. The deferred restore is now restoreBranchVariables, which reverts keys that existed in the snapshot and deletes added keys only when the branch owns them: a steps.* key namespaced under one of the concrete body step IDs recorded during the loop, or an output_var declared by the body (branchBodyOutputVars). Everything else added while the body ran belongs to a concurrent sibling iteration, or is deliberate global signaling like runtime.*, and is left untouched — leaking a variable is recoverable, destroying a sibling's output is not. Ownership is keyed on recorded body step IDs rather than a loose branch-ID prefix so an unrelated sibling step with a similar name is not swept away. bd-afwly's runtime-key stash is retained to cover a runtime key the body modified rather than added. Covered by TestRestoreBranchVariablesLeavesConcurrentSiblingWrites and TestBranchOwnsVariableRequiresRecordedBodyStepID; existing TestBranchVariableSnapshotRestoresMutations still passes, and the pipeline suite is green under -race.

title: serve: enabling auth makes the entire write API return 403
description:
`internal/serve/server.go:1592,1596` with `internal/serve/rbac.go:222-225`. `authenticateRequest` returns nil claims for `api_key` and `mtls` (only `local` returns `{"role": admin}`). `authMiddlewareFunc` only injects a context value when claims are non-nil, so `extractAuthClaims` yields `{}`, and `extractRoleFromClaims` — which short-circuits to admin only for local mode — falls through to `RoleViewer`. `RoleViewer` holds no `PermWrite*`.

Trigger: `ntm serve --auth-mode api_key --api-key K`, then `POST /api/v1/sessions` with a valid key -> `403 "role 'viewer' lacks permission 'sessions:write'"`. Identical for mtls. No test covers auth-mode plus a mutating route, so the only supported way to run the server authenticated is completely broken for writes.

Fix: have `authenticateAPIKey`/`authenticateMTLS` return a claims map carrying the configured role.
close_reason: authenticateRequest now returns role-bearing claims on every successful path. api_key and mtls previously returned nil claims, so RBAC saw an empty claim set and extractRoleFromClaims — which only short-circuits to admin for local mode — fell through to RoleViewer, which holds no PermWrite*, making every mutating endpoint 403 the moment authentication was enabled. Both shared-credential modes now resolve through AuthConfig.sharedCredentialRole(), defaulting to RoleAdmin because a correct shared key or a client cert admitted by the configured CA is the operator's own credential; the new optional AuthConfig.Role lets an operator downgrade it. mTLS claims carry the client cert CN as sub for RBAC context and audit. Covered by TestAuthenticateRequestGrantsRoleForSharedCredentials (including that a bad key still fails closed and a configured lower role is honored) and TestAuthenticatedAPIKeyReachesWriteGatedRoute, which drives a real authenticated request through authMiddleware + rbacMiddleware + RequirePermission — the combination no test exercised.

title: serve: WebSocket accepts any Origin in default local mode (CSWSH data exfiltration)
description:
`internal/serve/server.go:4102-4105`: `if s.auth.Mode == AuthModeLocal || s.auth.Mode == "" { return true }`. `wsUpgrader.CheckOrigin` is hardcoded true (`:811`) and delegates here. WebSocket handshakes are exempt from CORS, and the REST CSRF defence is `corsMiddlewareFunc`'s 403-on-bad-Origin (`:1336`), which never runs for the upgrade.

Trigger: any page the operator visits can open `new WebSocket("ws://127.0.0.1:7337/api/v1/ws")` and send `{"type":"subscribe","data":{"topics":["attention","*"],"since_cursor":0}}`. `isValidTopic` allows `*`, `canSubscribe` always returns true (`:4468-4477`), and `handleAttentionSubscribe` replays the entire attention journal (agent summaries and details) plus all subsequent bus, mail, and pane-output events.

Fix: validate Origin against `corsAllowedOrigins` in every mode; bypass only when the header is absent (non-browser clients).
close_reason: checkWSOrigin no longer bypasses the allowlist in local mode, which is the default. WebSocket upgrades are exempt from CORS and the REST CSRF defence is the CORS middleware's 403-on-bad-Origin, which never runs for an upgrade, so any page the operator visited could open ws://127.0.0.1:7337 and subscribe to the whole attention journal plus pane output and mail. An absent Origin header is still allowed, since only browsers send it and only browsers are the CSWSH vector. Matching now delegates to originAllowed, the same predicate CORS uses: the old code compared url.Host (port-sensitive) while CORS compares Hostname, so unifying was required or the default localhost allowlist (which carries no ports) would have rejected a browser at http://localhost:7337. An empty allowlist falls back to defaultLocalOrigins, making the documented 'empty means default localhost only' true at the enforcement point. Rewrote TestCheckWSOrigin_LocalMode/_EmptyMode, which asserted https://evil.com was accepted — they encoded the vulnerability — and added TestCheckWSOrigin_LocalModeAllowsLocalhostWithPort so the operator surfaces stay covered.

title: robot: a bad [models] context_limits entry makes --robot-route and --robot-context emit no JSON at all
description:
`internal/robot/routing.go:772-785` with `internal/models/registry.go:131`. `models.ApplyOverrides` writes any int from user TOML into `ContextLimits` with zero validation, so `"my-model" = 0` makes `usagePct := float64(withOverhead) / float64(contextLimit) * 100` (`robot.go:10157`) +Inf, or NaN when the pane is empty and `withOverhead == 0`. Neither clamp catches it (`NaN < 0` and `NaN > 100` are both false; `math.Round(NaN*100)/100` is NaN), so the value reaches `Score` and `json.Encode` fails with `UnsupportedValueError`. `printLegacyRobotOutput` (`types.go:790-792`) then returns 1 having written nothing — an empty stdout with a nonzero exit, violating the "always a success:false envelope" contract. `checkExclusion` also silently stops excluding (`NaN > 85` is false).

Fix: guard with `math.IsNaN`/`math.IsInf` in `calculateScoreComponents` (treat as 100% usage) and reject non-positive `context_limits` overrides at config load.
close_reason: Fixed at all three layers. models.ApplyOverrides now rejects non-positive context_limits overrides with a warning and keeps the built-in value, so the division by zero cannot be configured. GetContext treats a non-positive limit as 100% consumed instead of dividing, which is the safe direction for routing and rotation. calculateFinalScore explicitly tests math.IsNaN/IsInf before the clamps, because every comparison against NaN is false so neither clamp caught it — NaN previously reached json.Encode, which returns UnsupportedValueError, and printLegacyRobotOutput then exited 1 having written nothing, violating the always-emit-an-envelope contract. Covered by TestApplyOverridesRejectsNonPositiveLimits and TestCalculateFinalScoreRejectsNonFiniteValues, the latter asserting the result is JSON-encodable.

title: robot: --robot-route --strategy=round-robin recommends a pane it reports as excluded, and never rotates
description:
`internal/robot/route.go:230` with `routing.go:1014-1026`. `GetRoute` constructs a fresh `NewRouter()` per invocation (`:222`), so `RoundRobinStrategy.lastIndex` is always 0 and `startIdx := (s.lastIndex + 1) % len(agents)` is always 1. `Select` also explicitly ignores exclusion ("Round-robin ignores exclusion - use all agents"), and `GetRoute` passes the combined slice.

Trigger: a 3-agent session with pane 1 in ERROR. The response lists pane 1 in `excluded[]` AND as `recommendation.pane_index` with `score: 0`, reason "primary strategy succeeded", and `_agent_hints.send_command` tells the caller to send work into the dead pane. Pane 0 is never selected across any number of CLI calls.

Fix: in `GetRoute`, reject a `result.Selected` whose `Excluded` is true and fall through to the fallback chain (the strategy's internal semantics are pinned by `routing_test.go:619-661`), or map the stateless CLI path to `RoundRobinAvailableStrategy`.
close_reason: Three fixes, all live-verified on a 3-agent session with one deliberately killed agent. (1) Router.Route now rejects any Selected agent whose Excluded is true — for the primary strategy AND every fallback — so routing can never recommend a pane it simultaneously reports as excluded; the plain round-robin strategy keeps its documented ignore-exclusion internals (pinned by routing_test.go:619-661) but Route no longer surfaces that as a recommendation. All-excluded now yields no selection instead of a poisoned one. (2) Rotation across stateless CLI invocations: NewRouter() per process froze lastIndex at 0, so round-robin always returned index 1. New rotationAnchorIndex() anchors on ctx.LastAgent (survives process boundaries) and otherwise on the most recently active agent, so successive invocations advance; in-process callers with zero LastActivity keep the old cursor semantics (existing tests unchanged). Both round-robin strategies use it. (3) Root cause the audit did not name: the scorer had no notion of a dead agent CLI, so a pane whose agent exited to a bare shell was scored routable and recommended — a send the delivery layer then refuses with PANE_AGENT_DEAD. New excludeRouteAgent() adds that pane-level exclusion at both GetRoute sites. Also added the missing --last-agent CLI flag: RouteOptions.LastAgent existed but was unreachable from robot mode, so sticky routing and rotation anchoring were dead code from the CLI. Live evidence: before, a killed pane was recommended with excluded[] empty; after, excluded=[(2,'agent CLI exited to a bare shell')] and pane 1 recommended; --strategy=round-robin-available --last-agent rotates %55->%57->%55 skipping the dead pane. 4 new regression tests; robot+cli suites green; capabilities entry + golden updated.

title: robot: the dashboard attention panel replays the oldest events, so new action-required events are invisible
description:
`internal/robot/sections.go:741` calls `feed.Replay(0, replayLimit)` with `replayLimit = min(stats.Count, 60)`, and `Replay` walks `j.entries` from the head and breaks at `limit` (`attention_feed.go:239-248`) — i.e. the oldest 60. Once the journal holds more than 60 retained events, `GetDashboardAttentionSection` — consumed live by the TUI at `internal/tui/dashboard/commands.go:357` — shows events 1..60 forever regardless of what arrives. The newest-first sort happens after this window (`commands.go:387`), so it cannot recover them.

Fix: replay the tail — `since := stats.NewestCursor - int64(maxEvents); if since < 0 { since = 0 }`.
close_reason: GetDashboardAttentionSection now replays the tail rather than the head. Replay walks the journal from the oldest entry and breaks at the limit, so Replay(0, 60) returned events 1..60 — meaning the TUI attention panel showed the same oldest 60 forever once the journal exceeded that, and no newer action-required event could ever surface (the newest-first sort in commands.go happens after this window, so it cannot recover them). The window now starts near NewestCursor minus the limit, clamped to at least OldestCursor-1 so the request cannot be rejected as an expired cursor, and stays at 0 while the journal is smaller than the window.

title: robot: --wait-until=stalled can never fire at the default poll interval
description:
`internal/robot/activity.go:415-417`. When no sample has `CharsAdded > 0`, `lastOutputAgeLocked` returns `time.Since(vt.Samples[0].Timestamp)`, and `Samples` holds at most `DefaultMaxSamples` (10). `--robot-wait` polls every 2s (`root.go:4286`) reusing one `ActivityMonitor` (`wait.go:165/240`), so the oldest retained sample is at most 9x2s = 18s — always under `DefaultStallThreshold` (30s). `classifyState`'s `velocity == 0 && lastOutputAge > sc.stallThreshold` (`:1075`) is therefore unreachable, so `--robot-wait=S --wait-until=stalled` times out with exit 1 for a pane silent for hours, and `StateStalled` never reaches health or routing.

Fix: track `lastOutputAt time.Time` on `VelocityTracker`, set it in `Update*` whenever `charsAdded > 0`, and return `time.Since(vt.lastOutputAt)`.

title: robot: a failed restart prompt still returns success:true and exit 0
description:
`internal/robot/restart_pane.go:472`. On a non-cancellation send failure, `sendRestartPromptsContext` records `RestartPromptFailed` and appends to `promptErrors` (`:1679-1681`) but never calls `appendRestartFailureOnce`, so `output.Failed` stays empty and the honest-status block at `:487-495` (`if len(output.Failed) > 0`) never fires.

Trigger: `--robot-restart-pane=S --panes=1 --restart-prompt="..."` with a `send-keys` failure emits `success:true, error_code:""`, exit 0, with the failure visible only in `prompt_error`. `--robot-smart-restart` maps the identical event to `success:false` plus `PROMPT_SEND_FAILED` (`smart_restart.go:570-577`), so the two surfaces disagree.

Fix: in the `len(promptErrors) > 0` branch set `Success=false` and `ErrorCode = ErrCodePromptSendFailed`.

title: robot: the documented no-session modes of --robot-health/--robot-files/--robot-metrics are unreachable
description:
`internal/cli/root.go:3882/4109/4124` with `:1850/2294/2442`. All three are plain `StringVar`s with no `NoOptDefVal` (only `robot-dismiss-alert` sets one, `:4137`), yet the flag help and the capability catalog (`capabilities.go:714-722`) mark `session` optional. Dispatch is gated on `robotHealth != ""`.

Result: `ntm --robot-health` returns `INTERNAL_ERROR "flag needs an argument"` (the wrong code — `classifyRobotExecuteError`, `:427-437`, lacks that fragment), and `ntm --robot-health=` prints the colored human banner on stdout with exit 0. `robot.GetHealth()` (project health) has no CLI caller at all; only `internal/serve/server.go:2792` reaches it.

Fix: set `NoOptDefVal = "__present__"` on the three flags, gate on `cmd.Flags().Changed(...)`, and add "flag needs an argument" to the `INVALID_FLAG` fragments.

title: robot: --robot-verbosity=terse nondeterministically destroys one of two timestamp fields
description:
`internal/robot/verbosity.go:139-142` with `internal/robot/types.go:511`. `TerseKeyMap` maps `"timestamp"` to `"ts"`, but `SnapshotOutput.Timestamp` is already `json:"ts"` (`robot.go:4453`; same in `SnapshotDeltaOutput`, `:7235`). `shortenKeys` writes both into `out["ts"]`, so whichever the randomized map iteration reaches last wins.

Reproduced by the auditor: over 200 runs of the same payload the surviving value was the envelope timestamp 26 times and the snapshot timestamp 174 times. `ntm --robot-snapshot --robot-verbosity=terse` therefore loses a field at random.

Fix: detect collisions in `shortenKeys` (skip the mapping when the short key already exists), or remap `SnapshotOutput.Timestamp` / drop `"timestamp"` from `TerseKeyMap`.

title: robot: --robot-terse always reports C:0% because ContextPct is never assigned
description:
`internal/robot/robot.go:9478` / `:9522`. `TerseState.ContextPct` ("Average context usage %") is read by `String()` and by `ParseTerse` (`:9742`) but never assigned in production — `buildTerseOutputFromSnapshot` (`:9591-9635`) sets every other field and skips it. Every terse line is `...|C:0%|...` with `"context_pct":0`, and `getUsageLevel(0)` returns "Low", so an orchestrator using terse output to decide on context rotation always concludes there is full headroom.

Fix: compute it from `snapshot.Sessions[].Agents[].ContextPercent` (as `GetContext` does at `robot.go:10189`) and assign it per session.

title: robot: --errors-since is parsed, plumbed, and silently ignored
description:
`internal/robot/errors.go:23` with `:144`. `root.go:3756` registers `--errors-since` and `:1552` sets `ErrorsOptions.Since`, but `GetErrors` never reads `opts.Since`. `ntm --robot-errors=s --errors-since=5m` returns the full 1000-line scan with `success:true` and no warning, so an agent believes it is looking only at recent failures.

Fix: filter by `Since` in `GetErrors`. There is no per-line timestamp available, so either reject the flag with `INVALID_FLAG` or scope the capture window — silently accepting it is the bug.

title: robot: --robot-monitor --include-caut disables the caut cache and re-queries every provider each tick
description:
`internal/cli/root.go:1690`. The `MonitorConfig` literal omits `CautInterval`, so it is 0 (versus `2 * time.Minute` in `DefaultMonitorConfig`, `warnings.go:69`). `caut.NewCachedClient(client, 0)` makes `time.Since(cached.fetchedAt) < 0` always false (`internal/caut/client.go:206`), so the cache never hits; and `time.Since(m.lastCaut) > 0` (`monitor.go:121`) is always true, so `refreshCautData` spawns one `caut` subprocess per supported provider on every poll (default 30s) instead of every 2 minutes.

Fix: set `CautInterval: robot.DefaultMonitorConfig().CautInterval` in the literal, or clamp non-positive values to the default inside `NewMonitor`.

title: robot: the diagnose failure envelope claims overall_health "healthy"
description:
`internal/robot/diagnose.go:144`. `OverallHealth: "healthy"` is set at construction and never cleared on the `!exists` path (`:173-179`) or the tmux-error paths, so `ntm --robot-diagnose=nope` returns `{"success":false,"error_code":"SESSION_NOT_FOUND",...,"overall_health":"healthy"}`. `GetDiagnoseBrief` leaves it empty in the same case, so the two surfaces disagree and a consumer keying on `overall_health` reads a nonexistent session as healthy.

Fix: initialize `OverallHealth: ""` and set it only after the pane loop (it is already assigned at `:331`).

title: robot: --robot-diagnose --diagnose-brief counts degraded panes as healthy, contradicting itself
description:
`internal/robot/diagnose.go:711-716`. Brief mode maps `HealthDegraded` (non-rate-limited) to `summary.Healthy++`, while `getDiagnoseWithDependencies:251` maps the identical state to `summary.Degraded++`. Since `determineOverallHealth` only escalates on `Degraded > 0`, a stalled agent yields `overall_health:"degraded"` from `--robot-diagnose` but `overall_health:"healthy", has_issues:false` from `--robot-diagnose --diagnose-brief`. `summary.Degraded` is dead in brief mode.

Fix: `summary.Degraded++` in that branch, and include `summary.Degraded > 0` in `HasIssues` (`:735`).

title: robot: --robot-assign always reports an empty blocked_by for every blocked bead
description:
`internal/robot/assign.go:314` hardcodes `[]string{}`. `bv.GetBlockedListContext` (`internal/bv/bv.go:2924-2954`) parses only `id` and `title`, so the field can never be populated from that source — yet `BlockedBy` is the entire point of `BlockedBead` (`:55-59`). An agent therefore cannot tell what to unblock. The data exists: `bv.TriageRecommendation.BlockedBy` is read in this very file (`:479`) and `bv.BeadAssignmentDetails.BlockedBy` exists (`bv.go:2241`).

Fix: source blocked beads from the triage rows that carry `BlockedBy`, or fill each entry via `bv.GetBeadAssignmentDetailsContext`.

title: robot: PT attention events emit a pane title as --panes=, so the suggested next_action always fails
description:
`internal/robot/attention_feed.go:1894/1917/1968/1991`. `pt.ClassificationStateChange.Pane` comes from `rano.PaneIdentity.String()` (`internal/integrations/rano/pidmap.go:35-40`), i.e. `"myproject__cc_1"` or `"session:2"`. `attentionTailOrStatusActions` (`:3816`) formats `--robot-tail=myproject --panes=myproject__cc_1 --lines=50`, which `ParsePaneSelectorsArg` -> `tmux.ParsePaneSelector` rejects (only `N`, `W.P`, `%N`). Separately `attentionPaneIndex("myproject__cc_1")` returns 0 (`:3121-3133`) and `Pane` is `omitempty`, so the stuck/zombie events carry no pane at all. Live path: `internal/cli/serve.go:116/122`.

Fix: resolve the title to a pane index or `%ID` before building the event; otherwise fall back to `attentionStatusNextAction`.

title: robot: the user pane consumes one --spawn-names custom name (off-by-one)
description:
`internal/robot/spawn.go:869`. `nameMap.AssignNew("user", userPaneRef)` runs before any agent, and `generateNameLocked` (`agent_names.go:74-79`) pops `customNames[customOffset]` for any type including `"user"`.

Trigger (the flag's own example, `root.go:3939`, "Custom agent names"): `--robot-spawn=p --spawn-cc=3 --spawn-names=alice,bob,charlie` yields `user=alice, cc_1=bob, cc_2=charlie, cc_3=claude-alpha`. The dry-run preview does the same (`:648`), and adding `--spawn-no-user` shifts the mapping back, so the name-to-agent binding depends on an unrelated flag.

Fix: only draw from `m.customNames` when `agentType != "user"`.

title: robot: per-pane tmux capture errors are discarded, so --robot-status reports healthy defaults with no degraded marker
description:
`internal/robot/robot.go:7574`. `content, err := capture(ctx, job.paneID); if err != nil { content = "" }` throws the error away, and `captureNormalizedTmuxPanes` only stores non-empty content, so a failed capture is indistinguishable from "no output". `enrichAgentStatus` (`status_enrich.go:83`) then skips the whole output-analysis block, emitting `rate_limit_detected:false`, `context_percent:0`, `seconds_since_output:0`. `--robot-status`'s `sources` section comes from persisted rows and adapter signals, which know nothing about these failures, so nothing is marked degraded — unlike `--robot-tail`, which does surface `capture_provenance:"unavailable"` (`robot.go:4050-4064`).

Fix: propagate the per-pane error into the result and mark the `tmux` source degraded, mirroring the `--robot-tail` contract.

title: robot: non-atomic Load-then-Store on the attention cursor can regress it and re-issue cursors
description:
`internal/robot/attention_feed.go:4051-4053`. `if latestCursor > f.cursor.Current() { f.cursor.counter.Store(latestCursor) }` runs in `storeBackedStats`, called from `Stats()` without `appendMu` (`:1088-1096`), while `Append` (`:542`) concurrently stores its own value.

Interleaving: `Stats` reads 100 and decides to store 105; `Append` stores 110; `Stats` then stores 105 — the counter moves backwards and the next `Next()` re-issues 106-110. `--robot-attention`, `--robot-digest`, and `--robot-events` all call `Stats()` per request, so this races the serve-side event stream.

Fix: use a compare-and-swap loop instead of Load-then-Store.

title: robot: --robot-digest sizes its replay from a stale count but reports the live newest cursor, skipping events
description:
`internal/robot/attention_feed.go:1209-1219`. `limit := f.Stats().Count` and `f.Replay(sinceCursor, limit)` are two round trips. With `sinceCursor == 0` the count equals the events-after-cursor, so any event appended in between clips the tail via the store `LIMIT`; `Replay` still returns the live newest, which `BuildAttentionDigest` writes verbatim into `digest.CursorEnd` (`:1240-1241`). `--robot-digest` documents `cursor_end` as the next `--since-cursor` (`events.go:706`), so the operator advances past events the digest never processed.

Fix: when `len(events) == limit`, pass `events[len(events)-1].Cursor` as `cursorEnd`.

title: robot: --robot-mail-check caps unread/urgent/total_messages and pages_remaining at one page
description:
`internal/robot/mail_check.go:388-405` with `:444-452`. `fetchLimit` is `offset + limit (+1)` (`:320-327`), and every count is computed from `filtered`, which IS that fetched window.

Trigger: 500 project messages with defaults (`limit=20, offset=0`) reports `total_messages: 21`, `unread` at most 21, and `remaining := 21 - 20 = 1` giving `pages_remaining: 1`. An agent trusting `unread` under-reports its backlog by an order of magnitude; one paginating on `pages_remaining` stops after page 2 with 24 pages left.

Fix: compute the counts from a separate unbounded fetch (or rename them and add an explicit `counts_bounded_by_window` marker), and derive `pages_remaining` from the true total.

title: robot: --robot-tokens breakdown never reconciles with total_tokens and counts broadcast prompts N times
description:
`internal/robot/tokens.go:349-350` with `:359-361`. `tokensPerTarget := tokens / len(targetTypes)` truncates while `output.TotalTokens += tokens` keeps the full value, so a 10-token prompt fanned to 3 agent types contributes 9 to `agent_stats` but 10 to `total_tokens` — the `group_by=agent` percentages sum to under 100% and disagree with `time_stats` (which uses undivided tokens). Separately `agentPrompts[agent]++` / `modelPrompts[model]++` run inside the per-target loop, so `--group-by=model` reports `prompts: 3` where `total_prompts: 1`, breaking any tokens-per-prompt derivation.

Fix: distribute the remainder (`tokens/N`, plus 1 for the first `tokens%N` targets) and increment prompt counters once per event.

title: robot: --robot-markdown asserts "No active alerts" while the snapshot carries failure alerts
description:
`internal/robot/markdown.go:489-497` / `:531-552`. `alertSummaryCounts` reads only `AlertSummary` and `AlertsDetailed`; `snapshot.Alerts []string` is never read anywhere in `markdown.go`. `GetSnapshot` appends real failures to that legacy slice outside the detailed-alert block (`robot.go:4723` "failed to get panes for %s", `robot.go:4850` "failed to list active incidents") and only sets `AlertSummary` when `len(activeAlerts) > 0` (`:4838-4844`).

So a tmux enumeration failure yields `Alerts:["failed to get panes for foo: ..."]`, `AlertsDetailed:[]`, `AlertSummary:nil`, hence `totalActive == 0` and an all-clear that drops the error text entirely.

Fix: include `len(snapshot.Alerts)` in `totalActive` and render those strings when `AlertsDetailed` is empty.

title: robot: --robot-bulk-assign over-counts summary.total_panes in --allocation mode
description:
`internal/robot/bulk_assign.go:1676`: `TotalPanes: len(output.Assignments) + len(output.UnassignedPanes)`. An unresolvable selector appends an assignment row (`:1006`) without adding its key to `allocated`, so every real pane still lands in `UnassignedPanes` (`:1073-1078`); aliasing selectors that name one physical pane with different beads append two rows (`:1017-1035`).

Trigger: `--robot-bulk-assign=s --allocation '{"9":"bd-1"}'` against a 3-pane session reports `"total_panes": 4`.

Fix: carry the filtered pane count (`len(paneList)`) in `bulkAssignPlan` and use it for `TotalPanes`.

title: robot: the Work markdown heading renders two different meanings in the same field
description:
`internal/robot/markdown.go:415-416` renders `### Work (R:3 I:2 B:1 = 486)` because `summary.Total` is bv's `TotalIssues` (closed included, `bv.go:2740`), while the fallback renderer puts `Ready+InProgress+Blocked` in the identical slot (`:480-481`). The same rendered field therefore means two different things depending on whether `snapshot.Work` is populated.

Fix: pick one definition (almost certainly the not-closed sum) and use it in both renderers, or label them differently.

title: robot: two documented [routing] knobs are inert and the whole config block is unused
description:
`internal/robot/routing.go:739` and `:732`. `checkExclusion` excludes `StateError` unconditionally and never reads `s.config.ExcludeIfErrorState`, so `exclude_if_error = false` has no effect, and the following `HealthUnhealthy` branch duplicates the same condition. `calculateAffinity` scales by `AgentMail.ReservationBonus` (30) instead of `AffinityBonus` (20), making `affinity_bonus` inert and the "0-20" doc comment on `ScoreBreakdown.AffinityBonus` wrong.

Related and broader: `NewAgentScorerFromConfig` (`:383`) has no non-test callers — every production site passes `DefaultRoutingConfig()` — so the entire `[routing]` config block is currently inert.

Fix: honor both fields, drop the duplicated branch, and wire `NewAgentScorerFromConfig` into the production paths (or remove the config surface).

title: robot: --robot-route can never report a rate-limited exclusion
description:
`internal/robot/route.go:173` and `:389`. Both route builders hardcode `RateLimited: false` while discarding `activity.RateLimited`, which the classifier already computed from pattern evidence (`activity.go:787,800`). So the default `ExcludeIfRateLimited: true` is unreachable on this surface. The sibling `ScoreAgents` (`routing.go:568-571`) instead spends a second `tmux.CapturePaneOutput` per pane to recompute the same bit.

Fix: carry `activity.RateLimited` into both builders and drop the redundant re-capture in `ScoreAgents`.

title: robot: assign surfaces silently drop beads and suggest a claim command that poisons the bead
description:
Two related defects.

`internal/robot/assign.go:36`/`:76`: `unassignable_beads` is never written and `Summary.UnassignableBeads` is never set, while beads ARE silently dropped by the operator gate (`:479-497`) and the idle-agent shortage loop (`:584`). With `omitempty` on a nil slice the key vanishes entirely, so the caller cannot tell that anything was dropped.

`internal/robot/assign.go:734`: the suggested command is `br update <bead> --assignee=%12` — a tmux pane ID. Every real claim uses `assignment.StableClaimActor` values, so following the hint makes `currentAssignee != actor` (`internal/bv/bv.go:1772`) and permanently blocks `--robot-bulk-assign` from claiming that bead.

Fix: populate `unassignable_beads` with a reason per dropped bead, and emit the stable claim actor in the suggested command.

title: assign: allocation plan logs can never show the recommend decision
description:
`internal/assign/allocation.go:342`. `candidate.Decision = AllocationDecisionRecommend` writes to a loop-local copy after the log row was already appended at `:314`, so `plan.Logs[].decision` can never be `recommend` and contradicts `recommendations[]` for the same pair.

Fix: set the decision before appending the log row, or update the appended row in place.

title: robot: --robot-attention cannot suppress background items
description:
`internal/robot/events.go:1112-1113`: `if opts.BackgroundLimit <= 0 { opts.BackgroundLimit = 0 }` is a no-op that `normalizeAttentionDigestOptions` (`attention_feed.go:1301`) then rewrites 0 to 3. So `--robot-attention` cannot suppress background items and `background_limit=0` is unrepresentable over HTTP.

Fix: distinguish "unset" from "explicitly zero" (pointer or a sentinel) and honor an explicit 0.

title: robot: ensemble stop discards capture errors then kills the session, destroying partial outputs
description:
`internal/robot/ensemble_stop.go:150`. The `capture.CaptureAll` error is discarded, then `tmux.KillSession` runs at `:170`, destroying partial outputs while reporting `captured:0` under `success:true`.

Fix: on a capture error, do not kill the session; report `success:false` with the capture error so the operator can retrieve the output.

title: robot: capability catalog advertises deprecated flags and unsupported output formats
description:
`internal/robot/capabilities.go` documents 37 parameters naming flags that `root.go` has already `MarkDeprecated`, with no deprecation note and no canonical replacement. Separately `registry.go:515/525/542/805` advertises `output_formats: ["markdown"]` / `["text"]` while `RobotFormat.IsValid()` (`renderer.go:69-76`) accepts only json/toon/auto — so `--robot-dashboard --robot-format=markdown` returns `INVALID_FLAG`, exit 1.

Also `internal/cli/root.go:4435`: `MarkDeprecated("diagnose-pane", "use --pane instead")` points at `--pane`, which is bound to `robotHistoryPane` and never read by diagnose (`:1927` reads `robotDiagnosePane`), so following the official hint silently diagnoses all panes.

Fix: mark deprecated parameters in the catalog with their replacements, align advertised `output_formats` with `RobotFormat.IsValid()`, and correct the diagnose-pane deprecation target.

title: robot: --robot-agent-health advertises pt_available with an all-zero pt_summary
description:
`internal/robot/agent_health.go:261-278`. `PTAvailable` is set from binary presence, but `ptStates` is only populated when `pt.GetGlobalMonitor().Running()`, which nothing starts outside `ntm serve`. Every `--robot-agent-health` therefore advertises `pt_available:true` with an all-zero `pt_summary` and no per-pane `pt_health`.

Fix: report availability as "binary present but monitor not running" (a distinct state), or start the monitor for the duration of the call.

title: robot: last_known_state is permanently empty because every surface builds a fresh observer
description:
`internal/robot/is_working.go:499` and all five call sites. Every surface builds a fresh `SessionObserver`, so `PaneObservation.LastKnown` is always nil on its single `Observe`. `last_known_state` and `last_known_observed_at` are therefore permanently empty in `--robot-tail` and `--robot-is-working`, making the documented degraded-state fallback (`docs/freshness-degraded-state-contract.md`) dead.

Fix: persist the observation in the runtime projection so a later process can read the prior state, or drop the fields and the contract section.

title: watcher: file_reservation auto_reserve and extend_on_activity are read from config and never used
description:
`internal/watcher/config.go:33-89`. `FileReservationConfigValues.AutoReserve` and `.ExtendOnActivity` are read from TOML (`internal/config/config.go:1095,1098`), passed in at `internal/cli/dashboard.go:163,166`, and then never consumed: `NewFileReservationWatcherFromConfig` only checks `cfg.Enabled` and builds no option from either field. Grep confirms zero readers.

An operator who sets `auto_reserve = false` still gets exclusive 15-minute Agent Mail locks created on every detected edit, and `extend_on_activity` is unimplemented in both directions.

Fix: honor `AutoReserve` (skip `onFileEdit`'s reservation call, or do not attach the detector) and either implement or delete `ExtendOnActivity`.

title: status: unified Detect loses the agent type for the documented target-spec form
description:
`internal/status/unified.go:364-371`. `detector.go:9` documents that `paneID` may be `"mysession:0.1"`. `Detect` then calls `tmux.GetPanesWithActivity(paneID)` (which does resolve — verified `list-panes -s -t rst:0.1` lists the session's panes) but matches with `p.Pane.ID == paneID`, comparing a target spec against tmux IDs like `%3`. The loop never matches, so `status.PaneName` and `status.AgentType` stay empty and `determineState` classifies a Claude/Codex pane with the generic-shell/user heuristics (including the `agentType == "" -> empty output is idle` branch at `:161`). The error from `GetPanesWithActivity` is also discarded (`panes, _ :=`), so a failed lookup is indistinguishable from "pane not in list".

Fix: resolve the selector first (`ResolvePaneSelectors`/`ParsePaneSelector`) or match with `tmux.PaneMatchesSelector`, and propagate the lookup error instead of dropping it.

title: state: timeline Cleanup and CompressOldTimelines report success while discarding every failure
description:
`internal/state/timeline_persist.go:360`. `if err := p.DeleteTimeline(...); err == nil { deleted++ }` drops the error and the function returns `(deleted, nil)`. On a timelines directory that is readable but not unlinkable (permissions, read-only mount), `ntm timeline cleanup` prints `Deleted: 0` and exits 0 while `MaxTimelines` retention is silently never enforced. `CompressOldTimelines` (`:387`) has the identical pattern and its caller ignores the error too.

Fix: accumulate and return the delete errors (`errors.Join`) alongside the count.
close_reason: Cleanup and CompressOldTimelines now accumulate per-item failures with errors.Join instead of only counting successes. runTimelineCleanup already returned Cleanup's error; it now also surfaces compression and recount failures as TimelineCleanupResult.Warnings rather than discarding them with an underscore, and the text renderer prints warnings even on the 'No cleanup needed' path — which is exactly the case a compression failure produced. Covered by TestCleanupReportsDeleteFailures, which makes the timelines dir read-only and asserts (0, error) instead of the old silent (0, nil).

title: util: AtomicWriteFile never fsyncs the parent directory after rename
description:
`util.AtomicWriteFile` syncs the temp file but never fsyncs the parent directory after `os.Rename`, so a crash can lose the directory entry while the temp file is already unlinked, leaving neither the old nor the new file. The same gap exists at `internal/state/timeline_persist.go:579` and `:732`, and `compressTimeline` then `os.Remove`s the only other copy at `:737`.

Low probability, but it sits in the code whose entire purpose is crash-safe checkpointing.

Fix: open the parent directory and `Sync()` it after the rename, before reporting success or removing a source file.

title: state: three relayed findings needing independent verification
description:
These were reported by a delegated sweep but NOT independently reproduced, so treat the severity as provisional and verify first.

1. `internal/state/runtime_store.go:2064-2070` — `GetAttentionReplayWindow()` scans `SELECT MAX(ts) ...` into `sql.NullTime`; because `MAX(ts)` is an expression SQLite reports no decltype, so modernc returns a string and the scan errors on any non-empty `attention_events` table. Claimed effect: SQLite-backed attention replay and `CursorExpired` are dead code — `replayFromStore` treats the error as "no store" and always falls back to the in-memory journal, so post-restart cursor replay silently yields zero events. Proposed fix: scan into `sql.NullString` plus `time.Parse`, or use `SELECT ts ... ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 1` to retain the decltype.

2. `internal/state/schema.go:255-283` — `ApplyMigrations` reads the applied-version set outside the write transaction, so two ntm processes starting concurrently right after a version bump both see version N pending; the loser's `INSERT INTO _migrations` hits the primary key and fails startup with `UNIQUE constraint failed`. `busy_timeout` serializes the writes but does not close the check-then-act window. Proposed fix: `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` and re-read `_migrations` inside the transaction.

3. `internal/state/store.go:82,148` — `state.Open` uses `FileDSN` rather than `ImmediateTransactionFileDSN`, so `CreateOrUpdateIncident`'s read-check-write is not a cross-process CAS (`s.mu` guards goroutines only). Claimed effect: duplicate incidents per fingerprint, or an unretried `SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT`. Note `internal/sqliteutil/dsn.go:17` documents the immediate DSN as required for exactly this pattern, and `internal/bv/bv.go` uses it.

title: pipeline: two lower-severity defects behind the foreach output_var fix
description:
Both are currently masked and should be handled after the foreach `output_var` overwrite is fixed.

1. `internal/pipeline/foreach.go:1015` with `1091-1101` — latent index misalignment. `matchingForeachBodyResultIndex` returns an index into `plans[i].Steps`, but `iterResult.Results` accumulates across all rounds when `max_rounds > 1` (and skips control-only body steps whose `when` is false, `foreach.go:719-734`). So `iter.Results[idx]` is round 1's result, not the final round's, and shifts by one per suppressed control-only step. Observable today only where the overwrite does not apply (a foreach nested in a `loop:` body, since `loops.go:679-685` writes no `output_var`). Fix: match by resolved step ID rather than positional index.

2. `internal/pipeline/executor.go:725` — `e.state.UpdatedAt = time.Now()` is written with no mutex held, while `snapshotState` reads the field under `stateMu.RLock`. Racy against `backgroundCommandWG` workers (`markFireAndForgetCancelled` -> `persistState`). Fix: move the assignment inside the `stateMu.Lock` block at `705-707`, or drop it since `persistState` already sets `UpdatedAt`.

title: serve: five smaller verified defects across scanner, beads, safety, webhook, and shutdown
description:
1. `internal/serve/scanner.go:455-458` — `opts.Path` from the request body is unvalidated and passed to `ubs`; `POST /scanner/run {"path":"/home/victim"}` needs only `sessions:write`, and the results are readable with `health:read`. Fix: confine to `s.projectDir`.
