close_reason: Claude sends are now submission-verified like codex: after the double-Enter protocol both dispatch paths call VerifyAgentSubmission (generalized from VerifyCodexSubmission), which for claude panes captures the visible screen, uses agent.ClaudeActivelyWorking as the authoritative working signal, detects the payload stranded in the bottom-most '❯' composer line (raw text or [Pasted stand-in; history '>' turns and history '❯' echoes excluded), rescues with one Escape (dismisses an open picker; single Escape deliberately — double opens history jump) + Enter, and fails the delivery loudly when submission stays unconfirmed. Fixture tests cover unsubmitted text, [Pasted, empty composer, plain-'>' history turns, and history-echo-above-composer.

title: GH#242: assignment classifier must exclude epics (issue type) from auto-dispatch
description: From github.com/Dicklesworthstone/ntm/issues/242 (full spec there). classifyTriageRecForAssignmentWithGate (internal/cli/assign.go) checks blockers, gate labels, status, and active assignments but never issue type, so an unlabeled open epic is dispatched to a worker pane as implementation work. Fix: classifier reads issue_type and excludes container types (epic) from auto-assignment (operator can still assign explicitly with a flag if ever needed); restore type evidence from br ready + br list like the label gate does. Acceptance: epic in ready set is classified not-assignable with a distinct reason; unit test on the classifier; e2e auto-assign run skips epics.
close_reason: Assignment classifier now excludes container issue types: classifyTriageRecForAssignmentWithGate rejects epics with distinct reason container_issue_type (checked before the operator gate — intrinsic, not policy-liftable); type evidence is restored on plan-sourced recommendations from br ready + br list exactly like label evidence, with the same fail-closed coverage invariant (missing issue type stops assignment); live-details path carries IssueType from br show. Tests: classifier unit (epic/task/mixed-case), plan-path type restoration assertions, fail-closed missing-type test.

title: Async/queued mutation surface for flaky coordination ops (retire detached shell retry-loop folklore)
description:
## Leak (second-pass skill audit 2026-08-04)
OC-030 "Detach Background-Retry Loops To Keep The Pane Moving" and RECOVERY.md "Background-Close / Retry-Loop Detachment" teach agents to run `( for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do timeout 60 <cmd> && break; sleep 20; done ) &` for bead closes, mail sends, coordinator updates, and "any flaky-but-retryable operation" — the RECOVERY variant has the orchestrator dispatch this shell incantation into a pane as a prompt. Fire-and-forget subshells: no completion tracking, possible double-close when the retry eventually lands twice, orphaned loops when the pane restarts.

## Why it matters
ntm's own mutating coordination surfaces (bead close, mail send, coordinator updates) have no async/queue-with-retry mode, so a load-bearing operator card codifies ad-hoc `timeout`/`sleep` job control instead.

## Fix direction
An --async/--enqueue mode on mutating robot surfaces backed by a durable outbox (retry with backoff, idempotency keys, status queryable, completion/failure surfaced via the attention feed); or a generic `ntm defer -- <cmd>` verb with queryable job status.

## Acceptance criteria
- A bead close/mail send issued async during contention completes or reports failure via a queryable surface; no shell retry loop needed.
- Idempotent: a retried close that already succeeded is a no-op, not an error or double-mutation.
- OC-030 / RECOVERY.md retry-loop recipes retirable.

title: ntm doctor contention: cross-platform lock-holder forensics (replace pgrep/proc/kill sweeps; shipped script is Linux-only)
description:
## Leak (second-pass skill audit 2026-08-04)
OC-031, AP-49, RECOVERY.md "Cross-Session Process Contention", and the shipped process-contention-sweep.sh do box-wide lock forensics by hand: `pgrep -af 'br (create|close|...)'`, `readlink /proc/$PID/cwd`, D-state scans via `ps -eo pid,stat`, `lsof | grep beads.db`, then `kill -15; sleep 5; kill -9`. Declared "Step 0 of any 'something is locked' diagnosis". Bonus defect: `/proc` and `ps --sort` are Linux-only — on macOS the shipped script silently prints `cwd=?`, degrading the exact "confirm cwd is NOT in your swarm before killing" safety check.

## Fix direction
`ntm doctor contention` / `--robot-contention`: enumerate holders of shared resources (beads DB, cargo registry, rsync, D-state processes) with pid/cwd/etime cross-platform (gopsutil, not /proc), flag out-of-swarm PIDs, and offer a guarded terminate flow. Distinct from pane liveness (ntm-0g0b): this is box-wide shared-resource forensics, not pane state.

## Acceptance criteria
- One command answers "who is holding the beads DB / cargo lock, from which cwd, how old" on both Linux and macOS.
- Kill flow requires explicit confirmation and refuses in-swarm PIDs unless forced.
- process-contention-sweep.sh retirable.

title: Reconcile build_slots leases on worktree-mode transitions; stale leases as auto-fixable attention items
description:
## Leak (second-pass skill audit 2026-08-04)
AP-24 and RECOVERY.md "Stale build_slots Leases": switching between worktree and non-worktree mode leaves 1-hour build-slot leases active; documented remedies are `ntm --robot-snapshot | jq '.build_slots.leases'`, manual `ntm mail force-release-build-slot <lease_id>`, or "wait out the TTL (<=1 hour)".

## Why it matters
ntm changes isolation mode without reconciling the leases it created, then makes the operator spelunk raw snapshot internals with jq or eat an hour of dead time.

## Fix direction
Invalidate/release build-slot leases automatically on worktree-mode transitions (spawn/restart paths that change isolation); surface any stale lease as an attention item with a one-shot remediation in `--robot-diagnose --diagnose-fix`.

## Acceptance criteria
- Worktree-mode switch leaves no active stale leases (e2e).
- A manufactured stale lease appears in the attention feed with a working auto-fix.
- AP-24 workaround retirable.

## Addendum (third-pass audit 2026-08-04)
RECOVERY.md:311 prescribes `ntm mail force-release-build-slot <lease_id>` — that CLI verb does not exist (internal/cli/mail.go defines only send/inbox/read/ack; the only real release path is the Agent Mail MCP release_build_slot tool). Fix the fabricated verb as part of this bead: either implement it as the manual-release surface or correct the doc to the MCP tool.

title: First-class submit path for the user/control pane (docs prescribe raw tmux; suggested alternative is self-contradictory)
description:
## Leak (second-pass skill audit 2026-08-04)
vibing ROBOT-MODE.md gotcha: "--robot-send does not auto-submit for user pane 1 — prompt sits un-submitted for pane 1 only — for pane 1, use `ntm send --all --skip-first` ... OR raw `tmux send-keys ... Enter`." Two problems: (a) there is no sanctioned non-interactive way to run a command in the user/control pane, so docs prescribe raw tmux; (b) the suggested alternative is self-contradictory — `--all --skip-first` skips the user pane, so it cannot reach it at all.

## Fix direction
Give the user pane a first-class submit path: `--robot-send ... --include-user --submit` honoring the same verify-render contract, or a dedicated `ntm exec-in-pane` verb for the control shell (with dcg-aware safety since the target is a bare shell). Fix the contradictory doc text as part of the change. Distinct from ntm-hykz (accidental user-pane inclusion): this is the deliberate case.

## Acceptance criteria
- A robot command can deliver AND submit a line to the user pane, capture-verified.
- The gotcha entry and its self-contradictory workaround are retired.
close_reason: Verified working on current main — the gap is stale skill folklore, not a missing surface. Empirical evidence (live session, 2026-08-04): (1) --robot-send=SESSION --all --msg='echo ...' delivered AND submitted to the user pane (command executed, marker printed); (2) targeted --robot-send --panes=0 likewise delivered and executed. The robot protocol planner routes user panes through SingleEnter with ShellEnterDelay, which submits — so ntm already has a first-class non-interactive user-pane submit path via explicit selectors or --all (robot --all deliberately means include-user, diverging from CLI send --all which now excludes it per ntm-hykz; both documented in their help). Remaining action is doc-side: the vibing ROBOT-MODE gotcha ('does not auto-submit for pane 1' with the self-contradictory --all --skip-first workaround) must be deleted in the canonical skills repo — same fossil stratum as the restart two-step, folded into the ntm-ep45 skills-drift bead scope. No ntm code change needed or made.

title: spawn --pane-env: ntm-owned per-pane environment (replace prompt-delivered CARGO_TARGET_DIR exports)
description:
## Leak (second-pass skill audit 2026-08-04)
OC-032 and the marching-orders template deliver per-pane build isolation as chat prompts: dispatch `export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/build_<proj>_<role>_p<pane>` (plus GOPATH, BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR) to each agent and ask it to "make these persistent in your shell rc", validated via `lsof +D /tmp/build_*`.

## Why it matters
A core anti-contention control depends on every agent obediently pasting exports — unverifiable, lost when restart-pane respawns to a fresh shell, and validated only by lsof spelunking. ntm creates the panes; it should own their environment.

## Fix direction
`ntm spawn --pane-env KEY=TEMPLATE` (with {project}/{pane}/{role} substitution) or a build-isolation spawn profile that injects the env into the pane's launch command, so it survives respawns; expose the effective per-pane env in robot pane records for verification.

## Acceptance criteria
- Spawned (and respawned) panes carry the templated env without any prompt-delivered exports.
- Robot surface shows the effective env per pane.
- OC-032 prompt recipe retirable.

title: Own the double-Ctrl-C exit timing in code; retire OPERATIONS.md raw-tmux fossil (3 conflicting timings shipped)
description:
## Leak (second-pass skill audit 2026-08-04)
Three references ship three different timings for the same Claude Code exit choreography: OC-014 says C-c, sleep 0.3, C-c; OPERATIONS.md FAQ says 0.1s ("slower timing like 2s doesn't trigger the exit"); RECOVERY.md says "within ~1s". OPERATIONS.md is otherwise a raw-tmux fossil: restart_with_bead() drives assignment via /usr/bin/tmux send-keys against hardcoded session:1.$pane with sleep 0.1/3/6, plus binary-path folklore ("/usr/bin/tmux because the zsh tmux plugin can interfere"), --gmi counts, stale window-numbering claims, and "GPT 5.2".

## Why it matters
The divergent timings prove the double-C-c exit contract is untested folklore living in operator docs instead of one tested code path in ntm. The binary-path folklore only exists because operators hand-drive tmux at all.

## Fix direction
Own the exit choreography (including the empirically-validated inter-C-c delay) inside ntm's exit/kill/restart verbs (extends ntm-2p5x — dependency); then rewrite or delete OPERATIONS.md's raw-tmux sections and reconcile the timing story across OC-014/RECOVERY/OPERATIONS. ntm should also always invoke a resolved absolute tmux binary internally so alias interference is structurally impossible.

## Acceptance criteria
- One tested implementation of the double-C-c exit with a documented, single timing.
- OPERATIONS.md no longer teaches raw-tmux restart choreography; stale flags/model names fixed.
close_reason: Code side complete: one tested implementation of the double-C-c exit lives in --robot-exit-cli (ntm-2p5x, commit 50618431) with lifecycleDoubleTapGap=200ms; new pin test TestLifecycleDoubleTapGap_WithinExitWindow asserts the gap stays inside the empirical 100-300ms window, making code the single source of truth over the three conflicting doc timings. Absolute-binary requirement was already satisfied: internal/tmux/client.go BinaryPath() resolves standard install paths with /usr/bin/tmux fallback and NTM_TMUX_BINARY override, so shell alias/plugin interference is structurally impossible for ntm-driven calls. OPERATIONS.md/OC-014/RECOVERY.md live in the canonical skills repo, not this repo — their rewrite (single timing statement pointing at --robot-exit-cli, delete restart_with_bead() raw-tmux choreography, fix stale flags/model names) is scoped into skills-repo bead ntm-ep45.

title: Cancelable robot-wait handles (escape hatch today is pkill -f)
description:
## Leak (second-pass skill audit 2026-08-04)
CRON-AND-AUTOMATION.md "Escape Hatch": the only documented way to abort a blocking `--robot-wait` is `pkill -f "robot-wait"` — pattern-matching kill of ntm's own processes, which also nukes unrelated waits on other sessions. The same section teaches raw crontab read-modify-write (`crontab -l | grep -v <pattern> | crontab -`) because ntm has no native tick scheduler.

## Fix direction
Wait handles: `--robot-wait ... --wait-id=X` plus `--robot-wait-cancel=X` (and a list surface); longer-term, a built-in `ntm tick` scheduler so orchestrator loops need no crontab surgery.

## Acceptance criteria
- A specific wait can be canceled without killing others; cancel returns a structured result.
- pkill escape hatch retirable from the docs.

title: Disk usage trajectory + per-pane build-dir attribution in robot metrics (replace df-to-/tmp sampling)
description:
## Leak (second-pass skill audit 2026-08-04)
disk-trajectory.sh appends `df -P` samples to /tmp/vibing-disk.log; OBSERVABILITY.md keeps /tmp/disk_tick.$(date +%s) files ("disk trajectory beats absolute threshold"); AP-50. Meanwhile ntm SKILL.md claims operator state "now includes ... resource pressure".

## Why it matters
No robot surface exposes disk deltas per tick or per-pane build-dir attribution, so the operator skill hand-rolls df sampling with /tmp state files.

## Fix direction
Add disk usage + delta-per-interval to `--robot-snapshot`/`--robot-metrics` (ntm already samples on an interval for the monitor), plus optional per-pane target-dir sizes (pairs with the per-pane env bead), and a trajectory alert family ("N GB/hour toward full").

## Acceptance criteria
- One robot call answers "how fast is disk filling and who is filling it".
- disk-trajectory.sh and the /tmp tick files retirable.

title: send --loop-mode: sanctioned CASS dedup exemption (retire rotating-suffix prompt pollution)
description:
## Leak (second-pass skill audit 2026-08-04)
TROUBLESHOOTING.md lists as the PREFERRED fix for CASS duplicate detection: "Use a rotating suffix so it passes the similarity gate: 'Tend pass ${N} at $(date +%H:%M)'"; SEND.md calls the trick "widely used in operator loops".

## Why it matters
Beyond the confirm-hang/parser split (ntm-dv50, related), the skill teaches polluting every steady-state nudge with timestamp noise to game ntm's own similarity gate — junk tokens that also pollute the session archive CASS later searches. Evidence CASS dedup has no sanctioned loop/tending mode.

## Fix direction
A session-scoped dedup exemption: `ntm send --loop-mode` (or per-session config `send.cass_check=off`), letting orchestrator loops send identical periodic nudges cleanly; demote the rotating-suffix trick from the docs.

## Acceptance criteria
- Identical repeated nudges in loop mode dispatch without confirm or suffix games.
- TROUBLESHOOTING/SEND rotating-suffix guidance retirable.

title: Provider-pool health rollup in robot-health-oauth (rotate-by-pool decision needs hand-built jq)
description:
## Leak (second-pass skill audit 2026-08-04)
OC-002's "rotate by pool, not by pane" doctrine requires a hand-built jq aggregate every tick: `ntm --robot-health-oauth=<s> | jq '.panes | group_by(.provider) | map({provider: ..., any_rate_limited: any(.rate_limited)})'`.

## Why it matters
The pool-level rollup (per-provider any/all rate-limited, healthy accounts remaining, rotate recommendation) is the decision-relevant unit, yet it must be assembled client-side.

## Fix direction
Add a `pools` rollup to `--robot-health-oauth` / `--robot-quota-status`: provider -> {panes, rate_limited_count, all_rate_limited, healthy_accounts_remaining, recommendation}.

## Acceptance criteria
- One field answers rotate-by-pool vs rotate-by-pane; OC-002's jq retirable.

title: spawn must not interactively prompt to create directories when non-TTY (hangs orchestrator loops)
description:
## Leak (second-pass skill audit 2026-08-04)
OPERATIONS.md FAQ and the PLAYBOOK troubleshooting table document that `ntm spawn` interactively prompts "Create it? [y/N]" when the session name has no matching directory — an orchestrator loop that misspells a session name hangs on the confirm. The robot-spawn non-interactive contract for this case is undocumented. (Reproduced live this session: a scripted spawn sat at the prompt until "Aborted".)

## Fix direction
When stdin is not a TTY (or NTM_NONINTERACTIVE=1), spawn must not prompt: return a structured error (directory not found; hint: --create or ntm quick) with non-zero exit; add explicit --create opt-in. Adjacent to but distinct from the symlink-key beads (ntm-cx4e/ntm-w8wa).

## Acceptance criteria
- Piped/non-TTY spawn with a missing directory exits non-zero immediately with a structured error; --create performs the creation.
- Docs updated; interactive TTY behavior unchanged.
close_reason: spawn no longer blocks non-interactive callers on the Create it? [y/N] prompt: when stdin/stdout is not a TTY (or NTM_NONINTERACTIVE=1) a missing project directory is a structured non-zero error naming the fix (--create-dir or ntm quick); new --create-dir flag opts into creation explicitly; JSON/robot spawns keep their auto-create contract; interactive TTY behavior unchanged. E2E verified both paths (error exit 1, --create-dir creates+spawns); regression test TestSpawnMissingDirNonTTYFailsFast.

title: get_all_session_text: controller detection hardcodes pane.Index==1 (wrong for base-index-0 sessions)
description: Found during 2026-08-04 fresh-eyes review. internal/cli/get_all_session_text.go collectSessionStatus classifies the controller pane as pane.Index == 1 ('based on user's swarm setup' comment) — but tmux pane indices are base-index dependent and ntm's own spawn puts the user pane at the first index (0 on default configs). On base-0 sessions the user shell is misclassified as a worker and pane 1 (an agent) as controller. Same numbering-assumption family as ntm-bb87. Fix: classify by agent type (tmux.AgentUser) or pane title, never by raw index; unit test with base-0 and base-1 fixtures.
close_reason: Controller classification now keys on agent type (pane.Type.Canonical() == AgentUser) via extracted paneIsController predicate; raw pane-index check removed, doc comment fixed (was 'pane 1 is controller'). Fixture test covers user pane at base-0 and base-1 indices plus agent panes at both indices.

title: robot-wait: add rate_limit_lifted condition — rate_limited semantics are INVERTED across 5 doc sites and the cron recipe is harmful
description:
## Leak (third-pass skill audit 2026-08-04, source-verified)
Five doc sites teach `--robot-wait --wait-until=rate_limited` as "wake when the wall DROPS" (vibing SKILL.md:435,469; PLAYBOOK.md:242; ROBOT-MODE.md:144; RECOVERY.md:93; CRON-AND-AUTOMATION.md:98 which builds an unattended recipe on it: wait then broadcast "Rate limit lifted. Resume"). Reality (internal/robot/wait.go:627): the condition fires when a pane BECOMES rate-limited. No negated/lifted condition exists in isSingleValidWaitCondition or the capabilities registry.

## Why it matters
The documented cron recipe is actively harmful: if any pane is already limited the wait returns instantly and broadcasts "Rate limit lifted. Resume" into a rate-limited swarm; otherwise it wakes at the exact moment a pane hits the wall and does the same. ntm has no "wake me when the wall lifts" surface at all, so the skills paper over the hole with inverted semantics.

## Fix direction
Add a `rate_limit_lifted` wait condition (or a generic `--wait-not`/negation modifier) — wait.go's RequireTransition machinery is most of the plumbing. Register in capabilities. Then correct all five doc sites (canonical skills: ~/projects/je_private_skills_repo) to use the real condition, and keep `rate_limited` documented as "fires when a pane BECOMES limited".

## Acceptance criteria
- `--robot-wait --wait-until=rate_limit_lifted` blocks while any target pane is rate-limited and returns when none are (transition-aware; test with classifier fixtures).
- Capabilities registry lists both conditions with correct one-line semantics.
- The five doc sites corrected; CRON recipe rebuilt on the new condition.
close_reason: Added rate_limit_lifted wait condition: met per-pane when NOT rate-limited, so --robot-wait --wait-until=rate_limit_lifted blocks while any target pane shows the wall and returns once the whole set is clear. rate_limited keeps (and now documents) its real BECOMES-limited semantics in the constant docs, --wait-until help, and --robot-capabilities. Tests pin both directions plus the composed mixed-swarm case. Doc audit: the CANONICAL vibing skill (je_private_skills_repo) was already corrected to positive semantics with a healthy+--wait-transition workaround — the harmful inverted text exists only in the stale installed copy, refreshed by harmonize. Follow-up for the skill: replace the transition workaround with rate_limit_lifted once this ships.

title: Per-pane kill verb: recovery ladder Rung 6 prescribes ntm kill --pane=N which does not exist
description:
## Leak (third-pass skill audit 2026-08-04, source-verified)
The recovery ladder's terminal rung is unexecutable: RECOVERY.md:224 and OC-029 instruct `ntm kill <session> --pane=N` to remove a broken pane before `ntm add`-ing a replacement, but `ntm kill` has no --pane flag (internal/cli/send.go:2473 — only --force/--tag/--no-hooks/--summarize/--project; kills the whole session). No per-pane removal verb exists anywhere (respawn restarts in place; nothing removes), and no --robot-kill-pane. An agent following the ladder gets `unknown flag` and falls back to raw `tmux kill-pane`.

## Fix direction
Add per-pane removal: `ntm kill <session> --pane=<selector>` (shared N/W.P/%N grammar) plus a robot variant, with the usual guarded semantics (refuse the user pane without --force, report removed pane identity). Distinct from ntm-2p5x (exit-cli/kill-agent target the agent PROCESS and preserve the pane; this removes the pane itself) — coordinate the verb naming so the trio is coherent.

## Acceptance criteria
- Killing a specific pane via ntm works with the shared selector grammar and structured result; session and sibling panes untouched.
- RECOVERY Rung 6 / OC-029 become executable as written (skill text updated to the real flag; canonical skills repo).
- e2e: spawn 3 agents, remove 1, verify topology and that status/robot surfaces reflect it.
close_reason: Shipped per-pane removal both ways: 'ntm kill SESSION --pane=SELECTOR' (shared N/W.P/%N grammar, comma-separated, confirmation unless --force, rejects --project/--tag/--summarize combos) and --robot-kill-pane=SESSION --panes=... (explicit selection required — no default-all for a destructive verb). Guards: user pane refused without --force; selection covering every pane refused with hint to use 'ntm kill SESSION'; removal verified by pane-list refresh, structured {removed[{pane,target,title,agent_type}], failed, remaining_panes}. E2E on live 3-agent spawn: removed pane 2 via robot verb (siblings untouched, remaining_panes=3), topology renumbering reflected in pane-address, stale-selector error lists live selectors, CLI --pane=%ID removal worked, remove-all and user-pane guards fired. Schema binding kill_pane + capabilities + docs + registry golden. Suites green. Skill-text update (RECOVERY Rung 6 / OC-029) tracked in ntm-ep45.

title: Skill drift: unconditional restart two-step corrupts current builds (types 'cc' into a live agent composer)
description:
## Leak (third-pass skill audit 2026-08-04, source-verified)
Cross-drift inside the vibing skill: SKILL.md:525 correctly version-gates the restart two-step ("on ntm >= 1.18.4 restart-pane relaunches the agent; on older builds it leaves a bare shell"), but OC-027, AP-39, RECOVERY.md "Two-Step Relaunch", pane-liveness-audit.sh's legend, and the SKILL.md symptom table all teach the manual `tmux send-keys "cc" Enter; sleep 10` two-step UNCONDITIONALLY. Current ntm relaunches the agent, ready-gates it, and reports agent_relaunched/agent_relaunch_status/prompt_delivery per pane (internal/robot/restart_pane.go:55-91) plus --restart-model/--restart-agent-args.

## Why it matters
On a current binary, obeying OC-027 types the literal text "cc" into a pane whose agent already relaunched — junk prompt into the composer (or a nested CLI), a wasted 10s sleep, then a duplicate dispatch. The recipe that recovers old builds actively corrupts new ones.

## Fix direction
Skill-side rewrite (canonical: ~/projects/je_private_skills_repo, vibing-with-ntm): all restart guidance keys on the restart-pane response fields (agent_relaunched + prompt_delivery); the manual two-step survives only under an explicit "ntm < 1.18.4" gate. ntm-side: none required (behavior already shipped) — this bead tracks the doc reconciliation so the corrupting recipe dies. Related: ntm-tgkb covers the verification-contract half.

## Acceptance criteria
- No unconditional two-step remains in OC-027/AP-39/RECOVERY/script legends; response-field-driven flow documented instead.
notes:
+ ntm-34jt shipped: RECOVERY.md Rung 6 / OC-029 'ntm kill <session> --pane=N' is now real (CLI kill --pane=SELECTOR + --robot-kill-pane=SESSION --panes=...); update skill text to drop the raw tmux kill-pane fallback.
+ ntm-2p5x shipped: OPERATIONS.md manual double-C-c exit and pgrep/kill -9 recipes replaced by --robot-exit-cli / --robot-kill-agent (--relaunch supported); retire those doc sections.
+ ntm-3lbb: reconcile the double-C-c timing story across OC-014 / OPERATIONS.md FAQ / RECOVERY.md to ONE statement: 'use ntm --robot-exit-cli; ntm owns the timing (200ms tap gap, tested in code)'. Delete restart_with_bead()'s raw /usr/bin/tmux choreography and the binary-path folklore (ntm resolves an absolute tmux binary internally; NTM_TMUX_BINARY overrides). Fix stale --gmi counts, window-numbering claims, 'GPT 5.2'.
+ ntm-qdtd shipped: AP-14 ('skip ntm rotate, go straight to --robot-restart-pane') retirable — 'ntm rotate SESSION --pane=N --force' now does bounded kill-and-relaunch for wedged CLIs.
+ ntm-xcji shipped: RECOVERY.md 'Interactive Pane Blockers' blind-keystroke recipes (tmux send-keys '2' Enter etc.) replaced by --robot-dialogs + --robot-answer-dialog with destructive-confirm policy; update skill text.

title: Skill sweep: retired-gmi mix tables + invalid name-based --pane examples in ARCHITECTURE/OPERATIONS
description:
## Leak (third-pass skill audit 2026-08-04, source-verified)
Retired-gmi fossil layer in the vibing skill: ARCHITECTURE.md:113 recommends `--cc=3 --cod=2 --gmi=1` mixes and `:159` uses `ntm send --pane cc-4` — but `--pane` takes an integer/W.P/%N selector (name-based addressing fails outright, pushing agents to raw tmux); OPERATIONS.md:15-28 recommends `--gmi=4` swarms with a Gemini model-strengths table and stale model names ("GPT 5.2"). title: serve: request-derived id reaches a file write sink in the approvals/wrapper install path
description:
## Finding (UBS taint scan, 2026-08-04, while working bd-fresh-eyes-audit .30)
UBS lightweight taint analysis reports a request-derived path reaching a file read/write sink in internal/serve/safety.go:

- internal/serve/safety.go:1356  `_, err := os.Stat(path)`   [id -> approval -> approvalCopy -> file sink]
- internal/serve/safety.go:1365  `os.WriteFile(path, []byte(content), 0755)`   [id -> approval -> approvalCopy -> file sink]

The taint source is a request-supplied approval `id`, flowing through the approval record into installWrapperFile's path argument. Note the write mode is 0755 (executable) and installWrapperFile is how the git/rm safety wrappers get installed — so if the path is attacker-influenceable this writes an executable file at a chosen location, which is a privilege-escalation shape, not just a traversal.

## NOT introduced by the .30 fix
Confirmed pre-existing: the .30 change is confined to handlePolicyAutomationUpdateV1 (~line 845-870) and does not touch installWrapperFile or the approval path. Filed separately rather than expanding that bead's scope.

## Work
1. Confirm whether the trace is real or a taint false positive — walk id -> approval -> approvalCopy and determine whether any request-controlled component actually reaches the path argument, or whether the path is always derived from server-side constants.
2. If reachable: confine the path (filepath.Rel containment against the intended install root, reject absolute/.. components) before any Stat/WriteFile, and reconsider the 0755 mode.
3. If a false positive: document why in a comment at the sink so the next auditor does not re-litigate it.

## Acceptance criteria
- A definitive reachable/not-reachable verdict with the code path written down.
- If reachable, a test that a crafted approval id cannot cause a write outside the intended directory.
- UBS critical count for internal/serve/safety.go returns to 0, or the remaining finding is documented as an accepted false positive.
close_reason: VERDICT: not reachable — the taint trace is a false positive, and the scan incidentally surfaced two REAL bugs of a different class, both fixed. (1) False-positive proof: approvalCopy (safety.go:1074) is a value copy of an in-memory approval record whose only consumer is toJSONMap -> HTTP response; it never reaches a path argument. All three installWrapperFile call sites pass paths built entirely from server-side constants rooted at os.UserHomeDir — ~/.ntm/bin/git, ~/.ntm/bin/rm, ~/.claude/hooks/PreToolUse/ntm-safety.sh — with the only request-derived input being the force boolean and content being a package-level script constant. The 0755 mode is required (the shell must exec these wrappers). Documented at the sink with the reasoning AND the condition that would make it real, so the next auditor neither re-litigates it nor misses a future request-derived caller. (2) Real bugs found while tracing the write sinks: handlePolicyUpdateV1 and handlePolicyResetV1 both hardcoded $HOME/.ntm/policy.yaml — the exact shadowing class fixed in bd-fresh-eyes-audit .30, which had only covered handlePolicyAutomationUpdateV1. PUT /policy would write raw content to a home file that then takes precedence over an enforced project-local policy, and POST /policy/reset would neither reset the enforced rules nor leave them intact (it writes defaults to home, silently shadowing the project file it left on disk). Both now use policy.ResolveEffectivePath(). serve+policy suites green; vet clean.
